_about: Quranic near-synonyms (Nijanse / Nuances): per group what the words share, how each differs, and ayat that show why the word was chosen there. Keyed by the group's page slug. Each member names its corpus identity: `verb` (root_form, the verb catalogue) or `lemmas` (lemma|root of the noun catalogue, summed when the corpus files one word under several lemmas); `count` must equal the corpus count and every cited ayah must hold the member's lemma (fil.nuances.gate, run by the tests and `fil nuances check`). An optional `spoken` is the headword as voiced where the two speech readers disagree on how it is shown. Explanations are our own words, grounded in the classical works named in `sources`; `notes` record the decisions taken; `verified` names the classical text the group's attributed claims were checked against and the entries read there (ar-Rāġib's Mufradāt in OpenITI: `fil nuances mufradat ROOT`) — a group that names ar-Rāġib without it fails the gate. Validated on load (fil.nuances.model).

shared.bs: Svih pet riječi govore o čovjeku ili ljudima, ali svaka ističe drugu stranu: narav, tjelesnu i vidljivu pojavu, muški spol, pojedinca ili zajednicu ljudi.
shared.en: All five words speak of a human being or of people, but each looks from a different angle: human nature, the visible bodily creature, the male, the single individual, or people as a community.

tellApart.bs: Ljudska narav → إِنْسَان; tjelesno, vidljivo biće → بَشَر; muškarac (nasuprot ženi ili meleku) → رَجُل; pojedinac, kako ga Kur'an upotrebljava („svaki čovjek…”, 52:21) → اِمْرُؤ; ljudi kao zajednica → نَاس.
tellApart.en: Human nature → إِنْسَان; the visible, bodily creature → بَشَر; the male (as against a woman or an angel) → رَجُل; the single person, as the Quran uses it (“every person…”, 52:21) → اِمْرُؤ; people as a community → نَاس.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries إنس, بشر, رجل, مرأ, نوس
notes: اِمْرُؤ: the corpus files this one word under four lemmas (امْرِئ 5, مَرْء 4, امْرُؤٌا 1, امْرَأ 1); with the article it is الْمَرْء. Counted together (11), as ar-Rāġib treats them as one word.

رَجُل: the corpus lemmatises the broken plural رِجَال separately (28); counted together with the singular (29). Two of the plural's places (2:239, 22:27) mean 'on foot' (plural of رَاجِل) but are filed under the same lemma by the corpus; the count follows the corpus.
نَاس: the sense 'people of virtue' (2:13) is ar-Rāġib's reading and is attributed to him.
اِمْرُؤ: the lexicons define it as a person, a (male) human being; 'the individual' is our observation of its Quranic use, stated as such and not attributed to ar-Rāġib (blind review).

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries إنس, بشر, رجل, مرأ, نوس (2026-11-06): 11 attributed points confirmed; changed — sources/0 (reworded): The nās/2:13 reading is in his entry نوس, which the source line did not list; members/4/ayat/2/why (reworded): He reads 2:13 as 'those in whom the meaning of humanity is found', not explicitly 'the believers'
Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): اِمْرُؤ as 'the single person' is marked as Quranic usage (52:21), not ar-Rāġib's.
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (أنس → إنس).

nuance.bs: Čovjek kao vrsta, sa svojom naravi i slabostima. Ar-Rāġib riječ veže za uns – bliskost i druženje, jer čovjek ne može opstati bez drugih – a navodi i mišljenje da dolazi od nisjān (zaborav). Kur'an je najčešće koristi kada kazuje kakav je čovjek.
nuance.en: Man as a species, with his nature and his weaknesses. Ar-Rāġib links the word to uns — familiarity and company, since man cannot survive without others — and also mentions the view that it comes from nisyān (forgetting). The Quran mostly uses it when it says what man is like.

why.bs: Opisuje se ljudska narav – nestrpljivost s kojom je čovjek stvoren.
why.en: Human nature is described — the restlessness man was created with.

why.bs: Slabost kao crta ljudske prirode.
why.en: Weakness as a trait of human nature.

why.bs: Brzopletost – još jedna osobina koju Kur'an pripisuje čovjeku kao takvom.
why.en: Haste — another trait the Quran ascribes to man as such.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, riječ je od bašara (koža): čovjek onakav kakav se vidi izvana, biće od tijela i kože. Kur'an je koristi kad je riječ o tjelesnom stvaranju čovjeka ili kad se kaže da je poslanik čovjek kao i drugi. Isti oblik služi za jedninu i množinu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the word comes from bashara (skin): man as he appears outwardly, a creature of body and skin. The Quran uses it where man's bodily creation is meant, or where a messenger is said to be a man like others. The same form serves for one and for many.

why.bs: Stvaranje čovjekova tijela od ilovače – tjelesna strana, zato بَشَر.
why.en: The creation of man's body from clay — the bodily side, hence bashar.

why.bs: Poslanik je čovjek, smrtnik kao i oni kojima se obraća; razlikuje ga objava koja mu dolazi.
why.en: The Prophet is a man, mortal like those he addresses; what sets him apart is the revelation he receives.

why.bs: Od zemlje stvoreni, ljudi postaju tjelesna bića koja se rasprostiru po zemlji.
why.en: Created from dust, people become bodily beings spreading over the earth.

nuance.bs: Muška osoba. Ar-Rāġib kaže da je riječ svojstvena muškarcu među ljudima; u Kur'anu stoji nasuprot ženi, ali i nasuprot meleku. U množini (رِجَال) često hvali ljude čvrstog karaktera.
nuance.en: A male person. Ar-Rāġib says the word belongs to the male among people; in the Quran it stands against woman, and also against angel. In the plural (رِجَال) it often praises men of firm character.

why.bs: Muškarci i žene od jednog para – رِجَال nasuprot نِسَاء.
why.en: Men and women from one pair — rijāl as against nisāʾ.

why.bs: Da je poslan melek, imao bi lik čovjeka-muškarca: رَجُل kao suprotnost meleku.
why.en: Had an angel been sent, he would have been made a man: rajul as the opposite of an angel.

why.bs: Ljudi koje trgovina ne odvraća od sjećanja na Allaha – množina koja hvali karakter.
why.en: Men whom trade does not distract from remembering Allah — a plural that praises character.

nuance.bs: Osoba, čovjek (muškog roda; ženski oblik je imra'a). U Kur'anu se javlja uglavnom gdje se govori o pojedincu: o ličnoj odgovornosti i o propisima koji se tiču jedne osobe.
nuance.en: A person, a human being (a man; the feminine is imraʾa). In the Quran it appears mainly where the individual is in view: personal accountability and rulings about one person.

why.bs: Na Sudnjem danu svako bježi od svoga brata – čovjek kao pojedinac.
why.en: On the Day each one flees from his brother — man as an individual.

why.bs: Svaki je čovjek zalog onoga što je zaradio – lična odgovornost.
why.en: Every person is pledged for what he has earned — personal accountability.

why.bs: Propis o nasljedstvu jedne osobe koja umre bez djeteta.
why.en: A ruling on the inheritance of one person who dies without a child.

nuance.bs: Ljudi kao skupina, čovječanstvo u cjelini; riječ obraćanja svim ljudima („O ljudi”). Ar-Rāġib napominje da ponekad znači samo vrijedne ljude, kao u 2:13.
nuance.en: People as a group, mankind as a whole; the word of address to all people (“O mankind”). Ar-Rāġib notes that it sometimes means only people of worth, as in 2:13.

why.bs: Obraćanje cijelom čovječanstvu, stvorenom od muškarca i žene.
why.en: An address to all mankind, created from a male and a female.

why.bs: Gospodar svih ljudi – ljudi kao cjelina.
why.en: The Lord of mankind — people as a whole.

why.bs: „Vjerujte kao što su vjerovali ljudi”: prema ar-Rāġibu, ovdje su to ljudi u kojima je istinska ljudskost, ljudi od vrijednosti.
why.en: “Believe as the people have believed”: according to ar-Rāġib, here these are people in whom true humanity is found, people of worth.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače „doći” i često se mogu zamijeniti; klasični leksikografi ipak bilježe razliku u naglasku.
shared.en: Both verbs mean “to come” and are often interchangeable; the classical lexicographers nevertheless record a difference of emphasis.

tellApart.bs: Naglasak na stvarnom dolasku (stizanju) → جَاءَ; dolazak s lahkoćom, ili dolazak sagledan kao usmjeren ka cilju, bez naglaska na stizanju → أَتَى. Razlika je u naglasku, ne strogo pravilo: oba se kažu i za ono što tek treba doći.
tellApart.en: Stress on actual arrival → جَاءَ; a coming with ease, or a coming seen as directed toward its goal without stressing arrival → أَتَى. A difference of emphasis, not a strict rule: both are used of events still to come.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أتى, جاء
notes: The distinction is ar-Rāġib's (al-ityān is a coming with ease and may be said by intention before arrival; al-majīʾ is more general and said with regard to arrival) and is attributed to him.
Later scholars' view that جَاءَ is used for weightier matters and أَتَى for lighter ones is not used: it is not in the two classical works this section relies on.
Only Form I أَتَى is a member; Form IV آتَى 'to give' is a different verb.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries جاء, أتى (2026-11-06): 5 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): He says ityān may be said with regard to intent even if arrival never results, not 'on its way before fully arriving'
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (جيأ → جاء).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, općenitija riječ, koja se kaže s obzirom na stvarni dolazak – stizanje (ḥuṣūl).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the more general word, said with regard to actual arrival (ḥuṣūl).

why.bs: Istina je došla i neistina je nestala – dolazak s vidljivom posljedicom.
why.en: Truth has come and falsehood has vanished — an arrival with a visible result.

why.bs: Kad dođe njihov rok, ne može se odgoditi – stvarni, odlučujući dolazak.
why.en: When their term comes it cannot be delayed — a real, decisive arrival.

why.bs: Kad stigne Allahova pomoć i pobjeda – dolazak predstavljen kao stizanje.
why.en: When the help of Allah and the victory come — the coming presented as an arrival.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, „dolazak s lahkoćom”; može se reći i s obzirom na namjeru dolaska, čak i kad do samog dolaska ne dođe.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, “a coming with ease”; it may also be said with regard to the intent to come, even when the arrival does not take place.

why.bs: Allahova odredba „je došla”, a ipak se kaže „ne požurujte je”; tefsir prošlo vrijeme tumači sigurnošću onoga što dolazi. Primjer dolaska koji je tek na putu.
why.en: The command of Allah “has come”, yet they are told “do not hasten it”; tafsir explains the past tense as the certainty of what is coming. An example of a coming still on its way.

why.bs: Vrijeme je prošlo nad čovjekom dok još nije bio spomena vrijedan.
why.en: A period of time came upon man when he was not yet a thing worth mentioning.

why.bs: Vijest o Musau koja do slušaoca stiže.
why.en: The story of Moses, reaching the listener.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi su o vidu, ali jedna je čin gledanja, druga samo viđenje, a treća jasno opažanje – i očima i pronicljivošću.
shared.en: All three words are about sight, but one is the act of looking, one is seeing itself, and one is clear perception — by the eyes and by insight.

tellApart.bs: نَظَرَ je usmjeravanje pogleda (i misli) i može ostati bez viđenja; رَأَى je samo viđenje – očima, u snu ili razumom; أَبْصَرَ je jasno opažanje, često i uviđanje istine. U 7:198 je razlika na jednom mjestu: gledaju (يَنْظُرُونَ), a ne vide (لَا يُبْصِرُونَ).
tellApart.en: نَظَرَ is directing the gaze (and the mind) and may stop short of seeing; رَأَى is seeing itself — with the eyes, in a dream or with the mind; أَبْصَرَ is clear perception, often grasping the truth. 7:198 holds the difference in one place: they look (يَنْظُرُونَ) but do not see (لَا يُبْصِرُونَ).

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رأى, نظر, بصر
notes: أَبْصَرَ is the Form IV verb (29); the rare Form I بَصُرَ (3) is not a member.
105:1 أَلَمْ تَرَ: the Prophet was not an eyewitness of the event, so the seeing is read as knowing (cf. ar-Rāġib's 'seeing by the intellect'; he does not cite 105:1); stated as a reading.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رأى, نظر, بصر (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/1 (reworded): He has a category of seeing by the intellect (example 53:11) but does not cite 105:1; members/0/nuance (reworded): His second kind is supposition/imagination (example 'I think Zayd has left'), not dreams; and he says ra'ā means knowing when it takes two objects, without 'for certain'; members/1/nuance (reattributed): Al-ʿAskarī cannot be checked, but ar-Rāġib himself defines naẓar as turning the eye to perceive and see a thing, and says one may look and not see; sources/0 (dropped): al-ʿAskarī's source line dropped: his naẓar/ruʾya wording cannot be checked here, and ar-Rāġib (نظر) makes the same point, so the nuance now cites him
Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): naẓar given with his 'eye and insight (baṣīra)'.

nuance.bs: Viđenje kao opažaj. Ar-Rāġib navodi viđenje osjetilom, pretpostavkom i maštom, razmišljanjem i razumom – zato رَأَى znači i „vidjeti očima” i, s dva objekta, „znati”.
nuance.en: Seeing as perception. Ar-Rāġib lists seeing by the senses, by supposition and imagination, by reflection and by the intellect — so رَأَى means both “to see with the eyes” and, with two objects, “to know”.

why.bs: Ibrahim je ugledao zvijezdu – viđenje očima.
why.en: Abraham saw a star — sight with the eyes.

why.bs: Jusuf je vidio jedanaest zvijezda u snu – viđenje u snu.
why.en: Joseph saw eleven stars in a dream — seeing in a dream.

why.bs: „Zar nisi vidio…” o događaju koji Poslanik nije gledao očima: viđenje kao sigurno znanje.
why.en: “Have you not seen…” of an event the Prophet did not witness with his eyes: seeing as certain knowledge.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib: nazar je okretanje oka i unutrašnjeg uvida (بَصِيرَة) prema nečemu da bi se opazilo, a ru'ja je samo viđenje – pa se može gledati, a ne vidjeti. Znači i razmatranje i ispitivanje razumom.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib: naẓar is turning the eye and the mind's insight (بَصِيرَة) toward something in order to perceive it, while ruʾya is the seeing itself — so one may look and not see. It also means considering and examining with the mind.

why.bs: Gledaju prema tebi, a ne vide (jedni tumače: kipovi s izrezanim očima, drugi: mnogobošci) – gledanje bez viđenja.
why.en: They look toward you but do not see (some say the idols, whose carved eyes seem to look; others, the idolaters) — looking without seeing.

why.bs: Poziv da se pogled zadrži na devi i razmisli kako je stvorena.
why.en: A call to rest the gaze on the camel and reflect on how it was created.

why.bs: „Neka čovjek razmisli od čega je stvoren” – gledanje kao razmišljanje.
why.en: “Let man consider from what he was created” — looking as reflection.

nuance.bs: Od baṣar – vid kao moć opažanja; ar-Rāġib kaže da se ista riječ odnosi na oko i na pronicljivost srca (baṣīra). U Kur'anu أَبْصَرَ često upućuje na uvid – uviđanje istine.
nuance.en: From baṣar — sight as a power of perception; ar-Rāġib says the same word is used for the eye and for the insight of the heart (baṣīra). In the Quran أَبْصَرَ often points to insight — grasping the truth.

why.bs: Pogled je tu, ali viđenja nema: „a ne vide” – prema jednom tumačenju, ne uviđaju istinu.
why.en: The gaze is there, but no seeing: “but they do not see” — on one reading, they do not perceive the truth.

why.bs: Na Sudnjem danu grešnici kažu „sad smo vidjeli” – istina im je postala jasna.
why.en: On the Day the wrongdoers say “now we have seen” — the truth has become clear to them.

why.bs: Gledaju u Poslanika, a nemaju uvida; one koji ne uviđaju, slijepe srcem, puko gledanje ne upućuje.
why.en: They look at the Prophet yet have no insight; the blind of heart are not guided by looking alone.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače strah od nečega što može nauditi; خَشْيَة tom strahu dodaje poštovanje i znanje o veličini onoga od koga se strahuje.
shared.en: Both words mean fear of something that may harm; خَشْيَة adds to that fear reverence and knowledge of the greatness of the one who is feared.

tellApart.bs: Strah od bilo čega opasnog → خَوْف; strah sa strahopoštovanjem, najčešće prema Allahu → خَشْيَة. U 13:21 stoje oba glagola: „boje se (يَخْشَوْنَ) svoga Gospodara i strahuju (يَخَافُونَ) od teškog obračuna.”
tellApart.en: Fear of anything dangerous → خَوْف; fear joined with awe, most often toward Allah → خَشْيَة. 13:21 holds both verbs: “they fear (يَخْشَوْنَ) their Lord and are afraid (يَخَافُونَ) of the evil reckoning.”

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries خوف, خشى
notes: ar-Rāġib says khashya is 'most often' (akṯaru mā yakūnu) born of knowledge; 17:31 (fear of poverty) shows the word is also used of fear of a thing itself, so the page states a tendency and shows that ayah.

al-ʿAskarī's distinction between the two is held back: the blind reviewer recalled a different formulation of it, and it could not be checked against the text here. 13:21 uses the verbs, not these nouns, so it is quoted in the summary, not as an illustration.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries خوف, خشى (2026-11-06): 6 attributed points confirmed
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (خشي → خشى).

nuance.bs: Opća riječ za strah. Ar-Rāġib je opisuje kao očekivanje nečeg neželjenog na osnovu znaka koji se pretpostavlja ili zna. Strah od opasnosti, gladi, neprijatelja; suprotnost sigurnosti (أَمْن).
nuance.en: The general word for fear. Ar-Rāġib describes it as expecting something unwanted from a sign that is supposed or known. Fear of danger, hunger, an enemy; the opposite of security (أَمْن).

why.bs: Sigurnost od straha: خَوْف kao suprotnost sigurnosti.
why.en: Security from fear: khawf as the opposite of safety.

why.bs: Iskušenje strahom i glađu – strah od ovosvjetskih nedaća.
why.en: A trial of fear and hunger — fear of worldly hardship.

why.bs: „Neće se ničega bojati” – opća riječ, zanijekana u cijelosti.
why.en: “No fear will there be concerning them” — the general word, negated entirely.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, strah pomiješan s poštovanjem, koji najčešće proizlazi iz znanja o onome čega se boji. Ipak, riječ se kaže i za strah od same stvari (17:31), pa je ovo težnja, a ne pravilo.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, fear mixed with reverence, most often born of knowledge of what is feared. Yet the word is also said of fear of a thing itself (17:31), so this is a tendency, not a rule.

why.bs: Brdo bi se rascijepilo od strahopoštovanja prema Allahu – strah koji dolazi uz spoznaju Njegove veličine.
why.en: A mountain would split from awe of Allah — fear that comes with knowing His greatness.

why.bs: Vjernici zabrinuti iz strahopoštovanja prema svome Gospodaru.
why.en: Believers apprehensive out of awe of their Lord.

why.bs: „Iz straha od siromaštva” – iznimka: خَشْيَة i za strah od same nevolje.
why.en: “For fear of poverty” — the exception: khashya also for fear of the hardship itself.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi imenuju unutrašnjost čovjeka u kojoj su razumijevanje, vjerovanje i osjećanja; razlikuju se po tome koja je strana u prvom planu.
shared.en: All three words name the inner seat of understanding, faith and feeling; they differ in which side of it is in view.

tellApart.bs: Srce koje razumije i vjeruje → قَلْب; srce u žaru osjećanja → فُؤَاد; grudi koje srce nose – širenje, stezanje i ono što je skriveno → صَدْر.
tellApart.en: The heart that understands and believes → قَلْب; the heart aflame with feeling → فُؤَاد; the breast that holds the heart — expansion, constriction and what is hidden → صَدْر.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قلب, فأد, صدر
notes: The fuʾād-as-glowing link (faʾada, to roast) is ar-Rāġib's etymology and is attributed to him.

The saying that 'breast' covers the heart's understanding and the other inner forces (desire, anger) is given as 'it has been said': ar-Rāġib quotes it under صدر from 'some sages' (baʿḍ al-ḥukamāʾ), not as his own view.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries قلب, فأد, صدر (2026-11-06): 5 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/1 (improved): The saying is in the Mufradāt under صدر, quoted from 'some sages' (قال بعض الحكماء); members/0/nuance (reworded): He gives the taqallub etymology as a reported view ('qīla'), not as his own statement; members/1/ayat/2/why (reworded): On 104:7 he says singling out the afʾida points to the fire's overwhelming effect, not explicitly to the word's link with burning

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib prenosi da je srce, kako se kaže, tako nazvano zbog čestog prevrtanja (taqallub) i da se njime izražava ono što mu pripada: duša, znanje, hrabrost. U Kur'anu je sjedište razumijevanja, vjerovanja i sjećanja na Allaha.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib reports that the heart is said to be so named for its frequent turning (taqallub) and that it expresses what belongs to it: spirit, knowledge, courage. In the Quran it is the seat of understanding, faith and remembrance of Allah.

why.bs: Srca kojima se razumije – قَلْب kao sjedište razuma.
why.en: Hearts with which to understand — qalb as the seat of reason.

why.bs: Srca se smiruju spominjanjem Allaha – srce vjere.
why.en: Hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah — the heart of faith.

why.bs: Pouka za onoga ko ima srce – sposobnost da shvati.
why.en: A reminder for whoever has a heart — the capacity to understand.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, isto što i قَلْب, ali se zove fu'ād kad je u pitanju značenje žara i gorenja (od fa'ada – peći). Srce kao mjesto snažnog osjećanja i unutrašnjeg doživljaja; Kur'an فُؤَاد navodi i uz sluh i vid, kao organ spoznaje (17:36).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the same as قَلْب, but called fuʾād when the sense of glowing and burning is in view (from faʾada — to roast). The heart as the place of strong feeling and inner experience; the Quran also names the fuʾād beside hearing and sight, as an organ of perception (17:36).

why.bs: Srce (فُؤَاد) Musaove majke ostalo je „prazno” (tefsir se razilazi: bez strpljenja, ili bez svega osim misli na sina), a u istom ajetu Allah učvršćuje njeno قَلْب: unutrašnji nemir je فُؤَاد, postojanost قَلْب.
why.en: The heart (fuʾād) of Moses' mother became “void” (tafsir differs: of patience, or of all but her son), and in the same ayah Allah fortifies her qalb: the inner upheaval is named fuʾād, the steadfastness qalb.

why.bs: Srce nije poreklo ono što je vidjelo – unutrašnji doživljaj.
why.en: The heart did not deny what it saw — inner experience.

why.bs: Vatra koja se diže do srca – ar-Rāġib kaže da spominjanje srca ovdje ukazuje na to koliko ih vatra snažno pogađa.
why.en: The fire that mounts up to the hearts — ar-Rāġib says naming the hearts here points to how intensely the fire affects them.

nuance.bs: Grudi, koje obuhvataju srce (22:46). Rečeno je da se, kad se spominje srce, misli na razum i znanje, a kad se spominju grudi, i na to i na ostale unutrašnje sile – želju, strast, srdžbu. Riječ za širenje i stezanje i za ono što čovjek skriva u sebi.
nuance.en: The breast, which holds the heart (22:46). It has been said that when the heart is mentioned, intellect and knowledge are meant; when the breast is mentioned, these and the other inner forces too — desire, passion, anger. The word for expansion and constriction, and for what a person hides within.

why.bs: „Zar ti nismo grudi proširili” – širenje grudi.
why.en: “Did We not expand for you your breast” — the breast expanded.

why.bs: Grudi se šire za islam ili postaju tijesne – širenje i stezanje.
why.en: The breast opens to Islam or becomes tight — expansion and constriction.

why.bs: „Srca koja su u grudima” – صَدْر kao ono što obuhvata قَلْب.
why.en: “The hearts which are within the breasts” — ṣadr as what holds the qalb.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače „znati”; razlikuju se po tome kako se do znanja dolazi i ko je onaj koji zna.
shared.en: Both verbs mean “to know”; they differ in how the knowledge is reached and in who is said to know.

tellApart.bs: Znanje općenito, i Allahovo znanje → عَلِمَ; prepoznavanje onoga do čega se dolazi razmišljanjem i po tragovima, suprotno poricanju → عَرَفَ.
tellApart.en: Knowledge in general, and Allah's knowledge → عَلِمَ; recognising what is reached by reflection and by its traces, the opposite of denial → عَرَفَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries علم, عرف
notes: ar-Rāġib: ʿilm is grasping a thing in its reality; maʿrifa is perceiving a thing by reflecting on its traces, narrower than ʿilm, its opposite inkār; one says a person yaʿrifu Allah and Allah yaʿlamu, not Allah yaʿrifu — all attributed to him.
That Allah is never the subject of عَرَفَ in the Quran is our own observation (all 20 uses checked), said as such.
al-ʿAskarī's entry on ʿilm and maʿrifa is not used: its wording could not be verified here.
2:146: tafsir differs on what they recognise (the Prophet, or the truth of the qibla); both named.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries علم, عرف (2026-11-06): 8 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, „spoznaja stvari u njenoj zbilji”. Opća riječ za znanje; njome se govori i o Allahovom znanju, koje obuhvata skriveno i javno.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, “grasping a thing in its reality”. The general word for knowledge; it is used of Allah's knowledge, which encompasses the hidden and the open.

why.bs: „Allah zna, a vi ne znate” – znanje koje je samo Allahovo.
why.en: “Allah knows, while you know not” — knowledge that is Allah's alone.

why.bs: Ključeve gajba zna samo On – za Allahovo znanje stoji عَلِمَ, ne عَرَفَ.
why.en: The keys of the unseen none knows but He — Allah's knowledge is expressed with عَلِمَ, not عَرَفَ.

why.bs: „Znaj da nema boga osim Allaha” – znanje kao čvrsto uvjerenje.
why.en: “Know that there is no god but Allah” — knowledge as firm conviction.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, spoznaja do koje se dolazi razmišljanjem o tragovima stvari; uža je od عِلْم, a suprotnost joj je poricanje (inkār). Zato se, kaže on, za čovjeka kaže da „spoznaje” Allaha, a za Allaha da „zna”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, knowledge reached by reflecting on a thing's traces; narrower than ʿilm, and its opposite is denial (inkār). Hence, he says, a person is said to “recognise” Allah, while Allah is said to “know”.

why.bs: Jusuf je prepoznao svoju braću, a oni njega nisu – عَرَفَ nasuprot مُنكِرُونَ, kako ar-Rāġib i kaže.
why.en: Joseph recognised his brothers while they did not know him — عَرَفَ set against مُنكِرُونَ, just as ar-Rāġib says.

why.bs: Oni kojima smo dali Knjigu poznaju ga kao što poznaju sinove svoje (tefsir se razilazi: Poslanika, ili istinu o kibli) – prepoznavanje po poznatim znakovima.
why.en: Those given the Scripture recognise it as they recognise their sons (tafsir differs: the Prophet, or the truth of the qibla) — recognition by known signs.

why.bs: Oči im liju suze zbog istine koju su prepoznali.
why.en: Their eyes overflow with tears for the truth they have recognised.

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola govore o Allahovom stvaranju i mogu se prevesti sa „stvoriti”; razlikuju se po tome šta je u prvom planu.
shared.en: All three verbs speak of Allah's making and can be rendered “to create”; they differ in what is in view.

tellApart.bs: Stvaranje s mjerom, i stvaranje bez uzora → خَلَقَ; učiniti nešto nečim, postaviti, dati mu stanje → جَعَلَ; stvoriti iz početka, dati stvorenju prvobitnu narav → فَطَرَ.
tellApart.en: Creating by measure, and originating without a model → خَلَقَ; making a thing into something, placing it, giving it a state → جَعَلَ; bringing into being from the start, giving the creature its original nature → فَطَرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries خلق, جعل, فطر
aṭ-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-bayān — the report from Ibn ʿAbbās on fāṭir
notes: ar-Rāġib: khalq is at root right measuring, used of bringing a thing into being without origin or model, and in that sense only Allah creates; jaʿl is general for all doings, wider than fiʿl and ṣunʿ, including making one thing from another and turning a thing from one state to another; faṭr is at root splitting lengthwise, and Allah's faṭr is bringing a thing into being in a form ready for its work — attributed to him.

az-Zamaḫšarī's contrast on 6:1 (khalq: measuring; jaʿl: one thing from another, or one thing into another) is no longer used: al-Kaššāf could not be checked against a text here. The 6:1 note gives ar-Rāġib's own reading instead (خلق there = أبدع, 'originated'; جعل there 'runs like أوجد', one object).
The Ibn ʿAbbās report (two Bedouins disputing over a well: 'I faṭartuhā', i.e. I began it) is given as reported in tafsir (aṭ-Ṭabarī); the place where he cites it is not named (blind review).
Form I بَرَأَ (1×) and the noun بَارِئ are not members: too rare in the corpus to illustrate here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnovno značenje je „ispravno odmjeravanje”; kaže se za stvaranje bez prethodnog materijala i bez uzora – a takvo stvaranje pripada samo Allahu – ali i za stvaranje nečega iz nečega.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root sense is “right measuring”; it is used of bringing a thing into being without prior material or model — creation in that sense belongs to Allah alone — and also of making one thing from another.

why.bs: „Mi smo sve s mjerom stvorili” – خَلَقَ i mjera (qadar) u istom ajetu.
why.en: “We have created every thing by measure” — خَلَقَ and measure (qadar) in one ayah.

why.bs: Čovjeka je stvorio od kapi – خَلَقَ i za stvaranje iz nečega.
why.en: He created man from a drop — خَلَقَ also of making from something.

why.bs: Allah je stvorio (خَلَقَ) nebesa i Zemlju i učinio (جَعَلَ) tmine i svjetlo; ar-Rāġib خَلَقَ ovdje tumači kao stvaranje bez uzora, a جَعَلَ ovdje kao davanje postojanja.
why.en: Allah created (خَلَقَ) the heavens and the earth and made (جَعَلَ) the darkness and the light; ar-Rāġib reads خَلَقَ here as originating without a model, and جَعَلَ here as simply bringing into being.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, opća riječ za svaku vrstu činjenja, šira od فَعَلَ i صَنَعَ; između ostalog znači stvaranje nečega iz nečega i dovođenje stvari u jedno stanje umjesto drugog. Zato često ima dva objekta: „učiniti nešto nečim”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a general word for every kind of doing, wider than فَعَلَ and صَنَعَ; among its uses are making one thing from another and turning a thing from one state into another. Hence it often takes two objects: “make X into Y”.

why.bs: Zemlju vam je učinio posteljom, a nebo svodom – stvorenom je dato stanje i svrha.
why.en: He made the earth a bed for you and the sky a canopy — created things given a state and a purpose.

why.bs: Od vas samih vam je dao žene – stvaranje nečega iz nečega.
why.en: He has made for you mates from yourselves — making one thing from another.

why.bs: Kuću smo učinili utočištem ljudima – postojećoj stvari dato je novo značenje.
why.en: We made the House a place of return for people — an existing thing given a new standing.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnovno značenje je cijepanje po dužini; Allahovo فَطْر je stvaranje stvari prvi put, u obliku spremnom za ono za šta je stvorena – odatle فِطْرَة, iskonska narav. U tefsiru se prenosi da Ibn Abbas nije znao šta znači فَاطِر dok nije čuo beduina koji je za bunar rekao: „Ja sam ga فَطَرْتُ”, tj. ja sam ga prvi iskopao.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root sense is splitting lengthwise; Allah's faṭr is bringing a thing into being for the first time, in a form ready for what it is made for — hence فِطْرَة, original nature. Tafsir reports that Ibn ʿAbbās did not know what فَاطِر meant until he heard a Bedouin say of a well, “I faṭartuhā”, i.e. I first dug it.

why.bs: Allahova فِطْرَة, prema kojoj je ljude stvorio – glagol i imenica iz istog korijena: narav s kojom čovjek dolazi na svijet.
why.en: Allah's fiṭra upon which He originated mankind — verb and noun from one root: the nature a person is born with.

why.bs: Ibrahim: „Okrećem se Onome koji je nebesa i Zemlju stvorio” – Onaj koji je sve prvi put stvorio.
why.en: Abraham: “I have turned my face to Him who originated the heavens and the earth” — the One who brought all into being.

why.bs: „Zašto da ne obožavam Onoga koji me stvorio” – فَطَرَ za vlastito stvaranje.
why.en: “Why should I not worship Him who brought me into being?” — فَطَرَ for one's own creation.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače „poslati” i oba se kažu za slanje poslanika; razlikuju se po onome što svaki još obuhvata.
shared.en: Both verbs mean “to send” and both are said of sending messengers; they differ in what else each covers.

tellApart.bs: Pustiti nešto da ide – ljude i stvari (vjetrove, kišu, kaznu) → أَرْسَلَ; pokrenuti i uputiti, pa i podići iz smrti ili sna → بَعَثَ.
tellApart.en: Letting a thing go forth — people and things alike (winds, rain, punishment) → أَرْسَلَ; rousing and dispatching, and raising from death or sleep → بَعَثَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رسل, بعث
notes: ar-Rāġib: irsāl is said of people and of things, welcome and hateful, sometimes by subjection (wind, rain), sometimes by sending one who has choice (messengers); baʿṯ is at root rousing a thing and directing it, its sense varying with what it is applied to — attributed to him.
That the Quran uses بَعَثَ for raising the dead and waking the people of the cave is plain from the cited ayat, said as our own observation.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رسل, بعث (2026-11-06): 6 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, slanje se kaže i za ljude i za stvari, za ono što je drago i za ono što je mrsko; nekad potčinjavanjem, kao slanje vjetra i kiše, a nekad slanjem onoga ko ima izbor, kao slanje poslanika.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, sending is said both of people and of things, of what is welcome and what is hateful; sometimes by subjection, as with wind and rain, sometimes by sending one who has choice, as with messengers.

why.bs: Allah šalje vjetrove koji pokreću oblake – slanje potčinjenih stvari.
why.en: Allah sends the winds which stir up clouds — the sending of things made subject.

why.bs: „Mi smo poslali Nuha narodu njegovu” – slanje poslanika.
why.en: “We sent Noah to his people” — the sending of a messenger.

why.bs: Na vlasnike slona poslao je jata ptica – slanje kao kazna.
why.en: He sent against the people of the elephant birds in flocks — sending as punishment.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnovno značenje je pokrenuti nešto i uputiti ga; značenje se mijenja prema onome na šta se odnosi. U Kur'anu se kaže za slanje poslanika, za oživljavanje mrtvih i za buđenje stanovnika pećine.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root sense is to rouse a thing and direct it; the meaning shifts with what it is applied to. In the Quran it is used of sending a messenger, raising the dead and waking the people of the cave.

why.bs: On je nepismenima poslao Poslanika iz njihove sredine – poslanik podignut iz naroda i upućen njemu.
why.en: He it is who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves — a messenger raised up from a people and sent to them.

why.bs: „Zatim smo vas, poslije smrti vaše, oživili” – بَعَثَ za vraćanje u život.
why.en: “Then We revived you after your death” — بَعَثَ for bringing back to life.

why.bs: „I tako smo ih probudili” – stanovnici pećine podignuti iz dugog sna.
why.en: “And so We roused them” — the people of the cave raised from their long sleep.

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola govore o izgovorenoj riječi; razlikuju se po tome šta je u središtu: sadržaj, sagovornik ili sam čin govora.
shared.en: All three verbs concern the spoken word; they differ in what is at the centre: the content, the one addressed, or the act of speech itself.

tellApart.bs: Ono što je rečeno → قَالَ; onaj kome se govori, razgovor → كَلَّمَ; moć i čin artikuliranog govora, često u negaciji („ne govore”) → نَطَقَ.
tellApart.en: What was said → قَالَ; the one spoken to, conversation → كَلَّمَ; the power and act of articulate speech, often negated (“they do not speak”) → نَطَقَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قول, كلم, نطق
notes: ar-Rāġib's sense of qawl as what is conceived in the soul before it is uttered (58:8) and his definition of nuṭq (articulate sounds the tongue utters and the ears take in) are attributed to him.
That كَلَّمَ names the one addressed and that نَطَقَ is often negated in the Quran are our own observations, said as such.
Form V تَكَلَّمَ (4×) is not a member; كَلَّمَ is the studied verb.

Sources normalised (2026-11-06): كلم read and added to `verified` (consistent with the texts; no attributed point rests on it).

nuance.bs: Najopćenitija riječ za iskaz; u središtu je ono što je rečeno. Prema ar-Rāġibu, kaže se i za ono što se zamisli u duši prije nego što se izgovori.
nuance.en: The most general word for an utterance; what was said is at its centre. According to ar-Rāġib, it is also said of what is conceived in the soul before it is spoken.

why.bs: „I govore u sebi” – قَالَ za ono što ostaje u duši.
why.en: “And they say within themselves” — قَالَ for what stays in the soul.

why.bs: „Reci: On je Allah, Jedan” – قُلْ uvodi sadržaj koji treba prenijeti.
why.en: “Say: He is Allah, the One” — قُلْ introduces the content to be conveyed.

nuance.bs: Govoriti nekome, obraćati mu se: glagol imenuje sagovornika. Iz istog korijena su كَلَام, govor, i كَلِمَة, riječ.
nuance.en: To speak to someone, to address him: the verb names the one addressed. From the same root come كَلَام, speech, and كَلِمَة, word.

why.bs: „A s Musaom je Allah zaista govorio” – obraćanje Musau, naglašeno imenicom تَكْلِيمًا.
why.en: “And Allah spoke to Moses directly” — the address to Moses, stressed by the verbal noun تَكْلِيمًا.

why.bs: „Kako da govorimo s djetetom u kolijevci?” – كَلَّمَ za razgovor sa sagovornikom.
why.en: “How can we speak to one who is a child in the cradle?” — كَلَّمَ for speaking with someone.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, u uobičajenoj upotrebi: artikulirani glasovi koje jezik izgovara, a uši primaju. U Kur'anu se često javlja u negaciji – kod idola koji ne govore i kod ljudi kojima je govor uskraćen – pa je u prvom planu sama moć govora.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, in common usage: articulate sounds the tongue utters and the ears take in. In the Quran it often comes negated — idols that do not speak, people denied speech — so the very power of speech is in view.

why.bs: „Pitajte njih, ako govore!” – Ibrahim pokazuje da idoli nemaju moć govora.
why.en: “Ask them, if they can speak!” — Abraham shows the idols have no power of speech.

why.bs: „Ovo je Dan u kojem oni neće govoriti” – govor uskraćen.
why.en: “This is a day on which they will not speak” — speech withheld.

why.bs: „On ne govori po hiru svome” – čin govora Poslanika.
why.en: “Nor does he speak from his own inclination” — the act of the Prophet's speech.

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola su o primanju govora sluhom; razlikuju se po tome koliko je u njemu pažnje i namjere.
shared.en: All three verbs concern taking in speech by hearing; they differ in how much attention and intent is in it.

tellApart.bs: Čuti, pa i razumjeti i prihvatiti → سَمِعَ; pažljivo, namjerno slušati → اِسْتَمَعَ; ušutjeti da bi se slušalo → أَنْصَتَ.
tellApart.en: To hear, and also to understand and accept → سَمِعَ; to listen attentively, on purpose → اِسْتَمَعَ; to fall silent in order to listen → أَنْصَتَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سمع
Ibn Manẓūr, Lisān al-ʿarab — entry نصت
notes: ar-Rāġib: 'hearing' is sometimes said for understanding and sometimes for obedience — attributed to him.
اِسْتَمَعَ as attentive, deliberate listening is the sense of Form VIII here, said in our own words.
أَنْصَتَ as falling silent in order to listen is the classical dictionaries' definition (Lisān al-ʿarab).

nuance.bs: Opći glagol za čulo sluha. Prema ar-Rāġibu, „sluh” se nekad kaže za razumijevanje, a nekad za pokornost – otuda ukor onima koji kažu da čuju, a ne slušaju.
nuance.en: The general verb for the sense of hearing. According to ar-Rāġib, “hearing” is sometimes said for understanding and sometimes for obedience — hence the reproach of those who say they hear and do not heed.

why.bs: Allah je čuo riječi one koja se s tobom raspravljala o mužu svome – sluh kojem ništa ne izmiče.
why.en: Allah has heard the words of her who disputed with you about her husband — a hearing nothing escapes.

why.bs: „Čujemo”, a ne čuju – čuti bez razumijevanja i pokornosti.
why.en: “We hear,” though they do not hear — hearing without understanding and obedience.

why.bs: „Čujemo i pokoravamo se” – sluh kao prihvatanje.
why.en: “We hear and we obey” — hearing as acceptance.

nuance.bs: Osmi oblik istog korijena: slušanje s pažnjom i namjerom, okretanje sluha prema govoru.
nuance.en: Form VIII of the same root: listening with attention and intent, turning one's hearing toward the speech.

why.bs: Skupina džina slušala je Kur'an – namjerno slušanje koje vodi vjerovanju.
why.en: A company of jinn listened to the Quran — deliberate listening that led to belief.

why.bs: „Slušaj ono što se objavljuje” – Musau se naređuje pažljivo slušanje.
why.en: “So listen to what is revealed” — Moses is told to listen with full attention.

why.bs: „Kad se Kur'an uči, slušajte ga i šutite” – اِسْتَمِعُوا i أَنْصِتُوا jedno uz drugo.
why.en: “When the Quran is recited, listen to it and pay attention in silence” — اِسْتَمِعُوا and أَنْصِتُوا side by side.

nuance.bs: U klasičnim rječnicima: ušutjeti da bi se slušalo. U Kur'anu dolazi samo dvaput, oba puta uz slušanje Kur'ana.
nuance.en: In the classical dictionaries: to fall silent in order to listen. It occurs only twice in the Quran, both times with listening to the Quran.

why.bs: Šutnja koja prati slušanje kad se Kur'an uči.
why.en: The silence that goes with listening when the Quran is recited.

why.bs: Džini prisutni pri učenju Kur'ana rekoše: „Šutite!”
why.en: The jinn present at the recitation said, “Listen in silence!”

shared.bs: Oba glagola, iz istog korijena, znače „spustiti” i oba se kažu za objavu; razlikuju se po obliku: أَنْزَلَ (IV) i نَزَّلَ (II).
shared.en: Both verbs, from one root, mean “to send down” and both are said of revelation; they differ in form: أَنْزَلَ (IV) and نَزَّلَ (II).

tellApart.bs: Spuštanje općenito → أَنْزَلَ; prema ar-Rāġibu, kad je riječ o Kur'anu i melekima, spuštanje dio po dio, jedno za drugim → نَزَّلَ. To je sklonost, ne strogo pravilo (25:32).
tellApart.en: Sending down in general → أَنْزَلَ; according to ar-Rāġib, when the Quran and the angels are described, sending down piece by piece, one part after another → نَزَّلَ. A tendency, not a strict rule (25:32).

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نزل
notes: ar-Rāġib's distinction (in describing the Quran and the angels: tanzīl for what is sent down in parts, time after time; inzāl general) is attributed to him and given as a tendency.
25:32 is shown as a counter-example: نُزِّلَ with جُمْلَةً وَاحِدَةً, in the unbelievers' words.
97:1: tafsir differs (the whole Quran sent to the nearest heaven, or the beginning of revelation); both named.
Form I نَزَلَ and Form V تَنَزَّلَ are not members.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نزل (2026-11-06): 2 attributed points confirmed; changed — tellApart (reworded): He limits the inzāl/tanzīl distinction to the description of the Quran and the angels; notes/0 (reworded): He limits the distinction to the description of the Quran and the angels; members/1/nuance (reworded): He limits the distinction to the Quran and the angels; he also explains أنزل in 97:1 and 2:185 by the Quran's descent at once to the lowest heaven

nuance.bs: Opći glagol za slanje odozgo: objave, ali i kiše, željeza, smiraja. Prema ar-Rāġibu, إِنْزَال je općenitije od تَنْزِيل.
nuance.en: The general verb for sending from above: revelation, but also rain, iron, tranquillity. According to ar-Rāġib, inzāl is more general than tanzīl.

why.bs: „Mi smo ga objavili u Noći kadr” – tefsir se razilazi: spuštanje cijelog Kur'ana na najbliže nebo, ili početak objave.
why.en: “We sent it down on the Night of Decree” — tafsir differs: the whole Quran sent down to the nearest heaven, or the beginning of its revelation.

why.bs: „I spustili smo željezo” – أَنْزَلَ i za ono što nije objava.
why.en: “And We sent down iron” — أَنْزَلَ also for what is not revelation.

why.bs: Knjiga koju je objavio (نَزَّلَ) Svome Poslaniku i Knjiga koju je objavio (أَنْزَلَ) prije – oba oblika u jednom ajetu.
why.en: The Book He sent down (نَزَّلَ) upon His Messenger and the Book He sent down (أَنْزَلَ) before — both forms in one ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, kad se opisuju Kur'an i meleki, تَنْزِيل se odnosi na ono što je spušteno dio po dio, jedno za drugim, dok je إِنْزَال opće. Postepena objava Kur'ana kroz godine dobro odgovara tom značenju.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, when the Quran and the angels are described, tanzīl applies to what is sent down in parts, one after another, while inzāl is general. The Quran's gradual revelation over the years fits that sense well.

why.bs: Kur'anu stoji نَزَّلَ, a Tevratu i Indžilu أَنْزَلَ – dva oblika u istom ajetu.
why.en: For the Quran نَزَّلَ, for the Torah and the Gospel أَنْزَلَ — the two forms in one ayah.

why.bs: Kur'an smo podijelili da ga ljudima polahko čitaš, i postepeno smo ga objavljivali – نَزَّلْنَاهُ تَنزِيلًا.
why.en: A Quran We have divided, that you might recite it to the people over time, and We sent it down in stages — نَزَّلْنَاهُ تَنزِيلًا.

why.bs: Nevjernici pitaju zašto mu Kur'an nije objavljen (نُزِّلَ) „odjednom” – drugi oblik čak i uz „odjednom”: razlika je sklonost, ne pravilo.
why.en: The unbelievers ask why the Quran was not sent down (نُزِّلَ) “all at once” — Form II even with “all at once”: the difference is a tendency, not a rule.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače „vratiti se”; ar-Rāġib jedan određuje i preko drugog, pa je razlika u onome na šta se najčešće odnose.
shared.en: Both verbs mean “to return”; ar-Rāġib defines one partly through the other, so the difference lies in what each most often refers to.

tellApart.bs: Povratak mjestu, osobi i Allahu → رَجَعَ; povratak ranijem djelu ili stanju nakon što je napušteno, ponavljanje → عَادَ.
tellApart.en: Return to a place, a person, and to Allah → رَجَعَ; return to a former deed or state after leaving it, doing again → عَادَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رجع, عود
notes: ar-Rāġib: rujūʿ is return to where a thing began (place, deed or word); ʿawd is return to a thing after turning away from it, in person or in word and resolve — attributed to him.
The split by most frequent use is our own observation, given as a tendency.
Form IV أَعَادَ is a different verb and not a member.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رجع, عود (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, povratak onome odakle je nešto počelo – mjestu, djelu ili riječi. U Kur'anu najčešće povratak nekom mjestu ili osobi, i povratak Allahu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, return to where a thing began — a place, a deed or a word. In the Quran most often a return to a place or a person, and the return to Allah.

why.bs: Musa se vratio narodu svome srdit i ojađen – povratak ljudima.
why.en: Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved — a return to people.

why.bs: Kad su se vratili ocu svome – povratak osobi.
why.en: When they returned to their father — a return to a person.

why.bs: „Zatim ćete se Njemu vratiti” – povratak Allahu.
why.en: “Then to Him you will be returned” — the return to Allah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, povratak stvari nakon što se od nje okrenulo – tijelom, ili riječju i odlukom. Zato se često kaže za vraćanje ranijem djelu: ponavljanje zabranjenog, vraćanje staroj vjeri.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, return to a thing after turning away from it — in person, or in word and resolve. Hence it is often said of going back to a former deed: repeating what is forbidden, returning to an old religion.

why.bs: „A ko to ponovo učini, Allah će ga kazniti” – عَادَ za ponavljanje zabranjenog.
why.en: “Whoever returns to it, Allah will take retribution from him” — عَادَ for repeating what is forbidden.

why.bs: „Izmislili bismo laž o Allahu ako bismo se vratili vašoj vjeri” – povratak napuštenom stanju.
why.en: “We would have invented a lie about Allah if we returned to your religion” — a return to a state once left.

why.bs: Mjesec, dok ponovo ne postane kao stari suhi palmin prut – povratak ranijem obliku.
why.en: The moon, until it returns like the old date stalk — a return to an earlier shape.

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola znače „dati”; razlikuju se po onome što se daje i kako.
shared.en: All three verbs mean “to give”; they differ in what is given and how.

tellApart.bs: Najčešći glagol davanja – zekat, Knjiga, mudrost, vlast → آتَى; davanje kao poklon bez naknade, često djece i milosti → وَهَبَ; rijetka, opća riječ za davanje → أَعْطَى.
tellApart.en: The most frequent verb of giving — zakat, Scripture, wisdom, kingship → آتَى; giving as a gift without return, often of children and mercy → وَهَبَ; a rare, general word for giving → أَعْطَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أتى, وهب
notes: ar-Rāġib: īṭāʾ is iʿṭāʾ, and the Quran expresses the paying of zakat with īṭāʾ; hiba is making one's property another's without return — attributed to him.
Modern distinctions between آتَى and أَعْطَى (e.g. by what can be taken back) are not used: they are not in the classical works this section relies on.
Form I أَتَى 'to come' is a different verb (group jaa-ata).
15:87: tafsir differs on 'seven of the often repeated' (al-Fātiḥa, or the seven long surahs); both named (blind review).
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries أتى, وهب (2026-11-06): 5 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, إِيتَاء je isto što i davanje, a davanje zekata Kur'an izražava upravo ovim glagolom. Najčešći glagol davanja: Knjiga, mudrost, vlast, imetak.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, īṭāʾ is giving, and the Quran expresses the giving of zakat with this very verb. The most frequent verb of giving: Scripture, wisdom, kingship, wealth.

why.bs: „Molitvu obavljajte i zekat dajite” – davanje zekata izraženo glagolom آتَى.
why.en: “Establish prayer and give zakat” — the giving of zakat expressed with آتَى.

why.bs: Allah je Davudu dao vlast i mudrost.
why.en: Allah gave David kingship and wisdom.

why.bs: „Mi smo ti dali sedam od ponavljanih i veličanstveni Kur'an” – tefsir se razilazi: Fatiha, ili sedam dugih sura.
why.en: “We have given you seven of the often repeated and the great Quran” — tafsir differs: al-Fātiḥa, or the seven long surahs.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, hiba je kad svoje vlasništvo učiniš tuđim bez naknade. U Kur'anu se često kaže za dar djece i za Allahovu milost.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, hiba is making what is yours another's without return. In the Quran it is often said of the gift of children and of Allah's mercy.

why.bs: Ibrahimu smo darovali Ishaka i Jakuba – dar djece.
why.en: We gave Abraham Isaac and Jacob — the gift of children.

why.bs: „I daruj nam od Sebe milost” – dova.
why.en: “And grant us from Yourself mercy” — a supplication.

why.bs: Sulejman moli: „Daruj mi vlast” – dar bez naknade.
why.en: Solomon asks: “Grant me a kingdom” — a gift without return.

nuance.bs: Opća riječ za davanje, u Kur'anu rijetka. Kaže se i za Allahov dar i za ljudsko davanje.
nuance.en: A general word for giving, rare in the Quran. Said both of Allah's gift and of human giving.

why.bs: „Mi smo ti, zaista, dali Kevser” – Allahov dar Poslaniku.
why.en: “Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar” — Allah's gift to the Prophet.

why.bs: „Onaj ko udjeljuje i boji se” – ljudsko davanje.
why.en: “As for he who gives and fears Allah” — human giving.

why.bs: „Gospodar naš je Onaj koji je svakoj stvari dao njen oblik” – Musaov odgovor faraonu.
why.en: “Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form” — Moses' answer to Pharaoh.

title.en: To do, to work, to make

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola znače „činiti”; ar-Rāġib ih slaže od općenitijeg prema užem.
shared.en: All three verbs mean “to do”; ar-Rāġib orders them from the more general to the narrower.

tellApart.bs: Svako djelovanje, s namjerom ili bez nje → فَعَلَ; djelo živog bića učinjeno s namjerom → عَمِلَ; vješta izrada, dobro izvedeno djelo → صَنَعَ.
tellApart.en: Any doing, intended or not → فَعَلَ; a deed done on purpose by a living being → عَمِلَ; skilful making, a deed done well → صَنَعَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فعل, عمل, صنع
notes: ar-Rāġib: fiʿl is an effect from an agent, general (done well or not, knowingly or not, intended or not), and may be ascribed to animals and things; ʿamal is every doing of a living being with intent, narrower than fiʿl; ṣunʿ is doing a deed well, every ṣunʿ is fiʿl but not every fiʿl ṣunʿ — attributed to him.
29:45 is shown as the general use of صَنَعَ ('what you do').
The Quran's neutral and negative uses of صَنَعَ (5:62, 29:45) are named beside ar-Rāġib's definition (blind review).

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries فعل, عمل, صنع (2026-11-06): 9 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): He says ʿamal is used of righteous and evil deeds alike; he does not derive 'righteous deed' from the intent element
Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): 99:7 bs 'uradio' kept: Korkut's own wording.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, učinak koji dolazi od nekog uzročnika; opća riječ – bilo da je učinjeno dobro ili ne, sa znanjem ili bez, s namjerom ili bez. Zato se pripisuje i životinjama i stvarima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, an effect coming from an agent; a general word — whether done well or not, knowingly or not, intended or not. Hence it is ascribed even to animals and things.

why.bs: „Zar nisi vidio šta je Gospodar tvoj učinio s vlasnicima slona?” – فَعَلَ za Allahovo djelovanje.
why.en: “Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?” — فَعَلَ for Allah's doing.

why.bs: „Jesi li ti to učinio s bogovima našim, Ibrahime?” – pitanje o učinjenom činu.
why.en: “Have you done this to our gods, O Abraham?” — a question about a deed done.

why.bs: „On neće biti pitan za ono što radi” – Allahovo djelovanje.
why.en: “He is not questioned about what He does” — Allah's doing.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, svako djelovanje živog bića učinjeno s namjerom; uže je od فِعْل i rijetko se pripisuje životinjama i stvarima. Kaže da se koristi i za dobra i za loša djela – odatle عَمَلٌ صَالِحٌ, dobro djelo.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, every doing of a living being done with intent; narrower than fiʿl, and seldom ascribed to animals and things. He notes it is used of good and evil deeds alike — hence عَمَلٌ صَالِحٌ, the righteous deed.

why.bs: „Ko bude uradio koliko trun dobra, vidjet će ga” – namjerno djelo i njegova posljedica.
why.en: “Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it” — a deliberate deed and its outcome.

why.bs: „Neka čini dobra djela” – glagol uz imenicu عَمَل.
why.en: “Let him do righteous work” — the verb with its noun عَمَل.

why.bs: Džini su Sulejmanu izrađivali šta je htio – عَمِلَ i za rad po nalogu.
why.en: The jinn made for Solomon what he willed — عَمِلَ also for work done to order.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, „dobro izvesti djelo”: svaki صُنْع je فِعْل, ali svaki فِعْل nije صُنْع; i ne pripisuje se životinjama i stvarima kao فِعْل. Kur'an ga ipak koristi i neutralno, pa i za loša djela (5:62, 29:45).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, “doing a deed well”: every ṣunʿ is a fiʿl, but not every fiʿl is ṣunʿ; nor is it ascribed to animals and things as fiʿl is. The Quran nevertheless uses it neutrally too, even of bad deeds (5:62, 29:45).

why.bs: „I gradi lađu pod Našim nadzorom” – Nuhova vješta izrada.
why.en: “And construct the ship under Our observation” — Noah's skilled work.

why.bs: Ono što su napravili samo je spletka vračara – izrada, ovdje vještina u obmani.
why.en: What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician — crafting, here skill in deception.

why.bs: „A Allah zna šta radite” – i opće značenje: ono što ljudi čine.
why.en: “And Allah knows what you do” — the general sense too: what people do.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače „jesti”; razlikuju se po obimu i po prenesenom značenju.
shared.en: Both verbs mean “to eat”; they differ in range and in figurative use.

tellApart.bs: Jesti, pa i preneseno „jesti” tuđi imetak → أَكَلَ; okusiti, uzeti hranu – rečeno čak i za vodu i piće → طَعِمَ.
tellApart.en: To eat, and figuratively to “devour” others' wealth → أَكَلَ; to taste, to take food — said even of water and drink → طَعِمَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أكل, طعم
aṭ-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-bayān — on 2:249 and 5:93
notes: That طَعِمَ in 2:249 is said of water (tasting it) is the reading of tafsir; 5:93 is explained in tafsir as wine drunk before its prohibition — both given as tafsir.
The figurative 'eating' of wealth is plain Quranic usage (4:10, 2:188), said as our observation.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries أكل, طعم (2026-11-06): 1 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Opći glagol za jelo. U Kur'anu se preneseno kaže i za prisvajanje imetka: „jesti” imetak siročadi ili jedni drugih.
nuance.en: The general verb for eating. In the Quran it is also used figuratively for seizing wealth: “eating” the property of orphans or of one another.

why.bs: „Jedite odakle god hoćete, a ovom drvetu se ne približujte” – jelo u doslovnom smislu.
why.en: “Eat from wherever you will, but do not approach this tree” — eating in the literal sense.

why.bs: Oni koji nepravedno jedu imetke siročadi, oni u trbuhe svoje vatru trpaju – preneseno značenje.
why.en: Those who devour the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies — the figurative sense.

why.bs: „Pa ga je vuk pojeo” – kažu Jusufova braća.
why.en: “And a wolf ate him” — say Joseph's brothers.

nuance.bs: Uzeti hranu, okusiti. Tefsir na 2:249 bilježi da se ovdje kaže i za vodu, a 5:93 se tumači i pićem.
nuance.en: To take food, to taste. Tafsir on 2:249 notes that it is said there even of water, and 5:93 is explained of drink as well.

why.bs: „A ko je ne okusi, taj je moj” – Talutova vojska i rijeka: طَعِمَ za vodu.
why.en: “And whoever does not taste it is indeed of me” — Saul's army and the river: طَعِمَ of water.

why.bs: „A kad jedete, razilazite se” – gosti u Poslanikovoj kući.
why.en: “And when you have eaten, disperse” — guests in the Prophet's house.

why.bs: Nema grijeha vjernicima u onome što su ranije uzimali – tefsir: vino prije zabrane; طَعِمَ i za piće.
why.en: No blame on the believers for what they consumed before — tafsir: wine before its prohibition; طَعِمَ for drink too.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi imenuju bol u duši; razlikuju se po tome šta je u prvom planu.
shared.en: All three words name pain in the soul; they differ in what is in view.

tellApart.bs: Teška tuga, suprotna radosti → حُزْن; tuga pomiješana sa srdžbom → أَسَف; tjeskoba koja „prekrije” srce → غَمّ.
tellApart.en: Heavy grief, the opposite of joy → حُزْن; grief mixed with anger → أَسَف; distress that “covers” the heart → غَمّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حزن, أسف, غم
notes: ar-Rāġib: ḥuzn is at root roughness of the ground and, in the soul, the roughness grief brings, its opposite faraḥ; asaf is grief and anger together (towards one below it becomes anger, towards one above grief; 43:55 'when they angered Us'); ghamm is at root covering (ghamām, clouds veiling the sun) — attributed to him.
The corpus files حُزْن and حَزَن (two vocalisations of one word) as two lemmas; summed.
أَسِف 'grieved' (7:150, 20:86) is a different word (adjective) and not summed.
43:55 is given as tafsir explains it ('they provoked Our anger'), with 'as befits Allah' (content policy, blind review).
3:153: tafsir differs on what the two distresses were; said so.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حزن, أسف, غم (2026-11-06): 8 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (improved): Ar-Rāġib himself glosses 43:55 as 'they angered Us' and adds that Allah does not grieve as we do, so he can be cited instead of 'tafsir'; members/2/nuance (reworded): He glosses ghamm/ghumma as karb (distress); 'grief that covers the heart' is not his wording
Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): 43:55 given as his gloss plus the saying he quotes; 18:6 bs 'možda' (laʿalla); 3:153 bs keeps Allah as the subject.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnovno značenje je hrapavost tla, a u duši – hrapavost koja nastaje od tuge; suprotnost mu je radost (فَرَح).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root sense is roughness of the ground, and in the soul the roughness grief brings; its opposite is joy (فَرَح).

why.bs: „Ja se samo Allahu žalim na jad svoj i tugu svoju” – Jakubova tuga za Jusufom.
why.en: “I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah” — Jacob's grief for Joseph.

why.bs: Oči su mu od tuge pobijelile – tuga koja traje.
why.en: His eyes became white from grief — a grief that lasts.

why.bs: „Hvala Allahu koji je od nas tugu otklonio” – riječi stanovnika dženeta.
why.en: “Praise to Allah, who has removed from us all sorrow” — the words of the people of Paradise.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, tuga i srdžba zajedno, a kaže se i za svaku od njih posebno: prema slabijem postaje srdžba, prema jačem tuga. Ajet 43:55 فَلَمَّا آسَفُونَا on tumači „kad su Nas razgnjevili” i navodi izreku da Allah ne žalosti kao mi – kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, grief and anger together, though said of either alone: towards one below it becomes anger, towards one above, grief. He glosses 43:55 فَلَمَّا آسَفُونَا as “when they angered Us” and quotes the saying that Allah does not grieve as we do — as befits Him.

why.bs: „O, jada moga za Jusufom!” – bolna žalost.
why.en: “Oh, my sorrow over Joseph!” — painful sorrow.

why.bs: Možda ćeš sebe od žalosti uništiti ako oni u ovaj govor ne povjeruju – Poslanikova žalost zbog onih koji odbijaju.
why.en: You might kill yourself with grief if they do not believe in this message — the Prophet's sorrow over those who refuse.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnovno značenje je prekrivanje – odatle غَمَام, oblaci koji zaklanjaju sunce; غَمّ tumači kao karb – tjeskobu koja čovjeka pritisne.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root sense is covering — hence غَمَام, clouds that veil the sun; he glosses ghamm as karb, distress that closes in on one.

why.bs: „I Mi smo te tjeskobe spasili” – Musa nakon što je ubio čovjeka.
why.en: “And We saved you from distress” — Moses after he had killed a man.

why.bs: Junusa smo spasili od tjeskobe.
why.en: We saved Jonah from the distress.

why.bs: „Pa vas je On tjeskobom za tjeskobu naplatio” – Uhud; tefsir se razilazi o tome koje su to dvije tjeskobe.
why.en: “So He repaid you with distress upon distress” — Uḥud; tafsir differs on what the two distresses were.

shared.bs: Riječi radosti; razlikuju se po tome da li se radost pokazuje i čemu se ljudi raduju.
shared.en: Words of joy; they differ in whether the joy shows and in what people rejoice at.

tellApart.bs: Radost zbog nečega, često prolaznog – u Kur'anu najčešće pokuđena → فَرِحَ; radost i zadovoljstvo, prema ar-Rāġibu izvorno skrivena radost → سُرُور, مَسْرُور.
tellApart.en: Joy at something, often fleeting — in the Quran mostly blamed → فَرِحَ; gladness, at root (ar-Rāġib) joy concealed in the heart → سُرُور, مَسْرُور.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فرح, سرر
notes: ar-Rāġib: faraḥ is the breast's expansion at an immediate pleasure, mostly bodily, which is why it is mostly blamed (he names 10:58 and 30:4 as allowed; the review added 3:170, so 'only' is not said); surūr is what is concealed of joy — attributed to him.
84:13 is shown as a counter-example: مَسْرُور of the denier's careless joy in this world.
سُرُور and مَسْرُور are separate lemmas and separate members.
The tellApart no longer calls مَسْرُور hidden joy: 84:9 is open gladness; 'concealed joy' is kept as ar-Rāġib's root sense of سُرُور (blind review).

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries فرح, سرر (2026-11-06): 8 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): He says faraḥ is mostly at bodily pleasures and that it is permitted only in 10:58 and 30:4; 'worldly' is our addition; members/0/nuance (reworded): He says faraḥ is mostly at bodily pleasures and is permitted only in 10:58 and 30:4; 'worldly' and 3:170 were ours
Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): 57:23 bs 'obijesno' removed (not in the ayah).
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (سر → سرر).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, širenje grudi zbog trenutnog užitka, najčešće tjelesnog; zato je u Kur'anu uglavnom pokuđeno, a on kao dopuštenu navodi samo 10:58 i 30:4 (3:170 je još jedan ajet koji je hvali).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the expansion of the breast at an immediate pleasure, mostly bodily; hence in the Quran it is mostly blamed, and he names only 10:58 and 30:4 as allowing it (3:170 is another approving ayah).

why.bs: „I da se ne radujete onome što vam On daje” – pokuđena radost.
why.en: “Nor exult over what He has given you” — joy that is blamed.

why.bs: „Neka se Allahovoj blagodati i milosti raduju” – dopuštena radost.
why.en: “In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy — in that let them rejoice” — joy that is allowed.

why.bs: A oni se raduju životu na ovom svijetu – radost prolaznom.
why.en: And they rejoice in the worldly life — joy in what passes.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, „ono što je skriveno od radosti” – iz korijena riječi سِرّ, tajna: radost u srcu, ne razmetanje. U Kur'anu dolazi jednom, o nagradi pravednika.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, “what is concealed of joy” — from the root of سِرّ, secret: joy in the heart, not display. It occurs once in the Quran, of the reward of the righteous.

why.bs: Allah će im dati sjaj na licima i radost – nagrada pravednicima.
why.en: Allah will give them radiance and happiness — the reward of the righteous.

nuance.bs: Pasivni particip istog korijena: obradovan, ispunjen radošću. Kaže se za radost onoga kome je knjiga data u desnu ruku, ali i za bezbrižnu radost nevjernika na ovom svijetu.
nuance.en: The passive participle of the same root: gladdened, filled with joy. Said of the joy of the one given his record in his right hand, and also of the denier's careless joy in this world.

why.bs: Radostan će se vratiti svojima – onaj kome je knjiga data u desnu ruku.
why.en: He will return to his people in happiness — the one given his record in his right hand.

why.bs: Jer je on među svojima bio radostan – tefsir: ovosvjetska radost bez misli o Ahiretu, suprotno 84:9.
why.en: Indeed he had been among his people in happiness — tafsir: worldly joy without thought of the Hereafter, set against 84:9.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače laž, neistinu; razlikuju se po slici koju korijen nosi.
shared.en: All three words mean a lie, an untruth; they differ in the image each root carries.

tellApart.bs: Iskaz suprotan istini → كَذِب; neistina koja izokreće stvar od njenog pravog lica, teška kleveta → إِفْك; neistina koja skreće s pravca, lažno svjedočenje → زُور.
tellApart.en: A statement contrary to the truth → كَذِب; untruth that turns a thing from its proper face, grave slander → إِفْك; untruth that veers off course, false witness → زُور.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كذب, أفك, زور
notes: ar-Rāġib: ifk is anything turned from the face it ought to have, and a lie is so called for that; zūr is called so because it inclines away from its course — attributed to him.
25:72: tafsir differs on الزُّور there (false witness, or attending gatherings of falsehood and idolatry); both named.
24:11: the slander is named by tafsir (against ʿĀʾiša), not by the ayah; said so.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries أفك, زور (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): كذب read and added to `verified` (consistent with the texts; no attributed point rests on it).

nuance.bs: Opća riječ za laž: iskaz koji ne odgovara onome kako stvar jeste – suprotnost istini (صِدْق).
nuance.en: The general word for a lie: a statement not matching how a thing is — the opposite of truthfulness (صِدْق).

why.bs: Donijeli su košulju njegovu s lažnom krvlju – Jusufova braća.
why.en: They brought his shirt with false blood — Joseph's brothers.

why.bs: „I ne govorite lažno onim što vaši jezici iznose: Ovo je dozvoljeno, a ovo zabranjeno.”
why.en: “And do not say about what your tongues assert of untruth, ‘This is lawful and this is unlawful’.”

why.bs: Ko je veći zalim od onoga ko o Allahu laž izmišlja?
why.en: Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah?

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, sve što je okrenuto od lica koje treba da ima; laž se tako zove jer je izokrenuta. Iz istog korijena je أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ – „kuda se odvraćaju”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, anything turned from the face it ought to have; a lie is so called because it is turned about. From the same root comes أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ — “how are they turned away”.

why.bs: Oni koji su iznijeli klevetu – tefsir: kleveta protiv Aiše, majke vjernika.
why.en: Those who came with the slander — tafsir: the slander against ʿĀʾisha, mother of the believers.

why.bs: „Zar lažna božanstva mimo Allaha hoćete?” – Ibrahim: idoli kao izokrenuta istina.
why.en: “Is it falsehood — gods other than Allah — that you desire?” — Abraham: idols as truth turned about.

why.bs: To je bila njihova izmišljotina i ono što su izmišljali.
why.en: That was their falsehood and what they were inventing.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, laž je nazvana زُور jer skreće s pravca (iz korijena koji znači nagnutost). U Kur'anu dolazi uz riječi i svjedočenje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a lie is called zūr because it inclines away from its course (from a root meaning slant). In the Quran it comes with speech and witness.

why.bs: „I klonite se lažnih riječi” – قَوْلَ الزُّورِ.
why.en: “And avoid false statement” — قَوْلَ الزُّورِ.

why.bs: Oni koji ne svjedoče lažno – tefsir se razilazi: lažno svjedočenje, ili prisustvovanje skupovima laži i mnogoboštva.
why.en: Those who do not testify to falsehood — tafsir differs: false witness, or attending gatherings of falsehood and idolatry.

why.bs: Zihar: „oni govore ružne i lažne riječi”.
why.en: Ẓihār: “they are saying an objectionable statement and a falsehood”.

shared.bs: Sve četiri riječi imenuju loše djelo; razlikuju se po slici koju korijen nosi.
shared.en: All four words name a wrong deed; they differ in the image each root carries.

tellApart.bs: Djelo čija je posljedica teška („rep” djela) → ذَنْب; djelo koje zadržava od nagrade → إِثْم; ružno djelo, suprotnost dobrom (حَسَنَة) → سَيِّئَة; promašaj, skretanje s pravca → خَطِيئَة.
tellApart.en: A deed whose consequence is grievous (the deed's “tail”) → ذَنْب; a deed that holds back from reward → إِثْم; an ugly deed, the opposite of the good one (حَسَنَة) → سَيِّئَة; a missing of the mark, a turning from the course → خَطِيئَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ذنب, إثم, سوأ, خطأ
notes: ar-Rāġib: ḏanb from ḏanab (tail), used of any deed whose end is feared; iṯm a name for deeds that slow one from reward; sūʾ whatever grieves a person; ḵaṭaʾ a turning from the right direction — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib's further remark that ḵaṭīʾa is mostly said of what was not itself intended is now verified (لكن الخطيئة أكثر ما تقال فيما لا يكون مقصودا إليه في نفسه) and used in the ḵaṭīʾa nuance.
ذَنُوب (51:59, 'a portion') is a different word and not summed; the corpus files ذُنُوب under ذَنب.
2:81: many exegetes read the encompassing khaṭīʾa as shirk; said so.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ذنب, إثم, سوأ, خطأ (2026-11-06): 12 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/1 (improved): The remark is in the Mufradāt under خطأ: khaṭīʾa is mostly said of a wrong not itself intended but caused by something intended; members/3/nuance (improved): Confirmed; he also says khaṭīʾa is mostly a wrong not itself intended but arising from an intended act (e.g. shooting game and hitting a man)
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (أثم → إثم).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od ذَنَب – rep, kraj stvari: svako djelo čija je posljedica (kraj) teška. U Kur'anu najčešće uz traženje oprosta.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from ḏanab — the tail, a thing's end: any deed whose consequence (end) is grievous. In the Quran mostly with seeking forgiveness.

why.bs: Traže oprost za grijehe svoje – a ko oprašta grijehe osim Allaha?
why.en: They seek forgiveness for their sins — and who can forgive sins except Allah?

why.bs: „Allah, uistinu, sve grijehe oprašta.”
why.en: “Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.”

why.bs: „Zbog kakve krivice je ubijena?” – živa zakopana djevojčica.
why.en: “For what sin she was killed” — the girl buried alive.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ime za djela koja usporavaju (zadržavaju) od nagrade. Često stoji uz ono što je štetno i zabranjeno: vino i kocka, saradnja u neprijateljstvu, sumnjičenje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a name for deeds that slow one (hold one back) from reward. Often with what is harmful and forbidden: wine and gambling, cooperation in aggression, suspicion.

why.bs: „U njima je veliki grijeh, a i neke koristi” – vino i kocka.
why.en: “In them is great sin and some benefit” — wine and gambling.

why.bs: „I ne pomažite jedni drugima u grijehu i neprijateljstvu.”
why.en: “And do not cooperate in sin and aggression.”

why.bs: „Neka su sumnjičenja zaista grijeh.”
why.en: “Indeed, some assumption is sin.”

nuance.bs: Ružno djelo, suprotnost dobrom djelu (حَسَنَة); Kur'an to dvoje često spominje zajedno. Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen سوء je sve što čovjeka ožalosti.
nuance.en: An ugly deed, the opposite of the good deed (حَسَنَة); the Quran often names the two together. According to ar-Rāġib, the root sūʾ is whatever grieves a person.

why.bs: „Dobra djela zaista poništavaju hrđava.”
why.en: “Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds.”

why.bs: Ko učini hrđavo djelo, bit će kažnjen samo prema njemu.
why.en: Whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except the like thereof.

why.bs: „Nisu isto dobro i zlo” – حَسَنَة i سَيِّئَة jedno nasuprot drugom.
why.en: “Not equal are the good deed and the bad” — حَسَنَة and سَيِّئَة set against each other.

nuance.bs: Iz korijena خطأ; prema ar-Rāġibu, to je skretanje s pravog pravca; kaže da se خَطِيئَة najčešće kaže za grijeh koji nije sam bio namjeravan, nego je proistekao iz nečeg namjeravanog. U Kur'anu se kaže i za grijeh koji obuhvati čovjeka (2:81) i u Ibrahimovoj poniznoj nadi u oprost (26:82).
nuance.en: From the root ḵ-ṭ-ʾ; according to ar-Rāġib, a turning from the right direction; he says خَطِيئَة is mostly said of a wrong not itself intended, but arising from something that was. In the Quran it is said of the sin that encompasses a person (2:81) and in Abraham's humble hope of forgiveness (26:82).

why.bs: „Ko bude zlo činio i grijeh ga njegov sa svih strana obuhvati” – سَيِّئَة i خَطِيئَة u istom ajetu; mnogi mufessiri ovdje خَطِيئَة tumače kao širk.
why.en: “Whoever earns evil and his sin has encompassed him” — سَيِّئَة and خَطِيئَة in one ayah; many exegetes read the khaṭīʾa here as shirk.

why.bs: Ibrahim: „Koji će mi, nadam se, grijeh moj na Sudnjem danu oprostiti.”
why.en: Abraham: “Who I aspire will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense.”

why.bs: Ko učini prestup (خَطِيئَة) ili grijeh (إِثْم), pa ga svali na nevina – obje riječi jedna uz drugu.
why.en: Whoever earns an offence (خَطِيئَة) or a sin (إِثْم) and then blames it on an innocent — both words side by side.

shared.bs: Obje riječi se prevode s „kazna”; razlikuju se po tome šta je u prvom planu: bol ili posljedica djela.
shared.en: Both words are rendered “punishment”; they differ in what is in view: the pain, or the consequence of the deed.

tellApart.bs: Teška bol, patnja – pa i ona koju nanose ljudi → عَذَاب; kazna koja dolazi za djelom, kao njegova posljedica → عِقَاب.
tellApart.en: Severe pain, torment — even torment people inflict → عَذَاب; penalty that follows the deed as its consequence → عِقَاب.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عذب, عقب
notes: ar-Rāġib: ʿaḏāb is severe pain — attributed to him.
ʿIqāb is explained by its root ʿ-q-b ('what comes after'; ʿaqib heel, ʿāqiba outcome), said as the root's sense, not put in a lexicographer's mouth.
al-ʿAskarī's entry on the pair is not used: its wording could not be verified here.
That the noun عِقَاب in the Quran is always Allah's is our own observation (all 20 uses); the verb عَاقَبَ is used of people (16:126), so the claim is limited to the noun (blind review).
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries عذب, عقب (2026-11-06): 3 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, „teška bol”. Najčešća riječ za kaznu u Kur'anu; kaže se i za mučenje koje nanose ljudi, kao faraonovo mučenje sinova Israilovih.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, “severe pain”. The Quran's most frequent word for punishment; it is also said of torment people inflict, such as Pharaoh's tormenting of the Children of Israel.

why.bs: Faraonovi ljudi su vas najgorim mukama mučili – عَذَاب koji nanose ljudi.
why.en: Pharaoh's people afflicted you with the worst torment — عَذَاب inflicted by people.

why.bs: „A ako budete nezahvalni, kazna Moja je, zaista, žestoka.”
why.en: “But if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.”

why.bs: Njih čeka velika patnja.
why.en: And for them is a great punishment.

nuance.bs: Iz korijena عقب – ono što dolazi poslije (عَقِب: peta; عَاقِبَة: ishod): kazna sagledana kao posljedica koja slijedi djelo. Imenica عِقَاب je u Kur'anu uvijek Allahova (glagol عَاقَبَ kaže se i za ljude), najčešće u spoju شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ.
nuance.en: From the root ʿ-q-b — what comes after (ʿaqib: heel; ʿāqiba: outcome): punishment seen as the consequence that follows a deed. The noun ʿiqāb is always Allah's in the Quran (the verb ʿāqaba is said of people too), most often in شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ.

why.bs: „Allah, zaista, strogo kažnjava” – na kraju ajeta o zabranama.
why.en: “Indeed, Allah is severe in penalty” — closing an ayah of prohibitions.

why.bs: „Pa sam ih kaznio, i kakva je bila kazna Moja!”
why.en: “And I seized them, and how was My penalty!”

why.bs: Gospodar tvoj oprašta ljudima, a i žestoko kažnjava – oprost i kazna jedno uz drugo.
