why.en: Your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people, and severe in penalty — forgiveness and penalty side by side.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače „godina”; ar-Rāġib bilježi razliku u tome kakva se godina najčešće tako naziva, a Kur'an obje koristi i neutralno.
shared.en: Both words mean “year”; ar-Rāġib records a difference in what kind of year each most often names, while the Quran uses both neutrally as well.

tellApart.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, godina često teška i sušna → سَنَة; godina često berićetna → عَام. Sklonost, ne pravilo: u Kur'anu su obje riječi često neutralne (12:47, 9:28).
tellApart.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a year that is often hard and barren → سَنَة; a year often of plenty → عَام. A tendency, not a rule: in the Quran both words are often neutral (12:47, 9:28).

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عوم, سنة
notes: ar-Rāġib: sana is mostly used of a year of hardship or drought (drought itself is called sana), ʿām of a year of ease and plenty (12:49) — attributed to him. On 29:14 he only notes that sana for the whole and ʿām for the exception hides a subtle point, which he defers to a later work (checked against the text).

Quranic سَنَة is mostly neutral (2:96, 18:25, 32:5) and 12:47 uses سِنِين of years of sowing; 9:28 shows عَام used neutrally. The distinction is given as ar-Rāġib's, a tendency of the language, not of Quranic usage (blind review).
سَنَة and its plural سِنِين are two lemmas in the corpus; summed.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries عوم, سنة (2026-11-06): 11 attributed points confirmed; changed — sources/0 (reworded): His discussion of sana is under the headword سنة; the سنا entry is about light, not the year; notes/0 (improved): The 29:14 remark exists in the ʿām entry, but he only flags a subtle point and does not explain it

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, سَنَة se često kaže za godinu u kojoj je teškoća ili suša; zato se i sama suša zove „godina”. U Kur'anu je ipak najčešće neutralna mjera vremena.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, sana is often used of a year of hardship or drought; hence drought itself is called “a year”. In the Quran it is nonetheless mostly a neutral measure of time.

why.bs: „I kaznili smo faraonove ljude sušnim godinama i nerodicom plodova.”
why.en: “And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and a deficiency in fruits.”

why.bs: „Sijte sedam godina uzastopno” – سِنِين i za godine sjetve: sklonost, ne pravilo.
why.en: “Plant for seven years consecutively” — sinīn for years of sowing too: a tendency, not a rule.

why.bs: Nuh je među narodom proveo hiljadu godina (سَنَة) bez pedeset godina (عَام) – obje riječi u istom ajetu.
why.en: Noah remained among his people a thousand years (سَنَة) less fifty years (عَام) — both words in one ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, godina, često obilja i plodnosti, kao godina u kojoj će ljudi imati kiše (12:49). U Kur'anu dolazi i neutralno (9:28).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a year, often one of ease and plenty, like the year in which people are given rain (12:49). In the Quran it also comes neutrally (9:28).

why.bs: „Zatim će doći godina u kojoj će ljudi imati kiše i u kojoj će cijediti.”
why.en: “Then will come after that a year in which the people will be given rain and in which they will press.”

why.bs: Pedeset godina izuzetih od hiljadu – عَام uz سَنَة u istom ajetu.
why.en: Fifty years excepted from a thousand — عَام beside سَنَة in one ayah.

why.bs: „Neka se poslije ove godine ne približuju Časnom hramu” – عَام bez ikakve oznake obilja.
why.en: “So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this year” — عَام with no sense of plenty.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače „put”, doslovno i preneseno; razlikuju se po onome što je u prvom planu.
shared.en: All three words mean “path”, literally and figuratively; they differ in what is in view.

tellApart.bs: Put koji se gazi nogama, i doslovni put → طَرِيق; prohodan put, i put kao način i razlog („na Allahovom putu”) → سَبِيل; jedan pravi put, u Kur'anu uvijek u jednini → صِرَاط.
tellApart.en: A way beaten by feet, a literal road too → طَرِيق; a passable way, and the way as a means and cause (“in the way of Allah”) → سَبِيل; the one straight path, in the Quran always singular → صِرَاط.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries طرق, سبل, صرط
notes: ar-Rāġib: ṭarīq is the way beaten by feet (ṭaraqa, to strike); sabīl a way with ease in it; ṣirāṭ the straight way — attributed to him.
That صِرَاط is never plural in the Quran while سَبِيل has the plural سُبُل (6:153) is our own observation, said as such.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries طرق, سبل, صرط (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, put koji se gazi nogama (od طَرَقَ – udarati). U Kur'anu i doslovno i preneseno.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a way beaten by feet (from ṭaraqa — to strike). In the Quran both literal and figurative.

why.bs: „Načini im kroz more suh put” – doslovni put.
why.en: “Strike for them a dry path through the sea” — a literal road.

why.bs: Džini o Knjizi koja upućuje istini i na pravi put.
why.en: The jinn on the Book that guides to the truth and to a straight way.

why.bs: Osim na put u džehennem – preneseno: kraj kojem put vodi.
why.en: Except the path of Hell — figurative: the end a road leads to.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, put u kojem ima lahkoće. Najčešća riječ za put u Kur'anu; često preneseno: put kao način, razlog, mogućnost (فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ – na Allahovom putu).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a way with ease in it. The Quran's most frequent word for a way; often figurative: the way as a means, cause or possibility (فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ — in the way of Allah).

why.bs: „Ovo je pravi put Moj, pa njime idite, a ne slijedite druge puteve (السُّبُل)” – صِرَاط jedan, a putevi mnogi.
why.en: “This is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways (السُّبُل)” — one ṣirāṭ, many ways.

why.bs: Oni koji udjeljuju imetke svoje na Allahovom putu – put kao razlog.
why.en: Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah — the way as a cause.

why.bs: „Pozivaj na put Gospodara svoga mudro i lijepim savjetom.”
why.en: “Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, pravi put. U Kur'anu uvijek u jednini, najčešće „pravi put” (الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ) ili Allahov put.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the straight way. In the Quran always singular, mostly “the straight path” or Allah's path.

why.bs: „Uputi nas na pravi put.”
why.en: “Guide us to the straight path.”

why.bs: Jedan صِرَاط nasuprot mnogim سُبُل.
why.en: One ṣirāṭ against many subul.

why.bs: Put Allaha, čije je sve što je na nebesima i na Zemlji.
why.en: The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and on the earth.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi imenuju mjesto u kojem se živi; razlikuju se po slici koju korijen nosi.
shared.en: All three words name a place one lives in; they differ in the image each root carries.

tellApart.bs: Kuća, sklonište – izvorno za noćenje → بَيْت; prostor okružen zidom, pa i grad, zemlja, ovaj i onaj svijet → دَار; mjesto smiraja, prebivalište → مَسْكَن.
tellApart.en: A house, a shelter — originally for the night → بَيْت; a space ringed by a wall, and so a town, a land, this world and the next → دَار; a place of rest, a dwelling → مَسْكَن.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بيت, دار, سكن
notes: ar-Rāġib: bayt is at root a person's shelter for the night, then any house; dār is named from the wall that encircles it, then a town, a region, this world and the Hereafter; sukūn is stillness after motion, also used of dwelling — attributed to him.
59:9: tafsir takes الدَّار as Medina; said so.
24:27 keeps Korkut's 'dok ne zatražite dozvolu' in Bosnian beside Sahih International's 'ascertain welcome'; the reviewer's drift note is accepted as a difference of the two translations' wording.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries بيت, دار, سكن (2026-11-06): 11 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, izvorno čovjekovo sklonište za noć (od بَاتَ – prenoćiti), a zatim kuća uopće. U Kur'anu i Kaba – „Kuća”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, at root a person's shelter for the night (from bāta — to spend the night), then any house. In the Quran also the Kaʿba — “the House”.

why.bs: Ibrahim i Ismail podižu temelje Kuće.
why.en: Abraham and Ishmael raise the foundations of the House.

why.bs: Allah vam je kuće vaše učinio mjestom smiraja (سَكَن).
why.en: Allah has made for you from your homes a place of rest (سَكَن).

why.bs: „Ne ulazite u tuđe kuće dok ne zatražite dozvolu.”
why.en: “Do not enter houses other than your own houses until you ascertain welcome.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, kuća nazvana po zidu koji je okružuje (od دَارَ – kružiti); zatim se tako zove i grad, i kraj, i ovaj svijet, i onaj svijet (الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a house named from the wall that encircles it (from dāra — to go round); then a town, a region, this world and the next (الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ).

why.bs: „A onaj svijet je, zaista, pravi život” – الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ.
why.en: “And indeed, the home of the Hereafter — that is the true life” — الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ.

why.bs: I osvanuše u domu svome mrtvi, nepomični – Semudćani.
why.en: And they became within their home corpses fallen prone — the people of Thamūd.

why.bs: Oni koji su prije njih Medinu nastanili – tefsir: دَار je ovdje grad.
why.en: Those who were settled in the home before them — tafsir: the dār here is Medina.

nuance.bs: Iz korijena سكن; prema ar-Rāġibu, سُكُون je mirovanje nakon kretanja, a kaže se i za nastanjivanje: مَسْكَن je mjesto u kojem se boravi i smiruje.
nuance.en: From the root s-k-n; according to ar-Rāġib, sukūn is stillness after motion, also used of dwelling: maskan is the place one lives and rests in.

why.bs: Saba je u svom prebivalištu imala znak.
why.en: There was for Sabaʾ in their dwelling place a sign.

why.bs: „O mravi, ulazite u stanove svoje!”
why.en: “O ants, enter your dwellings!”

why.bs: Lijepi dvori u dženetima Adna.
why.en: Pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače „svjetlo”; Kur'an ih stavlja jednu uz drugu u 10:5.
shared.en: Both words mean “light”; the Quran sets them side by side in 10:5.

tellApart.bs: Svjetlo koje se širi i pomaže vidu, i preneseno uputa → نُور; sjaj, svjetlost sunca – prema ar-Rāġibu uže od نُور (a i Allahove knjige su ضِيَاء, 21:48) → ضِيَاء.
tellApart.en: Light that spreads and helps sight, and figuratively guidance → نُور; radiance, the sun's light — for ar-Rāġib more specific than نُور (and Allah's scriptures too are ضِيَاء, 21:48) → ضِيَاء.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نور, ضوأ
Tafsir on 10:5 (the stronger light), unattributed
notes: ar-Rāġib's definition of nūr (spread light that helps seeing, worldly or otherworldly, the worldly either seen with the eye or seen with insight) is attributed to him.

That ḍiyāʾ is the stronger light (10:5) is given as a common tafsir explanation; its attribution to az-Zamaḫšarī is held back — the blind reviewer could not vouch for it in the Kaššāf. ar-Rāġib himself explains 10:5 only by ḍawʾ being more specific (akhaṣṣ) than nūr.
The later explanation that ḍiyāʾ is light from its own source and nūr reflected light is not used: it is not in the works cited here.
24:35 carries the tafsir gloss (He illumines the heavens and the earth and guides those in them), so the ayah is not read literally (content policy, blind review).

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نور, ضوأ (2026-11-06): 3 attributed points confirmed; changed — sources/0 (improved): He also has a ḍawʾ entry and explains 10:5 by ḍawʾ being more specific than nūr, which we can cite; notes/0 (reworded): His first division is worldly vs otherworldly light; the eye/insight split is a subdivision of worldly light; notes/1 (improved): ar-Rāġib explains the sun/moon contrast in 10:5 by ḍawʾ being more specific than nūr, not by it being stronger; members/0/nuance (reworded): He divides light into worldly and otherworldly, splits worldly light into seen by eye or by insight, and names reason and the Quran (not guidance and faith) as examples
Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): tellApart: ḍiyāʾ 'more specific' (his aḵaṣṣ), not 'stronger' (that is the tafsir on 10:5); his 21:48 scriptures-as-ḍiyāʾ added.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, raširena svjetlost koja pomaže vidu; na ovom svijetu ili se vidi očima ili pronicljivošću – kao svjetlost razuma i Kur'ana; a postoji i svjetlost ahireta.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, spread light that helps seeing; in this world it is either seen with the eye or seen with insight — like the light of reason and of the Quran; there is also the light of the hereafter.

why.bs: Sunce je učinio sjajem (ضِيَاء), a Mjesec svjetlom (نُور).
why.en: He made the sun a shining light (ضِيَاء) and the moon a light (نُور).

why.bs: „Allah je svjetlo nebesa i Zemlje” – tefsir: On ih obasjava i Onaj je koji upućuje one na njima.
why.en: “Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth” — tafsir: He illumines them and guides those in them.

why.bs: Izvodi ih iz tmina na svjetlo – svjetlo kao uputa.
why.en: He brings them out from darknesses into the light — light as guidance.

nuance.bs: U Kur'anu tri puta. U tefsiru 10:5 često se objašnjava da je ضِيَاء jača svjetlost od نُور – zato je sunce ضِيَاء, a mjesec نُور.
nuance.en: Three times in the Quran. Tafsir on 10:5 often explains ḍiyāʾ as a stronger light than nūr — hence the sun is ḍiyāʾ and the moon nūr.

why.bs: Sunce kao ضِيَاء – jača svjetlost.
why.en: The sun as ḍiyāʾ — the stronger light.

why.bs: Musau i Harunu smo dali Furkan i svjetlo – Tevrat kao svjetlost.
why.en: We gave Moses and Aaron the criterion and a light — the Torah as radiance.

why.bs: „Koji bi vam bog osim Allaha donio svjetlost?” – svjetlost dana.
why.en: “What deity other than Allah could bring you light?” — the light of day.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače „kiša”; u Kur'anu ih razdvaja upotreba.
shared.en: Both words mean “rain”; Quranic usage sets them apart.

tellApart.bs: Kiša, u Kur'anu najčešće kiša kazne (kamenje na Lutov narod) → مَطَر; kiša koja pomaže i oživljava, spas nakon očaja → غَيْث. Sklonost, ne pravilo (4:102).
tellApart.en: Rain, in the Quran mostly a rain of punishment (stones on the people of Lot) → مَطَر; rain that helps and revives, relief after despair → غَيْث. A tendency, not a rule (4:102).

sources: Quranic usage — our own observation (all uses of both nouns checked)
notes: The split is our own observation of Quranic usage, given as a tendency with 4:102 (ordinary rain) as counter-example.
The view reported from some lexicographers that أَمْطَرَ is said of punishment and مَطَرَ of good is not used: it could not be verified here.
57:20: tafsir differs on الْكُفَّار there (tillers of the soil, or unbelievers); both named.

nuance.bs: Kiša. U Kur'anu se najčešće spominje kao kazna – kiša kamenja na Lutov narod; ali i kao obična kiša (4:102).
nuance.en: Rain. In the Quran it is mostly mentioned as punishment — the rain of stones on the people of Lot; but also as ordinary rain (4:102).

why.bs: „I na njih smo kišu spustili, pa pogledaj kakav je bio kraj zločinaca.”
why.en: “And We rained upon them a rain. Then see how was the end of the criminals.”

why.bs: „I grozna je bila kiša za one koji su bili opomenuti.”
why.en: “And evil was the rain of those who were warned.”

why.bs: Nema smetnje da ostavite oružje ako vam kiša smeta – obična kiša.
why.en: No blame if you put down your arms when hindered by rain — ordinary rain.

nuance.bs: Kiša koja donosi pomoć i život: u 42:28 poslije očaja, u 57:20 kiša od koje bilje niče, a u 31:34 Allah je Onaj koji je spušta.
nuance.en: Rain that brings help and life: in 42:28 after despair, in 57:20 rain that makes plants grow, and in 31:34 it is Allah who sends it down.

why.bs: On spušta kišu nakon što su izgubili nadu.
why.en: He sends down the rain after they had despaired.

why.bs: Kod Allaha je znanje o Času, i On spušta kišu.
why.en: With Allah is knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain.

why.bs: Kao kiša čije bilje oduševi sijače, pa se osuši – slika ovog svijeta; tefsir se razilazi: الْكُفَّار su ovdje sijači, ili nevjernici.
why.en: Like a rain whose growth pleases the tillers, then it dries — the likeness of this world; tafsir differs: الْكُفَّار here are tillers, or unbelievers.

shared.bs: Obje riječi se tiču gledanja; razlikuju se po tome da li imenuju organ ili moć.
shared.en: Both words concern seeing; they differ in whether they name the organ or the faculty.

tellApart.bs: Oko kao organ, i u izrazima (radost oka), a i izvor vode → عَيْن; vid – moć gledanja, a i organ koji gleda – često uz sluh (السَّمْعُ وَالْبَصَرُ) → بَصَر.
tellApart.en: The eye as an organ, also in idioms (the eye's comfort), and a spring of water → عَيْن; sight — the faculty of seeing, and the organ that sees — often beside hearing (السَّمْعُ وَالْبَصَرُ) → بَصَر.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عين, بصر
notes: ar-Rāġib: ʿayn is the organ of sight and is also said of a spring; baṣar is said of the seeing organ and of the faculty in it, the heart's perception being baṣīra — attributed to him.
The corpus files الأَبْصَار under بَصَر; one word, nothing to sum.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries عين, بصر (2026-11-06): 8 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, organ vida; kaže se i za izvor vode. U Kur'anu i u izrazima kao „da joj se oko obraduje”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the organ of sight; it is also said of a spring of water. In the Quran also in idioms such as “that her eye might be comforted”.

why.bs: „Oko za oko” – oko kao organ.
why.en: “An eye for an eye” — the eye as an organ.

why.bs: Da se majci tvojoj oko obraduje – Musa vraćen majci.
why.en: That her eye might be comforted — Moses returned to his mother.

why.bs: U njemu je izvor tekući – عَيْن kao izvor.
why.en: Within it is a flowing spring — عَيْن as a spring.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, kaže se za organ koji gleda i za moć vida u njemu; opažanje srcem zove se بَصِيرَة. U Kur'anu često stoji uz sluh i srce kao moć spoznaje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, said of the organ that sees and of the faculty of sight in it; the heart's perception is called بَصِيرَة. In the Quran it often stands with hearing and the heart as a means of knowing.

why.bs: „Sluh, vid i srce – za sve to će se, zaista, odgovarati.”
why.en: “The hearing, the sight and the heart — about all those one will be questioned.”

why.bs: Ne slijepe oči (الأَبْصَار), nego srca u grudima – vid i unutarnje sljepilo.
why.en: It is not eyes (الأَبْصَار) that are blinded, but hearts within the breasts — sight and inner blindness.

why.bs: Kao treptaj oka – brzina pogleda.
why.en: Like a glance of the eye — the swiftness of sight.

shared.bs: Obje riječi imenuju ono što je napisano; razlikuju se po tome da li je to sabrana cjelina ili listovi.
shared.en: Both words name what is written; they differ in whether it is a gathered whole or leaves.

tellApart.bs: Pisano djelo sabrano u cjelinu, objavljena Knjiga, pa i propis i odredba → كِتَاب; listovi na kojima se piše – Ibrahimovi i Musaovi listovi, listovi djela → صُحُف.
tellApart.en: A written work gathered into a whole, the revealed Scripture, and also decree and ordinance → كِتَاب; leaves one writes on — the scrolls of Abraham and Moses, the records of deeds → صُحُف.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كتب, صحف
notes: ar-Rāġib: kitāb is at root sewing leather to leather, in usage joining letters in writing; ṣaḥīfa is anything spread flat, then the leaf one writes on — attributed to him.
صِحَاف (43:71, 'platters') is a different word and not summed.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries كتب, صحف (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnovno značenje je spajanje kože s kožom šivenjem, a uobičajeno – spajanje slova pisanjem. U Kur'anu: objavljena Knjiga, zapis djela, ali i ono što je propisano i određeno (8:68).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root sense is joining leather to leather by sewing, and in usage joining letters in writing. In the Quran: the revealed Scripture, the record of deeds, and also what is ordained and decreed (8:68).

why.bs: „Ova Knjiga, u nju nema sumnje.”
why.en: “This is the Book about which there is no doubt.”

why.bs: Da nije odredbe od Allaha koja je prethodila – كِتَاب kao odredba.
why.en: If not for a decree from Allah that preceded — كِتَاب as decree.

why.bs: Na Sudnjem danu izvadit ćemo mu knjigu koju će otvorenu naći – zapis djela.
why.en: On the Day of Resurrection We will produce for him a record which he will find spread open — the record of deeds.

nuance.bs: Množina od صَحِيفَة; prema ar-Rāġibu, „ono što je razastrto” – list na kojem se piše. U Kur'anu: listovi objavljeni Ibrahimu i Musau, i listovi djela koji će se rastvoriti.
nuance.en: Plural of ṣaḥīfa; according to ar-Rāġib, “what is spread flat” — the leaf one writes on. In the Quran: the scrolls revealed to Abraham and Moses, and the records of deeds that will be spread open.

why.bs: Listovi Ibrahimovi i Musaovi.
why.en: The scriptures of Abraham and Moses.

why.bs: Kad se listovi (djela) rastvore.
why.en: And when the pages are spread.

why.bs: Poslanik od Allaha koji čita listove čiste.
why.en: A Messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače „velik” i obje su Allahova imena (الْكَبِير, الْعَظِيم); razlikuju se po onome što čini veličinu.
shared.en: Both words mean “great” and both are names of Allah (الْكَبِير, الْعَظِيم); they differ in what makes the greatness.

tellApart.bs: Velik, često u odnosu na drugo – razmjerom, godinama, rangom → كَبِير; velik po sebi, veličanstven (od عَظْم, kost) → عَظِيم.
tellApart.en: Great, often in relation to something else — in size, age, rank → كَبِير; great in itself, magnificent (from ʿaẓm, bone) → عَظِيم.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كبر, عظم
notes: ar-Rāġib: 'great' and 'small' (kabīr, ṣaġīr) are relative terms said of things compared with one another; ʿiẓam is at root bigness of bone, then borrowed for every great thing, perceptible or intelligible — attributed to him.
That كَبِير is said of age (28:23) and عَظِيم never is our own observation.
The relative sense of كَبِير is hedged as 'often': al-Kabīr is also a name of Allah (blind review).
68:4: Korkut's 'najljepše ćudi' is kept, with the literal 'velike ćudi' beside it.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries كبر, عظم (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, „velik” i „malen” su odnosni pojmovi: stvar je velika u poređenju s drugom. Kaže se i za starost i za rang.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, “great” and “small” are relative terms: a thing is great compared with another. It is also said of age and of rank.

why.bs: „A otac naš je starac dubokih godina” – كَبِير za starost.
why.en: “And our father is an old man” — كَبِير for age.

why.bs: „To je uradio ovaj najveći njihov” – Ibrahim o najvećem idolu.
why.en: “Rather, this — the largest of them — did it” — Abraham on the largest idol.

why.bs: „U njima je veliki grijeh” – veličina mjerena prema koristi.
why.en: “In them is great sin” — greatness weighed against the benefit.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, izvorno: onaj čija je kost (عَظْم) krupna, a zatim se kaže za svaku veliku stvar, opipljivu ili pojmovnu. Često uz ono što izaziva strahopoštovanje: Arš, kazna, ćud Poslanika.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, at root: big of bone (ʿaẓm), then said of every great thing, perceptible or intelligible. Often with what inspires awe: the Throne, punishment, the Prophet's character.

why.bs: „A ti si, zaista, najljepše ćudi” (doslovno: „velike ćudi”) – veličina karaktera, koja se ne vidi okom.
why.en: “And indeed, you are of a great moral character” — greatness of character, not seen with the eye.

why.bs: On je Uzvišeni, Veličanstveni – Allahovo ime.
why.en: He is the Most High, the Most Great — a name of Allah.

why.bs: Ona ima veličanstven prijesto – kraljica Sabe: عَظِيم i za ljudske stvari.
why.en: She has a great throne — the queen of Sabaʾ: عَظِيم also of human things.

shared.bs: Obje riječi izražavaju priznanje dobra; prema ar-Rāġibu, razlikuju se po obimu.
shared.en: Both words acknowledge good; according to ar-Rāġib, they differ in range.

tellApart.bs: Hvala za vrlinu i savršenstvo, i kad nije učinjena nama → حَمْد; zahvala za primljenu blagodat → شَكَرَ. Svaka zahvala je hvala, a svaka hvala nije zahvala.
tellApart.en: Praise for excellence and perfection, even when no favour was done to us → حَمْد; thanks for a favour received → شَكَرَ. Every thanks is praise, but not every praise is thanks.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حمد, شكر
notes: ar-Rāġib: ḥamd is praising for excellence, narrower than madḥ and wider than šukr; šukr is in return for a favour; every šukr is ḥamd but not every ḥamd šukr — attributed to him.
That كُفْر is set against شُكْر in 14:7, 2:152 and 27:40 is plain from the ayat, said as our observation.
حَمْد (noun) and شَكَرَ (verb) are the studied words; the verb حَمِدَ occurs once.
'Only in return for a favour' is softened: Allah is šākir (2:158), which tafsir explains as rewarding deeds (blind review).

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حمد, شكر (2026-11-06): 8 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (improved): ar-Rāġib himself explains Allah's šukr as His favour and recompense for worship, and names kufr (forgetting and hiding the favour) as its opposite
Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): šukr as 'picturing the favour and showing it'; Allah as šakūr is his on 64:17, applied to 2:158 by us.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, veličanje zbog vrline; uže je od مَدْح (pohvale), a šire od شُكْر, jer se ne veže samo za primljenu blagodat.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, praising for excellence; narrower than madḥ (commendation) and wider than šukr, since it is not tied to a favour received.

why.bs: „Hvala Allahu, Gospodaru svjetova!”
why.en: “All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”

why.bs: „Hvala Allahu koji Sebi nije uzeo dijete” – hvala za savršenstvo, ne za blagodat.
why.en: “Praise to Allah, who has not taken a son” — praise for perfection, not for a favour.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, šukr je predočiti sebi blagodat i ispoljiti je. Kad je Allah opisan kao شَكُور (64:17), ar-Rāġib to tumači Njegovom blagodati robovima i nagrađivanjem njihovog ibadeta – a tako se razumije i شَاكِر (2:158). Suprotnost mu je, kaže on, كُفْر – zaboravljanje i prikrivanje blagodati.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, šukr is picturing a favour to oneself and showing it. Where Allah is called شَكُور (64:17), ar-Rāġib explains it as His favour to His servants and His rewarding of their worship — and شَاكِر (2:158) is understood the same way. Its opposite, he notes, is kufr — forgetting and concealing the favour.

why.bs: „Ako budete zahvalni, sigurno ću vam još više dati.”
why.en: “If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.”

why.bs: „Zahvaljujte Mi i ne budite nezahvalni.”
why.en: “Be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.”

why.bs: Sulejman: „da me iskuša – hoću li zahvalan ili nezahvalan biti”.
why.en: Solomon: “to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful”.

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola znače „misliti, smatrati”; razlikuju se po tome koliko je uvjerenje čvrsto i koliko mu se može vjerovati.
shared.en: All three verbs mean “to think, to suppose”; they differ in how firm the belief is and how far it can be trusted.

tellApart.bs: Mišljenje zasnovano na znaku, od slutnje do izvjesnosti → ظَنَّ; misliti, a da suprotno i ne padne na pamet → حَسِبَ; tvrditi ono što je vjerovatno laž – u Kur'anu uvijek pokuđeno → زَعَمَ.
tellApart.en: An opinion resting on a sign, from guess to certainty → ظَنَّ; to think, without the opposite even coming to mind → حَسِبَ; to claim what is likely false — in the Quran always blamed → زَعَمَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ظن, حسب, زعم
aṭ-Ṭabarī, Jāmiʿ al-bayān — on 2:46
notes: ar-Rāġib: ẓann arises from a sign, leading to knowledge when strong and not passing imagination when very weak; ḥusbān is judging for one of two opposites without the other coming to mind, unlike ẓann where both are in mind and one prevails; zaʿm is reporting a claim open to suspicion of falsehood, which is why it comes in the Quran in blame of those who make it — attributed to him.
ẓann as certainty in 2:46 is the tafsir reading (aṭ-Ṭabarī), named as such.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ظن, حسب, زعم (2026-11-06): 11 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što proizlazi iz nekog znaka; kad je jako, vodi do znanja, a kad je vrlo slabo, ne prelazi granicu uobrazilje. Zato u 2:46 znači uvjerenje, a u 45:32 puku pretpostavku.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what arises from a sign; when strong it leads to knowledge, when very weak it goes no further than imagining. Hence in 2:46 it means conviction, and in 45:32 mere supposition.

why.bs: Oni koji znaju da će pred Gospodara svoga izaći – tefsir: ظَنَّ ovdje znači uvjerenje.
why.en: Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord — tafsir: ẓann here means certainty.

why.bs: „Mi samo nagađamo, mi nismo uvjereni” – ظَنَّ kao slaba pretpostavka.
why.en: “We think it is only assumption, and we are not convinced” — ẓann as weak supposition.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, presuditi za jednu od dvije suprotnosti, a da druga uopće ne padne na pamet – za razliku od ظَنّ, gdje čovjek ima obje na umu pa jedna prevlada. U Kur'anu često o pogrešnom uvjerenju.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, judging for one of two opposites without the other even coming to mind — unlike ẓann, where both are in mind and one prevails. In the Quran often of a mistaken belief.

why.bs: „Zar ljudi misle da će biti ostavljeni samo zato što govore: Mi vjerujemo?”
why.en: “Do the people think that they will be left to say, ‘We believe’ and they will not be tried?”

why.bs: Oni misle da dobro rade – pogrešno uvjerenje bez sumnje.
why.en: While they think that they are doing well in work — a mistaken belief without doubt.

why.bs: „Nikako ne smatraj mrtvima one koji su na Allahovom putu poginuli.”
why.en: “And never think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, prenošenje tvrdnje za koju se sumnja da je laž; zato je, kaže on, u Kur'anu svugdje pokuđeno onima koji tako tvrde.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, reporting a claim open to suspicion of falsehood; which is why, he says, it comes in the Quran everywhere in blame of those who claim so.

why.bs: Nevjernici tvrde da neće biti oživljeni.
why.en: Those who disbelieve have claimed that they will never be resurrected.

why.bs: „Gdje su vaši ortaci za koje ste tvrdili (da su božanstva)?”
why.en: “Where are your partners that you used to claim?”

why.bs: „Pozovite one za koje ste tvrdili da su Moji ortaci.”
why.en: “Call My partners whom you claimed.”

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o milosti; u Kur'anu su ponajviše Allahova svojstva. Razlikuju se po tome koliko je milost obuhvatna i kome se pripisuje.
shared.en: All three words speak of mercy; in the Quran they are above all attributes of Allah. They differ in how far the mercy reaches and to whom the word is applied.

tellApart.bs: Milost koja obuhvata sve, ime samo za Allaha → رَحْمٰن; milostiv – kaže se za Allaha, ali i za čovjeka → رَحِيم; nježna, blaga samilost, gotovo uvijek uz رَحِيم → رَءُوف.
tellApart.en: Mercy that embraces all, a name for Allah alone → رَحْمٰن; merciful — said of Allah and also of a human being → رَحِيم; tender compassion, almost always beside رَحِيم → رَءُوف.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رحم, رأف
notes: ar-Rāġib: raḥma is a tenderness that calls for doing good to the one shown mercy; when ascribed to Allah it means the doing of good alone, without the tenderness; ar-Raḥmān is said of Allah alone, while raḥīm is said of others too — all attributed to him. 9:128 is shown as the Quranic case of raḥīm said of a human being; ar-Rāġib himself cites it there, right after saying raḥīm is used of others too (checked against the text).

'Raḥmān of this world, Raḥīm of the hereafter' and 'Raḥmān for all creatures, Raḥīm for the believers' (with 33:43) are given as sayings found in tafsir, not attributed to one scholar; they are not the only views.
ar-Rāġib glosses raʾfa simply as raḥma; that raʾfa is a more tender or intense mercy is said in tafsir and stated as such, not put in his mouth.

That رَءُوف stands beside رَحِيم in 9 of its 11 places, and is said once of the Prophet (9:128) and otherwise of Allah, is our own observation (all 11 read). That ar-Raḥmān is never said of anyone but Allah holds for all 56 places (checked).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رحم, رأف (2026-11-06): 8 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (improved): ar-Rāġib does cite 9:128 as raḥīm said of the Prophet, directly after saying raḥīm is used of others than Allah

nuance.bs: Allahovo ime i svojstvo, nikada se ne kaže ni za koga drugog. Prema ar-Rāġibu, to je zato što Njegova milost „obuhvata sve”. U Kur'anu stoji i kao vlastito ime, u ravni imena Allah.
nuance.en: A name and attribute of Allah, never said of anyone else. According to ar-Rāġib this is because His mercy “embraces all things”. In the Quran it also stands as a proper name, on a par with the name Allah.

why.bs: رَحْمٰن i رَحِيم jedno uz drugo, na početku Kur'ana.
why.en: رَحْمٰن and رَحِيم side by side, at the opening of the Quran.

why.bs: „Zovite Allaha ili zovite Milostivog” – ar-Raḥmān kao ime, ravno imenu Allah.
why.en: “Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful” — ar-Raḥmān as a name, on a par with the name Allah.

why.bs: Mušrici pitaju „A šta je Milostivi?” – ime koje su odbijali da priznaju.
why.en: The idolaters ask “And what is the Most Merciful?” — a name they refused to acknowledge.

nuance.bs: Najčešći oblik u Kur'anu, obično na kraju ajeta uz Allahovo ime. Za razliku od رَحْمٰن, kaže se i za stvorenja: Poslanik je prema vjernicima رَءُوف رَحِيم.
nuance.en: The most frequent of the three, usually at the close of an ayah with a name of Allah. Unlike رَحْمٰن it is said of creatures too: the Prophet is رَءُوف رَحِيم towards the believers.

why.bs: O Poslaniku: „prema vjernicima je blag i milostiv” – رَحِيم rečeno za čovjeka.
why.en: Of the Prophet: “to the believers he is kind and merciful” — رَحِيم said of a human being.

why.bs: „On je prema vjernicima milostiv”; neki mufessiri odatle zaključuju da je رَحِيم milost posebno prema vjernicima (za razliku od رَحْمٰن, koje obuhvata sve).
why.en: “He is ever merciful to the believers”; some mufassirun draw from it that رَحِيم is mercy shown especially to the believers (unlike رَحْمٰن, which embraces all).

why.bs: Allahova jednoća, a odmah zatim Njegova milost: رَحْمٰن i رَحِيم.
why.en: Allah's oneness, followed at once by His mercy: رَحْمٰن and رَحِيم.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib ra'fu tumači jednostavno kao milost (raḥma); u tefsiru se kaže da je to posebno nježna, jaka samilost. U Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) stoji gotovo uvijek uz رَحِيم i dopunjuje ga.
nuance.en: ar-Rāġib glosses raʾfa simply as mercy (raḥma); tafsir describes it as an especially tender, intense compassion. In the Quran (our observation) it stands almost always beside رَحِيم and completes it.

why.bs: Allah neće dati da propadne vaše vjerovanje – „Allah je prema ljudima blag i milostiv”.
why.en: Allah would not let your faith go to waste — “Allah is, to the people, Kind and Merciful”.

why.bs: Jedino mjesto gdje se رَءُوف kaže za čovjeka: za Poslanika.
why.en: The one place رَءُوف is said of a human being: of the Prophet.

why.bs: „Allah je blag prema robovima Svojim” – jedno od dva mjesta bez رَحِيم.
why.en: “Allah is kind to His servants” — one of the two places without رَحِيم.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi opisuju odnos prema vjeri koji je suprotan imanu; razlikuju se po tome šta je u središtu: poricanje, pripisivanje druga Allahu ili skrivanje nevjerstva iza javnog vjerovanja.
shared.en: All three words describe a stance opposed to faith; they differ in what is at its heart: denial, ascribing partners to Allah, or hiding disbelief behind a public faith.

tellApart.bs: Prikrivanje i poricanje istine ili blagodati – najšira riječ → كَفَرَ; pripisivanje Allahu druga, ortaka → مُشْرِك; javno vjerovanje, a skriveno nevjerstvo → مُنَافِق.
tellApart.en: Covering over and denying the truth or a favour — the widest word → كَفَرَ; ascribing a partner to Allah → مُشْرِك; faith shown in public, disbelief kept hidden → مُنَافِق.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كفر, شرك, نفق
notes: ar-Rāġib: kufr is at root covering a thing; kufr of a favour is covering it by not giving thanks; the greatest kufr is denying the oneness of Allah, the sharīʿa or prophethood — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: nifāq is entering the religion by one door and leaving it by another, related, like nāfiqāʾ (the jerboa's bolt-hole), to nafaq, a tunnel that runs right through — attributed to him.
The distinction between major shirk and minor shirk (showing off in worship) is a common one among scholars, stated without naming one.
That كَفَرَ is wider than شِرْك (98:1 names among those who disbelieved both People of the Scripture and idolaters) is read from the ayah itself.
Members are the verb كَفَرَ and the agent nouns مُشْرِك, مُنَافِق: the forms a learner meets most; the nouns كُفْر (37), شِرْك (5) and نِفَاق (3) are rarer.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries كفر, شرك, نفق (2026-11-06): 9 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/1 (reworded): He derives both nāfiqāʾ al-yarbūʿ and nifāq from nafaq, a passage that goes through; 'two openings' is not his wording; members/0/nuance (reattributed): He does not rank the three words; he calls shirk the greatest kufr and reports that most jurists take 'mushrikūn' in 9:5 to mean all kuffār; members/2/nuance (reworded): He derives nifāq, like the jerboa's nāfiqāʾ, from nafaq (a tunnel that goes through); he does not mention two openings
Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): 9:67 bs 'nepokorni' for al-fāsiqūn.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnovno značenje je „prekriti”: nevjernik prekriva istinu, a nezahvalnik blagodat. U kur'anskoj upotrebi najšira od tri riječi – obuhvata i mušrike i one od sljedbenika Knjige koji ne vjeruju, a znači i nezahvalnost.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root sense is “to cover”: the disbeliever covers the truth, the ingrate covers a favour. In Quranic usage the widest of the three — it takes in the idolaters and those of the People of the Scripture who disbelieve, and it also means ingratitude.

why.bs: „Oni koji ne vjeruju, od sljedbenika Knjige i mušrika” – كَفَرَ obuhvata obje skupine.
why.en: “Those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists” — كَفَرَ takes in both groups.

why.bs: „Ako budete zahvalni… a ako budete nezahvalni” – كَفَرَ kao suprotnost zahvalnosti.
why.en: “If you are grateful… but if you deny” — كَفَرَ as the opposite of gratitude.

why.bs: Ko zahvaljuje, sebi zahvaljuje, a ko je nezahvalan – Allah je neovisan.
why.en: Whoever is grateful is grateful for himself; whoever is ungrateful — Allah is Free of need.

nuance.bs: Onaj ko Allahu pripisuje druga u božanstvu ili ibadetu. U Kur'anu se mušrici često spominju posebno, uz sljedbenike Knjige, kao zasebna skupina.
nuance.en: One who ascribes a partner to Allah in divinity or worship. The Quran often names the polytheists separately, beside the People of the Scripture, as a group of their own.

why.bs: Mušrici spomenuti odvojeno od sljedbenika Knjige – širk je jedna vrsta kufra.
why.en: The polytheists named apart from the People of the Scripture — shirk is one kind of kufr.

why.bs: „I nikako ne budi od mušrika!” – Poslanik se odriče svakog druga Allahu.
why.en: “And never be of the polytheists” — the Prophet disowns every partner to Allah.

why.bs: Ne ženite se mušrikama dok ne povjeruju – mušrik je zasebna kategorija u propisima o braku (obim ovog ajeta i njegov odnos prema 5:5 raspravlja se u fikhu).
why.en: Do not marry polytheistic women until they believe — the polytheist is a category of its own in the marriage rulings (the ayah's scope and its relation to 5:5 are discussed in fiqh).

nuance.bs: Onaj ko javno pokazuje vjerovanje, a krije nevjerstvo. Prema ar-Rāġibu, riječ dolazi od نَفَق, prolaza koji vodi skroz kroz zemlju, kao izlaz iz jazbine pustinjskog miša: munafik ulazi u vjeru na jedna vrata, a izlazi na druga.
nuance.en: One who shows faith in public and hides disbelief. According to ar-Rāġib the word comes from nafaq, a tunnel that runs right through, like the jerboa's bolt-hole: the hypocrite enters the religion by one door and leaves by another.

why.bs: Svjedoče da je on Allahov Poslanik, a Allah svjedoči da su lažljivci – riječi bez uvjerenja.
why.en: They bear witness that he is Allah's Messenger, and Allah bears witness that they are liars — words without conviction.

why.bs: „Licemjeri su, zaista, nepokorni” – ar-Rāġib ovaj ajet navodi uz nifāq.
why.en: “The hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient” — the ayah ar-Rāġib cites under nifāq.

why.bs: Licemjeri će biti na samom dnu vatre – težina skrivenog nevjerstva.
why.en: The hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire — the gravity of hidden disbelief.

title.en: To believe, to submit, to be certain

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola opisuju vjernikov odnos prema istini; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu srce, predanost ili čvrstina uvjerenja.
shared.en: All three verbs describe the believer's stance towards the truth; they differ in whether the heart, submission or firmness of conviction is in view.

tellApart.bs: Vjerovanje srcem, potvrđivanje istine → آمَنَ; predanost Allahu – u najmanjem javno prihvatanje vjere, u punini potpuna unutarnja i vanjska predanost → أَسْلَمَ; čvrsto uvjerenje bez sumnje → أَيْقَنَ.
tellApart.en: Belief in the heart, affirming the truth → آمَنَ; submitting to Allah — at the least outward acceptance of the religion, at the fullest complete inward and outward surrender → أَسْلَمَ; firm conviction free of doubt → أَيْقَنَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أمن, سلم, يقين
notes: ar-Rāġib: islām in the sharīʿa is of two kinds — one below īmān, acknowledgement by the tongue, with or without belief (49:14), and one above īmān, acknowledgement with belief in the heart, fulfilment in deed and submission to Allah in all He decrees (2:131, Ibrāhīm) — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: yaqīn is a quality of knowledge above maʿrifa — stillness of understanding with firmness of judgement — attributed to him.

Scholars differ on whether īmān and islām are one or two; a widespread view is that they differ when named together (as in 49:14) and each includes the other when named alone. Stated as a difference of views.
أَيْقَنَ is Form IV (يُوقِنُونَ); the noun يَقِين (8) is not a separate member.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries سلم, يقين (2026-11-06): 9 attributed points confirmed
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (يقن → يقين); أمن read and added to `verified` (consistent with the texts; no attributed point rests on it).

nuance.bs: Vjerovati i potvrditi istinu srcem, s povjerenjem; iz istog korijena kao sigurnost (أَمْن). Najčešći od tri glagola.
nuance.en: To believe and affirm the truth in the heart, with trust; from the same root as safety (أَمْن). The most frequent of the three.

why.bs: „Recite: ’Predali smo se’, jer vjerovanje još nije ušlo u srca vaša” – iman je u srcu.
why.en: “Say, ’We have submitted’, for faith has not yet entered your hearts” — īmān lives in the heart.

why.bs: Poslanik i vjernici vjeruju u Allaha, meleke, knjige i poslanike – predmet imana.
why.en: The Messenger and the believers believe in Allah, His angels, books and messengers — the objects of faith.

why.bs: „O vjernici, vjerujte…” – vjernicima se naređuje da vjeruju: iman se obnavlja i jača.
why.en: “O you who believe, believe…” — believers bidden to believe: faith renewed and strengthened.

nuance.bs: Predati se Allahu i prihvatiti Njegovu vjeru. Prema ar-Rāġibu, islam je dvojak: ispod imana – samo izgovor jezikom (49:14), i iznad imana – kad se jeziku pridruže srce, djelo i potpuna predanost (Ibrahim).
nuance.en: To submit to Allah and accept His religion. According to ar-Rāġib, islām is of two kinds: below īmān — the tongue's acknowledgement alone (49:14) — and above it, when heart, deed and complete submission join the tongue (Ibrāhīm).

why.bs: Beduinima je rečeno „predali smo se”, ne „vjerujemo” – islam ispod imana.
why.en: The Bedouins are told to say “we have submitted”, not “we believe” — islām below īmān.

why.bs: „Predaj se!” – „Predajem se Gospodaru svjetova” – Ibrahimova potpuna predanost, islam iznad imana.
why.en: “Submit!” — “I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds” — Ibrāhīm's complete submission, islām above īmān.

why.bs: Najbolji u vjeri je onaj ko lice svoje preda Allahu čineći dobro.
why.en: Best in religion is the one who submits his face to Allah while doing good.

nuance.bs: Biti čvrsto uvjeren, bez ikakve sumnje. Prema ar-Rāġibu, yaqīn je stepen znanja iznad spoznaje (maʿrifa): smirenost razumijevanja uz čvrst sud. Najčešće se kaže za uvjerenje u ahiret i u ajete.
nuance.en: To be firmly convinced, without any doubt. According to ar-Rāġib, yaqīn is a degree of knowledge above maʿrifa: stillness of understanding with firm judgement. Most often said of conviction in the hereafter and in the signs.

why.bs: „I u onaj svijet čvrsto vjeruju” – uvjerenje u ahiret.
why.en: “And of the Hereafter they are certain” — conviction in the hereafter.

why.bs: U stvaranju živih bića su znakovi za ljude koji su čvrsto uvjereni.
why.en: In the creation of living creatures are signs for a people who are certain.

why.bs: Predvodnici koji su bili strpljivi i u Naše ajete čvrsto vjerovali.
why.en: Leaders who were patient and were certain of Our signs.

title.en: To call and to call out

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače „zvati”; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu povišen glas ili molba i obraćanje.
shared.en: Both verbs mean “to call”; they differ in whether a raised voice or a request and an address is in view.

tellApart.bs: Zvati, moliti, prizivati – i Allaha u dovi → دَعَا; dozivati povišenim glasom da se čuje, često iz daljine → نَادَى.
tellApart.en: To call, to pray, to invoke — Allah too, in supplication → دَعَا; to call out aloud so as to be heard, often from afar → نَادَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries دعا, ندا
notes: ar-Rāġib: nidāʾ is raising the voice and making it heard; duʿāʾ is like nidāʾ, except that nidāʾ may be just “yā” or “ayā” without a name, while duʿāʾ is hardly said without the name; he cites 2:171 (duʿāʾan wa-nidāʾan, nouns, so not a member ayah here) — attributed to him.
19:3 'a secret call' (nidāʾan khafiyyan): that this joins a word for calling aloud with secrecy is commented on in tafsir; given as tafsir, not a named mufassir.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries دعا, ندا (2026-11-06): 6 attributed points confirmed
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (ندى → ندا).

nuance.bs: Zvati nekoga po imenu, pozivati, moliti; odatle دُعَاء – dova. Kaže se za molitvu Allahu, ali i za prizivanje lažnih božanstava i za pozivanje ljudi nečemu.
nuance.en: To call someone by name, to invite, to pray; hence دُعَاء, supplication. It is said of praying to Allah, but also of invoking false gods and of inviting people to something.

why.bs: „Molite Mene, odazvat ću vam se” – dova Allahu.
why.en: “Call upon Me; I will respond to you” — supplication to Allah.

why.bs: „Molite Gospodara svoga ponizno i u sebi” – dova ne traži povišen glas.
why.en: “Call upon your Lord in humility and privately” — duʿāʾ needs no raised voice.

why.bs: „Zovite Allaha ili zovite Milostivog” – دَعَا s imenom onoga koga se zove, kako ar-Rāġib i opisuje.
why.en: “Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful” — دَعَا with the name of the one called, as ar-Rāġib describes it.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nidāʾ je podizanje glasa da se čuje. Zato نَادَى često stoji tamo gdje se doziva iz daljine ili glasno – stanovnici dženneta dozivaju stanovnike vatre.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, nidāʾ is raising the voice so it is heard. Hence نَادَى often stands where someone calls from afar or aloud — the people of Paradise call out to the people of the Fire.

why.bs: Stanovnici dženneta doviknu stanovnicima vatre – dozivanje preko onoga što dvije skupine razdvaja.
why.en: The companions of Paradise call out to the companions of the Fire — calling across what separates the two groups.

why.bs: Junus je iz tmina zazvao: „Nema boga osim Tebe” – nidāʾ za usrdnu dovu iz nevolje, ne nužno za daljinu.
why.en: Jonah called out within the darkness: “There is no deity except You” — nidāʾ for an urgent supplication in distress, not necessarily distance.

why.bs: Zekerijja je Gospodara zazvao „tihim glasom” – riječ za glasno dozivanje uz tišinu; tefsir kaže da je dovu sakrio od ljudi.
why.en: Zechariah called to his Lord “a private call” — a word for calling aloud joined to secrecy; tafsir says he hid his prayer from people.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o pravom putu; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu pokazivanje puta ili zrelost i ispravnost onoga ko njime ide.
shared.en: Both words speak of the right way; they differ in whether showing the way or the soundness and maturity of the one who walks it is in view.

tellApart.bs: Uputa koju Allah daje, Knjiga kao uputa → هُدًى; ispravnost, zrelost i razboritost, suprotnost zabludi (غَيّ) → رُشْد.
tellApart.en: Guidance Allah gives, the Book as guidance → هُدًى; rightness, maturity and good sense, the opposite of error (غَيّ) → رُشْد.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries هدى, رشد
notes: ar-Rāġib: hidāya is guiding with gentleness; Allah's guidance is of four kinds — the general guidance given to every creature, the call through the prophets, the help (tawfīq) given to the guided, and the guidance to Paradise in the hereafter — attributed to him.

ar-Rāġib: rashad and rushd are the opposite of ghayy and used like hidāya; he reports that some said rushd is said of worldly and otherworldly matters and rashad of otherworldly matters only — given as the view of 'some' he reports.
رُشْد (6) and رَشَد (5) are two vocalisations of one word, filed by the corpus as two lemmas; counted together (11).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries هدى, رشد (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (improved): He adds that the Quran reserves the word hudā (unlike hidāya) for guidance Allah Himself grants, citing ﴿ هدى للمتقين ﴾

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, upućivanje s blagošću. Allahova uputa je četverostruka: opća uputa svakom stvorenju, poziv po poslanicima, pomoć (tevfik) upućenima i uvođenje u džennet. On ističe da je riječ هُدًى rezervisana za uputu koju daje sam Allah – zato se i Knjiga zove هُدًى.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, guiding with gentleness. Allah's guidance is fourfold: general guidance to every creature, the call through the prophets, help (tawfīq) to the guided, and leading into Paradise. He notes that the word هُدًى is reserved for guidance Allah Himself grants — so the Book itself is called هُدًى.

why.bs: „Uputa onima koji se boje Allaha” – Knjiga kao uputa.
why.en: “A guidance for those conscious of Allah” — the Book as guidance.

why.bs: Onima koji su na pravom putu On uputu povećava – uputa kao pomoć upućenima.
why.en: Those who are guided — He increases them in guidance: guidance as help to the guided.

why.bs: Ko bude slijedio Moju uputu, ni straha ni tuge za njih – uputa poslana ljudima.
why.en: Whoever follows My guidance — no fear for them, nor will they grieve: guidance sent to people.

nuance.bs: Ispravnost razuma i postupanja, suprotno zabludi (غَيّ). Kaže se i za zrelost siročeta koje može upravljati imetkom. Ar-Rāġib prenosi mišljenje da se رُشْد kaže za dunjalučke i ahiretske stvari, a رَشَد samo za ahiretske.
nuance.en: Soundness of mind and conduct, the opposite of error (غَيّ). It is said even of an orphan's maturity to manage property. ar-Rāġib reports the view that رُشْد is said of worldly and otherworldly matters, and رَشَد of otherworldly matters only.

why.bs: „Jasno se razlikuje pravi put od zablude” – رُشْد nasuprot غَيّ.
why.en: “The right course has become clear from the wrong” — رُشْد against غَيّ.

why.bs: Kad kod siročadi primijetite zrelost (رُشْد), predajte im imetak – dunjalučka razboritost.
why.en: When you perceive in the orphans sound judgement (رُشْد), release their property to them — worldly good sense.

why.bs: Oni koji su primili islam, pravi put (رَشَد) su izabrali – ispravnost u vjeri, koju mišljenje što ga ar-Rāġib prenosi veže za ahiret.
why.en: Whoever has accepted Islam — those have sought out the right course (رَشَد) — rightness in religion, which the view ar-Rāġib reports ties to the hereafter.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače skretanje s pravog puta; razlikuju se po uzroku: svako skretanje, ili zabluda koja izvire iz pogrešnog uvjerenja.
shared.en: Both words mean leaving the right way; they differ in the cause: any straying, or error that springs from a corrupt belief.

tellApart.bs: Svako skretanje s pravog puta, namjerno ili ne, malo ili veliko → ضَلَال; zabluda iz pogrešnog uvjerenja, suprotnost رُشْد → غَيّ.
tellApart.en: Any straying from the straight path, intended or not, small or great → ضَلَال; error rooted in a corrupt belief, the opposite of رُشْد → غَيّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ضل, غوى
notes: ar-Rāġib: ḍalāl is turning aside from the straight path, the opposite of guidance, said of every deviation, intended or unintended, small or great — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: ghayy is ignorance that comes from a corrupt belief, as distinct from ignorance with no belief at all — attributed to him.
53:2 (mā ḍalla … wa-mā ghawā) shows both roots side by side, but uses verbs, not these nouns; mentioned here only.
The corpus files ضَلَالَة (9) as a separate lemma; it is not added to ضَلَال.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ضل, غوى, رشد (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): His examples of the light end are oversight and forgetting (﴿ أن تضل إحداهما ﴾ = forgets), set against 'far error' which is kufr; 'being at a loss' is not his

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, skretanje s pravog puta – svako, namjerno ili nenamjerno, malo ili veliko. Zato se, kaže on, odnosi i na običan previd ili zaborav i na daleku zabludu nevjerstva (ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, turning aside from the straight path — any such turning, intended or not, small or great. Hence, he notes, it is said both of a mere oversight or forgetting and of the far error of disbelief (ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا).

why.bs: Ko Allahu pripisuje druga, daleko je zalutao – ضَلَال بَعِيد, najveća zabluda.
why.en: Whoever associates others with Allah has gone far astray — ضَلَال بَعِيد, the greatest error.

why.bs: Braća kažu da je njihov otac „u očitoj zabludi” – za njih je pogriješio u ljubavi prema Jusufu, ne u vjeri.
why.en: The brothers say their father is “in clear error” — to them he erred in his love for Joseph, not in faith.

why.bs: „A šta ima poslije istine osim zablude?” – ضَلَال kao sve što nije istina.
why.en: “What can be beyond truth except error?” — ضَلَال as all that is not the truth.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, neznanje koje izvire iz pogrešnog uvjerenja. Stoji nasuprot رُشْد, a Kur'an ga kaže za one koji biraju krivi put (7:146) i slijede strasti.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ignorance that springs from a corrupt belief. It stands against رُشْد, and the Quran uses it of those who choose the wrong way (7:146) and follow their desires.

why.bs: Pravi put se jasno razlikuje od zablude (غَيّ) – zato nema prisile u vjeri.
why.en: The right course is distinct from the wrong (غَيّ) — so there is no compulsion in religion.

why.bs: Ako vide put zablude, uzimaju ga za put – svjesno biranje krivog puta.
why.en: If they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way — knowingly choosing the wrong road.

why.bs: Pokoljenja koja su zapustila namaz i povela se za strastima – susrest će غَيّ (tefsir ga tumači kao propast ili kao dolinu u Džehennemu).
why.en: Generations that neglected prayer and followed desires will meet غَيّ (tafsir explains it as ruin, or as a valley in Hell).

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače činiti nepravdu; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu stavljanje stvari na krivo mjesto, oholo prekoračenje ili napad preko granice.
shared.en: All three words mean doing wrong; they differ in whether putting a thing in the wrong place, overbearing excess, or crossing a limit in attack is in view.

tellApart.bs: Nepravda u najširem smislu – i prema sebi, i prema Allahu → ظُلْم; oholo prekoračenje mjere, nasilje nad drugima → بَغْي; prelaženje granice, neprijateljski napad → عُدْوَان.
tellApart.en: Wrong in the widest sense — towards oneself and towards Allah too → ظُلْم; overbearing excess, oppressing others → بَغْي; overstepping a limit, hostile attack → عُدْوَان.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ظلم, بغى, عدا
notes: ar-Rāġib: ẓulm is putting a thing in other than its proper place, by falling short, by excess, or by deviating in time or place; he cites some sages that it is of three kinds — between man and Allah (the greatest: kufr, shirk and nifāq), between man and people, and between man and himself — attributed to him.

ar-Rāġib: baghy is seeking to go beyond the right measure, whether or not one goes beyond it; the blameworthy baghy is passing beyond the truth to falsehood or to the doubtful, and in most places in the Quran it is blameworthy — attributed to him.
ʿudwān is explained by its root ʿ-d-w (going beyond, overstepping); said as the root's sense.

2:193 (no ʿudwān except against the wrongdoers): many mufassirun explain that the just response is called ʿudwān by correspondence (mušākala) with the wrong it answers; given as their explanation (blind review).
6:82: the Prophet's explanation of ẓulm there as shirk (citing 31:13) is reported in the Ṣaḥīḥ collections; the ayah is not cited as a member ayah, the hadith is mentioned in 31:13's note only.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ظلم, بغى (2026-11-06): 6 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): He gives the definition as that of lexicographers and many scholars, and reports the three-fold division from 'some sages', naming kufr, shirk and nifāq as the gravest; notes/1 (reworded): He defines blameworthy baghy as passing from truth to falsehood or the doubtful, and says it is blameworthy in most Quranic places; 'against others' is not his definition; members/0/nuance (reworded): The three-fold division is reported by him from 'some sages', not stated as his own
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): عدا read and added to `verified` (consistent with the texts; no attributed point rests on it).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, stavljanje stvari na mjesto koje joj ne pripada. Najšira riječ; on navodi mudrace koji je dijele na nepravdu prema Allahu (širk), prema ljudima i prema samome sebi.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, putting a thing where it does not belong. The widest word; he cites sages who divide it into wrong against Allah (shirk), against people, and against oneself.

why.bs: „Širk je, zaista, velika nepravda” – ẓulm prema Allahu; Poslanik je tim ajetom objasnio ẓulm u 6:82.
why.en: “Association is great injustice” — ẓulm against Allah; with this ayah the Prophet explained the ẓulm of 6:82.

why.bs: Ko to učini „s neprijateljstvom i nepravdom” – عُدْوَان i ظُلْم jedno uz drugo.
why.en: Whoever does that “in aggression and injustice” — عُدْوَان and ظُلْم side by side.

why.bs: Allah ne želi nepravdu robovima – ẓulm koji Allah od Sebe odbija.
why.en: Allah wants no injustice for His servants — ẓulm, which Allah disowns for His servants.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, težnja da se pređe prava mjera. Ar-Rāġib razlikuje i pohvalni بَغْي (prelaženje pravde u dobročinstvo); u Kur'anu je imenica najčešće oholo nasilje nad drugima, i suparništvo iz zavisti zbog kojeg su se razišli oni kojima je data Knjiga.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, seeking to go beyond the right measure. ar-Rāġib also names a laudable baghy (going beyond justice to kindness); in the Quran the noun is mostly overbearing wrong against others, and the rivalry out of envy through which those given the Scripture fell into dispute.

why.bs: Allah zabranjuje razvrat, odvratnost i nasilje (بَغْي) – nepravda prema drugima.
why.en: Allah forbids immorality, bad conduct and oppression (بَغْي) — wrong done to others.

why.bs: Razišli su se tek kad im je došlo znanje, „iz međusobne zavisti” (بَغْيًا) – suparništvo, ne neznanje.
why.en: They differed only after knowledge came to them, “out of jealous animosity” (بَغْيًا) — rivalry, not ignorance.

why.bs: „O ljudi, nasilje vaše je samo vama na štetu” – بَغْي se vraća onome ko ga čini.
why.en: “O mankind, your injustice is only against yourselves” — بَغْي recoils on its doer.

nuance.bs: Iz korijena koji znači prelaziti granicu: nepravda kao prekoračenje, neprijateljski napad. Često stoji u paru s grijehom (إِثْم).
nuance.en: From a root meaning to go beyond: wrong as overstepping, hostile attack. Often paired with sin (إِثْم).

why.bs: „Ne pomažite se u grijehu i neprijateljstvu” – عُدْوَان uz إِثْم.
why.en: “Do not cooperate in sin and aggression” — عُدْوَان beside إِثْم.

why.bs: „Neprijateljstvo samo prema nasilnicima” – mnogi mufessiri tumače da se pravedan odgovor zove عُدْوَان po paralelizmu s nasiljem na koje odgovara.
why.en: “No aggression except against the oppressors” — many mufassirun explain the just response as called عُدْوَان by parallel with the aggression it answers.

why.bs: Musa: „Da ne bude nepravde prema meni” – prelaženje dogovorene granice.
why.en: Moses: “there is no injustice to me” — overstepping an agreed limit.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače pravdu; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu jednakost i ravnoteža ili pravedan udio koji svakome pripada.
shared.en: Both words mean justice; they differ in whether equality and balance or the fair share due to each is in view.

tellApart.bs: Pravda kao jednakost, pravedan sud, pa i „protuvrijednost” → عَدْل; pravedan udio, ispravna mjera i vaga → قِسْط.
tellApart.en: Justice as equality, a fair judgement, even an “equivalent” → عَدْل; the fair share, right measure and weight → قِسْط.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عدل, قسط
notes: ar-Rāġib: ʿadl is equality; ʿadl is used of what is grasped by insight (judgements), ʿidl of what is perceived by the senses (weights, numbers) — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: qisṭ is the share given justly; qasaṭa is taking another's share (injustice, 72:15 al-qāsiṭūn) while aqsaṭa is giving another his share (justice) — attributed to him.
That قِسْط often stands with weighing and measure (6:152, 55:9, 21:47) is our observation of its 15 places.
In 2:48 and 5:95 the Quran's word is read ʿadl (with fatḥa) in the sense of an equivalent, and ar-Rāġib himself cites 5:95 under ʿadl, as an equivalence grasped by insight rather than by the senses.
49:9 joins both (fa-aṣliḥū baynahumā bi-l-ʿadl wa-aqsiṭū): cited under عَدْل.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries عدل, قسط (2026-11-06): 10 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/3 (reworded): He cites ﴿ أو عدل ذلك صياما ﴾ (5:95) as the example of ʿadl, the equivalence grasped by insight, and glosses it as fasting equal to the food; members/0/nuance (reworded): He explains 5:95 as fasting equal to the food of the expiation; he does not discuss the ransom sense of 2:48
Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): 'ransom' in 2:48 given to the mufassirun, not ar-Rāġib (his gloss there is farīḍa).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, jednakost: podjela na jednake dijelove, a kaže se za ono što se shvata uvidom, poput presuda. Odatle i „protuvrijednost”: post jednak hrani iskupa (5:95, kako ga on tumači); u 2:48 mufesiri to razumiju kao otkupninu jednake vrijednosti.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, equality: dividing into equal shares, said of what is grasped by insight, such as rulings. Hence also an “equivalent”: fasting equal to the food of an expiation (5:95, as he explains it); in 2:48 mufassirun take it as a ransom of equal value.

why.bs: „Allah naređuje pravednost i dobročinstvo” – عَدْل kao temelj.
why.en: “Allah orders justice and good conduct” — عَدْل as the foundation.

why.bs: Kad sudite među ljudima, sudite pravedno – pravda u sudu.
why.en: When you judge between people, judge with justice — justice in judgement.

why.bs: Na Sudnjem danu „neće se primiti otkup” (عَدْل) – عَدْل kao protuvrijednost.
why.en: On that Day “no compensation will be accepted” (عَدْل) — عَدْل as an equivalent.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, udio koji se daje pravedno. Zato قِسْط često stoji uz mjeru i vagu (naše zapažanje), a od istog korijena قَاسِط je nepravednik koji otima tuđi udio, a مُقْسِط pravednik koji ga daje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the share given justly. So قِسْط often stands with measure and weighing (our observation), and from the same root a قَاسِط is the unjust who takes another's share, a مُقْسِط the just who gives it.

why.bs: „Mjerite pravedno i ne zakidajte na vagi” – qisṭ kao ispravna mjera.
why.en: “Establish weight in justice and do not make deficient the balance” — qisṭ as right measure.

why.bs: Postavit ćemo vage pravedne za Sudnji dan – qisṭ i vaga.
why.en: We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection — qisṭ and the scale.

why.bs: „Budite uvijek pravedni, svjedočeći Allaha radi, makar i protiv sebe” – pravo svakoga da dobije svoje.
why.en: “Be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if against yourselves” — each given his due.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače ono što čovjek dobije za svoje djelo; razlikuju se po tome je li riječ o naplati i za dobro i za zlo, o plaći za trud ili o onome što se vraća čovjeku.
shared.en: All three words mean what one receives for one's deed; they differ in whether it is requital for good and evil alike, a wage for work, or what returns to the doer.

tellApart.bs: Uzvraćanje za djelo – i dobro i zlo → جَزَاء; plaća, nagrada za trud, samo za dobro → أَجْر; ono što se čovjeku vraća za djelo, kao imenica u Kur'anu uvijek dobra nagrada → ثَوَاب.
tellApart.en: Requital for a deed, good or evil → جَزَاء; a wage, reward for effort, only for good → أَجْر; what returns to a person for his deed, as a noun in the Quran always a good reward → ثَوَاب.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries جزاء, أجر, ثوب
notes: ar-Rāġib: jazāʾ is what suffices, requital good for good and evil for evil; ajr is what returns from a deed, worldly or otherworldly, said of what comes under a contract or what is like one, and only of benefit, never harm, while jazāʾ is said with or without a contract and of benefit and harm — attributed to him.

ar-Rāġib: thawāb is from thawb, a thing's return to its first state — what returns to a person for his deeds; the word is used of good and evil but is mostly known for good (he cites the verb in 3:153) — attributed to him.
That the noun ثَوَاب in the Quran is always a reward (all 9 places read) is our observation; the verb أَثَابَ is used of grief in 3:153.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries جزاء, أجر, ثوب (2026-11-06): 16 attributed points confirmed
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (جزى → جزاء).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, uzvraćanje: dobro za dobro, zlo za zlo. Zato se kaže i za nagradu i za kaznu, i stoji tamo gdje je djelo mjera uzvrata.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, requital: good for good, evil for evil. So it is said of reward and of punishment alike, and stands where the deed is the measure of what is returned.

why.bs: „Zar je nagrada za dobro išta drugo do dobro?” – جَزَاء za dobro.
why.en: “Is the reward for good anything but good?” — جَزَاء for good.

why.bs: „Kazna za zlo je zlo slično njemu” – جَزَاء za zlo, po mjeri djela.
why.en: “The retribution for an evil act is an evil one like it” — جَزَاء for evil, by the deed's measure.

why.bs: „Kazna primjerena” (جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا) – uzvrat koji odgovara djelima.
why.en: “An appropriate recompense” (جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا) — requital fitting the deeds.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što se dobije za djelo, na dunjaluku ili ahiretu, kao po ugovoru, i to samo korist, nikad šteta. Otuda i obična plaća, i mehr.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what one receives for a deed, in this world or the next, as under a contract — and only benefit, never harm. Hence also an ordinary wage, and the bridal due.

why.bs: Poslanici kažu: „Ja od vas za ovo ne tražim nagrade” – أَجْر kao plaća.
why.en: The prophets say: “I do not ask you for it any payment” — أَجْر as a wage.

why.bs: „Otac moj te zove da te nagradi za to što si napojio” – جَزَى i أَجْر u istoj rečenici, plaća za učinjen posao.
why.en: “My father invites you that he may reward you for having watered for us” — جَزَى and أَجْر in one sentence, payment for work done.

why.bs: „A divna li je nagrada onih koji rade!” – أَجْر kao Allahova nagrada za trud.
why.en: “Excellent is the reward of the workers” — أَجْر as Allah's reward for effort.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što se čovjeku „vraća” za njegova djela (korijen znači povratak). Kaže on da se kaže i za dobro i za zlo, a najčešće za dobro; u Kur'anu je imenica uvijek nagrada (naše zapažanje).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what “returns” to a person for his deeds (the root means return). He says it is used of good and evil but mostly of good; in the Quran the noun is always a reward (our observation).

why.bs: „Nagrada od Allaha, a u Allaha je najljepša nagrada.”
why.en: “A reward from Allah, and Allah has with Him the best reward.”

why.bs: Allah im je dao nagradu na dunjaluku i lijepu nagradu na ahiretu – ثَوَاب na oba svijeta.
why.en: Allah gave them the reward of this world and the good reward of the Hereafter — ثَوَاب in both worlds.

why.bs: Allahova nagrada je najbolja – ثَوَاب kao ono što se vraća vjerniku.
why.en: He is best in reward — ثَوَاب as what returns to the believer.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi označavaju vatru i u Kur'anu najčešće kaznu na ahiretu; razlikuju se po tome je li to vatra uopće ili njena žestina i rasplamsalost.
shared.en: All three words denote fire and in the Quran most often the punishment of the hereafter; they differ in whether fire in general or its fierceness and blaze is in view.

tellApart.bs: Vatra uopće – i ova, dunjalučka, i ahiretska → نَار; žestoka, razbuktala vatra → جَحِيم; raspaljen plamen, oganj → سَعِير.
tellApart.en: Fire in general — of this world and of the hereafter → نَار; a fierce, blazing fire → جَحِيم; a kindled flame, a blaze → سَعِير.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نور, جحم, سعر
notes: ar-Rāġib: nār is said of the flame that is seen, of heat alone, and of the Fire of the hereafter; jaḥīm is from jaḥma, the fierce blazing of fire; saʿīr is from saʿara, to kindle a fire — attributed to him.
That جَحِيم is said once of the fire prepared for Ibrāhīm (37:97) and otherwise of Hell, and that all 16 places of سَعِير speak of the hereafter, is our observation (all places read).
جَهَنَّم is not a member: the corpus treats it as a proper name outside the noun catalogue.
Content: the ayat are quoted as warnings, with no description beyond the Quran's own words.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نور, جحم, سعر (2026-11-06): 8 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Opća riječ za vatru: i za vatru koju je Musa ugledao, i za vatru u koju je bačen Ibrahim, i za vatru na ahiretu, kada se kaže „vatra” bez ikakvog dodatka.
nuance.en: The general word for fire: the fire Moses saw, the fire Ibrāhīm was thrown into, and the Fire of the hereafter, when “the Fire” stands alone.

why.bs: Musa je ugledao vatru – vatra na dunjaluku (u tefsiru se raspravlja je li bila obična vatra ili svjetlo).
why.en: Moses saw a fire — a fire in this world (tafsir discusses whether it was ordinary fire or a light).

why.bs: „O vatro, postani hladna i spasonosna Ibrahimu!”
why.en: “O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham.”

why.bs: „Čuvajte se vatre čije će gorivo biti ljudi i kamenje” – vatra na ahiretu.
why.en: “Fear the Fire, whose fuel is men and stones” — the Fire of the hereafter.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od riječi koja znači žestoko razbuktavanje vatre. U Kur'anu je ime za vatru na ahiretu, a jednom za vatru koju su pripremili Ibrahimu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from a word for the fierce blazing of fire. In the Quran a name for the Fire of the hereafter, and once for the fire prepared for Ibrāhīm.

why.bs: „Bacite ga u oganj!” – Ibrahimovi neprijatelji o vatri koju su zapalili: jedino dunjalučko جَحِيم.
why.en: “Throw him into the burning fire” — Ibrāhīm's enemies speak of the fire they lit: the one worldly use of جَحِيم.

why.bs: „Kad se oganj razbukta” – جَحِيم uz glagol iz korijena سعر.
why.en: “And when Hellfire is set ablaze” — جَحِيم with a verb from the root of سَعِير.

why.bs: Onome ko je bio obijestan, prebivalište će biti oganj – opomena.
why.en: For the one who transgressed, Hellfire will be the refuge — a warning.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od glagola koji znači raspaliti vatru: plamen koji se raspiruje. U Kur'anu uvijek o ahiretu (naše zapažanje), često u spoju „patnja ognja”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from a verb meaning to kindle a fire: a flame that is stoked. In the Quran always of the hereafter (our observation), often in “the punishment of the Blaze”.

why.bs: Oni koji nepravedno jedu imetke siročadi gorjet će u ognju – opomena za nepravdu prema siročadi.
why.en: Those who devour orphans' property unjustly will be burned in a Blaze — a warning against wronging orphans.

why.bs: Šejtanima je pripremljena patnja u ognju – عَذَاب السَّعِير.
why.en: For the devils is prepared the punishment of the Blaze — عَذَاب السَّعِير.

why.bs: „Jedni će u džennet, a drugi u oganj” – سَعِير nasuprot džennetu.
why.en: “A party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze” — سَعِير set against Paradise.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače naselje u kojem žive ljudi; Kur'an ponekad isto mjesto zove i jednim i drugim imenom.
shared.en: Both words mean a settlement where people live; the Quran sometimes calls the same place by both names.

tellApart.bs: Svako naselje, mjesto okupljanja ljudi – i njegovi stanovnici → قَرْيَة; grad, često određeni grad (Medina, faraonov grad) → مَدِينَة.
tellApart.en: Any settlement, a place where people gather — and its people → قَرْيَة; a city, often a particular city (Medina, Pharaoh's city) → مَدِينَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قرى
notes: ar-Rāġib: qarya is a name for the place where people gather and for the people together, used of either — attributed to him.

That the Quran calls one place (as tafsir identifies it) both قَرْيَة and مَدِينَة (18:77 and 18:82; 36:13 and 36:20), and that Mecca is called قَرْيَة (47:13, umm al-qurā 6:92), is our observation; 'qarya = village' is therefore not the Quranic sense.
مَدِينَة: the corpus files the broken plural مَدَائِن (3, Pharaoh's cities) separately; counted together (17).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries قرى (2026-11-06): 3 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reattributed): He cites 47:13 ('your qarya') and calls qarya a name for a city, but never names Mecca, so the Mecca point is now a Quranic observation
Blind review of the verification-pass texts (2026-11-06): 'most often destroyed' softened to 'often'; قَرْيَة rendered town / naselje throughout, keeping city / grad for مَدِينَة.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, mjesto gdje se ljudi okupljaju – i sami ljudi. Ne znači samo selo: u Kur'anu se i Meka zove قَرْيَة (47:13). Često se govori o narodima i njihovim naseljima koja su uništena (naše zapažanje).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the place where people gather — and the people themselves. It does not mean only a village: in the Quran Mecca too is called قَرْيَة (47:13). Often said of peoples and their towns that were destroyed (our observation).

why.bs: „Pitaj naselje u kojem smo bili” – قَرْيَة za stanovnike.
why.en: “Ask the town in which we were” — قَرْيَة for its people.

why.bs: „Tvoje naselje koje te je izgnalo” – Meka nazvana قَرْيَة.
why.en: “Your town which drove you out” — Mecca called قَرْيَة.

why.bs: Došli su stanovnicima jednog naselja (قَرْيَة)… – isto mjesto (tako ga razumije većina mufesira) u 18:82 zove se مَدِينَة (grad).
why.en: They came to the people of a town (قَرْيَة)… — the same place (as most mufassirun take it) is called مَدِينَة (city) in 18:82.

nuance.bs: Grad; u Kur'anu često određeni grad: Poslanikova Medina, faraonov grad, grad u kojem je Musa zatekao dvojicu kako se tuku.
nuance.en: A city; in the Quran often a particular city: the Prophet's Medina, Pharaoh's city, the city where Moses found two men fighting.

why.bs: „Kad se vratimo u Medinu…” – مَدِينَة kao ime Poslanikovog grada.
why.en: “If we return to al-Madinah…” — مَدِينَة as the name of the Prophet's city.

why.bs: Zid je pripadao dvojici dječaka siročadi „u gradu” – isto mjesto koje je u 18:77 قَرْيَة.
