why.en: The wall belonged to two orphan boys “in the city” — the place that is قَرْيَة in 18:77.

why.bs: S kraja grada dotrča jedan čovjek – mjesto koje tefsir uzima kao قَرْيَة iz 36:13.
why.en: From the farthest end of the city a man came running — the place tafsir takes as the قَرْيَة of 36:13.

title.en: To die and to take the soul

shared.bs: Oba glagola govore o smrti; razlikuju se po tome ko je u središtu: onaj ko umire, ili Onaj (i meleki) koji dušu uzima.
shared.en: Both verbs speak of death; they differ in who is at the centre: the one who dies, or the One (and the angels) who takes the soul.

tellApart.bs: Umrijeti – subjekt je onaj ko umire → مَاتَ; uzeti dušu u potpunosti – subjekt je Allah, meleki ili smrt, a čovjek je trpni → تَوَفَّى.
tellApart.en: To die — the subject is the one who dies → مَاتَ; to take the soul in full — the subject is Allah, the angels or death, and the person is acted upon → تَوَفَّى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries موت, وفى
notes: ar-Rāġib: istīfāʾ (same root) is taking a thing in full; death and sleep are both expressed by tawaffī (6:60, 39:42) — attributed to him.
That the subject of تَوَفَّى in all 24 places is Allah, the angels or death, or the verb is passive, is our observation (all places read).
3:55 (mutawaffīka) and 5:117 (tawaffaytanī), about ʿĪsā, are not cited: tafsir differs on their meaning (sleep, being taken up, or death), and the participle in 3:55 is not filed under the verb.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries وفى, موت (2026-11-06): 3 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): He defines istīfāʾ, not tawaffī, as taking a thing in full; that death and sleep are both called tawaffī (6:60, 39:42) is his; members/1/nuance (reworded): 'Taking in full' is his gloss of istīfāʾ in the same root, not a definition of tawaffī; death and sleep being called tawaffī is his

nuance.bs: Umrijeti: subjekt je onaj ko umire. Opća riječ za smrt, i za ljude i za Poslanika – svako će umrijeti.
nuance.en: To die: the subject is the one who dies. The general word for death, of people and of the Prophet alike — everyone will die.

why.bs: „Pa zar ako umre ili bude ubijen…” – smrt Poslanika iskazana sa مَاتَ.
why.en: “So if he was to die or be killed…” — the Prophet's death expressed with مَاتَ.

why.bs: Merjem: „Kamo sreće da sam prije ovoga umrla!” – čovjek o svojoj smrti.
why.en: Mary: “Oh, I wish I had died before this” — a person speaking of her own death.

why.bs: Allah uzima duše kad umru (مَوْت), i one koje ne umru (لَمْ تَمُتْ) – u snu: oba glagola u jednom ajetu.
why.en: Allah takes the souls at death, and those that do not die (لَمْ تَمُتْ) during sleep — both verbs in one ayah.

meaning.bs: uzeti dušu (u smrti i u snu)
meaning.en: to take the soul (in death and in sleep)

nuance.bs: Iz korijena „uzeti nešto u potpunosti”; prema ar-Rāġibu, njime se izražavaju i smrt i san. Subjekt je Allah, meleki ili smrt; čovjek je onaj čija se duša uzima.
nuance.en: From the root of “taking a thing in full”; according to ar-Rāġib, death and sleep alike are expressed by it. The subject is Allah, the angels or death; the person is the one whose soul is taken.

why.bs: On vam noću uzima duše (يَتَوَفَّاكُم), u snu – تَوَفَّى i za san.
why.en: He takes your souls by night (in sleep) — تَوَفَّى said of sleep too.

why.bs: „Dušu će vam uzeti melek smrti” – melek kao subjekt.
why.en: “The angel of death will take you” — an angel as subject.

why.bs: „I daj nam da umremo s dobrima” – molba Allahu da On uzme dušu.
why.en: “And take us in death with the righteous” — asking Allah to take the soul.

title.en: To ask and to seek a ruling

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače „pitati”; razlikuju se po tome šta se traži: odgovor ili stvar uopće, ili rješenje nejasnog pitanja.
shared.en: Both verbs mean “to ask”; they differ in what is sought: an answer or a thing in general, or the resolution of an unclear question.

tellApart.bs: Pitati za bilo šta, ili tražiti nešto (i imetak) → سَأَلَ; pitati za rješenje nejasnog pitanja, tražiti fetvu, tumačenje → اِسْتَفْتَى.
tellApart.en: To ask about anything, or to ask for something (property too) → سَأَلَ; to ask for the answer to an unclear question, a ruling or an interpretation → اِسْتَفْتَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سأل, فتى
notes: ar-Rāġib: suʾāl is a request for knowledge (answered by tongue, or by writing) or for property (answered by hand) — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: futyā and fatwā are the answer to what is unclear in rulings; istaftā is asking for it — attributed to him.
اِسْتَفْتَى is used of a dream's interpretation (12:41) and of asking someone's opinion in argument (37:11, 18:22): our reading of all 6 places.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries سأل, فتى (2026-11-06): 4 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): His second kind of asking is a request for wealth (māl), not for any 'thing'

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, tražiti znanje ili tražiti imetak. Najopćija riječ za pitanje: od pitanja o mladom mjesecu do pitanja o samom Allahu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to ask for knowledge or to ask for wealth. The most general word for asking: from questions about the new moons to asking about Allah Himself.

why.bs: „Pitaju te o mlađacima” – pitanje radi znanja.
why.en: “They ask you about the new moons” — a question for knowledge.

why.bs: „Kad te robovi Moji upitaju o Meni, Ja sam zaista blizu.”
why.en: “When My servants ask you concerning Me — indeed I am near.”

why.bs: Ne prose od ljudi navaljujući – سَأَلَ kao traženje imetka.
why.en: They do not ask people persistently — سَأَلَ as asking for property.

meaning.en: to seek a ruling, to consult

nuance.bs: Tražiti odgovor na nejasno pitanje – fetvu u propisu, tumačenje sna ili mišljenje. Prema ar-Rāġibu, fetva je odgovor na ono što je nejasno u propisima.
nuance.en: To ask for the answer to an unclear question — a ruling, a dream's interpretation, or an opinion. According to ar-Rāġib, a fatwā is the answer to what is unclear in rulings.

why.bs: „Traže od tebe fetvu. Reci: ’Allah vam daje fetvu o kelali’” – pitanje o nasljedstvu.
why.en: “They request from you a ruling. Say, ’Allah gives you a ruling concerning kalālah’” — a question of inheritance.

why.bs: „Pitaju te o ženama. Reci: ’Allah vam o njima daje fetvu’” – propis koji odgovara na pitanje.
why.en: “They request from you a ruling concerning women. Say, ’Allah gives you a ruling about them’” — a ruling that answers the question.

why.bs: Jusuf zatvorenicima: „Riješeno je ono o čemu ste pitali” – tumačenje sna.
why.en: Joseph to the prisoners: “The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire” — a dream's interpretation.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače tražiti od nekoga da nešto čini; razlikuju se po tonu: zapovijed, ili brižna preporuka praćena savjetom.
shared.en: Both verbs mean asking someone to do something; they differ in tone: a command, or a caring charge joined with counsel.

tellApart.bs: Narediti, zapovjediti – i dobro i zlo → أَمَرَ; oporučiti, preporučiti uz savjet i brigu, nešto što treba trajno čuvati → وَصَّى.
tellApart.en: To command, to order — good or evil → أَمَرَ; to enjoin, to charge with counsel and care, something to be kept for good → وَصَّى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أمر, وصى
notes: ar-Rāġib: waṣiyya is directing another to something to be acted on, joined with admonition — attributed to him.
That وَصَّى in the Quran is said of what is to be kept across generations (2:132, 42:13) and of the core commandments (6:151–153) is our reading of its 10 places.
Form IV أَوْصَى (يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ, 4:11) is a separate verb in the catalogue and not a member.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Narediti, tražiti da se nešto učini. Kaže se za Allahove naredbe, ali i za ljude i šejtana koji naređuju zlo.
nuance.en: To command, to require something to be done. Said of Allah's commands, but also of people and of Satan commanding evil.

why.bs: „Allah naređuje pravednost i dobročinstvo” – Allahova naredba.
why.en: “Allah orders justice and good conduct” — Allah's command.

why.bs: „Allah vam naređuje da zakoljete kravu” – jasna, određena naredba.
why.en: “Allah commands you to slaughter a cow” — a plain, specific command.

why.bs: „Allah ne naređuje razvrat” – أَمَرَ o onome što ljudi pogrešno pripisuju Allahu.
why.en: “Allah does not order immorality” — أَمَرَ of what people wrongly ascribe to Allah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, uputiti nekoga na ono što treba činiti, uz opomenu i savjet. Zato وَصَّى stoji uz ono što se predaje u amanet: vjeru koju otac ostavlja sinovima, dobročinstvo prema roditeljima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, directing someone to what is to be done, joined with admonition. So وَصَّى stands with what is handed on in trust: the faith a father leaves his sons, kindness to parents.

why.bs: Ibrahim je to oporučio sinovima svojim, i Jakub – vjera predana u amanet.
why.en: Abraham instructed his sons with it, and so did Jacob — faith handed on in trust.

why.bs: „Naložili smo čovjeku da dobro postupa s roditeljima” – trajna preporuka.
why.en: “We have enjoined upon man goodness to parents” — a lasting charge.

why.bs: Nakon niza zapovijedi i zabrana: „To vam On preporučuje” – sažetak uz brigu i savjet.
why.en: After a series of commands and prohibitions: “This has He instructed you” — a summary given with care and counsel.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače „zabraniti”; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu čin odvraćanja ili proglašavanje nečega nedozvoljenim.
shared.en: Both verbs mean “to forbid”; they differ in whether the act of restraining or the declaring of a thing unlawful is in view.

tellApart.bs: Zabraniti, odvratiti nekoga od djela – reći mu „nemoj” → نَهَى; učiniti nešto haram, nedozvoljenim, ili uskratiti → حَرَّمَ.
tellApart.en: To forbid, to hold someone back from a deed — to tell him “do not” → نَهَى; to make a thing ḥarām, unlawful, or to withhold it → حَرَّمَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نهى, حرم
notes: ar-Rāġib: nahy is restraining from a thing; ḥarām is what is withheld, and taḥrīm may be by Allah's decree in creation (taskhīr, 28:12), by a human, or by the sharīʿa — attributed to him.
That people are reproached in the Quran for ḥarrama without authority (6:140, 7:32) is read from the ayat.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, odvratiti od nečega. نَهَى je obraćanje osobi: „ne čini”. Zabranjuje Allah, Poslanik, ali i ljudi – i dobro i zlo.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, restraining from a thing. نَهَى is addressed to a person: “do not”. Allah forbids, the Messenger forbids, and people forbid too — good and evil alike.

why.bs: „Što vam zabrani, toga se okanite” – zabrana Poslanika.
why.en: “What he has forbidden you — refrain from” — the Messenger's prohibition.

why.bs: Šejtan: „Gospodar vaš vam je zabranio ovo drvo samo zato…” – zabrana upućena Ademu i njegovoj ženi.
why.en: Satan: “Your Lord did not forbid you this tree except…” — a prohibition addressed to Adam and his wife.

why.bs: Onaj ko zabranjuje – čak i robu dok klanja (96:10) – نَهَى i za zlu zabranu.
why.en: The one who forbids — even a servant at prayer (96:10) — نَهَى for a wicked prohibition too.

nuance.bs: Proglasiti nešto haramom, nedozvoljenim – propis koji važi, a ne samo zabrana upućena osobi. Prema ar-Rāġibu, uskraćivanje može biti i Allahovom odredbom u stvaranju: Musa nije htio uzeti prsa nijedne dojilje.
nuance.en: To declare a thing ḥarām, unlawful — a standing ruling, not only a prohibition addressed to a person. According to ar-Rāġib, withholding may also be by Allah's decree in creation: the infant Moses would take no wet-nurse.

why.bs: „Reci: ’Ko je zabranio Allahove ukrase?’” – ukor onima koji haramom proglašavaju bez prava.
why.en: “Say, ’Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah?’” — reproach for declaring things unlawful without right.

why.bs: „Mi smo mu prije zabranili dojilje” – taḥrīm kao Allahova odredba, ne propis.
why.en: “We had prevented from him all wet nurses before” — taḥrīm as Allah's decree, not a law.

why.bs: „Dođite da vam kažem šta vam je Gospodar vaš zabranio” – haram kao propis.
why.en: “Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you” — ḥarām as a ruling.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače „ostaviti”; razlikuju se po obliku i tonu: ostavljanje uopće, ili ostavljanje onoga čemu se ne pridaje vrijednost.
shared.en: Both verbs mean “to leave”; they differ in form and tone: leaving in general, or leaving what one sets no store by.

tellApart.bs: Ostaviti, napustiti – svojevoljno ili prisilno; ostaviti iza sebe nasljedstvo → تَرَكَ; pustiti, okaniti se, „ostavi ih” – samo u sadašnjem vremenu i imperativu → وَذَرَ.
tellApart.en: To leave, abandon — by choice or by force; to leave an inheritance behind → تَرَكَ; to let be, give up, “leave them” — only in present and imperative → وَذَرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ترك, وذر
notes: ar-Rāġib: tark is rejecting a thing, intentionally and by choice, or by force and necessity — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: one says yadharu ash-shayʾ, 'he leaves the thing', i.e. casts it off for setting little store by it, and its past tense is not used — attributed to him.
That وَذَرَ appears in the Quran only in the present and the imperative (all 45 uses) is our observation; the headword وَذَرَ is the dictionary form.
74:11 (dharnī, 'leave Me with him') is not cited: it is an ayah of threat whose tafsir needs more room than a line.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, odbaciti nešto namjerno i svojevoljno, ili prisilno. Kaže se i za ono što umrli ostavi iza sebe.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to reject a thing intentionally and by choice, or by force and necessity. Said too of what the dead leave behind.

why.bs: Jusuf: „Ja sam napustio vjeru naroda koji ne vjeruje u Allaha” – svojevoljno napuštanje.
why.en: Joseph: “I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah” — leaving by choice.

why.bs: Koliko su samo vrtova i izvora ostavili! – ostavljanje prisilno, propašću.
why.en: How much they left behind of gardens and springs — leaving by force, in ruin.

why.bs: Muškarcima pripada dio onoga što ostave roditelji – تَرَكَ za nasljedstvo.
why.en: For men is a share of what the parents leave — تَرَكَ for inheritance.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ostaviti nešto kao da ga odbacuješ jer mu ne pridaješ vrijednost; prošlo vrijeme se, kaže, ne koristi – u Kur'anu se javlja samo u sadašnjem vremenu i imperativu (ذَرْ, ذَرُوا).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to leave a thing as if casting it off, setting little store by it; its past tense, he says, is not used — in the Quran it occurs only in present and imperative (ذَرْ, ذَرُوا).

why.bs: Kad se pozove na džumu, „ostavite kupoprodaju” – ostavite ono što je inače dozvoljeno.
why.en: When the call is made for Jumuʿah, “leave trade” — set aside what is otherwise permitted.

why.bs: „Okanite se ostatka kamate” – odreknite se potraživanja, jer je tako naređeno.
why.en: “Give up what remains due to you of interest” — give up a claim, set aside at Allah's command.

why.bs: „Zatim ih ostavi neka se zabavljaju svojim pričama” – pusti ih.
why.en: “Then leave them in their empty discourse, amusing themselves” — let them be.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače „sakupiti”; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu samo spajanje ili izvođenje i tjeranje mnoštva na jedno mjesto.
shared.en: Both verbs mean “to gather”; they differ in whether mere bringing together or driving a multitude out to one place is in view.

tellApart.bs: Sakupiti, spojiti – stvari, imetak, ljude → جَمَعَ; okupiti mnoštvo izvodeći ga i goneći na jedno mjesto – i na Sudnji dan → حَشَرَ.
tellApart.en: To gather, bring together — things, wealth, people → جَمَعَ; to assemble a multitude by bringing it out and driving it to one place — the Day of Judgement too → حَشَرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries جمع, حشر
notes: ar-Rāġib: jamʿ is bringing a thing together by drawing its parts close; ḥashr is bringing a group out of where they settled and driving them to war and the like, and is said only of a group — attributed to him.
20:124–125 (wa-naḥshuruhu … ḥashartanī aʿmā) use حَشَرَ of one person (both ayat) on the Day of Judgement: shown beside ar-Rāġib's rule as a counter-example.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, sakupiti stvar približavajući njene dijelove jedan drugom. Kaže se za kosti, za imetak, za spletke – i za sakupljanje ljudi na Sudnjem danu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, bringing a thing together by drawing its parts close. Said of bones, of wealth, of schemes — and of gathering people on the Day of Judgement.

why.bs: „Zar čovjek misli da kosti njegove nećemo sakupiti?” – spajanje dijelova.
why.en: “Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?” — bringing parts together.

why.bs: Onaj ko gomila imetak i prebrojava ga – جَمَعَ za imetak.
why.en: Who collects wealth and counts it — جَمَعَ for wealth.

why.bs: „Na Dan kada vas sakupi za Dan sakupljanja” – i جَمَعَ se kaže za Sudnji dan.
why.en: “The Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly” — جَمَعَ is said of the Last Day too.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, izvesti skupinu ljudi s njihovog mjesta i potjerati ih (u boj i sl.), i kaže se samo za skupinu. U Kur'anu je najčešće sabiranje na Sudnjem danu; kaže se i za pojedinca (20:124–125).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to bring a group out of their place and drive them on (to battle and the like), said only of a group. In the Quran most often the mustering on the Day of Judgement; it is also said of a single person (20:124–125).

why.bs: Musa: „i neka se ljudi skupe u pretpodne” – okupljanje mnoštva na jedno mjesto.
why.en: Moses: “and that the people be gathered at mid-morning” — a multitude brought to one place.

why.bs: „Kad divlje životinje budu sabrane” – mnoštvo dovedeno na jedno mjesto.
why.en: “And when the wild beasts are gathered” — a multitude brought to one place.

why.bs: „Gospodaru moj, zašto si me slijepim oživio (حَشَرْتَنِي)?” – حَشَرَ za pojedinca, protivprimjer pravilu.
why.en: “My Lord, why have You raised me blind?” (حَشَرْتَنِي) — حَشَرَ of one person, a counter-example to the rule.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače „uništiti”; razlikuju se po širini: propast u svakom obliku, ili potpuno zatiranje.
shared.en: Both verbs mean “to destroy”; they differ in breadth: perishing in any form, or utter destruction.

tellApart.bs: Uništiti, upropastiti – narode, ali i usjeve, imetak → أَهْلَكَ; zatrti, razoriti do temelja → دَمَّرَ.
tellApart.en: To destroy, cause to perish — peoples, but also crops and wealth → أَهْلَكَ; to wipe out, raze to the ground → دَمَّرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries هلك, دمر
notes: ar-Rāġib: halāk is used in several senses — loss of a thing, its corruption, death, and passing away altogether — attributed to him.

That دَمَّرَ is said in 7 of its 8 places of Allah's destruction of peoples and their works, and once of the wind 'by the command of its Lord' (46:25), and that its doubled form and the cognate accusative (17:16 tadmīran) stress completeness, is our observation, not a lexicographer's wording.
17:16 has both verbs: nuhlika then dammarnāhā.

meaning.en: to destroy, to cause to perish

nuance.bs: Uništiti, dovesti do propasti. Najčešće o narodima koje je Allah uništio zbog njihovih grijeha, ali i o čovjeku koji upropaštava usjeve ili imetak.
nuance.en: To destroy, bring to ruin. Most often of peoples Allah destroyed for their sins, but also of a man who ruins crops or squanders wealth.

why.bs: „Zar ne vide koliko smo naroda prije njih uništili?”
why.en: “Have they not considered how many generations We destroyed before them?”

why.bs: Kad se okrene (ili: kad dođe na vlast – tefsir se razilazi), nastoji da uništi usjeve i porod – čovjek kao uzrok propasti.
why.en: When he turns away (or: gains authority — tafsir differs), he strives to destroy crops and offspring — a man as the cause of ruin.

why.bs: „Uludo sam potrošio silno blago” – أَهْلَكَ i za rasipanje imetka.
why.en: “I have squandered wealth in abundance” — أَهْلَكَ also of squandering wealth.

nuance.bs: Uništiti potpuno, ne ostaviti ništa. U Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) gotovo uvijek o Allahovom kažnjavanju naroda i njihovih djela; jednom o vjetru koji uništava „Gospodarevom voljom”.
nuance.en: To destroy completely, leaving nothing. In the Quran (our observation) almost always of Allah's punishment of peoples and their works; once of the wind that destroys “by command of its Lord”.

why.bs: Kad hoćemo da uništimo (نُهْلِكَ) neki grad… pa ga potpuno zatremo (دَمَّرْنَاهَا تَدْمِيرًا) – oba glagola, drugi kao vrhunac.
why.en: When We intend to destroy (نُهْلِكَ) a city… and We destroy it with complete destruction (دَمَّرْنَاهَا تَدْمِيرًا) — both verbs, the second as the climax.

why.bs: „I razorili smo ono što su faraon i njegov narod gradili” – zatiranje djela.
why.en: “We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people were producing” — wiping out works.

why.bs: Vjetar „koji će sve uništiti Gospodarevom voljom” – jedini subjekt koji nije Allah, a i on po Njegovoj naredbi.
why.en: A wind “destroying everything by command of its Lord” — the one subject other than Allah, and that by His command.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače „steći, zaraditi” – i dobra i loša djela; razlikuju se po uloženom naporu i po tome za koga se stiče.
shared.en: Both verbs mean “to earn, to gain” — good deeds and bad; they differ in the effort involved and in for whom the gain is made.

tellApart.bs: Steći, zaraditi uopće – imetak, dobro ili zlo → كَسَبَ; steći za sebe (tefsir: s naporom) → اِكْتَسَبَ.
tellApart.en: To earn, gain in general — wealth, good or evil → كَسَبَ; to acquire for oneself (tafsir: with effort) → اِكْتَسَبَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كسب
notes: ar-Rāġib: kasb is what a person seeks to gain benefit and a share by; iktisāb is said only of what one gains for oneself, so every iktisāb is kasb but not every kasb is iktisāb; he cites 2:286 — attributed to him.

On 2:286 tafsir often explains why good is with kasabat and evil with iktasabat: the Form VIII stresses effort, and the soul strives harder after evil it desires. Given as the explanation of many mufassirun, not pinned to one; some treat the variation as stylistic only. 'Form VIII stresses effort' is theirs, not ar-Rāġib's (blind review).
4:32 (iktasabū / iktasabna, of men's and women's earnings) shows اِكْتَسَبَ used for what is not evil; so the 2:286 contrast is not a rule of the word.
اِكْتَسَبَ: 5 uses in 4 ayat.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono čime čovjek nastoji steći korist i udio. Opća riječ: zarađeni imetak, dobra djela i grijesi – sve što čovjek „zaradi”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what a person seeks to gain benefit and a share by. The general word: earned wealth, good deeds and sins — all that a person “earns”.

why.bs: „Njoj pripada ono što je zaradila (كَسَبَتْ), a na nju se odnosi ono što je stekla (اكْتَسَبَتْ)” – oba glagola.
why.en: “It will have what it has gained (كَسَبَتْ), and it will bear what it has earned (اكْتَسَبَتْ)” — both verbs.

why.bs: „Neće mu koristiti imetak njegov, ni ono što je stekao” – zarada, imetak.
why.en: “His wealth will not avail him or that which he gained” — earnings, wealth.

why.bs: „Onaj ko zlo zaradi” – كَسَبَ i za zlo.
why.en: “Whoever earns evil” — كَسَبَ for evil too.

meaning.en: to acquire, to earn for oneself

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, kaže se samo za ono što čovjek stiče za sebe. Mnogi mufessiri dodaju da oblik VIII podrazumijeva napor i time tumače 2:286, mada to ne prihvataju svi, a u 4:32 riječ je o dozvoljenoj zaradi muškaraca i žena.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, said only of what a person gains for himself. Many mufassirun add that Form VIII implies effort and explain 2:286 by it, though not all accept this, and 4:32 uses it for the lawful earnings of men and women.

why.bs: اكْتَسَبَتْ uz ono čime je duša opterećena – prema mnogim mufessirima: napor koji duša ulaže u ono što je privlači.
why.en: اكْتَسَبَتْ with what the soul bears — according to many mufassirun: the effort a soul spends on what draws it.

why.bs: Muškarcima pripada udio od onoga što zarade, i ženama od onoga što zarade – اِكْتَسَبَ bez ikakvog prizvuka zla.
why.en: For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women a share of what they have earned — اِكْتَسَبَ with no shade of evil.

why.bs: Svakom od njih – grijeh koji je stekao – اِكْتَسَبَ za lično stečen grijeh.
why.en: For every person among them is what he has earned of the sin — اِكْتَسَبَ for a sin acquired in person.

shared.bs: Obje riječi označavaju čovjeka u oskudici i obje su među primaocima zekata (9:60); učenjaci se razilaze ko je od njih u većoj nevolji.
shared.en: Both words denote a person in want and both are among the recipients of zakat (9:60); scholars differ over which of the two is in greater need.

tellApart.bs: Siromah, onaj ko je u potrebi – i čovjek u potrebi prema Allahu → فَقِير; nevoljnik, potrebit, najčešće uz siroče i putnika kao onaj koga treba nahraniti → مِسْكِين; ko je od njih u većoj nevolji, učenjaci se razilaze.
tellApart.en: The poor, one in need — and man in his need of Allah → فَقِير; the needy, most often named with the orphan and traveller as one to be fed → مِسْكِين; which is worse off, scholars differ.

sources: Tafsir and fiqh on 9:60 (e.g. al-Qurṭubī, al-Jāmiʿ li-aḥkām al-Qurʾān) — the views on faqīr and miskīn
notes: Scholars differ: in the Shāfiʿī view the faqīr is worse off (cf. 18:79, masākīn who own a boat); in the Ḥanafī view the miskīn is (cf. 90:16, miskīnan ḏā matraba, 'in the dust'). Both views and their proof ayat are given; neither is chosen.
That فَقِير is also said of man's need before Allah (35:15) and of Musa's prayer (28:24), while مِسْكِين is not used that way, is our observation of all places.
فَقِير includes the plural فُقَرَاء and مِسْكِين the plural مَسَاكِين: one lemma each in the corpus.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Onaj ko je u potrebi, kome nešto nedostaje. Kaže se i za čovjekovu potrebu prema Allahu: svi su ljudi „siromasi” pred Allahom, a Musa je za sebe rekao da je فَقِير dobra koje mu Allah spusti.
nuance.en: One in need, who lacks something. Said too of man's need of Allah: all people are “poor” before Allah, and Moses called himself فَقِير of whatever good Allah sends down.

why.bs: Zekat pripada siromasima (فُقَرَاء) i nevoljnicima (مَسَاكِين) – obje riječi, kao dvije skupine.
why.en: Zakat is for the poor (فُقَرَاء) and the needy (مَسَاكِين) — both words, as two groups.

why.bs: „O ljudi, vi ste Allahu potrebni, a Allah je Neovisni” – potreba svakog stvorenja.
why.en: “O mankind, you are those in need of Allah, while Allah is the Free of need” — the need of every creature.

why.bs: Siromasi koji ne dosađuju ljudima traženjem; zbog njihove suzdržanosti neupućeni ih smatraju bogatima.
why.en: The poor who do not ask people persistently; because of their restraint the ignorant think them self-sufficient.

nuance.bs: Potrebit, u oskudici; često se spominje uz siroče i putnika kao onaj kome treba dati hranu. Učenjaci se razilaze je li u većoj nevolji od فَقِير.
nuance.en: One in want; often named with the orphan and the traveller as one to be fed. Scholars differ on whether he is in greater need than the فَقِير.

why.bs: Lađa je pripadala nekim siromasima (مَسَاكِين) – imaju lađu, a ipak su مِسْكِين: dokaz onih koji kažu da je فَقِير u većoj nevolji.
why.en: The ship belonged to poor people (مَسَاكِين) — they own a ship yet are مِسْكِين: the proof of those who hold the faqīr worse off.

why.bs: „Ili nevoljnika bez igdje ičega” (ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ) – dokaz onih koji kažu da je مِسْكِين u većoj nevolji.
why.en: “Or a needy person in misery” (ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ) — the proof of those who hold the miskīn worse off.

why.bs: Onaj ko ne podstiče da se nahrani siromah – مِسْكِين kao onaj kome treba hrana.
why.en: Who does not encourage the feeding of the poor — the مِسْكِين as one who must be fed.

shared.bs: Obje riječi označavaju onoga ko je uz tebe i stoji za tebe; u Kur'anu često stoje jedna uz drugu, a razlikuju se po vrsti podrške.
shared.en: Both words denote one who is on your side and stands up for you; in the Quran they often stand together, and they differ in the kind of support.

tellApart.bs: Bliski zaštitnik, onaj ko se brine o tvojim poslovima, prijatelj, srodnik → وَلِيّ; pomagač koji pomaže protiv neprijatelja i daje pobjedu → نَصِير.
tellApart.en: A close protector, one who takes charge of your affairs, a friend, a kinsman → وَلِيّ; a helper who aids against an enemy and gives victory → نَصِير.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ولى, نصر
notes: ar-Rāġib: walāʾ is two or more things being so close that nothing comes between them, used of nearness in place, kinship, religion, friendship, help and belief — attributed to him.
That walī is the one who takes care of one's affairs and naṣīr the one who aids against an enemy is how tafsir often explains the pair; stated as such, not pinned to one mufassir.
That the two often stand together (2:107, 4:45, 9:116) is read from the ayat.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ولى (2026-11-06): 4 attributed points confirmed
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): نصر read and added to `verified` (consistent with the texts; no attributed point rests on it).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od bliskosti u kojoj ništa ne stoji između dvoje. Zato وَلِيّ znači zaštitnika, prijatelja, saveznika i najbližeg srodnika – onoga ko preuzima brigu o tebi.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from a nearness with nothing between the two. So وَلِيّ means protector, friend, ally and nearest kinsman — one who takes charge of you.

why.bs: „Allah je zaštitnik onih koji vjeruju; izvodi ih iz tmina na svjetlo” – Allahova briga o vjernicima.
why.en: “Allah is the ally of those who believe; He brings them out from darknesses into the light” — Allah's care for the believers.

why.bs: Ako neko bude ubijen nepravedno, njegovom bliskom srodniku (وَلِيّ), staratelju njegovog prava, dali smo vlast.
why.en: Whoever is killed unjustly — We have given his nearest kinsman (وَلِيّ), the guardian of his right, authority.

why.bs: „Mimo Allaha nemate zaštitnika ni pomagača” – وَلِيّ i نَصِير zajedno.
why.en: “You have not besides Allah any protector or any helper” — وَلِيّ and نَصِير together.

nuance.bs: Onaj ko pomaže i daje pobjedu (نَصْر) protiv neprijatelja ili nevolje. Često stoji odmah iza وَلِيّ ili مَوْلَى.
nuance.en: One who helps and gives victory (نَصْر) against an enemy or a hardship. It often comes right after وَلِيّ or مَوْلَى.

why.bs: „Allah je dovoljan zaštitnik i Allah je dovoljan pomagač.”
why.en: “Sufficient is Allah as an ally, and sufficient is Allah as a helper.”

why.bs: „Divan je On zaštitnik i divan pomagač!” – مَوْلَى i نَصِير.
why.en: “Excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper” — مَوْلَى and نَصِير.

why.bs: Isti ajet: zaštitnik koji se brine, pomagač koji brani.
why.en: The same ayah: a protector who takes care, a helper who defends.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače sumnju; obično se razlikuju po tome je li to puko kolebanje između dvije mogućnosti ili sumnja praćena nemirom i nepovjerenjem.
shared.en: Both words mean doubt; they tend to differ in whether it is a bare wavering between two possibilities or doubt that brings unease and suspicion.

tellApart.bs: Kolebanje između dvije mogućnosti, bez prevage → شَكّ; sumnja s nemirom i nepovjerenjem – „nema sumnje u nju” → رَيْب.
tellApart.en: Wavering between two possibilities with no preponderance → شَكّ; doubt with unease and suspicion — “no doubt about it” → رَيْب.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries شكك
Tafsir on 2:2 — the sense of rayb
notes: ar-Rāġib: shakk is two opposites being equal in a person's mind, with no sign tipping towards either — attributed to him.

That rayb is doubt joined with unease and suspicion is how tafsir often explains it on 2:2; stated as such. ar-Rāġib's own definition differs: rayb is imagining something about a thing that is then uncovered (entry ريب).
The two meet in 11:62 and 34:54 (shakk … murīb), where murīb is from the root of rayb; cited under شَكّ.
52:30 rayb al-manūn: tafsir explains it as the accidents of time, or death; given as tafsir.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries شكك, ريب (2026-11-06): 3 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/1 (improved): He does not speak of unease: he defines rayb as suspecting something in a thing that is then uncovered, and rība as a sign of rancour and little certainty
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (شك → شكك).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, stanje kada su dvije suprotne mogućnosti u čovjekovom umu jednake i nijedna ne preteže. Često se opisuje kao „sumnja koja uznemiruje” (مُرِيب).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the state in which two opposites are equal in the mind and neither tips the scale. Often described as a doubt “that disquiets” (مُرِيب).

why.bs: „Zar u Allaha ima sumnje, Stvoritelja nebesa i Zemlje?”
why.en: “Can there be doubt about Allah, Creator of the heavens and earth?”

why.bs: „Mi smo u sumnji koja uznemiruje” (شَكّ مُرِيب) – obje riječi: شَكّ i pridjev iz korijena رَيْب.
why.en: “We are in disquieting doubt” (شَكّ مُرِيب) — both: شَكّ and an adjective from the root of رَيْب.

why.bs: „Ako si u sumnji u ono što ti objavljujemo…” – uvjetna rečenica; prema većini mufessira ne podrazumijeva stvarnu sumnju kod Poslanika.
why.en: “If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you…” — a conditional; most mufassirun hold it implies no actual doubt in the Prophet.

nuance.bs: Sumnja praćena nemirom i nepovjerenjem; tako je često tumači tefsir na početku sure el-Bekara. Kur'an njome kaže da u Knjigu i u Sudnji dan „nema sumnje”.
nuance.en: Doubt joined with unease and suspicion; so tafsir often explains it at the opening of al-Baqarah. The Quran uses it to say there is “no doubt” about the Book and the Last Day.

why.bs: „Ova Knjiga, u nju nema sumnje” – prvo što Kur'an kaže o sebi.
why.en: “This is the Book about which there is no doubt” — the first thing the Quran says of itself.

why.bs: „Ako sumnjate u proživljenje…” – رَيْب o ahiretu, a odmah zatim dokaz.
why.en: “If you should be in doubt about the Resurrection…” — رَيْب about the hereafter, followed at once by proof.

why.bs: „Čekamo da ga zadesi nesreća” (رَيْب الْمَنُون) – ovdje رَيْب znači nedaću, ne sumnju; tefsir: nedaće vremena ili smrt.
why.en: “We await for him misfortune of time” (رَيْب الْمَنُون) — here رَيْب means a calamity, not doubt; tafsir: the accidents of time, or death.

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola govore o opraštanju grijeha; razlikuju se po slici: prekrivanje i zaštita, brisanje i odustajanje od kazne, ili pokrivanje grijeha kao da nije učinjen.
shared.en: All three verbs speak of forgiving sins; they differ in the image: covering and shielding, erasing and forgoing the penalty, or covering the sin as though it were not done.

tellApart.bs: Oprostiti i zaštititi od kazne → غَفَرَ; preći preko, ne kazniti – Allahov oprost, a često i oprost među ljudima (u odmazdi, mehru, uvredi) → عَفَا; izbrisati, pokriti loša djela → كَفَّرَ.
tellApart.en: To forgive and shield from punishment → غَفَرَ; to pardon, let pass unpunished — Allah's pardon, and often pardon between people (in retaliation, bridal due, offence) → عَفَا; to remove, cover over bad deeds → كَفَّرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries غفر, عفا, كفر
notes: ar-Rāġib: ghafr is clothing a thing with what shields it from dirt (hence mighfar, the helmet); maghfira from Allah is His shielding the servant from punishment — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: takfīr of a sin is covering it until it is as if it had not been done — attributed to him.
That ʿafw is from ʿafā, 'to efface' (as wind effaces a trace) is a common explanation in tafsir; given as such. Which of maghfira and ʿafw is the greater is not decided here: tafsir differs.
The ordering in 2:286 (wa-ʿfu ʿannā wa-ghfir lanā) is cited as it stands, without a claim about why.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries غفر, كفر (2026-11-06): 8 attributed points confirmed
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): عفا read and added to `verified` (consistent with the texts; no attributed point rests on it).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnovno značenje je prekriti onim što štiti (odatle مِغْفَر, kaciga); Allahov oprost je da roba zaštiti od kazne. Kaže se i za ljude koji praštaju.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root sense is covering with what shields (hence مِغْفَر, the helmet); Allah's forgiveness is shielding the servant from punishment. Said also of people who forgive.

why.bs: „Allah će sigurno sve grijehe oprostiti” – tefsir ga čita sa sljedećim ajetom: onima koji Mu se vrate (usp. 4:48).
why.en: “Allah forgives all sins” — tafsir reads it with the next ayah: for those who turn back to Him (cf. 4:48).

why.bs: Allah neće oprostiti da Mu se pridružuju druga božanstva (širk), a manje od toga oprostit će kome hoće.
why.en: Allah does not forgive association with Him, but forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.

why.bs: „Reci vjernicima neka oproste” – غَفَرَ među ljudima.
why.en: “Say to those who believe to forgive” — غَفَرَ between people.

nuance.bs: Preći preko grijeha, ne kazniti za njega; u tefsiru se veže za „brisanje” traga. Često o ljudima među sobom: oprost u odmazdi, u mehru, u uvredi.
nuance.en: To pass over a sin, to forgo its penalty; tafsir links it to “effacing” a trace. Often of people among themselves: pardon in retaliation, in the bridal due, in an offence.

why.bs: „Pređi preko naših grijeha, oprosti nam i smiluj nam se” – عَفَا i غَفَرَ jedno uz drugo.
why.en: “Pardon us, forgive us and have mercy upon us” — عَفَا and غَفَرَ side by side.

why.bs: „Neka oproste i neka preko toga pređu” – oprost među ljudima.
why.en: “Let them pardon and overlook” — pardon between people.

why.bs: Nesreće vas pogađaju zbog onoga što činite, a On mnogo prašta (يَعْفُو).
why.en: Disaster strikes you for what your hands have earned, but He pardons much (يَعْفُو).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, pokriti grijeh dok ne postane kao da nije učinjen. Objekt su gotovo uvijek „loša djela” (سَيِّئَات); iz istog je korijena كَفَّارَة, iskup.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, covering a sin until it is as though it were not done. Its object is almost always “bad deeds” (سَيِّئَات); from the same root is كَفَّارَة, expiation.

why.bs: Ako se klonite velikih grijeha, izbrisat ćemo vam loša djela (prema većini mufessira: manje grijehe) – كَفَّرَ za loša djela.
why.en: If you avoid the major sins, We will remove from you your misdeeds (most mufassirun: the lesser sins) — كَفَّرَ for bad deeds.

why.bs: „Sigurno ću im izbrisati loša djela njihova i uvesti ih u dženetske bašče.”
why.en: “I will surely remove from them their misdeeds and admit them to gardens.”

why.bs: Iskreno pokajanje – nada da će Gospodar izbrisati loša djela.
why.en: Sincere repentance — the hope that your Lord will remove your misdeeds.

title.en: To repent and to turn back

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače vratiti se Allahu; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu ostavljanje grijeha ili stalno okretanje Allahu srcem i djelom.
shared.en: Both verbs mean returning to Allah; they differ in whether leaving the sin or a constant turning to Allah in heart and deed is in view.

tellApart.bs: Pokajati se, ostaviti grijeh – i Allahovo primanje pokajanja (تَابَ عَلَى) → تَابَ; obraćati se Allahu, vraćati se Njemu iskreno, i bez spomena grijeha → أَنَابَ.
tellApart.en: To repent, leave the sin — and Allah's accepting it (تَابَ عَلَى) → تَابَ; to turn to Allah, return to Him sincerely, even with no sin in view → أَنَابَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries توب, نوب
notes: ar-Rāġib: tawb is leaving a sin in the best way, the most eloquent form of apology; when Allah is said to tāba ʿalā someone, He accepts his repentance — attributed to him.
ar-Rāġib: ināba to Allah is returning to Him with repentance and sincerity of deed — attributed to him.
That أَنَابَ is never said of Allah in the Quran (all 11 uses have a human subject) while تَابَ is said of both, is our observation.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries توب, نوب (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ostaviti grijeh na najljepši način. Isti glagol se kaže i za Allaha – تَابَ عَلَيْهِ: primio je njegovo pokajanje, okrenuo mu se milošću.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, leaving a sin in the finest way. The same verb is said of Allah — تَابَ عَلَيْهِ: He accepted his repentance, turned to him in mercy.

why.bs: „Zatim im je oprostio da bi se pokajali” – تَابَ za Allaha i za ljude u istom ajetu.
why.en: “Then He turned to them so they could repent” — تَابَ of Allah and of people in one ayah.

why.bs: Adem je primio riječi od Gospodara, pa mu je On oprostio – Allahovo primanje pokajanja.
why.en: Adam received words from his Lord, and He accepted his repentance.

why.bs: Ko se pokaje i čini dobro, on se Allahu istinski vraća – pokajanje uz dobro djelo.
why.en: Whoever repents and does righteousness does indeed turn to Allah with a true turning — repentance with good deeds.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, vraćanje Allahu pokajanjem i iskrenim djelom. Kaže se i bez spomena grijeha – kao stalno okretanje Allahu; nikad za Allaha (naše zapažanje).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, returning to Allah with repentance and sincere deeds. Said also with no sin in view — as a constant turning to Allah; never of Allah (our observation).

why.bs: Davud je pao ničice i Allahu se obratio – vraćanje poslije iskušenja.
why.en: David fell down bowing and turned in repentance — returning after a trial.

why.bs: „Obratite se Gospodaru svome i pokorite Mu se prije nego što vam dođe kazna.”
why.en: “Return to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you.”

why.bs: Šuajb: „Samo se na Njega oslanjam i samo Njemu se obraćam” – okretanje Allahu bez spomena grijeha.
why.en: Shuʿayb: “Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I return” — turning to Allah with no sin in view.

shared.bs: Obje riječi se mogu prevesti s „otac”; razlikuju se po tome je li u prvom planu očinstvo u širem smislu ili rađanje.
shared.en: Both words can be rendered “father”; they differ in whether fatherhood in a wider sense or begetting is in view.

tellApart.bs: Otac, i djed, predak, pa i amidža – očevi kao predaja koja se slijedi → أَب; roditelj koji je rodio, najčešće „oba roditelja” kojima se čini dobro → وَالِد.
tellApart.en: Father, also grandfather, forefather, even an uncle — the fathers as a tradition followed → أَب; the parent who begot, most often “both parents” to be treated well → وَالِد.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أبا, ولد
notes: ar-Rāġib: ab is the father, and anyone who is a cause of bringing a thing into being, reforming it or making it appear is called ab; the uncle is called ab with the father, citing 2:133 where Ismāʿīl is counted among Yaʿqūb's fathers though he was his uncle — attributed to him.
أَب: the corpus files the broken plural آبَاء (64) and the dual أَبَوَان (7) separately; counted together with أَب (46): 117.
وَالِد: the corpus files the dual with suffix (وَالِدَيْهِ, 10) as a lemma of its own beside وَالِد (14); counted together: 24.
12:100 abawayhi: tafsir differs on whether this is his father and mother (if she was still alive) or his father and maternal aunt; stated so.
90:3 wa-wālidin wa-mā walad: tafsir differs (Ādam and his offspring, or every begetter and what he begets); stated so.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries أبا (2026-11-06): 5 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): His examples of the 'cause' sense are the Prophet and the teacher; grandfather and uncle are called ab only when paired with the father (2:133)
Sources normalised (2026-11-06): entries cited as the book spells them (أب → أبا); ولد read and added to `verified` (consistent with the texts; no attributed point rests on it).

nuance.bs: Otac; prema ar-Rāġibu, i svako ko je uzrok nastanka ili popravka nečega; a uz oca se i djed, pa i amidža, ubrajaju među očeve (2:133). U množini (آبَاء) često „preci” čiju predaju ljudi slijede.
nuance.en: Father; according to ar-Rāġib, also anyone who is a cause of a thing's coming to be or its betterment; and alongside the father, a grandfather or even an uncle is counted among one's fathers (2:133). In the plural (آبَاء) often the “forefathers” whose way people follow.

why.bs: „Tvome Bogu i Bogu tvojih predaka Ibrahima, Ismaila i Ishaka” – Ismail, Jakubov amidža, među „očevima”.
why.en: “Your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac” — Ishmael, Jacob's uncle, among the “fathers”.

why.bs: „Slijedit ćemo ono na čemu smo zatekli pretke svoje” – آبَاء kao predaja.
why.en: “We will follow that which we found our fathers doing” — آبَاء as tradition.

why.bs: Jusuf je roditelje (أَبَوَيْهِ) popeo na prijesto – tefsir se razilazi: otac i majka, ili otac i tetka (majčina sestra).
why.en: Joseph raised his parents (أَبَوَيْهِ) upon the throne — tafsir differs: father and mother, or father and maternal aunt.

nuance.bs: Onaj koji je rodio – riječ iz glagola وَلَدَ, „roditi”. Najčešće u dvojini, „oba roditelja”, u naredbi da im se čini dobro i u propisima o nasljedstvu.
nuance.en: The one who begot — from the verb وَلَدَ, “to beget”. Most often in the dual, “both parents”, in the command to treat them well and in the laws of inheritance.

why.bs: „I da roditeljima dobročinstvo činite” – وَالِدَيْن uz zapovijed da se samo Allahu ibadet čini.
why.en: “And to parents, good treatment” — وَالِدَيْن beside the command to worship none but Allah.

why.bs: Dan kada roditelj neće moći pomoći djetetu svome – وَالِد i وَلَد, rađanje u prvom planu.
why.en: A Day when no parent will avail his child — وَالِد and وَلَد, begetting in view.

why.bs: Naložili smo čovjeku da roditeljima dobro čini; majka ga je s mukom nosila i s mukom rodila.
why.en: We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents; his mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o čovjekovom obraćanju Allahu. Prema ar-Rāġibu, mnogi jezikoslovci kažu da je osnovno značenje riječi ṣalāh upravo dova; u šerijatu je ona postala ime za propisani namaz.
shared.en: Both words speak of turning to Allah. ar-Rāġib reports that many lexicographers take the basic sense of ṣalāh to be supplication itself; in the Sharia it became the name of the prescribed prayer.

tellApart.bs: Propisani namaz, s određenim oblikom i vremenom (a, prema mnogim jezikoslovcima, u osnovi i dova) → صَلَاة; dova, molba upućena Allahu, u svako vrijeme i svojim riječima → دُعَاء.
tellApart.en: The prescribed prayer, with its set form and times (and, according to many lexicographers, at root a supplication too) → صَلَاة; supplication, a plea to Allah at any time and in one's own words → دُعَاء.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries صلا, دعا
notes: ar-Rāġib: many lexicographers say ṣalāh means duʿāʾ, blessing and glorifying; the prescribed prayer is called ṣalāh after a part of what it contains (the supplication) — paraphrased and attributed to him.
9:103 (ṣalli ʿalayhim … ṣalātaka) is explained in tafsir as the Prophet's supplication for those who gave; we say 'tafsir explains', not a named mufassir.
That دُعَاء in the Quran is also made by people in hardship who turn away once relieved (41:51), and that صَلَاة is once said of the idolaters' worship at the House (8:35), is our observation.
Blind review: 'at root a supplication' and 'almost always with أَقَامَ' softened (many lexicographers; most often — 23:2, 70:23, 62:9).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

Sources normalised (2026-11-06): دعا read and added to `verified` (consistent with the texts; no attributed point rests on it).

nuance.bs: Propisani namaz, najčešće uz glagol „obavljati, uspostavljati” (أَقَامَ) i često uz zekat. Ponegdje u Kur'anu zadržava i osnovno značenje dove i blagoslova.
nuance.en: The prescribed prayer, most often with the verb “to establish” (أَقَامَ) and often beside zakat. In places the Quran keeps its root sense of supplication and blessing.

why.bs: „Obavljajte namaz i dajite zekat” – namaz kao propisani ibadet, uz zekat.
why.en: “Establish prayer and give zakat” — prayer as a prescribed act of worship, beside zakat.

why.bs: „I moli se za njih, jer tvoja dova je njima smirenje” – u tefsiru: صَلَاة ovdje znači Poslanikovu dovu za njih.
why.en: “And invoke blessings upon them; your invocations are reassurance for them” — tafsir: صَلَاة here is the Prophet's supplication for them.

why.bs: „Namaz odvraća od razvrata i od onoga što je mrsko” – namaz kao ibadet koji oblikuje čovjeka.
why.en: “Prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing” — prayer as worship that shapes the one who prays.

nuance.bs: Molba upućena Allahu (ili, kod mušrika, nekom drugom), svojim riječima i u svako vrijeme. Vjerovjesnici u Kur'anu svoje molbe zovu دُعَاء.
nuance.en: A plea addressed to Allah (or, by idolaters, to others), in one's own words and at any time. In the Quran the prophets call their own pleas دُعَاء.

why.bs: Ibrahim moli da obavlja namaz i završava: „Gospodaru naš, primi moju dovu” – obje riječi u jednom ajetu.
why.en: Abraham asks to establish prayer and ends: “Our Lord, accept my supplication” — both words in one ayah.

why.bs: Zekerijja: „nikad nisam bio nesretan moleći Te” – dova kao lično obraćanje.
why.en: Zechariah: “never have I been in my supplication to You unhappy” — supplication as a personal plea.

why.bs: Kad čovjeka zadesi zlo, „on se dugo moli” – دُعَاء u nevolji, bez propisanog oblika.
why.en: When evil touches man, “he is full of extensive supplication” — supplication in hardship, with no set form.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o davanju imetka. Razlikuju se po tome je li davanje propisano, dobrovoljno ili bilo kakvo trošenje.
shared.en: All three words speak of giving wealth. They differ in whether the giving is prescribed, voluntary, or any spending at all.

tellApart.bs: Propisani zekat, riječ koja znači i čistoću i rast → زَكَاة; sadaka, u osnovi dobrovoljna, ali se kaže i za obavezno davanje → صَدَقَة; trošiti, udjeljivati – najšire, svako trošenje imetka → أَنْفَقَ.
tellApart.en: Prescribed zakat, a word that also means purity and growth → زَكَاة; charity, at root voluntary but also said of what is due → صَدَقَة; to spend — the widest, any spending of wealth → أَنْفَقَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries زكا, صدق, نفق
Tafsir on 9:60 (ṣadaqāt as the obligatory zakat) and on 19:13, 18:81 (zakāh as purity)
notes: ar-Rāġib: zakāh comes from growth that comes with Allah's blessing, and the prescribed alms are so called for the blessing hoped in them or for tazkiyat an-nafs, which he glosses as making the soul grow in good; ṣadaqa is what one gives from one's wealth seeking nearness to Allah, at root said of the voluntary gift, while zakāh is said of the due one — and the due one may also be called ṣadaqa. Paraphrased and attributed.
That 9:60's ṣadaqāt are the obligatory zakat is the reading of most tafsir and fiqh; we say 'most mufassirun'.

That many mufassirun take زَكَاة as purity (others: righteousness; some for 19:13: charity) in 19:13 and 18:81, that it stands beside صَلَاة in most of its places, and that أَنْفَقَ is also said of spending on one's family (65:7) and of disbelievers' spending against the faith (8:36), are our observations of all places.
Blind review: zakāh as purity in 19:13 / 18:81 given as many mufassirun's reading, not as fact; 9:103 marked as disputed (zakat or expiatory charity).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Propisano davanje, u Kur'anu najčešće odmah uz namaz. Prema ar-Rāġibu, riječ u osnovi znači rast koji dolazi s Allahovim blagoslovom, a zekat je tako nazvan zbog blagoslova koji se od njega očekuje, ili zato što dušu uzdiže u dobru. U 19:13 i 18:81 mnogi mufesiri je tumače kao čistoću (drugi: dobročinstvo).
nuance.en: The prescribed giving, in the Quran most often right beside prayer. According to ar-Rāġib, the word at root means growth that comes with Allah's blessing, and the alms are so named for the blessing hoped in them, or because they make the soul grow in good. In 19:13 and 18:81 many mufassirun take it as purity (others: righteousness).

why.bs: „…da obavljaju namaz i daju zekat – a to je prava vjera” – zekat kao temelj vjere.
why.en: “…to establish prayer and give zakat; that is the correct religion” — zakat as a pillar of the faith.

why.bs: Vjernici su oni „koji zekat daju” – većina mufesira: koji ga daju; ar-Rāġib slovo lām shvata kao namjeru: čine (ibadet) da bi se očistili.
why.en: The believers are those “who are observant of zakat” — most mufassirun: who give it; ar-Rāġib reads the lām as purpose: they act (in worship) to be purified.

why.bs: O Jahji: „i čistoću (زَكَاة)” od Nas – mufesiri: čistoća, dobročinstvo; neki: milostinja.
why.en: Of John: “and purity (زَكَاة)” from Us — mufassirun: purity, righteousness; some: charity.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što se daje da bi se čovjek približio Allahu: u osnovi dobrovoljno, ali se i propisani zekat može nazvati sadakom. Riječ je iz korijena istine (ṣidq).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what one gives to draw near to Allah: at root voluntary, though the prescribed zakat may also be called ṣadaqa. The word comes from the root of truthfulness (ṣidq).

why.bs: „Zekat (الصَّدَقَات) pripada samo siromasima…” – većina mufesira: ovdje je riječ o obaveznom zekatu.
why.en: “Zakah expenditures (الصَّدَقَات) are only for the poor…” — most mufassirun: here the obligatory zakat is meant.

why.bs: „Uzmi od imetka njihova sadaku, da ih njome očistiš” – sadaka koja čisti (tefsir se razilazi je li to zekat ili sadaka kao iskup); uz nju i glagol korijena zekata.
why.en: “Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them” — charity that cleanses (tafsir differs: zakat, or an expiatory charity); a verb of zakat's root beside it.

why.bs: „Ne kvarite svoje sadake prigovaranjem i uvredama” – dobrovoljna sadaka i njena pravila.
why.en: “Do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury” — voluntary charity and its manners.

nuance.bs: Najšira riječ: svako trošenje imetka – na Allahovom putu, na porodicu, pa i trošenje nevjernika protiv vjere. Kur'an je najčešće koristi kad poziva na davanje.
nuance.en: The widest word: any spending of wealth — in Allah's way, on one's family, even the disbelievers' spending against the faith. The Quran most often uses it when it calls to giving.

why.bs: Bogobojazni „od onoga čime ih opskrbljujemo – udjeljuju” – udjeljivanje uz vjeru i namaz.
why.en: The righteous “spend out of what We have provided for them” — spending beside faith and prayer.

why.bs: „Neka imućni troši prema svom imetku” – trošenje na porodicu, ne milostinja.
why.en: “Let a man of wealth spend from his wealth” — spending on one's family, not alms.

why.bs: Nevjernici „troše imetke svoje da bi od Allahova puta odvraćali” – ista riječ za trošenje protiv vjere.
why.en: The disbelievers “spend their wealth to avert people from the way of Allah” — the same word for spending against the faith.

shared.bs: Sve su to riječi korijena ṣ-w-m: oba imena su glagolske imenice od صَامَ. Prema ar-Rāġibu, ṣawm u osnovi znači suzdržavanje od nečega – jela, govora ili kretanja; u šerijatu je to post.
shared.en: All are words of the root ṣ-w-m: both nouns are verbal nouns of صَامَ. According to ar-Rāġib, ṣawm at root means holding back from something — food, speech or movement; in the Sharia it is the fast.

tellApart.bs: Propisani post, u Kur'anu uvijek u propisima → صِيَام; jedino mjesto, Merjemin zavjet, koji tefsir uglavnom tumači kao šutnju → صَوْم; postiti (glagol) → صَامَ.
tellApart.en: The prescribed fast, in the Quran always within the rulings → صِيَام; its one place, Mary's vow, which tafsir mostly explains as silence → صَوْم; to fast (the verb) → صَامَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries صوم
Tafsir on 19:26 (ṣawm as silence)
notes: ar-Rāġib: ṣawm is at root holding back from an act, be it eating, speech or walking; in the Sharia the fast; on 19:26 he notes it has been said that holding back from speech is meant, because of 'so I will not speak to any man today'. Paraphrased and attributed.
Tafsir on 19:26 mostly explains ṣawm as silence; some add that fasting in their law included silence. Both are named.

That صِيَام (9 times) is always the legal fast and صَوْم occurs only in 19:26 is our observation of all places. That the two forms differ in meaning is not claimed as a rule of the language: both are verbal nouns of صَامَ.
Blind review: the Bosnian of 19:26 now says abstention, matching the point; 2:184 is not called a Ramadan ayah (some take it as an earlier fast); 2:185 šahida rendered 'witnesses / dočeka'.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Propisani post: ramazanski post i post kao iskup (kefaret) u propisima. U Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) uvijek u tom pravnom značenju.
nuance.en: The prescribed fast: the fast of Ramadan and the fast of expiation in the rulings. In the Quran (our observation) always in this legal sense.

why.bs: „Propisuje vam se post (الصِّيَام) kao što je propisan onima prije vas” – temeljni ajet o postu.
why.en: “Decreed upon you is fasting (الصِّيَام) as it was decreed upon those before you” — the founding ayah of the fast.

why.bs: „Dozvoljava vam se u noćima posta…” – propisi o postu i noći.
why.en: “It has been made permissible for you the night preceding fasting…” — the rulings of the fast and its nights.

why.bs: „…post dva uzastopna mjeseca” – post kao iskup.
why.en: “…fasting for two months consecutively” — fasting as expiation.

nuance.bs: Samo jednom u Kur'anu: Merjemin zavjet. Odmah iza njega stoji „neću danas ni s kim govoriti”, pa ga tefsir uglavnom tumači kao šutnju; neki dodaju da je post u njihovom zakonu uključivao i šutnju.
nuance.en: Only once in the Quran: Mary's vow. It is followed at once by “I will not speak to any man today”, so tafsir mostly explains it as silence; some add that fasting in their law included silence.

why.bs: „Zavjetovala sam se Milostivom na suzdržavanje (صَوْمًا), pa danas ni s kim neću govoriti” – suzdržavanje od govora.
why.en: “I have vowed to the Most Merciful abstention (صَوْمًا), so I will not speak to any man today” — holding back from speech.

nuance.bs: Glagol od kojeg su obje imenice. U Kur'anu samo dva puta, oba puta u ajetima o postu (2:184–185).
nuance.en: The verb both nouns come from. Only twice in the Quran, both times in the ayat on fasting (2:184–185).

why.bs: „A da postite (تَصُومُوا), bolje vam je” – glagol u propisima o postu.
why.en: “And to fast (تَصُومُوا) is best for you” — the verb within the rulings of the fast.

why.bs: „Ko od vas dočeka taj mjesec, neka ga posti” – zapovijed ramazanskog posta.
why.en: “Whoever of you witnesses the month, let him fast it” — the command of the Ramadan fast.

shared.bs: Obje riječi označavaju putovanje Allahovoj Kući radi obreda. Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḥajj u osnovi znači namjeru (polazak) u posjetu, a ʿumra posjetu koja održava naklonost; šerijat je obje vezao za Kabu.
shared.en: Both words name the journey to Allah's House for its rites. According to ar-Rāġib, ḥajj at root means setting out to visit, and ʿumra a visit that keeps affection alive; the Sharia tied both to the Kaaba.

tellApart.bs: Hadž, u poznatim mjesecima, obaveza onome ko može → حَجّ; umra, posjeta Kabi, koja nije vezana za te mjesece → عُمْرَة.
tellApart.en: Hajj, in the well-known months, a duty on whoever is able → حَجّ; umrah, a visit to the Kaaba not tied to those months → عُمْرَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حج, عمر
Fiqh on 2:196 and 3:97 (whether umrah is obligatory)
notes: ar-Rāġib: the root of ḥajj is setting out to visit, in the Sharia setting out for the House of Allah to perform the rites; ʿumra is a visit, in the Sharia the particular visit — paraphrased and attributed to him.

That hajj is bound to its months (2:197) while umrah may be made at any time is the common ground of fiqh. Whether umrah is obligatory is disputed (Shāfiʿī and Ḥanbalī: yes, with 2:196; Ḥanafī and Mālikī: a sunna); both views are named, neither chosen.
حَجّ sums the corpus's lemmas حَجّ and حِجّ (3:97 is read ḥijju in Ḥafṣ).
Blind review: 'only in 2:196' restricted to the noun (the verb iʿtamara is in 2:158).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حج, عمر (2026-11-06): 6 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (improved): Confirmed, and he glosses ʿumra more precisely as a visit in which affection is kept alive (ʿimārat al-wudd), tying it to its root

nuance.bs: Hodočašće Kabi u određeno vrijeme, s Arefatom i ostalim obredima. Kur'an ga propisuje svakome ko može do Kuće doći.
nuance.en: The pilgrimage to the Kaaba at its set time, with ʿArafa and its other rites. The Quran makes it a duty on whoever is able to reach the House.

why.bs: „Hadž je u poznatim mjesecima” – hadž vezan za vrijeme.
why.en: “Hajj is during well-known months” — hajj bound to its time.

why.bs: „Allahu su ljudi dužni hodočastiti Hram (حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ) – ko god je u mogućnosti” – hadž kao obaveza.
why.en: “Due to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House — for whoever is able” — hajj as a duty.

why.bs: „I oglasi ljudima hadž” – Ibrahimov poziv na hodočašće.
why.en: “And proclaim to the people the Hajj” — Abraham's call to the pilgrimage.

nuance.bs: Posjeta Kabi s obredima ihrama, tavafa i sa'ja, koja nije vezana za mjesece hadža. Imenica ʿumra spomenuta je samo u 2:196 (glagol iʿtamara i u 2:158), uz hadž; je li obavezna, učenjaci se razilaze.
nuance.en: A visit to the Kaaba with the rites of iḥrām, ṭawāf and saʿy, not bound to the months of hajj. The noun ʿumra occurs only in 2:196 (the verb iʿtamara also in 2:158), beside hajj; whether it is obligatory, scholars differ.

why.bs: „I hadž i umru radi Allaha upotpunite” – obje riječi zajedno; neki učenjaci odatle zaključuju da je i umra obavezna, drugi ne.
why.en: “And complete the Hajj and umrah for Allah” — both words together; some scholars infer from it that umrah is obligatory too, others do not.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače zakleti se. Razlikuje ih (naše zapažanje) to ko se u Kur'anu zaklinje i čemu zakletva služi.
shared.en: Both verbs mean to swear an oath. What tells them apart (our observation) is who swears in the Quran and what the oath is for.

tellApart.bs: Zakletva uopće – i neke Allahove zakletve (لَا أُقْسِمُ…) i zakletve ljudi → أَقْسَمَ; zakletva koja u Kur'anu gotovo uvijek prati laž ili izgovor licemjera → حَلَفَ.
tellApart.en: Oath in general — some of Allah's oaths (لَا أُقْسِمُ…) and people's → أَقْسَمَ; an oath that in the Quran almost always goes with the hypocrites' lie or excuse → حَلَفَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قسم, حلف
Tafsir on لَا أُقْسِمُ (75:1, 90:1)
notes: That حَلَفَ describes, in 10 of its 11 ayat, the oaths of hypocrites or of people swearing to a lie (4:62, ch. 9, 58:14, 58:18), and is neutral only in the expiation ruling of 5:89, is our own observation of all places — not put in ar-Rāġib's mouth; some later writers draw a rule from it, which we do not.
That أَقْسَمَ is Allah's oath in 8 ayat (لَا أُقْسِمُ / فَلَا أُقْسِمُ) and otherwise people's oaths, often 'their strongest oaths' that are then belied, is our observation of all 19 ayat.
Tafsir differs on the لَا in لَا أُقْسِمُ: an emphasis ('Nay, I swear') or a rejection of what the deniers said before the oath; both are named.
Blind review: أَقْسَمَ carries only some of Allah's oaths — most use the particle wa-.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Opća riječ za zakletvu. Njime su izrečene neke Allahove zakletve u Kur'anu (većina ide česticom wa-, npr. وَالْفَجْرِ), a i zakletve ljudi – vjernika, svjedoka u propisima, ali i nevjernika „najtežim zakletvama”.
nuance.en: The general word for an oath. Some of Allah's oaths in the Quran are spoken with it (most use the particle wa-, e.g. وَالْفَجْرِ), and so are people's — believers', witnesses' in the rulings, and disbelievers' “strongest oaths”.

why.bs: „Kunem se Danom kijameta!” – Allahova zakletva; tefsir se razilazi je li لَا pojačanje ili odbijanje tvrdnje poricatelja.
why.en: “I swear by the Day of Resurrection” — Allah's oath; tafsir differs on whether لَا is emphasis or a rejection of the deniers' claim.

why.bs: „I kunu se Allahom, najtežim zakletvama, da će vjerovati ako im dođe znak” – zakletva nevjernika.
why.en: “They swear by Allah their strongest oaths that if a sign came to them they would surely believe” — the disbelievers' oath.

why.bs: Vlasnici vrta „zakleše se da će ga ujutro obrati” – zakletva ljudi o vlastitoj namjeri.
why.en: The owners of the garden “swore to cut its fruit in the morning” — people's oath about their own plan.

nuance.bs: Također „zakleti se”, ali u Kur'anu (naše zapažanje) gotovo uvijek o licemjerima i onima koji se kunu da bi prikrili laž ili se opravdali; neutralno je samo u propisu o iskupu za zakletvu.
nuance.en: Also “to swear”, but in the Quran (our observation) almost always of hypocrites and those who swear to cover a lie or excuse themselves; it is neutral only in the ruling on expiating an oath.

why.bs: „I kunu se Allahom da su vaši, a nisu vaši” – zakletva licemjera.
why.en: “They swear by Allah that they are from among you while they are not from among you” — the hypocrites' oath.

why.bs: „…i svjesno se krivo kunu (يَحْلِفُونَ عَلَى الْكَذِبِ)” – zakletva uz laž.
why.en: “…and they swear to a lie while they know” — an oath bound to a lie.

why.bs: „…to je iskup za zakletve vaše kad se zakunete” – jedino neutralno mjesto: propis o zakletvi.
why.en: “…that is the expiation for oaths when you have sworn” — the one neutral place: the ruling on oaths.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače vijest, obavijest o nečemu. Prema ar-Rāġibu, نَبَأ je vijest od velike koristi koja donosi znanje ili jaku vjerovatnoću.
shared.en: Both words mean news, a report of something. According to ar-Rāġib, نَبَأ is news of great benefit that brings knowledge or a strong probability.

tellApart.bs: Važna vijest od velike koristi – kazivanja o vjerovjesnicima, nevidljivom svijetu i Sudnjem danu → نَبَأ; vijest, obavijest uopće, i ono što se o nekome zna → خَبَر.
tellApart.en: Weighty news of great benefit — accounts of prophets, the unseen and the Last Day → نَبَأ; news, information in general, and what is known about someone → خَبَر.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نبأ, خبر
notes: ar-Rāġib: nabaʾ is news of great benefit from which knowledge or strong probability arises, and news is not properly called nabaʾ until it has these three things — paraphrased and attributed to him.

That نَبَأ (with its plural أَنْبَاء) is mostly said of the stories of earlier prophets and peoples, of the unseen and of the Last Day, is our observation of all 29 places; 49:6 (news brought by a fāsiq, to be verified) shows that a nabaʾ can still need checking.
خَبَر sums the corpus's lemmas خَبَر and its plural أَخْبَار (2 + 3).
Blind review: ġalabat aẓ-ẓann rendered 'strong probability'; the derivation of نَبِيّ from nabaʾ given as many's view (others: from nabwa).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نبأ, خبر (2026-11-06): 5 attributed points confirmed

nuance.bs: Vijest od težine i koristi. U Kur'anu najčešće o vjerovjesnicima i narodima prije, o nevidljivom svijetu i o Sudnjem danu. Mnogi iz istog korijena izvode i نَبِيّ – vjerovjesnik (drugi iz nabwa, uzvišenost).
nuance.en: News of weight and benefit. In the Quran most often of the prophets and peoples of old, of the unseen and of the Last Day. Many derive نَبِيّ, prophet, from the same root (others from nabwa, elevation).

why.bs: „…o velikoj vijesti (النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ)” – vijest o proživljenju.
why.en: “About the great news” — the tidings of the Resurrection.

why.bs: Pupavac: „donosim ti pouzdanu vijest (بِنَبَإٍ يَقِينٍ) iz Sebe” – vijest koja donosi sigurno znanje.
why.en: The hoopoe: “I have come to you from Sheba with certain news” — news that brings sure knowledge.

why.bs: „Ako vam nepošten čovjek donese kakvu vijest, provjerite je” – i važnu vijest treba provjeriti.
why.en: “If there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate” — even weighty news must be checked.

nuance.bs: Vijest, obavijest uopće; u množini i ono što se o nekome zna (njegova djela i stanje).
nuance.en: News, information in general; in the plural also what is known about someone (their deeds and state).

why.bs: Musa porodici: „donijet ću vam od nje kakvu vijest (بِخَبَرٍ)” – obična vijest o putu.
why.en: Moses to his family: “I will bring you from there information” — ordinary news about the way.

why.bs: „Tog dana će ona vijesti svoje kazivati” – zemlja govori o onome što se na njoj činilo.
why.en: “That Day, it will report its news” — the earth tells what was done upon it.

why.bs: „…i da provjerimo vijesti o vama” – أَخْبَار kao ono što se o ljudima zna.
why.en: “…and test your affairs” — أَخْبَار as what is known of people.

title.en: To walk, to travel, to hasten

shared.bs: Sva tri glagola govore o kretanju. Razlikuju se po načinu, dužini puta i po tome je li u kretanju trud.
shared.en: All three verbs speak of motion. They differ in manner, in the length of the way and in whether the motion carries effort.

tellApart.bs: Hodati, ići – kretanje i način hoda → مَشَى; putovati, ići kroz zemlju, najčešće s pozivom da se gleda i pouka uzme → سَارَ; žuriti, i trud u nekom poslu, dobrom ili lošem → سَعَى.
tellApart.en: To walk — motion and the manner of walking → مَشَى; to travel, to go through the land, most often with a call to look and take heed → سَارَ; to hasten, and effort in a matter, good or bad → سَعَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries مشى, سار, سعى
Tafsir on 62:9 (fa-sʿaw)
notes: ar-Rāġib: mashy is moving from place to place by will; sayr is going on through the land; saʿy is a quick walk short of running, and is used for earnest effort in a matter, good or evil — paraphrased and attributed to him.
That سَارَ occurs 13 times in 'travel through the land and see the end of…' is our observation of all 16 places; that مَشَى is often qualified by the manner of walking (17:37, 25:63, 28:25) likewise.
62:9 fa-sʿaw: tafsir mostly explains it as going with care and readiness, not running (the Prophet forbade running to prayer); both senses of saʿy are named.
Blind review: 62:9 fa-sʿaw given as most mufassirun's reading.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
