notes: ar-Rāġib (رود): irāda is the soul's leaning to a thing together with the judgement that it should or should not be done; said of Allah it means only the judgement, for He is above leaning; it may mean command (2:185) or intent (28:83), and, since will can follow a compelled (natural) force as well as choice, is said even of a wall (18:77). (شيء): most theologians take mašīʾa as irāda; some say mašīʾa is at root bringing into being, that Allah's mašīʾa entails the thing's existence while His irāda need not (2:185, 40:31), and that man's will comes only after Allah's (76:30). The distinction is reported, not his own ruling — attributed as 'some scholars, as ar-Rāġib reports'.
That شَاءَ carries the formula in šāʾa llāh and the conditional 'had Allah willed' in many places is our observation; 'often of Allah' is a tendency — people's will is also شَاءَ (18:29).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رود, شيء (2026-11-06): 18 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (improved): The reported distinction is that His irāda need not entail the existence of what is willed (2:185, 40:31). 'What He wants of people' is the command sense from entry رود, not the point of this distinction; notes/0 (reworded): He does not call the wall usage figurative; he explains it by irāda following a compelled/sensory force; members/0/nuance (reworded): 'Figuratively' is ours; he gives a non-figurative explanation (will according to a compelled/sensory force)

Blind review (2026-11-06): the mašīʾa/irāda split kept as 'some scholars' in tellApart and the شَاءَ nuance too (most theologians make them one; 36:82 uses irāda of what comes to be); أَرَادَ is željeti/namjeravati, شَاءَ htjeti; 18:77 by his 'compelled force', not 'figuratively'.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, težnja duše ka nečemu zajedno sa sudom da to treba učiniti; kada se kaže za Allaha, znači samo odluku, jer je On iznad težnje. Može značiti i namjeru (28:83) i ono što Allah od ljudi traži (2:185), a kako htijenje može proisticati i iz prirodne sile, a ne samo iz izbora, kaže se čak i za zid (18:77).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the soul's leaning towards a thing together with the judgement that it should be done; said of Allah it means only the decision, for He is above leaning. It can mean intent (28:83) and what Allah wants of people (2:185), and, since will can follow a compelled force and not only choice, is said even of a wall (18:77).

why.bs: „Allah želi da vam olakša, a ne želi da vam oteža” – ar-Rāġib: ovdje htijenje u značenju onoga što Allah naređuje i želi za vas.
why.en: “Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship” — ar-Rāġib: here wanting in the sense of what Allah commands and wants for you.

why.bs: Onaj svijet je za one „koji ne žele uzvisivanje na Zemlji” – htijenje kao namjera i cilj.
why.en: The home of the Hereafter is for those “who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth” — wanting as intent and aim.

why.bs: „Zid koji samo što se nije srušio” (doslovno: koji „hoće” da se sruši) – ar-Rāġib: htijenje može proisticati i iz prirodne sile, pa se riječ kaže i za ono što nema izbora.
why.en: “A wall about to collapse” (literally: that “wants” to collapse) — ar-Rāġib: will can also follow a compelled force, so the word is said even of what has no choice.

nuance.bs: Volja. Kur'an je često koristi za Allahovu volju i u izrazu „ako Allah htjedne”; i čovjek „hoće”, ali, prema 76:30, samo ono što Allah htjedne. Neki učenjaci, kako navodi ar-Rāġib, kažu da je Allahova مَشِيئَة upravo davanje postojanja stvari, pa biva ono što On htjedne.
nuance.en: Will. The Quran often uses it of Allah's will and in “if Allah wills”; man too “wills”, but, by 76:30, only what Allah wills. Some scholars, as ar-Rāġib reports, say that Allah's will (مَشِيئَة) is itself the bringing of a thing into being, so that what He wills, is.

why.bs: „A vi nećete htjeti, osim ako Allah htjedne” – čovjekova volja je pod Allahovom.
why.en: “And you do not will except that Allah wills” — man's will stands under Allah's.

why.bs: „…osim ako Allah htjedne” – izraz kojim se svaka buduća namjera veže za Allahovu volju.
why.en: “…except [when adding], “If Allah wills”” — the phrase that ties every future intent to Allah's will.

why.bs: „Pa ko hoće – neka vjeruje, a ko hoće – neka ne vjeruje” – ista riječ i za čovjekov izbor.
why.en: “Whoever wills – let him believe; and whoever wills – let him disbelieve” — the same word for man's choice.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače odlučiti o nečemu. Prema ar-Rāġibu, حُكْم je presuda da je nešto tako ili nije, a قَضَاء je presijecanje (konačno rješavanje) stvari, riječju ili djelom – zato قَضَى znači i naredbu, i stvaranje, i obavljanje.
shared.en: Both words mean deciding a matter. According to ar-Rāġib, حُكْم is judging that a thing is so or is not, while قَضَاء is settling a matter, cutting it off, by word or by deed — so قَضَى also means commanding, creating and carrying out.

tellApart.bs: Suditi, presuditi među ljudima, odlučiti šta je pravo → حَكَمَ; okončati stvar riječju ili djelom: odrediti, narediti, stvoriti, obaviti → قَضَى.
tellApart.en: To judge between people, to decide what is right → حَكَمَ; to settle a matter by word or deed: to decree, command, create, carry out → قَضَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حكم, قضى
notes: ar-Rāġib (حكم): the root is restraining in order to set right (the bridle is ḥakama); judging is deciding that a thing is so or not so, whether one binds another to it or not (4:58). (قضى): qaḍāʾ is settling a matter, by word or deed, divine or human: Allah's word as command (17:23), His act as creating and completing (41:12), people's act as carrying out (2:200); qaḍāʾ from Allah is more specific than qadar — qadar is measuring, qaḍāʾ is deciding and cutting.
That حَكَمَ in the Quran is mostly judging between people or in a dispute, and Allah's judging between them on the Day, is our observation of its places.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حكم, قضى (2026-11-06): 17 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): His definition is faṣl al-amr (separating/settling; cf. 'القضاء هو الفصل والقطع'). 'Finishing' (الفراغ) appears only in some uses (41:12, 10:11). Close, but 'settling/cutting' is truer; members/1/nuance (reworded): Same as shared: his core is faṣl (settling/cutting)
Blind review (2026-11-06): 17:23 bs 'naredio' (command); 41:12 bs 'dovršio'; قَضَى bs meaning without 'presuditi' (kept for حَكَمَ).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen znači sprječavati radi popravljanja (uzda konja je حَكَمَة), a suditi znači odlučiti da je nešto tako ili nije. U Kur'anu najčešće suđenje među ljudima i Allahovo presuđivanje među njima na Sudnjem danu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root means restraining in order to set right (a horse's bridle is حَكَمَة), and judging is deciding that a thing is so or is not. In the Quran it is mostly judging between people, and Allah's judging between them on the Day of Resurrection.

why.bs: „A kad ljudima sudite, pravedno sudite” – suđenje među ljudima.
why.en: “And when you judge between people, judge with justice” — judging between people.

why.bs: Davud i Sulejman „kad su sudili o usjevu” – presuda u sporu.
why.en: David and Solomon, “when they judged concerning the field” — a verdict in a dispute.

why.bs: „Allah će na Sudnjem danu presuditi među njima o onome u čemu su se razilazili.”
why.en: “Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.”

meaning.en: to decree; to settle, to complete

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, presjeći (konačno riješiti) stvar – riječju ili djelom: Allahova naredba (17:23), Allahovo stvaranje i dovršenje nebesa (41:12), ljudsko obavljanje obreda (2:200), pa i kraj života. Allahov قَضَاء je, kaže on, uže od kadera: kader je odmjeravanje, a قَضَاء konačna odluka.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, settling a matter, cutting it off — by word or by deed: Allah's command (17:23), Allah's creating and completing the heavens (41:12), people's carrying out their rites (2:200), even the end of a life. Allah's قَضَاء, he says, is narrower than qadar: qadar is the measuring, قَضَاء the final decision.

why.bs: „Gospodar tvoj je naredio da se samo Njemu klanjate” – قَضَى kao Allahova naredba.
why.en: “Your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him” — قَضَى as Allah's command.

why.bs: „I dovršio ih je kao sedam nebesa u dva dana (فَقَضَاهُنَّ)” – ar-Rāġib: stvaranje i njegovo dovršenje.
why.en: “And He completed them (فَقَضَاهُنَّ) as seven heavens within two days” — ar-Rāġib: creating, and finishing it.

why.bs: „A kad završite svoje obrede…” – ljudsko obavljanje i završavanje.
why.en: “And when you have completed your rites…” — people carrying a thing out to its end.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o tome da čovjek ne drži na umu ono što treba. Prema ar-Rāġibu, nemar (غَفْلَة) je jedan od uzroka zaborava: čovjek zaboravi iz slabosti, iz nemara ili namjerno.
shared.en: Both words speak of a person not keeping in mind what he should. According to ar-Rāġib, heedlessness (غَفْلَة) is one of the causes of forgetting: one forgets from weakness, from heedlessness, or on purpose.

tellApart.bs: Izgubiti iz sjećanja ono što je bilo povjereno – oprošteno kad nije čovjekova krivica, pokuđeno kad mu je uzrok u njemu samom → نَسِيَ; biti nemaran, nepažljiv, ne paziti → غَافِل.
tellApart.en: To lose hold of what one was entrusted with — excused when not one's own doing, blamed when its cause lies in the person himself → نَسِيَ; to be heedless, unaware, off one's guard → غَافِل.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نسى, غفل
notes: ar-Rāġib (نسى): nisyān is a person's failing to keep what was entrusted to him — from a weak heart, from heedlessness, or on purpose — until its remembrance is gone from the heart; every forgetting Allah blames had a deliberate origin, what is excused had no cause from the person; ascribed to Allah it is His leaving them, slighting them, in return for what they left (9:67, 32:14). (غفل): ġafla is an oversight that comes over a person from little care and alertness.
Allah's 'forgetting' is glossed beside 9:67 (He does not forget, 19:64: His leaving them). 20:115 (Adam) is not cited: tafsir differs on nasiya there (forgot / left).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نسى, غفل (2026-11-06): 12 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): He does not cite 19:64; his reason is requital ('مجازاة لما تركوه'), not 'Allah does not forget'
Blind review (2026-11-06): blamed forgetting is the one caused by the person himself (his 'ʿan taʿammud'), not 'neglect'; 12:13 bs 'ne pazite'.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, izgubiti iz srca ono što je povjereno – iz slabosti, iz nemara ili namjerno. Allah kudi samo zaborav koji je čovjek sam skrivio; kada se kaže za Allaha, znači da ih On ostavlja, kao kaznu za ono što su oni ostavili (a Kur'an kaže da Allah ne zaboravlja, 19:64).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, losing from the heart what was entrusted to it — from weakness, from heedlessness, or on purpose. Allah blames only the forgetting a person brought on himself; said of Allah it means He leaves them, in return for what they left (the Quran itself says Allah does not forget, 19:64).

why.bs: „Gospodaru naš, ne kazni nas ako zaboravimo” – zaborav koji nije namjeran.
why.en: “Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten” — forgetting that is not deliberate.

why.bs: Musaov mladić: „ja sam zaboravio ribu” – obični zaborav, koji mladić pripisuje šejtanu.
why.en: Moses' servant: “I forgot the fish” — ordinary forgetting, which he ascribes to Satan.

why.bs: „Zaboravili su Allaha, pa je i On njih zaboravio” – ar-Rāġib: kod Allaha znači da ih je ostavio, kao kaznu za ono što su oni ostavili.
why.en: “They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them” — ar-Rāġib: of Allah it means He left them, in return for what they left.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, غَفْلَة je propust koji obuzme čovjeka zbog malo opreza i budnosti. Kur'an često kaže da Allah nije غَافِل (nije nemaran) prema onome što ljudi rade, i upozorava da se ne bude među nemarnima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, غَفْلَة is an oversight that comes over a person from too little care and alertness. The Quran often says Allah is not غَافِل (unaware) of what people do, and warns against being among the heedless.

why.bs: „I ne budi od nemarnih” – nemar kao stanje protiv kojeg se upozorava.
why.en: “And do not be among the heedless” — heedlessness as a state to guard against.

why.bs: „A Allah nije nemaran prema onome što radite” – Allah zna sve što ljudi čine.
why.en: “And Allah is not unaware of what you do” — Allah knows all that people do.

why.bs: Jakub: „bojim se da ga ne pojede vuk dok vi na njega ne pazite” – nepažnja, a ne zaborav.
why.en: Jacob: “I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are of him unaware” — inattention, not forgetting.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o licu koje se razvedri. Kur'an riječ تَبَسَّمَ koristi samo jednom, za Sulejmana, i odmah uz nju ضَاحِكًا.
shared.en: Both words speak of a face that brightens. The Quran uses تَبَسَّمَ only once, of Solomon, and right beside it ضَاحِكًا, “laughing”.

tellApart.bs: Smijati se – od radosti, od čuđenja, ali i podrugljivo → ضَحِكَ; nasmiješiti se, blaži početak smijeha → تَبَسَّمَ.
tellApart.en: To laugh — from joy, from wonder, but also in mockery → ضَحِكَ; to smile, the gentler beginning of laughter → تَبَسَّمَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ضحك
notes: ar-Rāġib (ضحك): ḍaḥk is the face spreading and the teeth showing from the soul's joy; it is borrowed for mockery (23:110, 43:47), used for plain joy (80:39, 9:82, 27:19) and for wonder; Sarah's laughter (11:71) was from wonder, as 11:72–73 show — 'she menstruated' is not an explanation of fa-ḍaḥikat. He has no entry for tabassama; he cites 27:19 under joy.
That تَبَسَّمَ is the beginning of laughter / a smile that turned into laughter in 27:19 is how many mufassirun explain fa-tabassama ḍāḥikan; given as theirs.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ضحك (2026-11-06): 10 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): He makes no frequency claim; mark it as our Quranic observation

Blind review (2026-11-06): Sarah's laughter as wonder marked as ar-Rāġib's reading; 27:19 bs 'njenim riječima' (the ant's); the smile note given to some mufassirun (prophets' laughter mostly smiling).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, lice se razvedri i zubi se pokažu od radosti duše. Riječ se koristi za čistu radost, za čuđenje (smijeh Ibrahimove žene, 11:71, koji on tumači kao čuđenje) i za podsmijeh – u Kur'anu je smijeh nevjernika najčešće podsmijeh.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the face spreads and the teeth show from the soul's joy. The word is used for plain joy, for wonder (the laughter of Abraham's wife, 11:71, which he reads as wonder) and for mockery — in the Quran, the disbelievers' laughter is most often the last.

why.bs: Ibrahimova žena „se nasmija” – ar-Rāġib: od čuđenja, kako pokazuje njeno pitanje u 11:72.
why.en: Abraham's wife “laughed” — ar-Rāġib: from wonder, as her question in 11:72 shows.

why.bs: Grješnici „su se vjernicima smijali” – smijeh kao podsmijeh.
why.en: The criminals “used to laugh at those who believed” — laughter as mockery.

why.bs: „Neka se malo smiju, a mnogo će plakati” – smijeh nasuprot plaču.
why.en: “So let them laugh a little and weep much” — laughter against weeping.

nuance.bs: Osmijeh. U Kur'anu samo jednom: Sulejman se nasmiješi riječima mrava, i odmah zahvaljuje Allahu na blagodati. Neki mufesiri navode da je smijeh vjerovjesnika najčešće bio osmijeh, bez glasnosti.
nuance.en: A smile. Only once in the Quran: Solomon smiles at the ant's words and at once thanks Allah for His favour. Some mufassirun note that the laughter of the prophets was mostly smiling, without loudness.

why.bs: „Pa se on nasmiješi (فَتَبَسَّمَ), veseleći se (ضَاحِكًا) njenim riječima” – obje riječi u jednom izrazu; slijedi zahvala Allahu.
why.en: “So [Solomon] smiled (فَتَبَسَّمَ), amused (ضَاحِكًا) at her speech” — both words in one phrase; thanks to Allah follow.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o tome da se nešto ne pokaže. Prema ar-Rāġibu, أَخْفَى je suprotno od „pokazati” i „objaviti”, أَسَرَّ suprotno od „javno”, a كَتَمَ je skrivanje govora.
shared.en: All three words speak of not showing something. According to ar-Rāġib, أَخْفَى is the opposite of showing and declaring, أَسَرَّ the opposite of doing openly, and كَتَمَ is concealing speech.

tellApart.bs: Prešutjeti ono što se zna i treba kazati (svjedočenje, istinu) → كَتَمَ; sakriti bilo šta, suprotno od pokazati → أَخْفَى; tajiti, ili povjeriti nekome u tajnosti, a od drugih skriti → أَسَرَّ.
tellApart.en: To withhold what one knows and should tell (testimony, the truth) → كَتَمَ; to hide anything, the opposite of showing → أَخْفَى; to keep secret, or to confide to someone while hiding it from others → أَسَرَّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كتم, خفى, سرر
notes: ar-Rāġib (كتم): kitmān is concealing speech (satr al-ḥadīṯ): testimony (2:140), the truth (2:146); concealing Allah's bounty (4:37) is ingratitude. (خفى): iḫfāʾ is covering, set against ibdāʾ and iʿlān (2:271, 60:1). (سرر): isrār is the opposite of iʿlān (sirran wa ʿalāniya); asrartu ilā fulān is confiding to someone — showing it to him and hiding it from others (66:3, 60:1).

That كَتَمَ is mostly said of truth, testimony or knowledge owed to others is our observation of its 21 places (2:42, 2:146, 2:159, 2:174, 2:283, 3:187 …); 2:228 (what is in the wombs) is of the same kind.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries كتم, خفى, سرر (2026-11-06): 16 attributed points confirmed

Blind review (2026-11-06): كَتَمَ not always a sin (40:28, a believer hiding his faith); 4:42 with the Ibn ʿAbbās reconciliation he quotes; bs prikriti (كَتَمَ) / sakriti (أَخْفَى) kept apart; أَسَرَّ 'private, with one or a few' (71:9), not 'between two'.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, skrivanje govora. U Kur'anu najčešće prikrivanje istine, svjedočenja ili znanja koje se duguje drugima, i tada je pokuđeno kao grijeh (2:283); ali može biti i skrivanje vlastite vjere (40:28).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, concealing speech. In the Quran it is most often withholding the truth, a testimony, or knowledge owed to others, and then it is blamed as a sin (2:283); but it can also be hiding one's own faith (40:28).

why.bs: „I ne prikrivajte svjedočenje; ko ga prikriva, srce njegovo je grješno” – prešutjeti ono što se duguje.
why.en: “And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it – his heart is indeed sinful” — withholding what is owed.

why.bs: „A jedna skupina njih svjesno istinu prikriva” – prešućivanje istine.
why.en: “But indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know it” — withholding the truth.

why.bs: Na Sudnjem danu „neće moći od Allaha prikriti nijednu riječ” – ar-Rāġib navodi Ibn Abbasa: mnogobošci će isprva poricati, potom će im udovi svjedočiti, pa će poželjeti da ništa nisu prikrili.
why.en: On that Day “they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement” — ar-Rāġib quotes Ibn ʿAbbās: the polytheists first deny, then their limbs testify, and they wish they had concealed nothing.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, staviti nešto pod zaklon; suprotno je od „pokazati” (أَبْدَى) i „objaviti” (أَعْلَنَ). Opća riječ: sakriva se dobro djelo, osjećaj, misao.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to put a thing under cover; it is the opposite of showing (أَبْدَى) and declaring (أَعْلَنَ). A general word: one hides a good deed, a feeling, a thought.

why.bs: „Ako javno dijelite milostinju – lijepo je, a ako je sakrijete i date siromasima – bolje vam je” – sakriti nasuprot pokazati.
why.en: “If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you” — hiding against showing.

why.bs: „Oni u sebi kriju ono što tebi ne pokazuju” – sakrivena misao.
why.en: “They conceal within themselves what they will not reveal to you” — a hidden thought.

why.bs: „Pokazali vi ono što je u dušama vašim ili ga sakrili, Allah će vas za to pitati” – i skriveno je poznato Allahu.
why.en: “Whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it” — the hidden too is known to Allah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, suprotno od javnog; a „povjeriti nekome tajnu” znači jednom je otkriti, a od drugih je skriti. Zato riječ ide uz ono što se povjerava privatno, jednom ili nekolicini (71:9).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the opposite of doing openly; and to confide a secret to someone is to reveal it to him while hiding it from others. So the word goes with what is shared in private, with one person or a few (71:9).

why.bs: „Kad je Vjerovjesnik jednoj od svojih žena povjerio nešto u tajnosti” – tajna povjerena jednome.
why.en: “When the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement” — a secret entrusted to one person.

why.bs: „Vi im u povjerenju iskazujete prijateljstvo, a Ja najbolje znam šta ste sakrili i šta ste objavili” – povjeravanje, sakrivanje, objavljivanje.
why.en: “You confide to them affection, while I am most knowing of what you have concealed and what you have declared” — confiding, concealing, declaring.

why.bs: Nuh: „govorio sam im javno, i u povjerenju sam im govorio” – tajno nasuprot javnog.
why.en: Noah: “I announced to them and [also] confided to them secretly” — secret against open.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače okrenuti se od nečega. Prema ar-Rāġibu, أَعْرَضَ znači okrenuti se pokazujući bok, a تَوَلَّى s „od” (عَن) znači okrenuti se i udaljiti – tijelom ili neposluhom.
shared.en: Both words mean turning away from something. According to ar-Rāġib, أَعْرَضَ is turning away showing one's side, while تَوَلَّى with “from” (عَن) is turning away and leaving — with the body or by not obeying.

tellApart.bs: Okrenuti se u stranu, ne obazirati se – i kad je to pohvalno (od neznalica) → أَعْرَضَ; okrenuti leđa, napustiti; a bez „od”: prihvatiti nekoga za zaštitnika → تَوَلَّى.
tellApart.en: To turn aside, to pay no heed — even when that is praised (from the ignorant) → أَعْرَضَ; to turn one's back, to leave; and without “from”: to take someone as ally → تَوَلَّى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عرض, ولى
notes: ar-Rāġib (عرض): aʿraḍa is to show one's ʿarḍ (side); aʿraḍa ʿannī means he turned away showing his side (4:63, 7:199, 20:124). (ولى): tawallā with a direct object means taking someone as ally (5:51); with ʿan, stated or implied, it means turning away and leaving nearness (3:64); turning away may be with the body or by not listening and obeying (8:20); wallāhu duburahu is fleeing (8:16).
3:23 (yatawallā … wa hum muʿriḍūn) holds both roots, but مُعْرِض is a participle, not the verb أَعْرَضَ; it is cited for تَوَلَّى. 80:1 is not cited (tafsir on the Prophet).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries عرض, ولى (2026-11-06): 13 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): He does not cite 3:32; his examples include 3:63, 3:64, 88:23, 47:38. Also the side is ʿurḍ (عُرْض), as members/0 has it, not ʿarḍ; members/1/nuance (improved): His transitive sense is wilāya and nearness, illustrated first by turning one's face towards (2:144); ally-taking (5:51) is one case
Blind review (2026-11-06): تَوَلَّى in bs 'okrenuti leđa / odvraćati se', أَعْرَضَ 'okrenuti se'; 8:20 as not listening and obeying (he allows the body too).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, okrenuti se pokazujući bok (عُرْض) – ne obazirati se. Može biti pokuđeno (okrenuti se od Allahove opomene), ali i naređeno: Poslaniku je rečeno da se okrene od neznalica.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, turning away showing one's side (عُرْض) — paying no heed. It can be blamed (turning from Allah's reminder), but also commanded: the Prophet is told to turn away from the ignorant.

why.bs: „I okreni se od neznalica” – pohvalno ne obazirati se.
why.en: “And turn away from the ignorant” — a praised disregard.

why.bs: „A ko okrene glavu od Opomene Moje, taj će teškim životom živjeti” – pokuđeno okretanje.
why.en: “And whoever turns away from My remembrance – indeed, he will have a depressed life” — a blamed turning away.

why.bs: „Zato se od njih okreni, i savjetuj ih” – ne obazirati se, a ipak opominjati.
why.en: “So turn away from them but admonish them” — disregard, and yet admonish.

meaning.en: to turn away; to take as ally

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, s „od” (izrečenim ili prešućenim) znači okrenuti se i udaljiti – tijelom ili tako što se ne sluša i ne pokorava. Bez „od” znači približiti se: okrenuti lice prema nečemu (2:144) ili prihvatiti nekoga za zaštitnika i prijatelja.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, with “from” (said or implied) it means turning away and leaving — with the body or by not listening and not obeying. Without “from” it means drawing near: turning one's face towards something (2:144) or taking someone as ally and friend.

why.bs: „Pokoravajte se Allahu i Poslaniku! A ako okrenu leđa…” – okretanje leđa kao odbijanje poslušnosti.
why.en: “Obey Allah and the Messenger. But if they turn away…” — turning away as refusing obedience.

why.bs: „I ne odvraćajte se od njega dok slušate” – ar-Rāġib: ovdje je odvraćanje neslušanje i neposluh.
why.en: “And do not turn from him while you hear [his order]” — ar-Rāġib: here the turning away is by not listening and not obeying.

why.bs: „A ko ih od vas za zaštitnike prihvati, on je njihov” – تَوَلَّى bez „od”: prihvatiti za zaštitnika.
why.en: “And whoever is an ally to them among you – then indeed, he is [one] of them” — تَوَلَّى without “from”: to take as ally.

shared.bs: Sve četiri riječi govore o snu, od prvog drijemeža do dubokog sna. Ar-Rāġib نُعَاس i رُقُود objašnjava kao vrste sna (نَوْم), a سِنَة kao drijemež (غَفْوَة).
shared.en: All four words speak of sleep, from the first drowsiness to deep sleep. ar-Rāġib explains نُعَاس and رُقُود as kinds of نَوْم, and سِنَة as drowsing (غَفْوَة).

tellApart.bs: San, puni san → نَوْم; pospanost, omamljenost koja prethodi snu → سِنَة; kratki, lagani san, drijemež → نُعَاس; ugodan, kratak san (o stanovnicima pećine) → رُقُود.
tellApart.en: Sleep, full sleep → نَوْم; drowsiness, the heaviness before sleep → سِنَة; short, light sleep, dozing → نُعَاس; pleasant, short sleep (of the people of the cave, “asleep”) → رُقُود.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نوم, وسن, نعس, رقد
notes: ar-Rāġib (نوم): sleep is explained in several ways, all right from different views: a relaxing of the brain's nerves; Allah's taking the soul without death (39:42); a light death. (وسن): wasan and sina are ġafla and ġafwa (drowsing). (نعس): nuʿās is little sleep (8:11, 3:154); some say it means calm here. (رقد): ruqād is pleasant, short sleep; the people of the cave are called ruqūd (18:18) though they slept long, measured against death — they were thought dead, and that sleep was little beside death.

That سِنَة is the drowsiness that comes before sleep is how mufassirun explain 2:255; ar-Rāġib's own gloss is drowsing (ġafla, ġafwa). مَنَام (4×) and مَرْقَد (36:52) are other lemmas, not counted here.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نوم, وسن, نعس, رقد (2026-11-06): 19 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): For sina he glosses ġafla/ġafwa; he only adds 'وأرى أن وسن يقال لتصور النوم منه'. رقد: 'المستطاب من النوم القليل'; notes/0 (reworded): النوم القليل = little/short sleep, not 'light' (members/3 already says short); members/0/nuance (reworded): He says the brain's nerves relax (from rising vapours), not the body; members/1/nuance (reworded): His second gloss is ġafla (inattention), not heaviness; the 'before sleep' sense is correctly given to the mufassirun
Blind review (2026-11-06): bs pospanost (سِنَة) / drijemež (نُعَاس) kept apart; رُقُود 'pleasant, short sleep' (his), not 'rest'; سِنَة before sleep given to many mufassirun.

nuance.bs: Puni san. Prema ar-Rāġibu, san se tumači na više načina, svaki tačan sa svoje strane: kao opuštanje moždanih živaca, kao Allahovo uzimanje duše bez smrti (39:42), i kao „lahka smrt”. Kur'an ga spominje kao Allahov znak i kao odmor.
nuance.en: Full sleep. According to ar-Rāġib, sleep is explained in several ways, each right from its own side: as a slackening of the brain's nerves, as Allah taking the soul without death (39:42), and as a “light death”. The Quran names it among Allah's signs and as rest.

why.bs: „I san vaš učinili smo počinkom” – san kao odmor.
why.en: “And made your sleep [a means for] rest” — sleep as rest.

why.bs: „On vam je noć učinio pokrivačem, a san odmorom” – san kao Allahov dar.
why.en: “It is He who has made the night for you as clothing and sleep [a means for] rest” — sleep as Allah's gift.

why.bs: „Ne obuzima Ga ni pospanost ni san” – Allah je iznad i jednog i drugog.
why.en: “Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep” — Allah is above both.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, isto što i وَسَن: pospanost, odsutnost svijesti (غَفْلَة). Mnogi mufesiri u 2:255 objašnjavaju da je to omamljenost koja prethodi snu – Allaha ne obuzima ni ona, a kamoli san.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the same as وَسَن: drowsing, a lapse of awareness (غَفْلَة). Many mufassirun explain it in 2:255 as the heaviness that comes before sleep — not even that overtakes Allah, let alone sleep.

why.bs: „Ne obuzima Ga ni pospanost (سِنَة) ni san (نَوْم)” – od lakšeg prema težem: ni početak sna.
why.en: “Neither drowsiness (سِنَة) overtakes Him nor sleep (نَوْم)” — from the lighter to the heavier: not even the onset of sleep.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, malo sna. U Kur'anu oba puta Allah spušta drijemež na vjernike u boju kao sigurnost i smirenje (neki, kako on navodi, ovdje razumiju samo smirenost).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a little sleep. Both times in the Quran Allah sends drowsiness on the believers in battle as security and calm (some, he reports, take it here as calm itself).

why.bs: „Kad vas je On drijemežom obuzeo, kao sigurnost od Njega” – lagani san kao smirenje pred boj.
why.en: “[Remember] when He overwhelmed you with drowsiness [giving] security from Him” — light sleep as calm before battle.

why.bs: „Zatim vam je poslije tuge spustio sigurnost – drijemež koji je obuzeo neke od vas” – nakon Uhuda.
why.en: “Then after distress, He sent down upon you security [in the form of] drowsiness, overcoming a faction of you” — after Uhud.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, رُقَاد je ugodan, kratak san. Stanovnike pećine Kur'an naziva رُقُود iako su dugo spavali – ar-Rāġib kaže: u poređenju sa smrću, jer su ih smatrali mrtvima, taj san bio je kratak.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, رُقَاد is pleasant, short sleep. The Quran calls the people of the cave رُقُود though they slept long — ar-Rāġib says: measured against death, for they were thought dead, that sleep was short.

why.bs: „Pomislio bi da su budni, a oni su spavali (رُقُود)” – san koji izgleda kao budnost.
why.en: “And you would think them awake, while they were asleep (رُقُود)” — a sleep that looks like waking.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o potomku. Prema ar-Rāġibu, وَلَد je onaj koji je rođen – jedan ili više, malo ili odraslo (navodi Ebu el-Hasena da obuhvata i sina i kćer) – a ابْن je sin, nazvan tako jer ga je otac „sagradio”, pa se kaže i za sve što od nečega potječe.
shared.en: Both words speak of offspring. According to ar-Rāġib, وَلَد is the one born — one or many, small or grown (he quotes Abū l-Ḥasan that it covers son and daughter) — while ابْن is a son, so called because his father “built” him, and is said of anything that comes from something.

tellApart.bs: Dijete, potomak po rođenju, sin ili kćerka, jedan ili više → وَلَد; sin; i preneseno, „sin” nečega – putnik (ابْن السَّبِيل), sinovi Ademovi → ابْن.
tellApart.en: A child, offspring by birth, son or daughter, one or many → وَلَد; a son; and figuratively the “son” of something — the traveller (ابْن السَّبِيل), the children of Adam → ابْن.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ولد, بنى
notes: ar-Rāġib (ولد): walad is the one born, said of one and many, small and grown; an adopted child is also called walad (12:21, 28:9). (بنى): ibn is from banā — the father built him; anything that comes from a thing, its nurture or its service is called its ibn (ibn as-sabīl the traveller).
ابْن sums the corpus lemmas ابْن and بُنَيّ (banū, banī, abnāʾ, bunayya): one word, which the corpus files under two lemmas. The daughter (ابْنَت, بِنْت) is not counted.
That the Quran negates a وَلَد for Allah (19:88–92) and reports the claims ابْنُ اللَّهِ only to refute them (9:30) is stated as the Quran's own word; no ayah of the claim is cited.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ولد, بنى (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): He cites يا بني آدم only for the plural, not as an extended use; his own examples are ابن حرب, ابن السبيل, ابن الليل, ابن العلم
Blind review (2026-11-06): 'son or daughter' is Abū l-Ḥasan's, quoted by ar-Rāġib; the Quran rejects offspring for Allah with وَلَد, 'son' and 'daughters' alike; 19:92 en 'a child'.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, onaj koji je rođen – jedan ili više, malo ili odraslo; navodi Ebu el-Hasena da obuhvata i sina i kćer; i posvojče se naziva وَلَد. Kur'an ovom riječju, kao i riječima „sin” i „kćeri”, odbacuje da Allah ima potomstvo.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the one born — one or many, small or grown; he quotes Abū l-Ḥasan that it covers son and daughter; an adopted child too is called وَلَد. The Quran uses this word, as well as “son” and “daughters”, to reject that Allah has offspring.

why.bs: „…ako je ostavitelj imao dijete (وَلَد)” – riječ obuhvata i sinove i kćeri.
why.en: “…if he had a child (وَلَد)” — the word covers sons and daughters alike.

why.bs: „Možda će nam od koristi biti, ili ćemo ga posiniti (نَتَّخِذَهُ وَلَدًا)” – posvojče kao وَلَد.
why.en: “Perhaps he will benefit us, or we will adopt him as a son (نَتَّخِذَهُ وَلَدًا)” — the adopted child as وَلَد.

why.bs: „A Milostivom ne priliči da ima dijete” – Allah nema potomka.
why.en: “And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful that He should take a child (وَلَد)” — Allah has no offspring.

nuance.bs: Sin. Prema ar-Rāġibu, od „graditi”: otac ga je „sagradio”. Zato se „sinom” naziva sve što od nečega potječe: putnik je „sin puta”, a učen čovjek „sin znanja”.
nuance.en: A son. According to ar-Rāġib, from “to build”: the father “built” him. So whatever comes from something is called its “son”: the traveller is the “son of the road”, and a man of learning is the “son of knowledge”.

why.bs: Dobročinstvo je dati imetak i „putniku (ابْن السَّبِيل)” – „sin puta”, preneseno.
why.en: Righteousness is to give wealth also to “the traveller (ابْن السَّبِيل)” — the “son of the road”, figuratively.

why.bs: „O sinovi Ademovi (يَا بَنِي آدَمَ)” – svi ljudi kao Ademovi potomci.
why.en: “O children of Adam (يَا بَنِي آدَمَ)” — all people as Adam's descendants.

why.bs: Nuh: „Gospodaru moj, sin moj je od moje porodice” – sin po rodu.
why.en: Noah: “My Lord, indeed my son is of my family” — a son by lineage.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o bolesti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, سَقَم je bolest samo tijela, a مَرَض može biti i u tijelu i u duši – kao u izrazu „bolest u srcima”.
shared.en: All three words speak of illness. According to ar-Rāġib, سَقَم is illness of the body alone, while مَرَض may be in the body or in the soul — as in “a disease in their hearts”.

tellApart.bs: Bolest – kao imenica u Kur'anu uvijek „u srcima”: sumnja, licemjerje, strast → مَرَض; bolesnik, tjelesno bolestan (olakšice u propisima) → مَرِيض; oboljeo samo tijelom → سَقِيم.
tellApart.en: Disease — as a noun, in the Quran always “in the hearts”: doubt, hypocrisy, desire → مَرَض; a sick person, ill in body (the allowances of the law) → مَرِيض; ill in body alone → سَقِيم.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries مرض, سقم
notes: ar-Rāġib (مرض): maraḍ is leaving the balance proper to man, of two kinds: bodily (24:61) and the vices — ignorance, cowardice, avarice, hypocrisy (2:10). (سقم): saqam is illness proper to the body, while maraḍ may be in body or soul; innī saqīm (37:89) is an allusion (taʿrīḍ), or refers to a past or coming illness, or to a slight present one, since man is never free of some ailment.
That the noun مَرَض is in all 12 of its places illness of the heart (2:10 … 74:31) is our observation of every place; the bodily sense goes with مَرِيض (2:184, 24:61, 48:17).
37:89 (Abraham) is given with ar-Rāġib's readings, none chosen; no wording that could read as a lie.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries مرض, سقم (2026-11-06): 12 attributed points confirmed

Blind review (2026-11-06): 'always in the hearts' restricted to the noun (the verb is bodily, 26:80); سَقِيم bs 'oboljeo' (not 'iscrpljen'); 37:89 quoted neutrally; 37:145 'weak and worn' given to many mufassirun.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, izlazak iz ravnoteže svojstvene čovjeku – u tijelu ili u duši (neznanje, kukavičluk, škrtost, licemjerje). Imenica مَرَض je u Kur'anu na svih 12 mjesta bolest srca.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, leaving the balance proper to man — in the body or in the soul (ignorance, cowardice, avarice, hypocrisy). The noun مَرَض is in all 12 of its Quranic places a disease of the heart.

why.bs: „U srcima njihovim je bolest, pa im Allah bolest povećava” – licemjerje kao bolest.
why.en: “In their hearts is disease, so Allah has increased their disease” — hypocrisy as disease.

why.bs: „…pa da ne bi poželio onaj u čijem je srcu bolest” – bolest srca kao strast.
why.en: “…lest he in whose heart is disease should covet” — the heart's disease as desire.

why.bs: „Ima li u srcima njihovim bolest, ili sumnjaju…?” – bolest uz sumnju.
why.en: “Is there disease in their hearts? Or have they doubted…?” — disease beside doubt.

nuance.bs: Bolesnik u tjelesnom smislu. Kur'an ga spominje uglavnom u olakšicama: bolesnik smije omrsiti post, nema mu grijeha ako izostane.
nuance.en: A sick person in the bodily sense. The Quran names him mostly in its allowances: the sick may break the fast, there is no blame on him if he stays behind.

why.bs: „A ko od vas bude bolestan ili na putu, neka isti broj dana naposti” – tjelesna bolest i olakšica.
why.en: “So whoever among you is ill or on a journey – then an equal number of other days” — bodily illness and an allowance.

why.bs: „Nije grijeh … ni bolesnome” – olakšica bolesniku.
why.en: “There is not upon … the ill any discomfort” — an allowance for the sick.

why.bs: „Nema grijeha … ni na bolesnome” ako izostane iz boja.
why.en: “There is not upon … the ill any guilt” if he stays behind from battle.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, bolest samo tijela. U Kur'anu dva puta: Ibrahimove riječi „ja sam bolestan” (37:89), koje ar-Rāġib tumači kao aluziju (تَعْرِيض), kao prošlu ili buduću bolest, ili kao malu bolest koje čovjek nikad nije sasvim lišen; i Junus izbačen na obalu bolestan (37:145).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, illness of the body alone. Twice in the Quran: Abraham's words “I am ill” (37:89), which ar-Rāġib reads as an allusion (تَعْرِيض), as a past or coming illness, or as the slight ailment no one is ever wholly free of; and Jonah cast on the shore while ill (37:145).

why.bs: Ibrahim: „Ja sam bolestan” – ar-Rāġib navodi više čitanja: aluzija, prošla ili buduća bolest, ili mala bolest.
why.en: Abraham: “Indeed, I am ill” — ar-Rāġib gives several readings: an allusion, a past or coming illness, or a slight one.

why.bs: „I Mi smo ga izbacili na pusto mjesto, a bio je bolestan” – tjelesna bolest; mnogi mufesiri dodaju da je bio slab i iznuren.
why.en: “But We threw him onto the open shore while he was ill” — bodily illness; many mufassirun add that he was weak and worn.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače ući. Prema ar-Rāġibu, دُخُول je suprotno od izlaska – u mjesto, vrijeme ili djela – a وُلُوج je ulazak u nešto tijesno.
shared.en: Both words mean to enter. According to ar-Rāġib, دُخُول is the opposite of going out — into a place, a time or deeds — while وُلُوج is entering into something narrow.

tellApart.bs: Ući – opća riječ: u grad, u Dženet, u vjeru → دَخَلَ; ući, provući se kroz tijesno, prodrijeti u nešto → وَلَجَ.
tellApart.en: To enter — the general word: a town, Paradise, the religion → دَخَلَ; to pass into something narrow, to penetrate → وَلَجَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries دخل, ولج
notes: ar-Rāġib (دخل): duḫūl is the opposite of ḫurūǧ, used of place, time and deeds. (ولج): wulūǧ is entering into a narrow place (7:40); awlaǧa of night and day (3:27) is the one lengthening into the other by the sun's rising and setting.
وَلَجَ (3×): 7:40 and 34:2 = 57:4 (what goes into the earth); the Form IV أَوْلَجَ (night into day) is another verb, not counted.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries دخل, ولج (2026-11-06): 8 attributed points confirmed
Blind review (2026-11-06): وَلَجَ bs 'provući se, prodrijeti' (ući kept for دَخَلَ); Dženet spelled as Korkut.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, suprotno od izlaska; kaže se za mjesto, vrijeme i djela. Najopćenitija riječ: ući u grad, u kuću, u Dženet, pa i u vjeru.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the opposite of going out; it is said of place, time and deeds. The most general word: entering a town, a house, Paradise, even the religion.

why.bs: „Uđite u ovaj grad” – ulazak u mjesto.
why.en: “Enter this city” — entering a place.

why.bs: „…i vidiš ljude kako u Allahovu vjeru skupinama ulaze” – ulazak u vjeru.
why.en: “…and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes” — entering a religion.

why.bs: „Uđite u njih u miru, sigurni!” – ulazak u Dženet.
why.en: “Enter it in peace, safe [and secure]” — entering Paradise.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ući u nešto tijesno. Najpoznatiji primjer: deva koja bi trebala proći kroz iglene uši – slika nemogućeg.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, entering into something narrow. The best-known case: a camel passing through a needle's eye — an image of the impossible.

why.bs: „…i neće ući u Dženet dok deva ne prođe kroz iglene uši” – دَخَلَ i وَلَجَ u istom ajetu: ulazak naspram provlačenja.
why.en: “…nor will they enter Paradise until a camel enters into the eye of a needle” — دَخَلَ and وَلَجَ in one ayah: entering against passing through.

why.bs: „Zna šta u zemlju ulazi i šta iz nje izlazi” – prodiranje u zemlju (mufesiri: kiša, sjeme, mrtvi).
why.en: “He knows what penetrates into the earth and what emerges from it” — going into the earth (mufassirun: rain, seeds, the dead).

shared.bs: Obje riječi Kur'an kaže za srca onih koji ne vjeruju. Prema ar-Rāġibu, obje su utiskivanje pečata, a طَبْع je šira: oblikovati nešto u neki lik (odatle i طَبِيعَة, narav).
shared.en: The Quran says both of the hearts of those who disbelieve. According to ar-Rāġib, both are the impress of a seal, and طَبْع is the wider: shaping a thing into a form (hence also طَبِيعَة, nature).

tellApart.bs: Zapečatiti, zatvoriti i dovršiti – pečat koji zatvara (i „pečat vjerovjesnika”) → خَتَمَ; utisnuti pečat, dati oblik – srce kojem je grijeh postao narav → طَبَعَ.
tellApart.en: To seal, close and complete — the seal that shuts (and the “seal of the prophets”) → خَتَمَ; to imprint, to give a shape — a heart for which sin has become nature → طَبَعَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ختم, طبع
notes: ar-Rāġib (ختم): ḫatm and ṭabʿ are the impress of a seal; figuratively securing a thing and barring it (2:7), and reaching the end (ḫātam an-nabiyyīn, 33:40). Allah's sealing of hearts refers to the way He has set: when a person goes to the extreme in false belief or the forbidden with no turning to the truth, it leaves in him a disposition that makes sins seem good — as if his heart were sealed (cites 16:108). (طبع): ṭabʿ is shaping a thing into a form like minting coins, more general than ḫatm and more specific than engraving; ṭabīʿa (nature) is from it; some read ṭabaʿa in 47:16 and 10:74 as soiling, like rāna (83:14).

The bs/en texts give the sealing as a consequence of the people's own persistence — ar-Rāġib's reading, and the Quran's 'because of their disbelief' (4:155). 42:24 (said to the Prophet, conditional) is not cited.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ختم, طبع (2026-11-06): 16 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): The 'soiling' reading is applied to ﴿طبع الله على قلوبهم﴾ (47:16; cf. 9:93) and ﴿كذلك نطبع على قلوب المعتدين﴾ (10:74); 4:155 (بل طبع الله عليها) is not cited; members/1/nuance (reworded): He calls ṭabīʿa an imprint on the soul (by creation or by habit) and, under ختم, says persistence leaves a disposition that makes sins seem good; he never says sin becomes the heart's nature. The fix keeps only what he says
Blind review (2026-11-06): 2:7 glossed with 2:6 as it reads (warned or not, they do not believe), not 'after they refused'.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, pečat koji zatvara i sprječava, i ono čime se nešto završava. Allah pečati srca, kaže on, po zakonu koji je postavio: kad čovjek ustraje u laži i grijehu i nikako se ne okreće istini, to mu ostavi stanje u kojem mu grijesi postanu lijepi – kao da mu je srce zapečaćeno.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the seal that shuts and bars, and that by which a thing is finished. Allah seals hearts, he says, by the way He has set: when a person persists in falsehood and sin and never turns to the truth, it leaves him in a state where sins seem good to him — as if his heart were sealed.

why.bs: „Allah je zapečatio srca njihova i sluh njihov” – slijedi nakon 2:6: opominjao ih ili ne, oni ne vjeruju.
why.en: “Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing” — follows 2:6: whether warned or not, they do not believe.

why.bs: „Danas ćemo zapečatiti usta njihova, a ruke njihove će Nam govoriti” – pečat koji sprječava govor.
why.en: “That Day, We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us” — a seal that bars speech.

why.bs: Onaj ko je strast svoju uzeo za boga – „i zapečatio mu sluh i srce” – pečat kao posljedica.
why.en: The one who takes his desire as his god — “and set a seal upon his hearing and his heart” — the seal as a consequence.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dati nečemu oblik, kao kad se kuje novac; šire je od خَتْم, a od iste riječi je i طَبِيعَة – narav. I sama narav je, kaže on, oblik utisnut u dušu, po stvaranju ili po navici; neki to razumiju i kao „zaprljati”, kao رَانَ (83:14).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, giving a thing its shape, as when coins are minted; it is wider than خَتْم, and from the same word comes طَبِيعَة, nature. Nature itself, he says, is a form imprinted on the soul, by birth or by habit; some take it as “soiled”, like رَانَ (83:14).

why.bs: „Allah im je zapečatio srca zbog nevjerovanja njihova” – uzrok je izrečen.
why.en: “Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief” — the cause is stated.

why.bs: „Tako Allah pečati srce svakog oholog nasilnika” – pečat kao posljedica oholosti.
why.en: “Thus does Allah seal over every heart [belonging to] an arrogant tyrant” — the seal as the result of arrogance.

why.bs: Zadovoljili su se da ostanu s onima koji izostaju, „i srca su im zapečaćena”.
why.en: They were satisfied to be with those who stay behind, “and their hearts were sealed over”.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o slabosti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, وَهْن je slabost tijela ili ćudi, a ضَعْف je opća suprotnost snazi – u duši, tijelu ili stanju.
shared.en: Both words speak of weakness. According to ar-Rāġib, وَهْن is a weakness of the body or of character, while ضَعْف is the general opposite of strength — in soul, body or circumstances.

tellApart.bs: Klonuti, oslabiti – posustati tijelom ili duhom (vjernicima je to zabranjeno: „ne klonite”) → وَهَنَ; slab, nemoćan – suprotno od jakog → ضَعِيف.
tellApart.en: To weaken, to lose heart — to give way in body or spirit (forbidden to the believers: “do not weaken”) → وَهَنَ; weak, powerless — the opposite of strong → ضَعِيف.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries وهن, ضعف
notes: ar-Rāġib (وهن): wahn is weakness in constitution or in character (ḫalq / ḫuluq): 19:4, 3:146, 31:14 (each time it grows in her womb, weakness upon weakness), 3:139, 4:104. (ضعف): ḍaʿf is the opposite of strength, in soul, body or state; al-Ḫalīl: ḍuʿf in the body, ḍaʿf in reason and judgement (2:282); man's weakness in 4:28 is his many needs, which the Higher Assembly does not have; Satan's plot is weak (4:76) against Allah's servants (15:42).
That وَهَنَ is forbidden to the believers in 3:139, 4:104, 47:35 (lā tahinū) is our observation of all five places; 3:146 holds both roots (wahanū, ḍaʿufū) — the verb ضَعُفَ, not the adjective.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries وهن, ضعف (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): الحال is one's condition/circumstances, not specifically social standing (notes/0 already says 'state'); members/1/nuance (reworded): الحال = condition/circumstances
Blind review (2026-11-06): 2:282 weakness of mind and judgement (al-Ḫalīl, as ar-Rāġib quotes), bs 'nerazuman'.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, slabost tijela ili ćudi. U Kur'anu: kosti koje oslabe od starosti (19:4) i duh koji klone u nevolji – vjernicima je naređeno da ne klonu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a weakness of body or of character. In the Quran: bones weakened by age (19:4) and a spirit that gives way in hardship — the believers are commanded not to lose heart.

why.bs: Zekerija: „Gospodaru moj, kosti su moje oslabile” – tjelesna slabost starosti.
why.en: Zechariah: “My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened” — the bodily weakness of age.

why.bs: „Nisu klonuli zbog onoga što ih je na Allahovom putu snašlo, niti su posustali (ضَعُفُوا)” – obje riječi u jednom ajetu.
why.en: “They never lost assurance due to what afflicted them in the cause of Allah, nor did they weaken (ضَعُفُوا)” — both words in one ayah.

why.bs: „I ne budite malodušni i ne žalostite se, a vi ste gornji” – zabrana klonuća.
why.en: “So do not weaken and do not grieve, and you will be superior” — losing heart forbidden.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, suprotno od jakog – slabost duše, tijela ili stanja. Čovjek je „stvoren slab” jer, kaže on, ima mnogo potreba; a šejtanovo lukavstvo je slabo prema Allahovim robovima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the opposite of strong — weakness of soul, body or circumstances. Man was “created weak” because, he says, he has many needs; and Satan's plot is weak against Allah's servants.

why.bs: „A čovjek je stvoren slab” – ar-Rāġib: slabost u mnoštvu potreba.
why.en: “And mankind was created weak” — ar-Rāġib: weakness in the many needs.

why.bs: „Lukavstvo šejtanovo je zaista slabo” – slabo prema onima koji vjeruju.
why.en: “Indeed, the plot of Satan has ever been weak” — weak against those who believe.

why.bs: „A ako je dužnik nerazuman ili slab…” – ar-Rāġib (po el-Halilu): ovdje slabost uma i rasuđivanja, pa za njega diktira staratelj.
why.en: “But if the one who has the obligation is of limited understanding or weak…” — ar-Rāġib (after al-Khalīl): weakness here of mind and judgement, so his guardian dictates.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače skupinu ljudi. Prema ar-Rāġibu, أُمَّة je svaka zajednica koju nešto spaja – vjera, vrijeme ili mjesto – a قَوْم je u osnovi skupina muškaraca, iako u većini Kur'ana obuhvata i žene.
shared.en: Both words mean a group of people. According to ar-Rāġib, أُمَّة is any community held together by something — a religion, a time or a place — while قَوْم is at root a group of men, though in most of the Quran it includes women too.

tellApart.bs: Zajednica spojena nečim zajedničkim – vjerom, putem, vremenom (i životinjske vrste) → أُمَّة; narod, ljudi jednog plemena; vjerovjesnikov narod („O narode moj”) → قَوْم.
tellApart.en: A community joined by something shared — faith, way, time (even animal kinds) → أُمَّة; a people, the folk of one tribe; a prophet's people (“O my people”) → قَوْم.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أم, قوم
notes: ar-Rāġib (أم): umma is every group gathered by one thing — one religion, one time or one place — whether that bond is by subjection or by choice; animals are umam (6:38), each kind on the way Allah set for it; Abraham was an umma (16:120), standing in the place of a community in worship; ʿalā umma (43:22) is a religion; baʿda umma (12:45) after a time. (قوم): qawm is at root a group of men without women (49:11), but in most of the Quran both are meant.
That قَوْم is the word of the prophets' address 'O my people' (7:59 …) is our observation. 2:213 (kāna n-nāsu ummatan wāḥida) is not cited: tafsir differs (one in guidance / in error).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries أم, قوم (2026-11-06): 17 attributed points confirmed
Blind review (2026-11-06): 3:110 bs 'ummet' (narod kept for قَوْم); 16:120 en follows ar-Rāġib; 49:11 with his reason (women named next); 13:11 bs 'ono što je u njima'.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, svaka skupina koju spaja jedna stvar – vjera, vrijeme ili mjesto – svojevoljno ili po Allahovom određenju; zato su i životinje „zajednice kao vi”. Za Ibrahima Kur'an kaže da je bio أُمَّة: sam je, kaže ar-Rāġib, stajao umjesto cijele zajednice u ibadetu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, any group joined by one thing — a religion, a time or a place — by choice or by Allah's ordering; so even animals are “communities like you”. Of Abraham the Quran says he was an أُمَّة: alone, ar-Rāġib says, he stood in place of a whole community in worship.

why.bs: „Nema životinje … a da nisu zajednice poput vas” – zajednice po vrsti i načinu života.
why.en: “There is no creature … but [they are] communities like you” — communities by kind and way of life.

why.bs: „Vi ste najbolji ummet (خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ) koji se pojavio među ljudima” – zajednica spojena vjerom.
why.en: “You are the best nation (خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ) produced for mankind” — a community joined by faith.

why.bs: „Ibrahim je bio أُمَّة, pokoran Allahu” – ar-Rāġib: sam kao cijela zajednica u ibadetu.
why.en: “Abraham was an أُمَّة, devoutly obedient to Allah” — ar-Rāġib: alone like a whole community in worship.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, u osnovi skupina muškaraca bez žena (zato 49:11 spominje i jedne i druge), ali u većini Kur'ana obuhvata i muškarce i žene. Najčešća riječ za narod kojem je poslan vjerovjesnik.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, at root a group of men without women (so 49:11 names both), but in most of the Quran it means men and women alike. The usual word for the people a prophet was sent to.

why.bs: „Neka se ljudi (قَوْم) ne rugaju ljudima … niti žene ženama” – ar-Rāġib: pošto se zatim spominju žene, ovdje قَوْم znači muškarce.
why.en: “Let not a people (قَوْم) ridicule [another] people … nor let women ridicule [other] women” — ar-Rāġib: since women are named next, here قَوْم means men.

why.bs: Nuh: „O narode moj, Allahu se klanjajte” – vjerovjesnikov narod.
why.en: Noah: “O my people, worship Allah” — a prophet's people.

why.bs: „Allah neće izmijeniti stanje jednog naroda dok oni sami ne promijene ono što je u njima.”
why.en: “Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o onima koje Allah šalje ljudima. Kur'an neke vjerovjesnike naziva i jednim i drugim imenom (19:51), a u 22:52 ih spominje odvojeno – dakle se razlikuju.
shared.en: Both words speak of those Allah sends to people. The Quran calls some prophets by both names (19:51), and in 22:52 names the two apart — so they differ.

tellApart.bs: Poslani, onaj koji nosi poruku – vjerovjesnik ili melek → رَسُول; vjerovjesnik, onaj koji donosi vijest od Allaha (a, po nekima, onaj koji je uzdignut) → نَبِيّ.
tellApart.en: One sent, the bearer of a message — a prophet or an angel → رَسُول; a prophet, one who brings news from Allah (and, for some, one raised high) → نَبِيّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رسل, نبأ, نبى, ختم
notes: ar-Rāġib (رسل): the root is going forth gently; rasūl is said of the message and of its bearer; Allah's rusul are sometimes angels (innahu la-qawlu rasūlin karīm; 11:81, 11:77, 11:69), sometimes prophets (3:144, 5:67). (نبأ): nabaʾ is news of great benefit; nubuwwa is an embassy between Allah and the rational among His servants; the nabī is so called as one who informs, and may be agent or patient (informing / informed). (نبى): some scholars derive nabī from nubuwwa, height — his rank raised above others (19:57).

The common distinction 'a rasūl brings a new law, a nabī follows an earlier one' is not ar-Rāġib's and scholars differ on it: left out. That نَبِيّ is never said of an angel in the Quran, while رُسُل is (11:81, 22:75), is our observation.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رسل, نبأ, نبى, ختم (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed
Blind review (2026-11-06): 19:51 bs 'odabran' (muḫlaṣ).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, onaj koji je poslan; riječ se kaže i za samu poruku i za onoga ko je nosi. Allahovi poslanici su ponekad meleki, a ponekad vjerovjesnici.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, one who is sent; the word is said both of the message and of the one who bears it. Allah's messengers are sometimes angels and sometimes prophets.

why.bs: „Muhammed je samo poslanik” – vjerovjesnik kao poslanik.
why.en: “Muhammad is not but a messenger” — a prophet as messenger.

why.bs: Meleki Lutu: „Mi smo izaslanici (رُسُل) Gospodara tvoga” – meleki kao poslanici.
why.en: The angels to Lot: “Indeed, we are messengers (رُسُل) of your Lord” — angels as messengers.

why.bs: „Prije tebe nismo poslali nijednog poslanika ni vjerovjesnika…” – dvije riječi navedene odvojeno.
why.en: “And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet…” — the two words named apart.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od نَبَأ – važne vijesti: vjerovjesnik obavještava od Allaha, a i sam je obaviješten; neki učenjaci, kako on navodi, riječ izvode od „uzvišenosti” (19:57). Kur'an tu riječ kaže samo za ljude, nikad za meleke.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from نَبَأ — weighty news: the prophet informs from Allah and is himself informed; some scholars, he reports, derive it from “height” (19:57). The Quran says it only of humans, never of angels.

why.bs: „On je bio odabran, i poslanik i vjerovjesnik” – Musa nazvan i jednim i drugim imenom.
why.en: “Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet” — Moses called by both names.

why.bs: „…nego je Allahov Poslanik i pečat vjerovjesnika” – ar-Rāġib: njime je vjerovjesništvo dovršeno.
why.en: “…but [he is] the Messenger of Allah and seal of the prophets” — ar-Rāġib: with him prophethood was completed.

why.bs: „Ibrahimu su najbliži … ovaj Vjerovjesnik i vjernici.”
why.en: “The most worthy of Abraham among the people are … this prophet, and those who believe.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o ružnim djelima. Prema ar-Rāġibu, فَاحِشَة je ono čija je ružnoća velika, a مُنكَر sve što zdrav razum smatra ružnim, ili šerijat kad razum zastane.
shared.en: Both words speak of foul deeds. According to ar-Rāġib, فَاحِشَة is what is grave in its ugliness, while مُنكَر is anything sound reason judges ugly, or the Sharia where reason hesitates.

tellApart.bs: Djelo ili riječ velike ružnoće, često blud i razvrat → فَاحِشَة; sve što razum ili šerijat odbacuje, suprotnost dobru (مَعْرُوف) → مُنكَر.
tellApart.en: A deed or word of grave ugliness, often fornication and lewdness → فَاحِشَة; whatever reason or the Sharia rejects, the opposite of the right (مَعْرُوف) → مُنكَر.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فحش, نكر
notes: ar-Rāġib (فحش): fuḥš, faḥšāʾ and fāḥiša are what is grave in ugliness among deeds and words (16:90, 7:28); fāḥiša mubayyina is an allusion to zinā (4:19, 65:1; likewise 4:15). (نكر): munkar is every deed sound minds judge ugly, or on which minds hesitate and the Sharia judges it ugly (3:104, 9:112, 29:29).
فَحْشَاء (7×) is another lemma of the same root and sense; it is named in the texts, not counted.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries فحش, نكر (2026-11-06): 7 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): He gives the Sharia the verdict only where reason hesitates; members/1 already says this correctly; notes/0 (reworded): The fāḥiša mubayyina he glosses is ﴿إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة﴾ (4:19 / 65:1); 4:15 (no mubayyina) is added 'likewise'. The verse he cites is الآمرون بالمعروف والناهون عن المنكر = 9:112, not 9:71 (he also cites 5:79)
Blind review (2026-11-06): 'mostly fornication' dropped: 'clear fāḥiša' is his euphemism for zinā, the word also any grave foul deed.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, djelo ili riječ čija je ružnoća velika; „očitu فَاحِشَة” on naziva ublaženim izrazom za blud. U Kur'anu se kaže za blud, za djelo Lutova naroda, ali i za svako veliko ružno djelo.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a deed or word whose ugliness is grave; a “clear فَاحِشَة” he calls a euphemism for fornication. In the Quran it is used of fornication, of the deed of Lot's people, and of any grave foul deed.

why.bs: „I ne približujte se bludu, jer je to razvrat (فَاحِشَة)” – blud kao velika ružnoća.
why.en: “And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is ever an immorality (فَاحِشَة)” — fornication as grave ugliness.

why.bs: Lut: „Zar da činite razvrat kakav prije vas niko nije učinio?”
why.en: Lot: “Do you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with?”

why.bs: Kad učine razvrat, kažu: tako smo zatekli očeve – „Allah ne naređuje razvrat (الْفَحْشَاء)”.
why.en: When they commit an immorality, they say: we found our fathers doing it — “Allah does not order immorality (الْفَحْشَاء)”.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, svako djelo koje zdrav razum smatra ružnim, ili o kojem razum zastane, pa ga šerijat proglasi ružnim. Najčešće uz مَعْرُوف: naređivati dobro i odvraćati od zla.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, every deed sound reason judges ugly, or about which reason hesitates and the Sharia then judges ugly. Most often beside مَعْرُوف: enjoining the right and forbidding the wrong.

why.bs: „…koji će … tražiti da se čini dobro, a odvraćati od zla” – مُنكَر nasuprot مَعْرُوف.
why.en: “…inviting to [all that is] good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong” — مُنكَر against مَعْرُوف.

why.bs: „…i zabranjuje razvrat (الْفَحْشَاء) i zlo (الْمُنكَر) i nasilje” – obje riječi u jednom ajetu.
why.en: “…and forbids immorality (الْفَحْشَاء) and bad conduct (الْمُنكَر) and oppression” — both words in one ayah.

why.bs: Oni koji izgovore zihar „govore ružne riječi (مُنكَرًا) i neistinu” – i riječ može biti مُنكَر.
why.en: Those who pronounce ẓihār “are saying an objectionable statement (مُنكَرًا) and a falsehood” — a word too can be مُنكَر.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o dobru koje čovjek čini. Prema ar-Rāġibu, بِرّ je širina u činjenju dobra, a إِحْسَان je davanje više nego što se duguje – iznad pravde.
shared.en: Both words speak of the good a person does. According to ar-Rāġib, بِرّ is breadth in doing good, while إِحْسَان is giving more than one owes — above justice.

tellApart.bs: Čestitost, širina u dobru – u vjerovanju i djelima (2:177) → بِرّ; činiti dobro drugome, i činiti lijepo – više od dužnog (uz pravdu u 16:90) → إِحْسَان.
tellApart.en: Righteousness, breadth in goodness — in belief and in deeds (2:177) → بِرّ; doing good to others and doing things well — more than what is due (beside justice in 16:90) → إِحْسَان.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بر, حسن
notes: ar-Rāġib (بر): from barr, land as against sea, came the sense of breadth: birr is breadth in doing good; ascribed to Allah (52:28) and to the servant; two kinds, in belief and in deeds, both in 2:177; birr to parents is breadth in iḥsān to them. (حسن): iḥsān is of two kinds — doing good to another, and doing one's own work well; it is wider than inʿām; it is above justice (16:90): justice is giving what one owes and taking what one is owed, iḥsān giving more and taking less; justice is obligatory, iḥsān recommended.
That إِحْسَان is the word for treatment of parents in 2:83, 4:36, 6:151, 17:23, 46:15 is our observation of its places.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries بر, حسن (2026-11-06): 13 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): He glosses birr from Allah as الثواب (reward) and from the servant as الطاعة (obedience); 'beneficence, as befits Him' is not his wording
Blind review (2026-11-06): بِرّ in bs 'čestitost' (Korkut 2:177), dobročinstvo kept for إِحْسَان; 3:92 al-birr also as the reward (many mufassirun).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od بَرّ (kopno, širina): širina u činjenju dobra – i u vjerovanju i u djelima, kako ih nabraja 2:177. Kad se kaže za Allaha (الْبَرّ, 52:28), znači Njegovu nagradu, kao što od roba znači pokornost.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from بَرّ (land, wide space): breadth in doing good — in belief and in deeds, as 2:177 lists them. Said of Allah (الْبَرّ, 52:28) it means His reward, as from the servant it means obedience.

why.bs: „Nije čestitost u tome da okrećete lica svoja prema istoku i zapadu, nego…” – vjerovanje i djela zajedno.
why.en: “Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but…” — belief and deeds together.

why.bs: „Nećete postići čestitost dok ne udijelite od onoga što volite” – mnogi mufesiri الْبِرّ ovdje shvataju i kao nagradu u Dženetu.
why.en: “Never will you attain righteousness (البِرّ) until you spend from that which you love” — many mufassirun also understand البِرّ here as the reward of Paradise.

why.bs: „I pomažite jedni drugima u čestitosti i bogobojaznosti” – بِرّ uz takvu.
why.en: “And cooperate in righteousness and piety” — بِرّ beside taqwā.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, na dva načina: činiti dobro drugome, i lijepo obaviti svoj posao. Iznad je pravde: pravda je dati koliko se duguje i uzeti koliko pripada, a إِحْسَان dati više i uzeti manje. Kur'an njime opisuje odnos prema roditeljima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, in two ways: doing good to another, and doing one's own work well. It is above justice: justice is giving what one owes and taking what one is owed, إِحْسَان giving more and taking less. The Quran uses it for how one treats parents.

why.bs: „Allah naređuje pravednost i dobročinstvo” – ar-Rāġib: إِحْسَان je iznad pravde.
why.en: “Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct” — ar-Rāġib: إِحْسَان is above justice.

why.bs: „…i da roditeljima dobročinstvo činite” – إِحْسَان prema roditeljima.
why.en: “…and to parents, good treatment” — إِحْسَان towards parents.

why.bs: „Zar je nagrada za dobro išta drugo do dobro?”
why.en: “Is the reward for good [anything] but good?”

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o šteti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, ضُرّ je loše stanje čovjeka – u duši, tijelu ili imetku – a أَذًى je ono što živo biće pogodi od štete; u 3:111 أَذًى je ono malo što će ih pogoditi, a ne prava šteta.
shared.en: Both words speak of harm. According to ar-Rāġib, ضُرّ is a bad state of a person — in soul, body or means — while أَذًى is harm that reaches a living being; in 3:111 أَذًى is the little that will reach them, not real harm.

tellApart.bs: Nevolja, teško stanje – bolest, siromaštvo, gubitak (ono što Allah otklanja) → ضُرّ; uznemiravanje, uvreda, povreda – često riječima ili postupcima drugih → أَذًى.
tellApart.en: Adversity, a bad state — illness, poverty, loss (what Allah removes) → ضُرّ; hurt, annoyance, injury — often from others' words or deeds → أَذًى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ضر, أذى
notes: ar-Rāġib (ضر): ḍurr is a bad state — in the soul (little knowledge, virtue, chastity), in the body (a lost or defective limb), or in outward circumstances (little wealth or standing); 21:84 may hold all three; 3:111 lan yaḍurrūkum illā aḏā tells them how little will reach them and assures them against real harm. (أذى): aḏā is harm reaching a living being, in soul, body or what follows from it, worldly or otherworldly (2:264, 9:61, 33:69, 2:222).
3:111 holds the verb ضَرَّ, not the noun ضُرّ; it is cited for أَذًى. Ayyub's plea (21:83) is cited through 21:84 (Allah's removing it).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ضر, أذى (2026-11-06): 13 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): He comments on this verse only; he does not state as a rule that aḏā is the lesser term; members/0/nuance (reworded): He says loss of a limb and deficiency, not illness. The 'touches … Allah removes' sentence is unattributed (he does cite مس and كشف verses)
Blind review (2026-11-06): 'mostly' softened to 'often' (ḍurr is also the harm idols cannot do).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, loše stanje – u duši (malo znanja i vrline), u tijelu (gubitak uda, nedostatak) ili u prilikama (siromaštvo, nizak položaj). U Kur'anu je to često nevolja koja „dotakne” čovjeka, i koju Allah otklanja.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a bad state — in the soul (little knowledge and virtue), in the body (a lost limb, a defect) or in one's circumstances (poverty, low standing). In the Quran it is often adversity that “touches” a person, and which Allah removes.

why.bs: „A kad čovjeka nevolja snađe, On Nam se moli … a čim ga oslobodimo nevolje, on nastavi” – nevolja i zaborav nakon nje.
why.en: “And when affliction touches man, he calls upon Us … but when We remove from him his affliction, he continues” — adversity, and forgetting after it.

why.bs: „Pa smo mu se odazvali i otklonili nevolju koja ga je snašla” – ar-Rāġib: Ejjubova nevolja može obuhvatiti sve tri vrste.
why.en: “So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity” — ar-Rāġib: Job's adversity may cover all three kinds.

why.bs: „Ako ti Allah dade kakvu nevolju, niko je osim Njega ne može otkloniti.”
why.en: “And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, šteta koja pogodi živo biće – u duši, tijelu ili posljedicama, na ovom ili budućem svijetu. Često dolazi od drugih: prigovaranje uz sadaku, uvrede upućene vjerovjesnicima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, harm that reaches a living being — in soul, body or consequences, in this world or the next. Often it comes from others: reproach that follows charity, insults aimed at the prophets.

why.bs: „Oni vam ne mogu nauditi, osim malo uznemiravanja (أَذًى)” – ar-Rāġib: malo će vas od njih pogoditi.
why.en: “They will not harm you except for [some] annoyance (أَذًى)” — ar-Rāġib: little will reach you from them.

why.bs: „Ne kvarite svoje sadake prigovaranjem i uvredom (الْأَذَى)” – povreda riječima.
why.en: “Do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury (الْأَذَى)” — hurt by words.

why.bs: „Pitaju te o mjesečnom pranju. Reci: „To je neugodnost (أَذًى)”” – ar-Rāġib: po šerijatu i po medicini.
why.en: “They ask you about menstruation. Say, “It is harm (أَذًى)”” — ar-Rāġib: by the Sharia and by medicine.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o tome da je čovjek oboren. Prema ar-Rāġibu, i poniznost (ذُلّ) i sramota (خِزْي) mogu doći od samog čovjeka ili od drugoga: za poniznost: od sebe je pohvalna, nametnuta od drugog pokuđena.
shared.en: All three words speak of a person brought low. According to ar-Rāġib, both lowliness (ذُلّ) and shame (خِزْي) may come from the person himself or from another: for lowliness, from oneself it is praised, imposed by another it is blamed.

tellApart.bs: Poniženje koje je nametnuto, kazna → ذِلَّة; poniznost – pohvalna kad je od sebe (prema roditeljima), pokuđena kad je nametnuta (42:45) → ذُلّ; sramota, osramoćenost pred drugima → خِزْي.
tellApart.en: Abasement imposed, a punishment → ذِلَّة; lowliness — praised when one's own (towards parents), blamed when imposed (42:45) → ذُلّ; disgrace, being shamed before others → خِزْي.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ذل, خزى, جنح, ولى
notes: ar-Rāġib (ذل): ḏull (with ḍamma) is from subjugation, ḏill (with kasra) is after unruliness, without subjugation (tameness); 17:24 janāḥa ḏ-ḏull: be as one subdued before them; ḏilla in 2:61, 7:152, 10:27; lowliness a person takes on himself is praised (5:54, 3:123). (خزى): ḫizy is a brokenness that comes over a man, either from himself — excessive shame (ḫazāya) — or from another — a kind of disgrace (ḫizy) (2:114, 16:27, 39:26); likewise ḏull and hūn: from oneself praised, from another blamed.

20:134 (an naḏilla wa naḫzā) holds both roots as verbs, not the members' nouns; named in the text only. 17:111 (Allah has no protector out of weakness) is cited with 'as befits Him' implicit in the negation.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries ذل, خزى, جنح, ولى (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): Praise/blame is stated for ḏull and hūn (by analogy with ḫizy), not for ḫizy itself; ḫizy from oneself is 'excessive shame', never called praised; members/2/nuance (reworded): He defines the other-inflicted kind as 'a kind of being slighted / held in contempt' (istiḫfāf); 'disgraced' is close but looser. The Quranic-usage sentence is not attributed

Blind review (2026-11-06): praise/blame tied to the source, not to ذُلّ (42:45 is imposed); 10:27 'humiliation will overtake them' (the faces are covered by night); 'far from Allah' limited to weakness and need (17:111); 42:45 bs 'nepravednici'.

nuance.bs: Poniženje koje je nametnuto – u Kur'anu kazna: „udaren im je biljeg poniženja”, „stići će ih poniženje”.
nuance.en: Abasement that is imposed — in the Quran a punishment: “humiliation was stamped upon them”, “humiliation will overtake them”.

why.bs: „I na njih je pao biljeg poniženja i bijede” – poniženje kao kazna.
why.en: “And they were covered with humiliation and poverty” — abasement as punishment.

why.bs: „…stići će ih poniženje” – poniženje kao kazna za one koji su činili zlo.
why.en: “…humiliation will overtake them” — abasement as the punishment of those who did evil.

why.bs: „Stići će ih srdžba Gospodara njihova i poniženje u životu na ovom svijetu.”
why.en: “Those who took the calf will obtain anger from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, poniznost je pohvalna kada je čovjek sam uzme na sebe – kao prema roditeljima: „spusti nad njima krilo poniznosti”, budi pred njima kao savladan, kaže on. Allah je daleko od svake slabosti: ne treba Mu zaštitnik zbog nemoći (17:111).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, lowliness is praised when a person takes it on himself — as towards parents: “lower to them the wing of humility”, be before them as one subdued, he says. Allah is far above any weakness: He needs no protector out of lowliness (17:111).

why.bs: „I budi prema njima pažljiv i ponizan (جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ)” – pohvalna poniznost.
why.en: “And lower to them the wing of humility (جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ) out of mercy” — praised lowliness.

why.bs: Nepravednici izvedeni pred Vatru, „ponizni od poniženja” – nametnuta poniznost.
why.en: The wrongdoers brought before the Fire, “humbled from humiliation” — imposed lowliness.

why.bs: „…niti Mu treba zaštitnik zbog slabosti (مِنَ الذُّلِّ)” – Allah je slobodan od svake slabosti.
why.en: “…and has no [need of a] protector out of weakness (مِنَ الذُّلِّ)” — Allah is free of all weakness.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, slomljenost koja čovjeka obuzme – od sebe (pretjeran stid) ili od drugoga (prezir drugih). U Kur'anu najčešće sramota kao kazna, na ovom svijetu i na onom.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a brokenness that comes over a person — from himself (excessive shame) or from another (being treated with contempt). In the Quran it is mostly disgrace as punishment, in this world and the next.

why.bs: „Njih na ovom svijetu čeka sramota, a na onom svijetu patnja velika.”
why.en: “For them in this world is disgrace, and they will have in the Hereafter a great punishment.”

why.bs: „I Allah im je dao da iskuse sramotu u životu na ovom svijetu.”
why.en: “So Allah made them taste disgrace in worldly life.”

why.bs: „Danas je sramota i zlo na nevjernicima” – sramota na Sudnjem danu.
why.en: “Indeed disgrace, this Day, and evil are upon the disbelievers” — disgrace on the Day.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o onome što se vidi u snu. U Kur'anu je رُؤْيَا uvijek istinit san koji se ostvari, a kao „snovi” أَحْلَام dolazi samo u izrazu „zbrkani snovi” (12:44, 21:5).
shared.en: Both words speak of what is seen in sleep. In the Quran رُؤْيَا is always a true dream that comes to pass, while as “dreams” أَحْلَام comes only in “confused dreams” (12:44, 21:5).

tellApart.bs: San koji se vidi i ima značenje – u Kur'anu uvijek istinit → رُؤْيَا; snovi (samo u izrazu „zbrkani snovi”), a ista riječ znači i punoljetnost i, preneseno, razum → حُلُم.
tellApart.en: What is seen in sleep and has a meaning — in the Quran always true → رُؤْيَا; dreams (only in “confused dreams”), and the same word also means maturity and, by extension, minds → حُلُم.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رأى, حلم
notes: ar-Rāġib (رأى): ruʾyā is what is seen in sleep; he quotes the report that nothing of the heralds of prophethood remains but the ruʾyā, and cites 48:27, 17:60.
