(حلم): ḥilm is restraint of the soul from rage; aḥlāmuhum (52:32) was explained as their minds — ḥilm is not reason itself but one of its fruits; al-ḥulum (24:59) is maturity; ḥalama is to see in a dream (12:44).

That رُؤْيَا is in all its places a true dream (12:5, 12:43, 12:100, 17:60, 37:105, 48:27) and أَحْلَام only the deniers' or courtiers' 'confused dreams' is our observation of all places. The lemma حُلُم (6×) holds dream (12:44 ×2, 21:5), maturity (24:58, 24:59) and minds (52:32).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رأى, حلم (2026-11-06): 11 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): The report as he quotes it says only 'al-ruʾyā'; 'true' is added. The Quranic-usage sentence is not attributed to him; members/1/nuance (improved): He derives 'minds' and 'maturity' from ḥilm with stated reasons, but lists 'to dream' without deriving it from self-restraint; he also stresses ḥilm is not reason itself. The 'confused dreams' sentence is Quranic usage, unattributed; members/1/ayat/2/why (improved): He reports the gloss ('qīla') and qualifies it: ḥilm is not reason itself but an effect of it

Blind review (2026-11-06): 'only in confused dreams' limited to the dream sense (52:32 is minds); 'reason' as ḥilm's source, not ḥilm itself; 'meaning not recognised' replaced by who says the phrase (12:44, 21:5).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što se vidi u snu; navodi predanje da od nagovještaja vjerovjesništva nije ostalo ništa osim sna (ruʾyā). U Kur'anu je رُؤْيَا svaki put san koji se ostvari: Jusufov, vladarev, Ibrahimov, Poslanikov.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what is seen in sleep; he cites the report that nothing of the heralds of prophethood remains but the dream (ruʾyā). In the Quran every رُؤْيَا comes to pass: Joseph's, the king's, Abraham's, the Prophet's.

why.bs: „Sinko moj, ne kazuj svoj san braći svojoj” – Jusufov san, koji se ostvario (12:100).
why.en: “O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers” — Joseph's dream, fulfilled in 12:100.

why.bs: Vladar: „Protumačite mi san moj, ako snove znate tumačiti” – san sa značenjem.
why.en: The king: “Explain to me my vision, if you should interpret visions” — a dream with a meaning.

why.bs: „Ti si san već ostvario” – Ibrahimov san.
why.en: “You have fulfilled the vision” — Abraham's dream.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, iz korijena koji znači savladavanje sebe od srdžbe: „razum” (52:32), jer blagost proizlazi iz razuma, i „punoljetnost” (24:59), kad čovjek postane dostojan blagosti; isti korijen daje i „sanjati”. Kao snovi, u Kur'anu dolazi samo u izrazu „zbrkani snovi”, koji govore oni što odbacuju viđenje (12:44) ili objavu (21:5).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from a root meaning self-restraint from anger: “minds” (52:32), since forbearance springs from reason, and “maturity” (24:59), when one becomes worthy of forbearance; the same root gives “to dream”. As dreams it comes in the Quran only in “confused dreams”, said by those who dismiss a vision (12:44) or the revelation (21:5).

why.bs: „To su zbrkani snovi (أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ), a mi snove ne znamo tumačiti” – dvorjani o vladarevom istinitom snu.
why.en: “[It is but] a mixture of false dreams (أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ), and we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams” — the courtiers on the king's true dream.

why.bs: „A kad djeca vaša stignu do punoljetnosti (الْحُلُم)…” – ista riječ za punoljetnost.
why.en: “And when the children among you reach puberty (الْحُلُم)…” — the same word for maturity.

why.bs: „Zar im to naređuje njihov razum (أَحْلَامُهُم)?” – ar-Rāġib: tumači se kao razum, jer blagost proizlazi iz razuma.
why.en: “Or do their minds (أَحْلَامُهُم) command them to [say] this?” — ar-Rāġib: explained as their minds, since forbearance springs from reason.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o oduzimanju života. Prema ar-Rāġibu, قَتْل je najopćenitija riječ za to, a ذَبْح je presijecanje grla.
shared.en: Both words speak of taking life. According to ar-Rāġib, قَتْل is the most general word for it, while ذَبْح is cutting the throat.

tellApart.bs: Ubiti – na bilo koji način, kao nečije djelo → قَتَلَ; zaklati, presjeći grlo (najčešće životinju) → ذَبَحَ.
tellApart.en: To kill — in any way, as someone's act → قَتَلَ; to slaughter, to cut the throat (most often of an animal) → ذَبَحَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قتل, ذبح
notes: ar-Rāġib (قتل): qatl is removing the spirit from the body, like death; called qatl when seen as someone's act, mawt when seen as the loss of life (3:144); in 5:95 He said qatl, not ḏabḥ or ḏakāh, because qatl is the most general of these words — taking a game animal's life in any way is forbidden. (ذبح, headed without any mark in OpenITI; the parser lists it by its opening words): ḏabḥ is cutting animals' throats (2:67, 37:107); yuḏabbiḥūna (2:49) is intensive — slaughtering one after another.
ذَبَحَ (Form I, 5×) is counted; the intensive ذَبَّحَ (2:49, 14:6, 28:4, Pharaoh's killing of the sons) is another verb, named in the text only.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries قتل, ذبح (2026-11-06): 13 attributed points confirmed
Blind review (2026-11-06): ذَبَحَ also names Pharaoh's slaughter of the sons (2:49), which ar-Rāġib cites.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, oduzeti dušu tijelu, kao smrt; kaže se قَتْل kad se gleda kao nečije djelo, a „smrt” kad se gleda kao gubitak života. To je najopćenitija riječ za ubijanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, removing the soul from the body, like death; it is called قَتْل when seen as someone's act, and death when seen as the loss of life. It is the most general word for killing.

why.bs: „Pa zar ako on umre ili bude ubijen…” – ar-Rāġib: smrt kao gubitak života, ubistvo kao nečije djelo.
why.en: “So if he was to die or be killed…” — ar-Rāġib: death as loss of life, killing as someone's act.

why.bs: „Ne ubijajte divljač dok ste u ihramu” – ar-Rāġib: rečeno قَتْل, a ne „klanje”, jer je opće – zabranjen je svaki način.
why.en: “Do not kill game while you are in the state of iḥrām” — ar-Rāġib: قَتْل, not slaughter, because it is general — every way is forbidden.

why.bs: „Ko ubije nekoga ko nije ubio … kao da je sve ljude poubijao.”
why.en: “Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul … it is as if he had slain mankind entirely.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, presjeći grlo životinji. U Kur'anu: krava koju je Allah naredio da se zakolje; Ibrahimov san da kolje sina – a Allah ga je otkupio velikom žrtvom (37:107); i faraonovi ljudi koji „kolju sinove vaše” (2:49), što ar-Rāġib shvata kao klanje koje se ponavlja, jedno za drugim.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, cutting an animal's throat. In the Quran: the cow Allah ordered slaughtered; Abraham's dream of sacrificing his son — whom Allah ransomed with a great sacrifice (37:107); and Pharaoh's men “slaughtering your sons” (2:49), which ar-Rāġib takes as slaughter repeated, one after another.

why.bs: „Allah vam naređuje da zakoljete kravu” – klanje životinje.
why.en: “Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow” — slaughtering an animal.

why.bs: „Sinko moj, u snu sam vidio da te koljem” – Ibrahimov san; sin je otkupljen (37:107).
why.en: “O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you” — Abraham's dream; the son was ransomed (37:107).

why.bs: Sulejman o pupavcu: „…ili ću ga zaklati, ili neka mi donese jasan dokaz” – klanje kao kazna.
why.en: Solomon of the hoopoe: “…or slaughter him, unless he brings me clear authorization” — slaughter as a penalty.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o obavezi koja se mora ispuniti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, عَهْد je čuvanje i paženje nečega iznova i iznova, a مِيثَاق je ugovor učvršćen zakletvom i zavjetom.
shared.en: Both words speak of a bond that must be kept. According to ar-Rāġib, عَهْد is guarding and attending to a thing again and again, while مِيثَاق is a pact made firm by oath and pledge.

tellApart.bs: Zavjet, obaveza koju treba čuvati – Allahova i ljudska → عَهْد; čvrsti ugovor, učvršćen zakletvom (s vjerovjesnicima, sa sinovima Israilovim, u braku) → مِيثَاق.
tellApart.en: A pledge, a bond to be kept — Allah's and people's → عَهْد; a firm covenant, sealed by oath (with the prophets, the Children of Israel, in marriage) → مِيثَاق.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عهد, وثق
notes: ar-Rāġib (عهد): ʿahd is keeping and attending to a thing time after time; the binding pledge is called ʿahd (17:34); Allah's ʿahd is sometimes what He set in our minds, sometimes what He commanded in the Book and through His messengers, sometimes what we take upon ourselves, like vows (9:75). (وثق, headed without any mark in OpenITI; the parser lists it by its opening words): mīṯāq is a pact confirmed by oath and pledge (3:81, 33:7, 4:154).
2:27 and 13:20 hold both words. 2:124 (lā yanālu ʿahdī) is not cited: tafsir differs on what the ʿahd is there.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.
ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries عهد, وثق (2026-11-06): 10 attributed points confirmed
Blind review (2026-11-06): مِيثَاق in bs 'čvrst ugovor' (zavjet kept for عَهْد).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, čuvanje i paženje nečega iznova i iznova; zato se zavjet koji se mora paziti zove عَهْد. Allahov zavjet je ono što je usadio u razum, ono što je naredio Knjigom i poslanicima, i ono što ljudi sami preuzmu, kao zavjet.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, keeping and attending to a thing time after time; so a pledge that must be watched over is called عَهْد. Allah's pledge is what He set in the mind, what He commanded by the Book and the messengers, and what people take upon themselves, like a vow.

why.bs: „I ispunjavajte obavezu (الْعَهْد), jer će se za obavezu odgovarati.”
why.en: “And fulfil [every] commitment (الْعَهْد). Indeed, the commitment is ever [that about which one will be] questioned.”

why.bs: „Koji krše Allahov zavjet (عَهْد) nakon što su ga čvrsto prihvatili (مِيثَاق)” – obje riječi zajedno.
why.en: “Who break the covenant (عَهْد) of Allah after contracting it (مِيثَاق)” — both words together.

why.bs: „A ko od Allaha bolje ispunjava zavjet svoj?”
why.en: “And who is truer to his covenant than Allah?”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ugovor učvršćen zakletvom i zavjetom. Kur'an ga koristi za Allahov ugovor s vjerovjesnicima, sa sinovima Israilovim, i za brak – „čvrsti ugovor” (4:21).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a pact confirmed by oath and pledge. The Quran uses it for Allah's covenant with the prophets, with the Children of Israel, and for marriage — “a solemn covenant” (4:21).

why.bs: „I kad je Allah uzeo čvrst ugovor (مِيثَاق) od vjerovjesnika…” – ugovor s vjerovjesnicima.
why.en: “And when Allah took the covenant (مِيثَاق) of the prophets…” — the pact with the prophets.

why.bs: „…a one su od vas uzele čvrst ugovor (مِيثَاقًا غَلِيظًا)” – brak kao čvrst ugovor.
why.en: “…and they have taken from you a solemn covenant (مِيثَاقًا غَلِيظًا)” — marriage as a firm pact.

why.bs: „Oni koji ispunjavaju Allahov zavjet i ne krše ugovor” – عَهْد i مِيثَاق jedno uz drugo.
why.en: “Those who fulfil the covenant of Allah and do not break the contract” — عَهْد and مِيثَاق side by side.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi su optužbe kojima su poricatelji nazivali Poslanika, a Kur'an ih odbacuje: vrača i pjesnika (52:29, 69:41–42), dok čarobnjak „neće uspjeti” (20:69).
shared.en: All three words are charges the deniers laid against the Prophet, and the Quran rejects them: the soothsayer and the poet (52:29, 69:41–42), while the magician “will not succeed” (20:69).

tellApart.bs: Onaj ko obmanjuje oči opsjenom ili traži pomoć šejtana → سَاحِر; vrač koji tvrdi da zna skriveno nagađanjem → كَاهِن; pjesnik – a po nekima, u toj optužbi: onaj ko izmišlja → شَاعِر.
tellApart.en: One who deceives the eye with illusion or seeks the devils' help → سَاحِر; a soothsayer who claims hidden knowledge by guessing → كَاهِن; a poet — and for some scholars, in that charge: a teller of fictions → شَاعِر.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سحر, كهن, شعر
notes: ar-Rāġib (سحر): siḥr is said of deception and illusions without reality (7:116, 20:66) — in this sense Moses was called sāḥir (43:49) — of seeking the devils' help by drawing near to them (2:102), and of what the ignorant believe — changing forms and natures — which has no reality. (كهن): the kāhin tells hidden past matters by a kind of guessing, the ʿarrāf future ones; both rest on guessing that errs and hits. (شعر): shiʿr is at root fine knowledge, then measured rhymed speech; many mufassirun took 'poet' as a charge of bringing verse; some careful scholars say they charged him with lying, as shiʿr stands for falsehood (26:224).
That all three are the deniers' charges against the Prophet (and sāḥir also against Moses, 43:49), each refuted, is the Quran's own word; the texts present them as charges only.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries سحر, كهن, شعر (2026-11-06): 18 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): He attaches 'in this view they called Moses a sāḥir' to the FIRST sense (deception, illusion, sleight of hand), not to the third (the ignorant's belief in transformation). Fix key 'en' applies to this plain-string note; members/0/ayat/2/why (improved): 'This view' refers to the first sense he lists — deception, illusions without reality, like the juggler's sleight of hand
Blind review (2026-11-06): 'the Quran rejects each' made precise: soothsayer and poet (52:29, 69:41–42), the magician 'will not succeed' (20:69).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, sihr je opsjena bez stvarnosti, ili traženje pomoći šejtana; a vjerovanje da sihr mijenja oblike stvari nema stvarnosti. Poricatelji su tako zvali i Musaa i Poslanika; Kur'an kaže da čarobnjak nikad neće uspjeti.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, sorcery is illusion without reality, or seeking the devils' help; the belief that it changes the forms of things has no reality. The deniers called both Moses and the Prophet by this name; the Quran says the magician will never succeed.

why.bs: „A čarobnjak neće uspjeti, ma gdje bio” – sihr bez stvarne moći.
why.en: “And the magician will not succeed wherever he is” — sorcery without real power.

why.bs: Nevjernici o Poslaniku: „Ovo je zaista pravi čarobnjak!” – optužba koju Kur'an odbacuje.
why.en: The disbelievers of the Prophet: “Indeed, this is an obvious magician” — a charge the Quran rejects.

why.bs: Faraonovi ljudi Musau: „O čarobnjače, zamoli Gospodara svoga za nas” – ar-Rāġib: tako su ga zvali u smislu opsjene i vještine ruku.
why.en: Pharaoh's people to Moses: “O magician, invoke for us your Lord” — ar-Rāġib: they called him so in the sense of illusion and sleight of hand.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, onaj ko kazuje skrivene prošle stvari nekom vrstom nagađanja (a عَرَّاف buduće); obje vještine počivaju na nagađanju koje nekad pogodi, a nekad promaši. U Kur'anu dva puta, oba puta odbačena optužba.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, one who tells hidden past matters by a kind of guessing (the عَرَّاف tells future ones); both crafts rest on guessing that sometimes hits and sometimes misses. Twice in the Quran, both times a rejected charge.

why.bs: „Ti, milošću Gospodara svoga, nisi ni vrač ni lud.”
why.en: “By the favour of your Lord, you are not a soothsayer or a madman.”

why.bs: „Niti su riječi vrača – kako vi malo razmišljate!”
why.en: “Nor the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, شِعْر u osnovi znači tanano znanje, a zatim odmjeren i rimovan govor. Mnogi mufesiri optužbu „pjesnik” razumiju kao optužbu da je Kur'an stih; neki učenjaci kažu da su ga time nazvali lažovom, jer je poezija mjesto izmišljanja (26:224).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, شِعْر at root means fine knowledge, then measured, rhymed speech. Many mufassirun take the charge “poet” as calling the Quran verse; some scholars say they meant to call him a liar, since poetry is the home of invention (26:224).

why.bs: „I nisu to riječi pjesnika – kako vi malo vjerujete!”
why.en: “And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe.”

why.bs: „…ne, on je to izmislio, ne, on je pjesnik” – optužbe se nižu jedna za drugom.
why.en: “…rather, he has invented it; rather, he is a poet” — the charges follow one another.

why.bs: „A pjesnike slijede zalutali” – ar-Rāġib: odatle veza poezije i izmišljanja.
why.en: “And the poets – [only] the deviators follow them” — ar-Rāġib: hence poetry's link to invention.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o nedostatku razboritosti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, جَهْل je neznanje, pogrešno vjerovanje ili postupanje kako ne treba, a سَفَه je lakoća duše zbog manjka razuma.
shared.en: Both words speak of a lack of sound judgement. According to ar-Rāġib, جَهْل is not knowing, wrong belief or acting as one should not, while سَفَه is a lightness of soul from lack of reason.

tellApart.bs: Neznalica – onaj ko ne zna, ili postupa kako ne treba (najčešće kao prijekor) → جَاهِل; lakouman, nerazborit – u imetku ili u vjeri → سَفِيه.
tellApart.en: One who does not know, or behaves as one should not (mostly as blame) → جَاهِل; light-minded, without sound judgement — in wealth or in religion → سَفِيه.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries جهل, سفه
notes: ar-Rāġib (جهل): jahl has three kinds — the soul empty of knowledge; believing a thing other than it is; doing a thing other than it should be done, whatever one believes (2:67: mockery counted as jahl); the jāhil is mostly named in blame, sometimes not (2:273: one who does not know their state). (سفه): safah is lightness in the body, then lightness of soul from lack of reason, in worldly matters (4:5) and in religion (72:4, 2:13, 2:142).
25:63 (the ignorant addressing the servants of the Merciful) is the rude-behaviour sense, glossed as such. 7:199 is cited in aarada-tawalla, not here.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries جهل, سفه (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): He illustrates worldly safah with 4:5 but does not mention squandering
Blind review (2026-11-06): 72:4 bs 'bezumnik' (neznalica kept for جَاهِل) and 'preko svake mjere'; 4:5 bs 'nerazumnima'.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, neznanje je trojako: neznanje, pogrešno vjerovanje, i postupanje kako ne treba – zato Musa podsmijeh naziva neznanjem. Riječ najčešće kudi, ali ne uvijek: u 2:273 „neznalica” je samo onaj ko ne poznaje stanje siromaha.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ignorance is of three kinds: not knowing, believing wrongly, and acting as one should not — so Moses calls mockery ignorance. The word mostly blames, but not always: in 2:273 the “ignorant” is simply one who does not know the poor's state.

why.bs: Musa: „Utječem se Allahu da ne budem od neznalica” – ar-Rāġib: podsmijeh kao neznanje.
why.en: Moses: “I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant” — ar-Rāġib: mockery as ignorance.

why.bs: „Ko ih ne poznaje, misli da su imućni” – neznalica bez prijekora.
why.en: “An ignorant [person] would think them self-sufficient” — the ignorant without blame.

why.bs: „…a kad im se neznalice obrate, odgovaraju: „Mir!”” – neznanje kao grubo ponašanje.
why.en: “…and when the ignorant address them [harshly], they say [words of] peace” — ignorance as rude behaviour.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, u osnovi lakoća (i tijela), a zatim lakoća duše zbog manjka razuma – u svjetovnim stvarima (kojima se ne predaje imetak, 4:5) i u vjeri. Licemjeri su vjernike zvali سُفَهَاء, a Kur'an kaže da su to oni sami.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, at root lightness (even of the body), then lightness of soul from lack of reason — in worldly matters (those not to be given wealth, 4:5) and in religion. The hypocrites called the believers سُفَهَاء, and the Quran says they themselves are.

why.bs: „I ne dajite nerazumnima (السُّفَهَاء) imetke svoje” – nerazboritost u imetku.
why.en: “And do not give the weak-minded (السُّفَهَاء) your property” — unsoundness in handling wealth.

why.bs: „Zar da vjerujemo kao što vjeruju bezumnici?” Zaista su oni bezumnici” – optužba vraćena licemjerima.
why.en: “Should we believe as the foolish have believed?” Unquestionably, it is they who are the foolish” — the charge turned back on the hypocrites.

why.bs: Džini: „Bezumnik naš je o Allahu govorio preko svake mjere” – lakoumnost u vjeri.
why.en: The jinn: “Our foolish one has been saying about Allah an excessive transgression” — foolishness in religion.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o brzini. Prema ar-Rāġibu, عَجَلَة je tražiti nešto prije njegova vremena – dolazi od strasti, pa je pokuđena u većini Kur'ana – a سُرْعَة je samo suprotnost sporosti.
shared.en: All three words speak of speed. According to ar-Rāġib, عَجَلَة is seeking a thing before its time — it springs from desire, so it is blamed in most of the Quran — while سُرْعَة is simply the opposite of slowness.

tellApart.bs: Požuriti, prije vremena → عَجِلَ; tražiti da nešto dođe brže (poricatelji traže kaznu) → اِسْتَعْجَلَ; hitati, natjecati se u brzini – hvaljeno ili kuđeno po cilju → سَارَعَ.
tellApart.en: To hurry, before the time → عَجِلَ; to ask for a thing to come sooner (the deniers demanding the punishment) → اِسْتَعْجَلَ; to hasten, to vie in speed — praised or blamed by its goal → سَارَعَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عجل, سرع
notes: ar-Rāġib (عجل): ʿaǧala is seeking a thing and pursuing it before its time; it comes from desire, so it is blamed in most of the Quran (21:37, 20:114, 20:83, 16:1, 13:6, 10:11); Moses' haste (20:84), though haste is blamed, was moved by a praised thing — seeking Allah's pleasure; 'man was created of haste' (21:37) means it is one of the traits he is made with. (سرع): surʿa is the opposite of slowness; sāriʿū (3:133), yusāriʿūna fi l-ḫayrāt (3:114).
That سَارَعَ is praised or blamed by its goal — good deeds and forgiveness (3:114, 3:133, 21:90, 23:61) or disbelief and sin (3:176, 5:41, 5:52, 5:62) — is our observation of all nine places.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

meaning.en: to hasten, to be in haste

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, tražiti nešto prije njegova vremena; dolazi od strasti, pa je u većini Kur'ana pokuđeno. Musaova žurba ka Allahu (20:84) je, kaže on, bila žurba, ali ju je pokrenulo nešto hvale vrijedno – traženje Allahova zadovoljstva.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, seeking a thing before its time; it comes from desire, so in most of the Quran it is blamed. Moses' haste to Allah (20:84) was, he says, haste, but what moved it was praiseworthy — seeking Allah's pleasure.

why.bs: Musa: „Požurio sam k Tebi, Gospodaru moj, da budeš zadovoljan” – ar-Rāġib: žurba s hvale vrijednim povodom.
why.en: Moses: “I hastened to You, my Lord, that You be pleased” — ar-Rāġib: haste with a praised motive.

why.bs: „I ne žuri s Kur'anom prije nego što ti se objavljivanje završi” – ne prije vremena.
why.en: “And do not hasten with [recitation of] the Quran before its revelation is completed to you” — not before its time.

why.bs: „Zato ne žuri protiv njih, Mi im samo dane brojimo” – sve ima svoj rok.
why.en: “So be not impatient over them. We only count out to them a [limited] number” — everything has its term.

meaning.en: to ask to hasten, to be impatient for

nuance.bs: Tražiti da nešto dođe prije vremena. U Kur'anu najčešće poricatelji koji podrugljivo traže da kazna dođe odmah.
nuance.en: To ask for a thing to come before its time. In the Quran most often the deniers mockingly demanding that the punishment come at once.

why.bs: „Allahova odluka dolazi, zato je ne požurujte!”
why.en: “The command of Allah is coming, so be not impatient for it.”

why.bs: „I traže od tebe da kazna što prije dođe” – poricatelji požuruju kaznu.
why.en: “And they urge you to hasten the punishment” — the deniers hurrying the punishment.

why.bs: Salih: „O narode moj, zašto požurujete zlo prije dobra?”
why.en: Ṣāliḥ: “O my people, why are you impatient for evil before good?”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, سُرْعَة je suprotnost sporosti, za tijela i za djela. Kur'an hvali hitanje ka oprostu i dobrim djelima, a kudi hitanje u nevjerovanje i grijeh – vrijednost daje cilj.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, سُرْعَة is the opposite of slowness, said of bodies and of acts. The Quran praises hastening to forgiveness and good deeds and blames hastening into disbelief and sin — the goal gives it its worth.

why.bs: „I nastojte da zaslužite oprost Gospodara svoga” (doslovno: hitajte ka oprostu) – hvaljeno hitanje.
why.en: “And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord” — praised hastening.

why.bs: „Takvi se trude da što više dobra urade i oni će u tome druge preteći.”
why.en: “It is those who hasten to good deeds, and they outstrip [others] therein.”

why.bs: „I vidiš mnoge od njih kako se natječu u grijehu i nasilju” – kuđeno hitanje.
why.en: “And you see many of them hastening into sin and aggression” — blamed hastening.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o uspjehu. Prema ar-Rāġibu, فَوْز je postići dobro i pri tome ostati siguran, a فَلَاح je postići ono čemu se teži – na ovom ili na budućem svijetu.
shared.en: Both words speak of success. According to ar-Rāġib, فَوْز is attaining good while being kept safe, while فَلَاح is attaining what one strives for — in this world or the next.

tellApart.bs: Postići dobro uz spas (od Vatre) – „veliki uspjeh” → فَوْز; uspjeti, postići cilj – na dunjaluku ili na ahiretu → أَفْلَحَ.
tellApart.en: To win the good while kept safe (from the Fire) — “the great attainment” → فَوْز; to prosper, to reach one's aim — in this world or the next → أَفْلَحَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فوز, فلح
notes: ar-Rāġib (فوز): fawz is winning the good together with safety (85:11, 4:13, 33:71); one moved away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has won (3:185); in 4:73 the hypocrites count their booty a great fawz. (فلح): falḥ is splitting (the farmer is fallāḥ); falāḥ is winning and reaching one's aim, worldly — life, wealth, honour — or otherworldly: lasting without end, wealth without poverty, honour without humiliation, knowledge without ignorance; in 20:64 Pharaoh's magicians most likely meant worldly success.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries فوز, فلح (2026-11-06): 17 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): He calls it 'al-fawz al-kabīr' (the great triumph), contrasting death seen from this world vs. the Hereafter; no superlative. The 'most often with great' sentence is Quranic usage, unattributed
Blind review (2026-11-06): فَوْز bs 'pobjeda, dobitak' (uspjeti kept for أَفْلَحَ); 91:9 bs without 'samo'; 23:1 'above all the Hereafter'; Dženet.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, postići dobro i pri tome ostati siguran; veliki je uspjeh biti udaljen od Vatre i uveden u Dženet. Riječ najčešće dolazi s „velik”: الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيم.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, winning the good while being kept safe; the great triumph is to be moved from the Fire and admitted to Paradise. The word most often comes with “great”: الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيم.

why.bs: „Njih čekaju dženetske bašče … – to je uspjeh veliki.”
why.en: “For them will be gardens … That is the great attainment.”

why.bs: „…a i Allahovo zadovoljstvo je veće – to je uspjeh veliki.”
why.en: “…but approval from Allah is greater. It is that which is the great attainment.”

why.bs: Licemjer: „Da sam bio s njima, postigao bih uspjeh veliki” – ar-Rāġib: plijen koji oni smatraju uspjehom.
why.en: The hypocrite: “Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could have attained a great attainment” — ar-Rāġib: booty they count as triumph.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od „cijepati” (zemljoradnik je فَلَّاح): postići ono čemu se teži. Uspjeh je dvojak: dunjalučki – život, imetak, ugled – i ahiretski: trajanje bez nestanka, bogatstvo bez siromaštva, ugled bez poniženja, znanje bez neznanja.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from “to split” (the farmer is فَلَّاح): reaching what one strives for. Success is twofold: worldly — life, wealth, honour — and otherworldly: lasting without end, wealth without poverty, honour without humiliation, knowledge without ignorance.

why.bs: „Uspjeli su vjernici” – uspjeh, prije svega ahiretski.
why.en: “Certainly will the believers have succeeded” — success, above all that of the Hereafter.

why.bs: „Uspio je onaj ko je očisti” – uspjeh kroz čišćenje duše.
why.en: “He has succeeded who purifies it” — success through purifying the soul.

why.bs: Faraonovi čarobnjaci: „Danas će uspjeti onaj ko pobijedi” – ar-Rāġib: najvjerovatnije dunjalučki uspjeh.
why.en: Pharaoh's magicians: “And he has succeeded today who overcomes” — ar-Rāġib: most likely worldly success.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače da skriveno postaje vidljivo ili poznato. Razlikuju se po onome što se otkriva i po tome čemu se suprotstavljaju.
shared.en: All three words mean that something hidden becomes seen or known. They differ in what is disclosed and in what each is set against.

tellApart.bs: Pokazati ono što je bilo u duši ili pokriveno → أَبْدَى; izvesti na vidjelo, a u Kur'anu najčešće dati prevlast ili dati da se sazna → أَظْهَرَ; javno činiti, nasuprot tajnom → أَعْلَنَ.
tellApart.en: To show what was in the soul or covered → أَبْدَى; to bring out into view, in the Quran mostly to make prevail or to let be known → أَظْهَرَ; to do openly, as against in secret → أَعْلَنَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بدا, ظهر, علن
notes: ar-Rāġib (بدا): badā is to appear plainly (ẓahara ẓuhūran bayyinan); he gives no separate remark on the Form IV ibdāʾ. (ظهر): ẓahara is at root a thing being on the back (surface) of the earth so that it is not hidden, as against baṭana, being in its belly; then used of anything prominent, seen by sight or by insight; 9:33 li-yuẓhirahu may be from emergence or from helping and overpowering — 'to make it prevail'; 72:26 lā yuẓhiru = He does not let anyone see (His unseen); 30:18 tuẓhirūna = entering the time of noon. (علن): ʿalāniya is the opposite of sirr, said mostly of meanings rather than of concrete things.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 14 / 7 / 12 places read): أَبْدَى is paired with أَخْفَى or كَتَمَ in most places (2:271, 2:284, 3:29, 4:149, 5:99, 24:29, 33:54) and is also said of the visible (adornment 24:31, the private parts 7:20); أَظْهَرَ means 'to make prevail' in 9:33, 48:28, 61:9, 'to let know' in 66:3 and 72:26, 'make appear' in 40:26, and in 30:18 'at noon'; every one of the 12 أَعْلَنَ places sets it against a secret counterpart (أَسَرَّ, أَخْفَى, أَكَنَّ).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 of 4 claims flagged, fixed: 'in one's hands' for أَبْدَى dropped (no ayah shows it); 72:26 now his 'lets no one become aware of it', not 'let see'; 40:26 bs keeps 'make appear'.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries بدا, ظهر, علن (2026-11-06): 13 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/2/nuance (reworded): He gives no examples of 'meanings'; the list words/intentions/deeds is ours

nuance.bs: Od badā – pojaviti se jasno, kako ga opisuje ar-Rāġib. U kur'anskoj upotrebi najčešće stoji nasuprot skrivanju (أَخْفَى, كَتَمَ): pokazati ono što je u duši ili što se daje javno, a i ono što je pokriveno, kao ukras ili stidna mjesta.
nuance.en: From badā, to appear plainly, as ar-Rāġib describes it. In Quranic usage it mostly stands against hiding (أَخْفَى, كَتَمَ): to show what is in the soul or what one gives openly, and also what is covered, such as adornment or the private parts.

why.bs: „Bilo da pokažete ono što je u vašim dušama ili to sakrijete, Allah će vas za to pitati” – pokazati nasuprot skriti.
why.en: “Whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it” — showing set against concealing.

why.bs: „Ako javno dajete milostinju (doslovno: ako je pokažete), lijepo je to, a ako je sakrijete i date siromasima, to vam je bolje.”
why.en: “If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you.”

why.bs: Vjernice „neka ne pokazuju svoje ukrase, osim onoga što se vidi” – pokazati ono što je pokriveno.
why.en: Believing women “should not expose their adornment except that which [necessarily] appears thereof” — showing what is covered.

meaning.en: to bring to light, to make prevail

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ẓahara je izvorno biti na površini zemlje, pa se ne skriva, nasuprot baṭana – biti u njenoj utrobi; zatim sve što je istaknuto pogledu ili uvidu. U Kur'anu أَظْهَرَ najčešće znači dati prevlast (9:33) ili dati da se sazna (66:3, 72:26).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ẓahara is at root being on the surface of the earth, so not hidden, as against baṭana, being in its belly; then anything prominent to sight or to insight. In the Quran أَظْهَرَ mostly means to make prevail (9:33) or to let be known (66:3, 72:26).

why.bs: „Da ga uzdigne iznad svih vjera” – ar-Rāġib: može biti od pojavljivanja, ili od pomaganja i nadvladavanja, tj. da prevlada.
why.en: “To manifest it over all religion” — ar-Rāġib: it may be from appearing, or from helping and overpowering, i.e. to make it prevail.

why.bs: „On zna nevidljivi svijet i ne otkriva nikome Svoju tajnu” – ar-Rāġib: ne daje nikome da ga dozna.
why.en: “[He is] Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His [knowledge of the] unseen to anyone” — ar-Rāġib: He lets no one become aware of it.

why.bs: Faraon se boji da Musa ne učini da se „nered pojavi na Zemlji” – učiniti da se nešto pojavi.
why.en: Pharaoh fears that Moses will “cause corruption to appear in the land” — making a thing appear.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, javnost (عَلَانِيَة) je suprotnost tajni (سِرّ), i to se najčešće kaže za značenja, a ne za konkretne stvari. U Kur'anu svih dvanaest puta stoji uz svoju suprotnost: ono što se tajno krije.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, openness (عَلَانِيَة) is the opposite of secrecy (سِرّ), and is said mostly of meanings rather than of concrete things. In the Quran all twelve times it stands beside its opposite: what is kept secret.

why.bs: „Allah zna ono što tajite i ono što javno činite.”
why.en: “And Allah knows what you conceal and what you declare.”

why.bs: Nuh: „Zatim sam ih javno pozivao, a i u tajnosti sam ih pozivao” – javno nasuprot tajno; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Noah: “Then I announced to them and [also] confided to them secretly” — openly against secretly; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Ibrahim: „Gospodaru naš, Ti zaista znaš ono što krijemo i ono što javno iznosimo.”
why.en: Abraham: “Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare.”

shared.bs: Sve četiri riječi znače skupinu ljudi. Prema ar-Rāġibu, svaka je gleda s druge strane: po čvrstini, po odvojenosti, po dijelu cjeline i po onima koji nekoga osnažuju i od njega se šire.
shared.en: All four words mean a group of people. According to ar-Rāġib, each sees it from another side: its toughness, its separation, its being a part of a whole, and those who strengthen someone and spread out from him.

tellApart.bs: Skupina sa čvrstinom, tabor (Allahova stranka, šejtanova stranka, saveznici) → حِزْب; skupina odvojena od drugih → فَرِيق; dio neke cjeline, i od ljudi i od stvari → طَائِفَة; pristaše koji nekoga osnažuju i slijede njegov put → شِيعَة.
tellApart.en: A group with toughness, a camp (the party of Allah, of Satan, the confederates) → حِزْب; a group set apart from others → فَرِيق; a portion of a whole, of people or of things → طَائِفَة; followers who strengthen someone and keep to his way → شِيعَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حزب, فرق, طوف, شيع
notes: ar-Rāġib (حزب): ḥizb is a group with toughness (ġilaẓ); al-aḥzāb in 33:20–22 are those gathered to fight the Prophet; ḥizb Allāh (5:56) = Allah's helpers. (فرق): farīq is a group separated from others (al-jamāʿa al-mutafarriqa ʿan āḫarīn), with 42:7, 3:78, 2:85, 2:146. (طوف): ṭāʾifa of people is a group of them, and of a thing a piece of it; on 9:122 'some said' it can apply to one and more (49:9, 3:122). (شيع): the root is spreading and strengthening; šīʿa are those by whom a man is strengthened and who spread out from him (37:83, 28:15, 28:4, 15:10, 54:51).
The corpus files the plurals with their singulars (أَحْزَاب under حِزْب; شِيَع, أَشْيَاع under شِيعَة); the duals الْحِزْبَيْن, الْفَرِيقَيْن, طَائِفَتَان are counted too.
37:83: 'his' šīʿa is Nūḥ's by most mufassirun (the previous ayat speak of him); a minority refer it to the Prophet Muhammad — so the why says 'Nuh's, by most mufassirun'.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حزب, فرق, طوف, شيع (2026-11-06): 22 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): He says šīʿa strengthen a man and spread out from him; 'follow' is not his. 'Each sees it from another side' is our synthesis of four separate definitions, acceptable

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, skupina u kojoj ima čvrstine (غِلَظ). Množina الْأَحْزَاب su saveznici okupljeni protiv Poslanika (33:22); „Allahova stranka” su, kaže on, Allahovi pomagači, a Kur'an spominje i „šejtanovu stranku”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a group with toughness (غِلَظ) in it. The plural الْأَحْزَاب are the confederates gathered against the Prophet (33:22); “the party of Allah” are, he says, Allah's helpers, and the Quran also speaks of “the party of Satan”.

why.bs: „Allahova stranka će zacijelo pobijediti” – ar-Rāġib: Allahovi pomagači.
why.en: “Indeed, the party of Allah – they will be the predominant” — ar-Rāġib: Allah's helpers.

why.bs: „Oni su šejtanova stranka; šejtanova stranka će zacijelo nastradati.”
why.en: “Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan – they will be the losers.”

why.bs: „A kad su vjernici vidjeli saveznike (الْأَحْزَاب)…” – skupine okupljene za borbu protiv Poslanika.
why.en: “And when the believers saw the companies (الْأَحْزَاب)…” — the groups gathered to fight the Prophet.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, skupina koja se odvojila od drugih – od korijena f-r-q, rastaviti. Zato se često kaže u parovima i podjelama: jedni ovako, drugi onako.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a group separated from others — from the root of parting. So it often comes in pairs and divisions: some this way, others that.

why.bs: „Jedni će u Džennet, a drugi u oganj” (doslovno: jedna skupina…, druga skupina…) – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “A party will be in Paradise and a party in the Blaze” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Neki od njih (فَرِيقًا) uvijaju jezicima svojim dok čitaju Knjigu” – jedna skupina izdvojena od ostalih.
why.en: “And indeed, there is among them a party who alter the Scripture with their tongues” — one group singled out from the rest.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od ljudi – skupina od njih, a od stvari – njen komad; dakle dio neke cjeline. On navodi da neki kažu da se riječ može odnositi i na jednog čovjeka i više.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, of people a group of them, and of a thing a piece of it — a portion of a whole. He reports that some say the word can apply to one person and more.

why.bs: „Zašto iz svake zajednice (فِرْقَة) ne bi otišao po jedan dio (طَائِفَة) da nauče vjeru?” – dio od cjeline; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “For there should separate from every division of them a group [remaining] to obtain understanding in the religion” — a part of a whole; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ako se dvije skupine vjernika sukobe, izmirite ih” – dva dijela iste zajednice.
why.en: “And if two factions among the believers should fight, then make settlement between the two” — two parts of one community.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen znači širenje i jačanje; شِيعَة su oni kojima se čovjek osnaži i koji se od njega šire. Otuda i pristaše nekog puta, a u množini (شِيَع) – zajednice podijeljene na sljedbe.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root means spreading and strengthening; شِيعَة are those by whom a man is strengthened and who spread out from him. Hence the adherents of a way, and in the plural (شِيَع) communities split into sects.

why.bs: „A od njegovih sljedbenika bio je i Ibrahim” – po većini mufesira, Nuhovih: istog puta i vjere.
why.en: “And indeed, among his kind was Abraham” — by most mufassirun, Noah's: of the same way and faith.

why.bs: Musa zateče dvojicu kako se tuku: „jedan je bio od njegovih, a drugi od njegovih neprijatelja” – pristaša nasuprot neprijatelju.
why.en: Moses found two men fighting: “one from his faction and one from among his enemy” — a follower as against a foe.

why.bs: „Od onih koji su vjeru svoju razjedinili i u sljedbe se podijelili (شِيَعًا) – svaka stranka (حِزْب) radosna onim što ima.”
why.en: “[Or] of those who have divided their religion and become sects, every faction rejoicing in what it has.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače dobro koje Allah daje. Prema ar-Rāġibu, نِعْمَة je dobro stanje u kojem se čovjek nađe, a فَضْل je ono što je preko onoga što je dovoljno – dar koji davalac nije dužan dati.
shared.en: Both words mean the good Allah gives. According to ar-Rāġib, نِعْمَة is the good state a person finds himself in, while فَضْل is what goes beyond what suffices — a gift the giver is not bound to give.

tellApart.bs: Dobro stanje, blagodat koja se uživa i koja se ne može izbrojati → نِعْمَة; višak, dar iz dobrote preko dužnog, i ono što se trudom stječe → فَضْل.
tellApart.en: The good state, a favour enjoyed and beyond counting → نِعْمَة; the surplus, a gift of bounty beyond what is due, and what is sought by effort → فَضْل.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نعم, فضل
notes: ar-Rāġib (نعم): niʿma is the good state (al-ḥāla al-ḥasana), its pattern that of a state like jilsa; as a genus it is said of little and much (14:34, 2:40, 5:3); inʿām is bringing good to another, said only when the receiver is a rational being. (فضل): faḍl is excess over what suffices, praised or blamed, mostly of the praised; every gift that is not binding on the giver is faḍl (4:32, 57:21, 10:58); 'that you may seek faḍl from your Lord' means wealth and what is earned.
The corpus files the plurals نِعَم / أَنْعُم under نِعْمَة. That فَضْل is often 'sought' (اِبْتَغَى فَضْلًا) of trade and earning — 2:198, 62:10, 73:20 — is our observation of its places.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 of 3 flagged, fixed: 5:3 and 10:58 now say what they show; 62:10 'earning and trade' given to the mufassirun.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نعم, فضل (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): He glosses one phrase (li-tabtaġū faḍlan min rabbikum), not every 'seeking of faḍl'; 4:32 'ask Allah of His faḍl' he files under the non-binding gift

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dobro stanje u kojem se čovjek nalazi; kao rod kaže se i za malo i za mnogo. Glagol أَنْعَمَ je, kaže on, ukazati dobro drugome, a kaže se samo kad je primalac razumno biće.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the good state a person is in; as a genus it is said of little and of much. The verb أَنْعَمَ is, he says, to bring good to another, and is said only when the receiver is a rational being.

why.bs: „Ako biste Allahove blagodati brojali, ne biste ih nabrojali” – jednina kao rod: sva dobra stanja.
why.en: “And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them” — the singular as a genus: every good state.

why.bs: „Danas sam vam vjeru vašu usavršio i blagodat Svoju prema vama upotpunio” – blagodat kao dobro stanje koje Allah upotpunjuje; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you” — favour as the good state Allah brings to completion; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, višak preko onoga što je dovoljno; svaki dar koji davalac nije dužan dati zove se فَضْل. U „da tražite فَضْل od svoga Gospodara” to je, kaže on, imetak i ono što se stječe.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the surplus over what suffices; every gift the giver is not bound to give is called فَضْل. In “that you may seek فَضْل from your Lord” it is, he says, wealth and what is earned.

why.bs: „I molite Allaha za Njegovu dobrotu” – dar koji On nije dužan dati; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And ask Allah of His bounty” — a gift He is not bound to give; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „…raziđite se po zemlji i tražite Allahovu dobrotu” – mufesiri to tumače kao traženje opskrbe zaradom i trgovinom.
why.en: “…disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah” — the mufassirun explain this as seeking provision, by earning and trade.

why.bs: „Reci: ‘Allahovoj dobroti i Njegovoj milosti, tome neka se raduju!’” – dobrota kao dar od Allaha preko dužnog; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Say, ‘In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy – in that let them rejoice’” — bounty as a gift from Allah beyond what is due; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače vlast nad nečim. Prema ar-Rāġibu, مُلْك je raspolaganje stvarju po svom sudu, a pravi i trajni pripada Allahu; سُلْطَان je moć da se nadvlada – a i dokaz, jer navaljuje na srca.
shared.en: Both words mean power over something. According to ar-Rāġib, مُلْك is controlling a thing by one's rule, and the true, lasting one belongs to Allah; سُلْطَان is the power to overpower — and also proof, since it storms the hearts.

tellApart.bs: Vladavina, carstvo: raspolagati onim čime se vlada; pravo i trajno samo Allahovo → مُلْك; moć da se nadvlada, ovlast nad nekim; i dokaz koji nadvladava → سُلْطَان.
tellApart.en: Dominion, kingship: control of what one rules; the true and lasting one only Allah's → مُلْك; the power to overpower, authority over someone; and proof that prevails → سُلْطَان.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ملك, سلط
notes: ar-Rāġib (ملك): mulk is the controlling (ḍabṭ) of a thing one disposes of by rule; milk (ownership) is like the genus of mulk — every mulk is milk, not every milk is mulk; the true and lasting mulk is Allah's (64:1, 3:26); he also cites 4:54 'a great kingdom' for Abraham's family. (سلط): salāṭa is the power to overpower; sulṭān is said of that power (17:33, 16:99–100, 55:33), more often of the one who holds it; proof is called sulṭān for how it assails hearts (40:35, 14:10, 4:144); 69:29 may bear both senses.
69:29 (sulṭāniyah) is left out: ar-Rāġib himself says it may mean either power or proof.

He also limits it: its hold is mostly over believers of knowledge and wisdom (dropped); members/1/nuance (reworded): Same as shared: hujūm = assailing/storming

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, raspolaganje stvarju po svom sudu i vlasti; svako مُلْك je posjedovanje, ali svako posjedovanje nije مُلْك. Pravo i trajno مُلْك pripada Allahu, a On ga daje kome hoće.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the controlling of a thing by one's rule; every مُلْك is ownership, but not every ownership is مُلْك. The true and lasting مُلْك belongs to Allah, and He gives it to whom He wills.

why.bs: „Reci: ‘O Allahu, Vladaru carstva, Ti daješ carstvo kome hoćeš i oduzimaš ga od koga hoćeš’” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Say, ‘O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will’” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Njegovo je carstvo i Njemu pripada hvala” – pravo i trajno carstvo.
why.en: “To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs [all] praise” — the true and lasting dominion.

why.bs: „…i dali smo im veliko carstvo” – carstvo koje Allah daje ljudima; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “…and conferred upon them a great kingdom” — dominion that Allah gives to people; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od سَلَاطَة – moći da se nadvlada: سُلْطَان je ta moć, a češće onaj ko je ima. Dokaz se, kaže on, zove سُلْطَان jer navaljuje na srca – mada najviše djeluje na ljude znanja i mudrosti među vjernicima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from سَلَاطَة, the power to overpower: سُلْطَان is that power, and more often the one who holds it. Proof, he says, is called سُلْطَان because it storms the hearts — though its force falls mostly on the people of knowledge and wisdom among the believers.

why.bs: „On (šejtan) nema nikakve moći nad onima koji vjeruju i koji se na Gospodara svoga oslanjaju.”
why.en: “Indeed, there is for him [Satan] no authority over those who have believed and rely upon their Lord.”

why.bs: „A ko bude ubijen nepravedno, njegovom nasljedniku smo dali ovlast” – ovlast kao moć; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And whoever is killed unjustly – We have given his heir authority” — authority as power; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Pa donesite nam neki jasan dokaz!” – سُلْطَان kao dokaz.
why.en: “So bring us a clear authority” — سُلْطَان as proof.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o predanosti drugome. Prema ar-Rāġibu, ibadet je krajnja poniznost i zaslužuje ga samo Allah, dok je pokornost (طَاعَة) najčešće slijeđenje naredbe; u Kur'anu se pokornost duguje i Poslaniku.
shared.en: Both words speak of yielding to another. According to ar-Rāġib, worship is the utmost humbling, which only Allah deserves, while obedience (طَاعَة) is mostly said of following a command; in the Quran obedience is owed to the Messenger too.

tellApart.bs: Krajnja poniznost – ibadet, koji pripada samo Allahu → عَبَدَ; pokoriti se, poslušati naredbu (Allahovu, Poslanikovu, ali i drugih) → أَطَاعَ.
tellApart.en: The utmost humbling — worship, which belongs only to Allah → عَبَدَ; to comply, to obey a command (Allah's, the Messenger's, but also others') → أَطَاعَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries عبد, طوع
notes: ar-Rāġib (عبد): ʿubūdiyya is showing humbleness; ʿibāda is more intense, the utmost humbling, deserved only by the One of utmost favour, Allah (17:23 'that you worship none but Him'); ʿibāda is of two kinds: by subjection (taṣḫīr) and by choice, the latter of rational beings, the one commanded (2:21). (طوع): ṭawʿ is compliance, its opposite compulsion (41:11, 3:83); ṭāʿa is like it but said mostly of carrying out what is commanded and keeping to what is prescribed (4:80).
That أَطَاعَ also takes the Messenger and 'those in authority among you' (4:59), and that obeying parents is limited where they call to shirk (29:8, 31:15), is our observation of Quranic usage.

al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

Plain-string note: fix given under 'en'

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ibadet je krajnja poniznost, jača od pukog robovanja, i zaslužuje ga samo Onaj čija je dobrota najveća – Allah. Ibadet je, kaže on, dvojak: onaj iz potčinjenosti, kojim Allahu služi sve, i onaj po izboru, koji je naređen razumnim bićima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, worship is the utmost humbling, stronger than mere servitude, and only the One whose favour is greatest deserves it — Allah. Worship, he says, is of two kinds: by subjection, by which all things serve Allah, and by choice, which is commanded to rational beings.

why.bs: „Samo Tebi ibadet činimo i samo od Tebe pomoć tražimo” – ibadet pripada samo Allahu.
why.en: “It is You we worship and You we ask for help” — worship belongs to Allah alone.

why.bs: „O ljudi, ibadet činite Gospodaru svome” – ibadet po izboru, koji je naređen.
why.en: “O mankind, worship your Lord” — worship by choice, the kind that is commanded.

why.bs: „Gospodar tvoj je odredio da samo Njemu ibadet činite” – ar-Rāġib: zato što ga zaslužuje samo Allah.
why.en: “And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him” — ar-Rāġib: because only Allah deserves it.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ṭawʿ je pristajanje, a suprotno mu je prisila; طَاعَة je isto, ali se najčešće kaže za izvršavanje naredbe i držanje propisanog. U Kur'anu se pokornost duguje Allahu i Poslaniku, i onima koji su nadležni, a roditeljima ne kad pozivaju na širk.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ṭawʿ is compliance, its opposite compulsion; طَاعَة is the same but said mostly of carrying out a command and keeping to what is prescribed. In the Quran obedience is owed to Allah and the Messenger, and to those in authority, but not to parents when they call to shirk.

why.bs: „Pokoravajte se Allahu i pokoravajte se Poslaniku i nadležnima između vas” – pokornost i ljudima, za razliku od ibadeta.
why.en: “Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you” — obedience to people too, unlike worship.

why.bs: „Ko se pokorava Poslaniku, pokorava se i Allahu” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “He who obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A ako te budu nagovarali da Meni drugog ravnim smatraš… ti ih ne slušaj” – granica pokornosti roditeljima.
why.en: “But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them” — the limit of obedience to parents.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače ustezanje imetka. Prema ar-Rāġibu, بُخْل je zadržavanje onoga što se ne smije zadržati, a شُحّ je škrtost spojena s pohlepom, kao trajna narav.
shared.en: Both words mean holding back one's goods. According to ar-Rāġib, بُخْل is withholding what should not be withheld, while شُحّ is stinginess joined with greed, as a settled habit.

tellApart.bs: Škrtariti: zadržati ono što treba dati (glagol) → بَخِلَ; čin škrtosti, u Kur'anu i kad se drugima naređuje → بُخْل; škrtost s pohlepom, koja je postala navika duše → شُحّ.
tellApart.en: To be stingy: to withhold what should be given (the verb) → بَخِلَ; the act of stinginess, in the Quran also when urged on others → بُخْل; stinginess with greed, grown into the soul's habit → شُحّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بخل, شح
notes: ar-Rāġib (بخل): buḵl is withholding possessions from where they should not be withheld, its opposite jūd (generosity); baḵīl is one who does it much; buḵl is of two kinds, with one's own possessions and with others', the latter more blameworthy — his proof 4:37 / 57:24 'who are stingy and enjoin stinginess on people'. (شح): šuḥḥ is buḵl with greed (ḥirṣ), in what has become habit (4:128, 59:9 / 64:16, 33:19).

The noun بُخْل (2×) is a member of its own beside the verb, since its two places carry ar-Rāġib's point about enjoining stinginess. The corpus files أَشِحَّة (33:19) under شُحّ. That the noun شُحّ is the soul's in all three of its places (4:128, 59:9, 64:16) is our observation.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 of 3 flagged, fixed: tellApart now follows him — شُحّ is the habitual one, بُخْل the act.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, zadržati imetak ondje gdje ga ne treba zadržati; suprotno mu je darežljivost. U Kur'anu se najčešće kaže za uskraćivanje onoga što je Allah dao iz Svoje dobrote.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to withhold possessions where they should not be withheld; its opposite is generosity. In the Quran it is mostly said of holding back what Allah has given of His bounty.

why.bs: „Neka ne misle oni koji škrtare onim što im je Allah iz obilja Svoga dao da je to dobro za njih; ne, to je zlo za njih.”
why.en: “And let not those who [greedily] withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty ever think that it is better for them. Rather, it is worse for them.”

why.bs: „A ko škrtari, škrtari na svoju štetu” – uskraćivanje se vraća onome ko uskraćuje.
why.en: “And whoever withholds only withholds [benefit] from himself” — the withholding returns on the one who withholds.

nuance.bs: Imenica, u Kur'anu samo dvaput, oba puta u istom izrazu: oni koji škrtare i ljudima škrtost naređuju. Prema ar-Rāġibu, škrtost s tuđim imetkom je teža od škrtosti sa svojim, i za to navodi upravo ovaj ajet.
nuance.en: The noun, only twice in the Quran, both times in the same phrase: those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess on people. According to ar-Rāġib, stinginess with others' possessions is worse than with one's own, and this is the very ayah he gives for it.

why.bs: „Oni koji škrtare i od ljudi traže da budu škrti, i kriju ono što im je Allah od obilja Svoga dao.”
why.en: “Who are stingy and enjoin upon [other] people stinginess and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty.”

why.bs: „Oni koji škrtare i od drugih traže da budu škrti” – isti izraz, drugi put.
why.en: “[Those] who are stingy and enjoin upon people stinginess” — the same phrase, the second time.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, škrtost spojena s pohlepom (حِرْص), u onome što je postalo navika. U kur'anskoj upotrebi imenica je sva tri puta lakomost duše: duše su joj sklone, a uspješan je onaj ko je od nje sačuvan.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, stinginess joined with greed (حِرْص), in what has become habit. In Quranic usage the noun is all three times the soul's avarice: souls are prone to it, and successful is the one kept from it.

why.bs: „A duše su sklone lakomosti” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And present in [human] souls is stinginess” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A oni koji budu sačuvani od lakomosti duše svoje – ti su ti koji će uspjeti.”
why.en: “And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul – it is those who will be the successful.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače ono što je loše. Prema ar-Rāġibu, شَرّ je ono što svi izbjegavaju, kao što je dobro (خَيْر) ono što svi žele; سُوء je sve što čovjeka ožalosti, i ružno djelo.
shared.en: Both words mean what is bad. According to ar-Rāġib, شَرّ is what everyone shuns, as good (خَيْر) is what everyone desires; سُوء is whatever grieves a person, and a foul deed.

tellApart.bs: Zlo, protivnost dobru (خَيْر): ono što svi izbjegavaju → شَرّ; ono što ožalosti – na ovom i na onom svijetu, u duši, tijelu i imetku – i ružno djelo → سُوء.
tellApart.en: Evil, the counterpart of good (خَيْر): what everyone shuns → شَرّ; what grieves — in this world and the next, in soul, body and property — and a foul deed → سُوء.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries شر, سوأ
notes: ar-Rāġib (شر): šarr is what all shun, as ḵayr is what all desire (25:34, 8:22). (سوأ): sūʾ is everything that grieves a person, of worldly and otherworldly matters, of inner and bodily states and of external ones such as loss of wealth, standing or a dear one; 20:22 'without sūʾ' = without blemish, explained (fussira) as leprosy; 4:123 'whoever does sūʾ' = a foul deed; sūʾ al-ḥisāb, sūʾ ad-dār.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): شَرّ is paired with خَيْر in many places (21:35, 17:11, 99:7–8, 2:216, 3:180, 24:11) and is also what 'touches' man (17:83, 41:49, 70:20); سُوء often qualifies another word — sūʾ al-ʿaḏāb (2:49, 40:45), sūʾ al-ḥisāb (13:21), sūʾ ad-dār (40:52), sūʾ ʿamalihi (35:8).

al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što svi izbjegavaju, kao što je dobro ono što svi žele. U Kur'anu često stoji uz dobro (خَيْر) kao njegov par: kao djelo, kao kušnja i kao ono što čovjeka zadesi.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what everyone shuns, as good is what everyone desires. In the Quran it often stands with good (خَيْر) as its pair: as a deed, as a trial, and as what befalls a person.

why.bs: „Mi vas iskušavamo i zlom i dobrom” – zlo i dobro kao par.
why.en: “And We test you with evil and with good as trial” — evil and good as a pair.

why.bs: „A onaj ko bude uradio koliko trun zla – vidjet će ga” – zlo kao djelo.
why.en: “And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it” — evil as a deed.

why.bs: „Od zla onoga što On stvara” – zlo od kojeg se traži utočište.
why.en: “From the evil of that which He created” — evil from which refuge is sought.

meaning.en: ill, what grieves; a foul deed

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, sve što čovjeka ožalosti – od ovosvjetskih i onosvjetskih stvari, stanja duše i tijela, i gubitka imetka, ugleda ili bliske osobe; a i ružno djelo. U Kur'anu često stoji kao odredba: „najteža kazna” (سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ), „zao obračun”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, whatever grieves a person — of worldly and otherworldly matters, states of soul and body, and the loss of wealth, standing or someone dear; and also a foul deed. In the Quran it often qualifies another word: “the worst torment” (سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ), “the evil reckoning”.

why.bs: „I vratiše se s Allahovom blagodati i dobrotom, nikakva ih nevolja (سُوء) nije dotakla” – سُوء kao ono što čovjeka ožalosti, ovdje šteta koja ih nije zadesila.
why.en: “So they returned with favor from Allah and bounty, no harm (سُوء) having touched them” — سُوء as what grieves a person, here harm that did not reach them.

why.bs: „Ko bude zlo radio, bit će mu za to uzvraćeno” – ar-Rāġib: سُوء kao ružno djelo.
why.en: “Whoever does a wrong will be recompensed for it” — ar-Rāġib: سُوء as a foul deed.

why.bs: „Izaći će bijela, ali ne od bolesti” (bez سُوء) – ar-Rāġib: bez ikakve mane; tumači se kao guba.
why.en: “It will come out white without disease” (without سُوء) — ar-Rāġib: without any blemish; explained as leprosy.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače dobro. Prema ar-Rāġibu, خَيْر je ono što svi žele, a suprotno mu je zlo (شَرّ); حَسَنَة je sve što obraduje – blagodat koja čovjeka zadesi – i dobro djelo, a suprotna joj je سَيِّئَة.
shared.en: Both words mean good. According to ar-Rāġib, خَيْر is what everyone desires, its opposite evil (شَرّ); حَسَنَة is whatever gladdens — a blessing that reaches a person — and a good deed, its opposite سَيِّئَة.

tellApart.bs: Dobro koje svi žele, a i imetak, i „bolje od” → خَيْر; ono što obraduje, blagostanje koje zadesi čovjeka, i dobro djelo nasuprot rđavom → حَسَنَة.
tellApart.en: The good all desire, also wealth, and “better than” → خَيْر; what gladdens, good fortune that reaches a person, and a good deed against an evil one → حَسَنَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries خير, حسن, سوأ
notes: ar-Rāġib (خير): ḵayr is what all desire, such as reason, justice, virtue and what benefits; its opposite šarr. He reports ('qīla') a division into absolute ḵayr and relative ḵayr/šarr (wealth good for one, bad for another); in 2:180 ḵayr = wealth, and some scholars say only much wealth from a good source; ḵayr is also comparative ('better', 2:106; in 2:184 it may be either); it is set against šarr and sometimes against ḍurr (10:107). (حسن): ḥasana is said of every blessing that gladdens, in one's self, body and circumstances, its opposite sayyiʾa; in 4:78 = fertility, plenty, victory. (سوأ): ḥasana and sayyiʾa are of two kinds — by reason and the Law (6:160) and by natural liking (7:131).
ḥasana as a feminine adjective (16:125 al-mawʿiẓa al-ḥasana, 33:21 uswa ḥasana) is filed under the same corpus lemma and counted.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što svi žele – razum, pravda, vrlina, ono što koristi; suprotno mu je zlo. Kaže se i za imetak (2:180) i u značenju „bolje od”. On navodi i mišljenje da je nešto dobro u svakom pogledu, a nešto samo za jednog, kao imetak.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what everyone desires — reason, justice, virtue, what benefits; its opposite is evil. It is said also of wealth (2:180) and in the sense of “better than”. He also reports the view that some good is good in every respect, and some only for one person, like wealth.

why.bs: „Neka među vama bude skupina koja poziva dobru” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za خَيْر kao imenicu.
why.en: “And let there be [arising] from you a nation inviting to [all that is] good” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for خَيْر as a noun.

why.bs: „Kad neko od vas bude na samrti, ako ostavlja imetak (خَيْرًا)…” – ar-Rāġib: ovdje خَيْر znači imetak.
why.en: “When death approaches one of you if he leaves wealth (خَيْرًا)…” — ar-Rāġib: here خَيْر means wealth.

why.bs: „Pa ko bude uradio koliko trun dobra – vidjet će ga.”
why.en: “So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, sve što obraduje od blagodati koja čovjeka zadesi – u njemu samom, tijelu i prilikama; suprotna joj je سَيِّئَة. On razlikuje dvije vrste: dobro po razumu i Šerijatu – dobro djelo (6:160) – i ono što je ugodno naravi (7:131).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, whatever gladdens of a blessing that reaches a person — in himself, his body and his circumstances; its opposite is سَيِّئَة. He tells two kinds apart: good by reason and the Law — a good deed (6:160) — and what is pleasant to one's nature (7:131).

why.bs: „Ko dođe s dobrim djelom, dobit će deseterostruko” – حَسَنَة po Šerijatu.
why.en: “Whoever comes [on the Day of Judgement] with a good deed will have ten times the like thereof” — حَسَنَة by the Law.

why.bs: „Ako ih zadesi kakvo dobro, govore: ‘Ovo je od Allaha’” – ar-Rāġib: plodnost, obilje i pobjeda.
why.en: “And if good comes to them, they say, ‘This is from Allah’” — ar-Rāġib: fertility, plenty and victory.

why.bs: „Gospodaru naš, daj nam dobro i na ovom svijetu i na onom svijetu” – riječ je حَسَنَة; mufesiri je tumače na više načina (zdravlje, znanje, ibadet; na ahiretu – dženet).
why.en: “Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good” — the word is حَسَنَة; mufassirun explain it in several ways (well-being, knowledge, worship; in the Hereafter, Paradise).

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o onome što je istinito. Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova riječi حَقّ je podudaranje i sklad – ono što stoji kako treba; صِدْق je, kaže on, kada se riječ podudara i s onim što govornik u sebi misli i sa stvarnošću o kojoj govori.
shared.en: Both words speak of what is true. According to ar-Rāġib, the root of حَقّ is matching and agreement — what stands as it should; صِدْق, he says, is when a statement matches both what the speaker holds within and the reality it reports.

tellApart.bs: Istina sama – ono što postoji i stoji kako treba (i Allahovo ime الْحَقّ) → حَقّ; istinitost onoga ko govori ili radi – kad se riječ slaže s nutrinom i stvarnošću → صِدْق.
tellApart.en: Truth itself — what exists and stands as it should (also Allah's name الْحَقّ) → حَقّ; the truthfulness of one who speaks or acts — word matching heart and reality → صِدْق.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حق, صدق
notes: ar-Rāġib (حق): root is matching and agreement (the door's pivot turning true in its socket); ḥaqq is said (1) of the One who brings things into being by wisdom — so Allah is al-Ḥaqq (10:32); (2) of what is brought into being by wisdom — Allah's every act is ḥaqq (10:5, of the sun and moon), and of the Resurrection (10:53); (3) of a belief that matches the thing as it is; (4) of a deed or word that occurs as, as much as, and when it should. (صدق): ṣidq and kaḏib are at root in speech, and only in reports; ṣidq is the statement matching both the inner conviction (ḍamīr) and what is reported — if a condition fails it is not full ṣidq (a disbeliever saying 'Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah' without belief: true by the fact, a lie by his heart; so Allah calls the hypocrites liars in 63:1); ṣidq is also used of deeds — fulfilling what is due (33:23); 33:8 means the one truthful in tongue is asked about the truth of his deed; 39:33 he realised in deed what he brought in word; every virtuous act outward and inward is called ṣidq and annexed to it (54:55 'seat of ṣidq', 26:84 'tongue of ṣidq' = a praise of him that will not be false).
The corpus files حَقّ as one lemma (247×), including حَقًّا; صِدْق is the noun only (not صَادِق, صِدِّيق or the verb صَدَقَ).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što se podudara i stoji kako treba. Kaže se za Allaha, koji je الْحَقّ jer sve stvara mudrošću; za ono što On stvara, jer je svako Njegovo djelo istina; za vjerovanje koje odgovara stvarnosti; i za riječ ili djelo koji dođu onako, onoliko i onda kada treba.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what matches and stands as it should. It is said of Allah, who is الْحَقّ for He brings all things into being by wisdom; of what He creates, for His every act is truth; of a belief that matches reality; and of a word or deed that comes as, as much as, and when it should.

why.bs: „To vam je, dakle, Allah, Gospodar vaš istinski; a šta ima poslije istine osim zablude?” – ar-Rāġib: الْحَقّ kao Allahovo ime.
why.en: “For that is Allah, your Lord, the Truth. And what can be beyond truth except error?” — ar-Rāġib: الْحَقّ as a name of Allah.

why.bs: Sunce i Mjesec – „Allah je to stvorio samo po istini (بِالْحَقِّ)” – ar-Rāġib: Allahovo djelo je istina jer je po mudrosti.
why.en: The sun and the moon — “Allah has not created this except in truth (بِالْحَقِّ)” — ar-Rāġib: Allah's work is truth, for it is by wisdom.

why.bs: „Je li to istina?” – „Da, Gospodara mi moga, to je zaista istina” – o Sudnjem danu; ar-Rāġib i ovaj ajet navodi.
why.en: “Is it true?” — “Yes, by my Lord. Indeed, it is truth” — of the Day of Judgement; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah too.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je u govoru: riječ je istinita kad se slaže i s onim što govornik misli i sa stvarnošću. Zato su licemjeri (63:1) lažljivci iako je ono što su rekli istina. Kaže se i za djelo – kad čovjek ispuni ono što je obećao – a svako lijepo djelo, vanjsko i unutrašnje, naziva se صِدْق.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, it is rooted in speech: a word is truthful when it matches both what the speaker holds and the reality. So the hypocrites (63:1) are liars though what they said is true. It is also said of a deed — when one fulfils what he pledged — and every virtuous act, outward and inward, is called صِدْق.

why.bs: „Da bi iskrene upitao za iskrenost njihovu” – ar-Rāġib: onaj ko je iskren jezikom biva pitan za iskrenost svog djela.
why.en: “That He may question the truthful about their truth” — ar-Rāġib: one truthful in tongue is asked about the truth of his deeds.

why.bs: „A onaj koji donosi istinu (بِالصِّدْقِ) i onaj koji je prihvati” – ar-Rāġib: potvrdio je djelom ono što je donio riječju.
why.en: “And the one who has brought the truth (بِالصِّدْقِ) and [they who] believed in it” — ar-Rāġib: he made good in deed what he brought in word.

why.bs: Ibrahimova dova: „I učini da me po dobru spominju (لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ) budući naraštaji” – ar-Rāġib: da pohvala njemu ne bude laž.
why.en: Abraham's prayer: “And grant me a reputation of honor (لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ) among later generations” — ar-Rāġib: that the praise of him not be false.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o izgovaranju napisanog ili objavljenog teksta. Prema ar-Rāġibu, تِلَاوَة je uža od قِرَاءَة: svaka تِلَاوَة je قِرَاءَة, ali nije svaka قِرَاءَة تِلَاوَة, a تَرْتِيل je način izgovora – lagano i pravilno.
shared.en: All three words concern voicing a written or revealed text. According to ar-Rāġib, تِلَاوَة is narrower than قِرَاءَة: every تِلَاوَة is a قِرَاءَة, but not every قِرَاءَة is a تِلَاوَة, while تَرْتِيل is a manner of voicing — with ease and evenness.

tellApart.bs: Kazivati Allahovu objavu i slijediti je (osnova: ići za nečim) → تَلَا; čitati, izgovarati slova i riječi spojene, bilo koji tekst → قَرَأَ; izgovarati lako i ujednačeno, riječ za riječju po redu → رَتَّلَ.
tellApart.en: To recite Allah's revelation and follow it (root: to follow after) → تَلَا; to read, to voice letters and words joined together, any text → قَرَأَ; to voice with ease and evenness, word after word in order → رَتَّلَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries تلى, قرأ, رتل
notes: ar-Rāġib (تلى): to follow with nothing between, by body, by imitation, or by reading / reflecting on the meaning (masdar tilāwa); 91:2 the moon following the sun in rank; tilāwa is specific to following Allah's revealed books, by reading or by conforming to their commands — it is more specific than qirāʾa: every tilāwa is qirāʾa, not the reverse; one does not say 'talawtu your note'; 2:121 'recite it with its true recital' = following it in knowledge and deed; 2:102 the devils' 'reciting' is so called because they claimed it was from Allah's books. (قرأ): qirāʾa is joining letters and words one to another in tartīl; a single letter uttered is not called qirāʾa; Qurʾān is at root a masdar. (رتل): ratal is a thing's being even and orderly; tartīl is sending the word from the mouth with ease and evenness (73:4, 25:32).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 60 places of تلو_1 read): the object of تَلَا is almost always Allah's ayat, the Book or news revealed by Him; the exceptions are 91:2 and 11:17 (following) and 2:102 (the devils), which ar-Rāġib explains. قَرَأَ is also used of reading one's own record of deeds (17:14, 69:19) and of a book the deniers demand (17:93).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je slijediti nešto bez ičega između. تِلَاوَة se, kaže on, odnosi na Allahove objavljene knjige – i na njihovo čitanje i na pridržavanje onoga što naređuju – pa se ne kaže za obično pismo. U kur'anskoj upotrebi predmet je gotovo uvijek Allahova objava.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is to follow a thing with nothing between. تِلَاوَة, he says, belongs to Allah's revealed books — both reading them and keeping to what they command — so it is not said of an ordinary letter. In Quranic usage its object is almost always Allah's revelation.

why.bs: „Oni kojima smo dali Knjigu, a oni je čitaju onako kako je treba čitati” – ar-Rāġib: slijede je znanjem i djelom.
why.en: “Those to whom We have given the Book recite it with its true recital” — ar-Rāġib: they follow it in knowledge and deed.

why.bs: „I Mjeseca kad ga slijedi” – osnovno značenje: ići za nečim.
why.en: “And [by] the moon when it follows it” — the root sense: to follow after.

why.bs: „Kazuj ono što ti se objavljuje u Knjizi” – kazivanje objave.
why.en: “Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book” — reciting the revelation.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, čitanje je spajanje slova i riječi jednih s drugima uz odmjeren izgovor; jedno izgovoreno slovo nije čitanje. Šira je riječ od تِلَاوَة: kaže se za svaki tekst, a u kur'anskoj upotrebi i za knjigu djela na Sudnjem danu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, reading is joining letters and words one to another in measured delivery; a single uttered letter is not reading. It is wider than تِلَاوَة: it is said of any text, and in Quranic usage even of the record of deeds on the Day of Judgement.

why.bs: „Čitaj knjigu svoju! Dovoljan si danas sam sebi kao obračunavalac” – čitanje teksta koji nije objava.
why.en: “Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant” — reading a text that is not revelation.

why.bs: „Čitaj, u ime Gospodara tvoga koji stvara!” – naredba اقْرَأْ, od قَرَأَ.
why.en: “Read in the name of your Lord who created” — the command اقْرَأْ, from قَرَأَ.

why.bs: „Kad budeš čitao Kur'an, zatraži od Allaha zaštitu od prokletog šejtana.” – قَرَأَ se kaže i za Kur'an, a ne samo za druge tekstove.
why.en: “So when you recite the Quran, [first] seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the expelled” — قَرَأَ is said of the Quran too, not only of other texts.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen znači da je nešto ujednačeno i uredno, a تَرْتِيل je izgovarati riječi lako i pravilno. U Kur'anu samo dva puta, oba puta o Kur'anu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root means that a thing is even and orderly, and تَرْتِيل is sending the words out with ease and evenness. Only twice in the Quran, both times of the Quran.

why.bs: „I Kur'an polagano i razgovijetno izgovaraj (وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا)” – način izgovora, a ne samo čitanje.
why.en: “And recite the Quran with measured recitation (وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا)” — a manner of reciting, not reciting alone.

why.bs: „I Mi ga ovako, malo-pomalo, objavljujemo (وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلًا)” – Allah govori o Kur'anu; mufessiri to tumače kao objavljivanje dio po dio, uredno.
why.en: “And We have spaced it distinctly (وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلًا)” — Allah speaks of the Quran; mufassirun explain it as revealing it part by part, in order.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače očistiti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, čistoća (طَهَارَة) je dvojaka – čistoća tijela i čistoća duše – dok je osnova riječi زَكَاة rast koji dolazi od Allahova blagoslova: تَزْكِيَة je čišćenje koje čovjeka uvećava u dobru.
shared.en: Both words mean to purify. According to ar-Rāġib, purity (طَهَارَة) is of two kinds — of the body and of the soul — while the root of زَكَاة is growth that comes from Allah's blessing: تَزْكِيَة is a purifying that makes a person grow in good.

tellApart.bs: Očistiti tijelo, mjesto ili dušu od nečistoće → طَهَّرَ; oplemeniti dušu tako da raste u dobru; i hvaliti sebe kao čista (pokuđeno) → زَكَّى.
tellApart.en: To cleanse body, place or soul of impurity → طَهَّرَ; to purify the soul so that it grows in good; also to call oneself pure (blamed) → زَكَّى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries طهر, زكا
notes: ar-Rāġib (طهر): ṭahāra is of two kinds, of the body and of the soul, and most ayat are taken to mean both; 3:55 'purify you from those who disbelieve' = take you out from among them; 3:42 'purified you' among the soul-purification ayat; 2:125 purifying the Kaʿba from the filth of idols (some say: purifying the heart); 74:4 qīla 'your self'. (زكا): root is growth from Allah's blessing, worldly and otherworldly; zakāh named for hoped-for blessing or for growing the soul in good; tazkiya is ascribed to man as its earner (91:9), to Allah as its true doer (4:49), to the Prophet as the means (9:103, 62:2), and to worship as the instrument; man's tazkiya of himself is by deed — praised (91:9, 87:14) — or by word, praising himself — blamed and forbidden (53:32).

Quranic usage (our observation, all places of the two Form II verbs read): طَهَّرَ has Allah, Abraham and Ishmael (the House), and the Prophet (9:103, 74:4) as subjects; زَكَّى has Allah (also negated: 2:174, 3:77), the Prophet (2:129, 2:151, 3:164, 62:2, 9:103) and man himself (91:9 praised; 4:49 and 53:32 blamed). 9:103 has both verbs side by side. 74:4 and 2:125 are not cited (readings differ).
