nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, čistoća je i tjelesna i duševna, i većina ajeta se odnosi na obje. U Kur'anu se čisti tijelo vodom (8:11), Ka'ba (2:125) i duša – Allah je očistio Merjemu (3:42).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, purity is of the body and of the soul, and most ayat are taken to mean both. In the Quran water cleanses the body (8:11), the Kaʿba is cleansed (2:125), and the soul — Allah purified Mary (3:42).

why.bs: „I spuštao vam je s neba kišu da vas njome očisti” – čišćenje tijela.
why.en: “And sent down upon you from the sky, rain by which to purify you” — cleansing of the body.

why.bs: „O Merjema, Allah je tebe odabrao i očistio te” – ar-Rāġib ovo ubraja u čišćenje duše.
why.en: “O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you” — ar-Rāġib counts this as purifying of the soul.

why.bs: „Uzmi od dobara njihovih milostinju, da ih njome očistiš (تُطَهِّرُهُمْ) i uzdigneš u dobru (وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ)” – obje riječi zajedno.
why.en: “Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them (تُطَهِّرُهُمْ) and cause them increase (وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ)” — both words together.

meaning.en: to purify (cause to grow in good)

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, čišćenje duše koje donosi rast i blagoslov. Pripisuje se čovjeku koji se trudi (91:9), Allahu koji to stvarno čini (4:49) i Poslaniku kao posredniku (62:2). Čovjekovo pročišćavanje sebe djelom je pohvaljeno, a hvaljenje sebe riječima pokuđeno (53:32).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a purifying of the soul that brings growth and blessing. It is ascribed to man who strives for it (91:9), to Allah who truly does it (4:49), and to the Prophet as the means (62:2). Purifying oneself by deeds is praised; praising oneself in words is blamed (53:32).

why.bs: „Uspjet će onaj ko je oplemeni (dušu)” – oplemenjivanje sebe djelom, pohvaljeno.
why.en: “He has succeeded who purifies it” — purifying oneself by deeds, praised.

why.bs: „Zato se ne hvalite (فَلَا تُزَكُّوا أَنفُسَكُمْ), On dobro zna onoga koji se boji” – ar-Rāġib: zabranjeno je hvaliti sebe riječima.
why.en: “So do not claim yourselves to be pure (فَلَا تُزَكُّوا أَنفُسَكُمْ); He is most knowing of who fears Him” — ar-Rāġib: praising oneself in words is forbidden.

why.bs: Poslanik „koji im ajete Njegove kazuje i čisti ih (وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ)” – Poslanik kao posrednik.
why.en: A Messenger “reciting to them His verses and purifying them (وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ)” — the Prophet as the means.

shared.bs: Sve četiri riječi su tvar od koje je, prema Kur'anu, stvoren čovjek. Prema ar-Rāġibu, طِين je zemlja (تُرَاب) pomiješana s vodom, صَلْصَال sasušena glina, a حَمَأ crno, ustajalo blato. Mnogi mufessiri ih vide kao faze jedne iste tvari.
shared.en: All four are matter from which, according to the Quran, man was created. According to ar-Rāġib, طِين is earth (تُرَاب) mixed with water, صَلْصَال is dried clay, and حَمَأ is black, foul-smelling mud. Many mufassirun see them as stages of one and the same matter.

tellApart.bs: Suha zemlja, prašina → تُرَاب; zemlja pomiješana s vodom → طِين; sasušena glina koja zveči → صَلْصَال; crno, izmijenjeno blato → حَمَأ.
tellApart.en: Dry earth, dust → تُرَاب; earth mixed with water → طِين; dried clay that rings → صَلْصَال; black, altered mud → حَمَأ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries تراب, طين, صلل, حمى
notes: ar-Rāġib (تراب): quotes 'created you from turāb' and 'would that I were dust' (78:40); turāb is the earth itself; tariba = became poor, as if cleaving to the dust (90:16). (طين): ṭīn is turāb and water mixed, and is still so called when the water's strength has gone (37:11 'sticky clay', 38:76, 28:38 Pharaoh's bricks). (صلل): the root of ṣalṣāl is the echoing sound of a dry thing; dry clay is called ṣalṣāl (55:14, 15:26); qīla: ṣalṣāl is foul-smelling clay, from ṣalla al-laḥm. (حمى): al-ḥamaʾ and al-ḥamʾa are black foul-smelling clay (15:26).

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): تُرَاب 17× — creation from dust (3:59, 18:37, 22:5, 30:20, 35:11, 40:67), and in eight places the deniers' 'when we have become dust' (13:5 … 56:47); طِين 12× — man's creation (6:2, 7:12, 17:61, 23:12, 32:7, 37:11, 38:71, 38:76), Jesus' birds by Allah's permission (3:49, 5:110), Pharaoh's bricks (28:38), stones of clay (51:33); صَلْصَال 4× (15:26, 15:28, 15:33, 55:14) and حَمَأ 3× — always in 15:26/28/33, together with صَلْصَال. حَمِئَة (18:86) is left out: its reading differs. 'Stages of one matter' is the mufassirun's harmonisation, not ar-Rāġib's.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries تراب, طين, صلل, حمى (2026-11-06): 17 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): He says "قد يسمى" (may be called) and "the strength of the water", not the water itself

nuance.bs: Suha zemlja; prema ar-Rāġibu, تُرَاب je sama zemlja. U Kur'anu je početak čovjekova stvaranja (30:20), a u osam ajeta i riječ poricatelja: „Zar kad postanemo prašina…”, koja izražava nevjericu u proživljenje.
nuance.en: Dry earth; according to ar-Rāġib, تُرَاب is the earth itself. In the Quran it is the beginning of man's creation (30:20), and in eight ayat the deniers' words “When we have become dust…”, voicing disbelief in the resurrection.

why.bs: „Od znamenja Njegovih je to što vas od zemlje stvara, a vi ste potom ljudi koji se po zemlji šire.”
why.en: “And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then, suddenly you were human beings dispersing.”

why.bs: „Isa je kod Allaha kao i Adem: od zemlje ga je stvorio, zatim rekao: ‘Budi!’ – i on bi.”
why.en: “The example of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was.”

why.bs: Poricatelji: „Zar kad pomremo i zemlja postanemo…? To je povratak dalek!”
why.en: The deniers: “When we have died and have become dust…? That is a distant return.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, zemlja pomiješana s vodom; tako se može zvati i kad voda u njoj izgubi snagu. U Kur'anu najčešće tvar Ademova stvaranja, ali i ptice koje Isa, Allahovom dozvolom, oblikuje i opeka koju faraon peče (28:38).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, earth mixed with water; it may keep the name even when the water's strength has gone from it. In the Quran mostly the matter of Adam's creation, but also the birds Jesus shapes by Allah's permission and the bricks Pharaoh has fired (28:38).

why.bs: „Ja ću stvoriti čovjeka od ilovače.”
why.en: “Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay.”

why.bs: „Mi smo ih stvorili od ljepljive ilovače (مِّن طِينٍ لَّازِبٍ)” – ilovača s vodom, koja se lijepi.
why.en: “Indeed, We created them from sticky clay (مِّن طِينٍ لَّازِبٍ)” — clay with water, which clings.

why.bs: Faraon: „Peci mi, Hamane, ciglu od ilovače” – ista riječ za građu.
why.en: Pharaoh: “Ignite for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay” — the same word for building material.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je odjek zvuka suhe stvari, pa se sasušena glina zove صَلْصَال. On navodi i mišljenje da je to ustajala, pokvarena glina. U Kur'anu samo četiri puta, uvijek o stvaranju čovjeka.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is the echoing sound of a dry thing, so dried clay is called صَلْصَال. He also reports a view that it is foul, spoilt clay. Only four times in the Quran, always of man's creation.

why.bs: „Stvorio je čovjeka od suhe gline, kao što je grnčarija” – suha, tvrda glina.
why.en: “He created man from dry clay like [that of] pottery” — dry, hard clay.

why.bs: „Mi smo stvorili čovjeka od suhe zvonke gline (صَلْصَالٍ), od blata ustajalog (حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ)” – obje riječi zajedno.
why.en: “And We did certainly create man out of dry ringing clay (صَلْصَالٍ) from an altered black mud (حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ)” — both words together.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, crna glina neugodnog mirisa. U Kur'anu tri puta, uvijek u istom izrazu uz صَلْصَال (15:26, 28, 33).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, black clay with a foul smell. Three times in the Quran, always in the same phrase with صَلْصَال (15:26, 28, 33).

why.bs: „Ja ću stvoriti čovjeka od suhe zvonke gline, od blata ustajalog” – riječi upućene melekima.
why.en: “I will create a human being out of dry ringing clay from an altered black mud” — words to the angels.

why.bs: „Od blata ustajalog (مِّنْ حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ)” – blato od kojeg je glina.
why.en: “From an altered black mud (مِّنْ حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ)” — the mud of which the clay is.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače biti prisutan. Prema ar-Rāġibu, شُهُود i شَهَادَة su prisutnost uz gledanje – očima ili uvidom – mada kaže da se može reći i za samu prisutnost: شُهُود više priliči golom prisustvu, a شَهَادَة prisustvu uz gledanje. Riječ حُضُور on objašnjava riječju شَهَادَة, „prisutnost na mjestu ili kod nekoga”. Zato je svjedočenje (شَهَادَة) govor iz znanja stečenog gledanjem.
shared.en: Both words mean being present. According to ar-Rāġib, شُهُود and شَهَادَة are presence together with seeing — by eye or by insight — though he says presence alone can also be so called: شُهُود suits bare presence better, شَهَادَة presence with seeing. He explains حُضُور with the word شَهَادَة, “being present at a place or with someone”. So testimony (شَهَادَة) is speech from knowledge gained by seeing.

tellApart.bs: Biti prisutan i vidjeti; posvjedočiti ono što se zna → شَهِدَ; biti prisutan, nastupiti, doći (smrt, ljudi) → حَضَرَ.
tellApart.en: To be present and see; to testify to what one knows → شَهِدَ; to be present, to come upon (death, people) → حَضَرَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries شهد, حضر
notes: ar-Rāġib (شهد): shuhūd and shahāda are presence with seeing, by sight or insight; sometimes said of bare presence, but shuhūd fits bare presence better and shahāda presence with seeing; 27:49 'we did not witness' = we were not present; 25:72 'do not witness falsehood' = are not present at it in person nor in intent; shahāda is speech issuing from knowledge gained by seeing with insight or eye; 12:81 'we testified only to what we knew' = what we reported; the witness must say 'I testify', not 'I know'; shahida may run as an oath. (حضر): ḥaḍar is the opposite of desert life; then made a name for 'being at (šahāda) a place or a person' (2:180, 4:8); 23:98 'that they be present with me' = the jinn, by allusion; muḥtaḍar of one at death.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 7 places of حضر_1 read): in four (2:133, 2:180, 4:18, 5:106) the subject is death; the others are relatives at the division (4:8), the devils (23:98) and the jinn at the Quran (46:29). شهد_1 (38 places) is mostly testifying (3:18, 24:24, 41:20 …); bare presence in 2:185, 22:28, 27:49, 25:72.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 3 of 3 flagged, fixed: his own distinction restored (شُهُود suits bare presence, شَهَادَة presence with seeing); حَضَرَ no longer 'says nothing of seeing' (of مُحْضَر 3:30 he does); 25:72 shows the majority reading (false testimony) beside his.

Fix keeps the contrast honest

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, prisutnost uz gledanje – očima ili uvidom; zato i svjedočenje, govor iz znanja stečenog gledanjem. Dodaje da imenica شُهُود više priliči golom prisustvu. Svjedok, kaže on, mora reći „svjedočim”, a ne „znam”. U Kur'anu najčešće svjedočenje, ponekad i sama prisutnost.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, presence together with seeing — by eye or by insight; hence also testimony, speech from knowledge gained by seeing. He adds that the noun شُهُود suits bare presence better. A witness, he says, must say “I testify”, not “I know”. In the Quran it is mostly testifying, sometimes bare presence.

why.bs: „Mi svjedočimo samo ono što znamo” – ar-Rāġib: „svjedočiti” ovdje znači „obavijestiti”.
why.en: “We did not testify except to what we knew” — ar-Rāġib: “testified” here means “reported”.

why.bs: Zavjerenici protiv Saliha: „Mi nismo bili prisutni (مَا شَهِدْنَا) pogibiji porodice njegove” – ar-Rāġib: nismo bili tu.
why.en: The plotters against Ṣāliḥ: “We did not witness (مَا شَهِدْنَا) the destruction of his family” — ar-Rāġib: we were not present.

why.bs: „I oni koji ne svjedoče lažno (لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ)” – mnogi mufesiri: lažno svjedočenje; ar-Rāġib: ne prisustvuju laži ni tijelom ni namjerom.
why.en: “And [they are] those who do not testify to falsehood (لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ)” — many mufassirun: false testimony; ar-Rāġib: they are not present at it, in body or in intent.

meaning.en: to be present, to come upon

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je život u naselju (suprotno pustinji), a onda bivanje na nekom mjestu ili kod nekoga. Objašnjava je riječju شَهَادَة, u značenju golog prisustva, bez gledanja i znanja u toj odredbi. U kur'anskoj upotrebi, u četiri od sedam mjesta, smrt je ta koja „nastupi” čovjeku.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is settled life (the opposite of the desert), then being at a place or with someone. He defines it with the word شَهَادَة itself, meaning bare presence, adding nothing of seeing or knowing in that definition. In Quranic usage, in four of its seven places, it is death that “comes upon” a person.

why.bs: „Propisano vam je, kad nekom od vas smrt dođe (حَضَرَ)… oporuka” – smrt koja nastupa.
why.en: “Prescribed for you when death approaches (حَضَرَ) any of you… is that he should make a bequest” — death that comes upon.

why.bs: „A kad diobi prisustvuju rođaci, siročad i siromasi, podarite im nešto od toga” – prisutnost ljudi.
why.en: “And when [other] relatives and orphans and the needy are present at the [time of] division, then provide for them from it” — people being present.

why.bs: Džini koji slušaju Kur'an – „pa kad su ga prisustvovali (حَضَرُوهُ), rekoše: ‘Šutite!’”
why.en: The jinn listening to the Quran — “and when they attended it (حَضَرُوهُ), they said, ‘Listen quietly’”.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače zadržati nekoga od nečega. Prema ar-Rāġibu, صَدّ je ili okretanje sebe od nečega ili odvraćanje drugoga, dok je مَنْع suprotnost davanju (uskraćivanje), a znači i zaštitu.
shared.en: Both words mean keeping someone from something. According to ar-Rāġib, صَدّ is either turning oneself away from a thing or turning another away, while مَنْع is the opposite of giving (withholding), and also means protection.

tellApart.bs: Okrenuti se od, odvraćati druge od (puta, upute) → صَدَّ; spriječiti, uskratiti, zaštititi → مَنَعَ.
tellApart.en: To turn away from, to turn others away from (a way, guidance) → صَدَّ; to prevent, to withhold, to protect → مَنَعَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries صدد, منع
notes: ar-Rāġib (صدد): ṣudūd / ṣadd may be turning away from a thing and refusing (4:61), or turning another away and preventing (27:24 / 29:38 'Satan barred them from the way', 47:1, 2:217, 28:87). (منع): manʿ is said of the opposite of giving — mānīʿ, mannāʿ = miser (107:7, 50:25); and of protection — a manīʿ place; 4:141 'did we not protect you'; 2:114 'who prevents the mosques of Allah'; 7:12 'what prevented you' = what led you, and qīla: what turned you away (ṣaddaka).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 37 places of صدد_1 read): in 22 the object is 'the way of Allah' or 'the way' (عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ / عَنِ السَّبِيلِ); intransitive turning away in 4:55, 4:61, 43:57, 63:5. 28:87 and 20:16 are not cited (addressed to the Prophet).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 of 3 flagged, fixed: 'more than half its places' → 'most often'; 107:7 al-māʿūn no longer glossed (tafsir differs), only his use of it for withholding.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dvojako: okrenuti se od nečega i odbiti ga, ili okrenuti drugoga i spriječiti ga. U Kur'anu je najčešće riječ o odvraćanju ljudi „od Allahova puta”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, two ways: turning away from a thing and refusing it, or turning another away and preventing him. In the Quran it is most often turning people away “from the way of Allah”.

why.bs: „Vidiš licemjere kako se od tebe sasvim odvraćaju” – ar-Rāġib: okretanje sebe, odbijanje.
why.en: “You see the hypocrites turning away from you in aversion” — ar-Rāġib: turning oneself away, refusing.

why.bs: „Šejtan im je prikazao lijepim postupke njihove i od Pravog puta ih odvratio” – odvraćanje drugih.
why.en: “Satan has made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from [His] way” — turning others away.

why.bs: Šejtan želi „da vas od sjećanja na Allaha i od molitve odvrati” – odvraćanje od cilja.
why.en: Satan wants “to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer” — turning away from a goal.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, suprotnost davanju – uskratiti nekome nešto – a znači i zaštititi. Za Iblisovo „šta te je spriječilo” (7:12) navodi tumačenje „šta te je navelo”, i mišljenje „šta te je odvratilo (صَدَّكَ)”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the opposite of giving — withholding a thing from someone — and also protecting. For “what prevented you” said to Iblis (7:12) he gives “what led you”, and reports the view “what turned you away (صَدَّكَ)”.

why.bs: „I uskraćuju al-māʿūn (sitnu pomoć)” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za suprotnost davanju.
why.en: “And they withhold al-māʿūn (small help)” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for the opposite of giving.

why.bs: „Ima li većeg nasilnika od onoga koji brani da se u Allahovim džamijama spominje ime Njegovo?”
why.en: “And who are more unjust than those who prevent the name of Allah from being mentioned in His mosques?”

why.bs: „Šta te je spriječilo da se pokloniš kad sam ti naredio?” – Allahovo pitanje Iblisu.
why.en: “What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?” — Allah's question to Iblis.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače brojati. Prema ar-Rāġibu, عَدّ je spajanje brojeva jednih s drugima, a إِحْصَاء je dokučiti nešto brojem, obuhvatiti ga u potpunosti; riječ dolazi od حَصًى, kamenčića kojima se nekad brojalo.
shared.en: Both words mean to count. According to ar-Rāġib, عَدّ is joining numbers one to another, while إِحْصَاء is to obtain a thing by number, to encompass it fully; the word comes from حَصًى, the pebbles once used for counting.

tellApart.bs: Brojati; i ubrajati nekoga među → عَدَّ; pobrojati sve, obuhvatiti brojem u potpunosti → أَحْصَى.
tellApart.en: To count, to number; also to reckon someone among → عَدَّ; to enumerate all, to encompass fully by number → أَحْصَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حصا, عد
notes: ar-Rāġib (حصا): iḥṣāʾ is taḥṣīl (obtaining) by number, from ḥaṣā, pebbles counted as we count on fingers; 72:28 'enumerated everything in number' = obtained and encompassed it; 73:20 'you will not be able to iḥṣāʾ it' — he then explains the hadith 'be upright, and you will not iḥṣāʾ' = not obtain it, hard because truth is one and falsehood many; lexicographers: 'not count its reward'. (عد): ʿadad is units composed; ʿadd is joining numbers to one another (19:94 aḥṣāhum wa-ʿaddahum ʿaddā); 'counted' (maʿdūd) is used for few, as against what cannot be counted for its multitude (2:80 'a few days').

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): أَحْصَى (10) — Allah encompassing all things (19:94, 36:12, 58:6, 72:28, 78:29), the record leaving nothing (18:49), people unable (14:34, 16:18, 73:20) and told to keep count of the ʿidda (65:1). عَدَّ (7) — 14:34 and 16:18 put the two side by side: if you count (تَعُدُّوا) Allah's favour you cannot enumerate it (لَا تُحْصُوهَا). 73:20 not cited (readings of 'lan tuḥṣūhu' differ).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 3 of 3 flagged, fixed: brojati / izbrojati for عَدَّ, pobrojati for أَحْصَى throughout; 'reckon among' (38:62) given to Quranic usage, not to him; 58:6 bs 'pobrojao', not 'zapamtio'.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dokučiti nešto brojem i obuhvatiti ga. Kad je Allah subjekt, ništa ne izmiče (72:28); kad su ljudi, najčešće je to ono što ne mogu – Allahove blagodati ne mogu se pobrojati (14:34).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to obtain a thing by number and encompass it. With Allah as subject nothing escapes (72:28); with people, it is mostly what they cannot do — Allah's favours cannot be enumerated (14:34).

why.bs: „Ako biste Allahove blagodati brojali (تَعُدُّوا), ne biste ih pobrojali (لَا تُحْصُوهَا)” – brojanje je moguće, potpuno obuhvatanje nije.
why.en: “And if you should count (تَعُدُّوا) the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them (لَا تُحْصُوهَا)” — counting is possible, encompassing is not.

why.bs: „I zna sve što je u njih i zna broj svega (وَأَحْصَىٰ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَدًا)” – ar-Rāġib: dokučio je i obuhvatio.
why.en: “And He has encompassed whatever is with them and has enumerated all things in number” — ar-Rāġib: obtained and encompassed it.

why.bs: „Allah je to sve pobrojao (أَحْصَاهُ اللَّهُ), a oni su to zaboravili.”
why.en: “Allah had enumerated it (أَحْصَاهُ اللَّهُ), while they forgot it.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, spajanje brojeva jednih s drugima. U Kur'anu može značiti i „smatrati, ubrajati među” (38:62). Sam broj ne kaže da je nešto obuhvaćeno: ljudi broje, ali ne mogu sve pobrojati (14:34).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, joining numbers one to another. In the Quran it can also mean to reckon someone among (38:62). The count alone does not say a thing is encompassed: people count, but cannot enumerate all (14:34).

why.bs: „On ih je zaista sve pobrojao (أَحْصَاهُمْ) i tačno izbrojao (وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا)” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet uz عَدّ, gdje obje riječi stoje jedna uz drugu.
why.en: “He has enumerated them (أَحْصَاهُمْ) and counted them a [full] counting (وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا)” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for عَدّ, where both words stand side by side.

why.bs: „A dan u Gospodara tvoga je kao hiljadu godina, kako vi računate (مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ)” – ljudsko brojanje.
why.en: “And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count (مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ)” — human counting.

why.bs: „Kako to da ne vidimo ljude koje smo ubrajali u nevaljale?” – brojati kao ubrajati, smatrati.
why.en: “Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the worst?” — counting as reckoning among.

shared.bs: Obje riječi opisuju ono što nije ozbiljno, i Kur'an ih često spaja kad govori o ovom svijetu. Prema ar-Rāġibu, لَهْو je ono što čovjeka zaokupi i odvrati od onoga što mu je važno, a لَعِب je djelo bez ispravnog cilja.
shared.en: Both words describe what is not earnest, and the Quran often joins them when speaking of this world. According to ar-Rāġib, لَهْو is what occupies a person and distracts him from what concerns him, while لَعِب is an act done without a sound aim.

tellApart.bs: Ono što zaokupi i odvrati od važnog, razonoda → لَهْو; igra, radnja bez ozbiljnog cilja → لَعِب.
tellApart.en: What occupies and distracts from what matters, amusement → لَهْو; play, an act with no earnest aim → لَعِب.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries لهى, لعب
notes: ar-Rāġib (لهى): lahw is what busies a person away from what concerns and matters to him; any enjoyment is called lahw; alhāhu = it busied him from what is more important (102:1, 24:37 — not a prohibition of trade but of being consumed by it to the neglect of prayer); those who take lahw in 21:17 as wife and child are specifying part of the world's adornment. (لعب): root luʿāb, flowing saliva; laʿiba when one's act is not aimed at a sound purpose (29:64, 6:70, 7:98, 21:55, 44:38).

Quranic usage (our observation, all places of both nouns read): لَعِب (8) never stands alone — six times with لَهْو (6:32, 6:70, 7:51, 29:64, 47:36, 57:20) and twice with هُزُو 'mockery' (5:57, 5:58); لَهْو (10 uses in 9 ayat) also alone (21:17, 31:6, 62:11). 21:17 and 31:6 are not cited: tafsir differs on what lahw means there.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 of 3 flagged, fixed: لَعِب is 'play' in every English line ('amusement' belongs to لَهْو). The noun-only scope of 'never alone' was set after verification (the verb stands alone, 12:12).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što zaokupi čovjeka i odvrati ga od onoga što mu je važno; tako se naziva i svaki užitak. U Kur'anu i samostalno – za ono što odvlači od molitve (62:11).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, what occupies a person and distracts him from what matters to him; any enjoyment is also called so. In the Quran it also stands alone — for what draws people away from prayer (62:11).

why.bs: „A kad vide kakvu trgovinu ili zabavu, oni se raziđu… Reci: ‘Ono što je u Allaha bolje je od zabave i trgovine.’”
why.en: “But when they saw a transaction or a diversion, [some] rushed to it… Say, ‘What is with Allah is better than diversion and than a transaction.’”

why.bs: „Život na ovom svijetu nije ništa drugo do zabava i igra, a onaj svijet je pravi život.”
why.en: “And this worldly life is not but diversion and amusement. And indeed, the home of the Hereafter – that is the [eternal] life.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je pljuvačka koja curi (لُعَاب), a igra je djelo kojim se ne teži ispravnom cilju. U Kur'anu imenica لَعِب nikad ne stoji sama (glagol stoji, npr. 12:12): uz لَهْو ili uz ruganje (هُزُو), kad nevjernici uzimaju vjeru i namaz kao igru.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is flowing saliva (لُعَاب), and play is an act aimed at no sound purpose. In the Quran the noun لَعِب never stands alone (the verb does, e.g. 12:12): it comes with لَهْو or with mockery (هُزُو), when disbelievers take religion and prayer as play.

why.bs: „Život na ovom svijetu je samo igra i zabava, a onaj svijet je, zaista, bolji za one koji se boje Allaha.”
why.en: “And the worldly life is not but play and diversion; but the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear Allah.”

why.bs: „A kad pozivate na molitvu, oni je uzimaju kao predmet za podsmijeh i igru” – igra uz ruganje.
why.en: “And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and play” — play joined with mockery.

why.bs: „I ostavi one koji vjeru svoju smatraju igrom i zabavom.”
why.en: “And leave those who take their religion as play and diversion.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače ono što nešto čini lijepim za oko. Prema ar-Rāġibu, زُخْرُف je ukras koji je dotjeran i uljepšan – zato se i zlato zove زُخْرُف – dok je زِينَة širi pojam: ukras duše, tijela i imetka.
shared.en: Both words mean what makes a thing pleasing to the eye. According to ar-Rāġib, زُخْرُف is adornment that has been embellished — hence gold too is called زُخْرُف — while زِينَة is the wider word: adornment of the soul, of the body and of possessions.

tellApart.bs: Ukras uopće – znanje i vjera, snaga i stas, imetak i ugled; dozvoljen ili zavodljiv, prema tome kako se koristi → زِينَة; kićenost, dotjerani sjaj – zlato, kićene riječi, Zemlja okićena pred propast → زُخْرُف.
tellApart.en: Adornment in general — knowledge and faith, strength and stature, wealth and standing; lawful or tempting, by how it is used → زِينَة; embellishment, polished glitter — gold, embellished words, the earth decked out before its ruin → زُخْرُف.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries زين, زخرف
notes: ar-Rāġib (زين): true zīna is what does not disgrace a person in any state, in this world or the next; what adorns in one state and not another is in one respect a disgrace. Zīna is of three kinds: of the soul (knowledge, good beliefs), of the body (strength, stature), external (wealth, standing); 49:7 is of the soul, 7:32 was taken as external (a report that some circled the House naked), while some said the zīna there is karam (49:13); 28:79 is worldly zīna. Allah ascribes tazyīn to Himself, to Satan, and leaves the doer unnamed. (زخرف): zuḫruf is ornamented (muzawwaq) zīna, hence gold is called zuḫruf; 17:93 a house of ornamented gold (ḏahab muzawwaq); 6:112 zuḫruf al-qawl = embellished speech.

That زُخْرُف, in its four places (6:112, 10:24, 17:93, 43:35), is never praised — deceptive speech, the earth's finery before it is cut down, a gold house the disbelievers demand, worldly enjoyment — is our observation of Quranic usage.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 of 3 flagged, fixed: 'tests' dropped from زِينَة (18:46, 28:79 do not say it); زُخْرُف is kićenost / embellishment, gold, not 'gilt' or 'ukras'.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, pravi ukras je onaj koji čovjeka ne sramoti ni na ovom ni na onom svijetu. Ukras je trojak: duševni (znanje, ispravno vjerovanje), tjelesni (snaga, stas) i vanjski (imetak, ugled). Kur'an ga spominje i kao dozvoljen dar (7:32) i kao ukras ovosvjetskog života koji prolazi (18:46, 28:79).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, true adornment is that which does not disgrace a person in this world or the next. Adornment is of three kinds: of the soul (knowledge, right belief), of the body (strength, stature) and external (wealth, standing). The Quran names it both as a lawful gift (7:32) and as the adornment of worldly life that passes (18:46, 28:79).

why.bs: „Ko je zabranio Allahov ukras koji je On za robove Svoje stvorio?” – ar-Rāġib: shvaćen je kao vanjski ukras (odjeća), a neki kažu da je to plemenitost (كَرَم).
why.en: “Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants?” — ar-Rāġib: it has been taken as external adornment (clothing); others say it is nobility (كَرَم).

why.bs: „Imetak i sinovi su ukras života na ovome svijetu” – ukras koji prolazi.
why.en: “Wealth and children are [but] adornment of the worldly life” — adornment that passes.

why.bs: Karun izađe pred svoj narod „u svom sjaju” – ar-Rāġib: ovosvjetski ukras, imetak i ugled.
why.en: Qārūn came out before his people “in his adornment” — ar-Rāġib: worldly adornment, wealth and standing.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ukras koji je dotjeran i uljepšan; zato se zlato zove زُخْرُف, a „kićene riječi” (زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ) su uljepšan govor. U kur'anskoj upotrebi riječ nikad nije pohvalna: varljive riječi, Zemlja okićena prije propasti, zlatna kuća koju traže nevjernici, prolazno uživanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, adornment that has been embellished; hence gold is called زُخْرُف, and “embellished speech” (زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ) is speech dressed up. In Quranic usage the word is never praised: deceptive words, the earth decked out before its ruin, a house of gold the disbelievers demand, passing enjoyment.

why.bs: Šejtani jedni drugima došaptavaju „kićene riječi, da bi zaveli” – sjaj bez istine.
why.en: Devils inspire to one another “decorative speech in delusion” — glitter without truth.

why.bs: Nevjernici traže od Poslanika „kuću od zlata” – ar-Rāġib: od ukrašenog zlata.
why.en: The disbelievers demand of the Prophet “a house of gold” — ar-Rāġib: of ornamented gold.

why.bs: „I zlatni sjaj – a sve je to samo uživanje u životu na ovome svijetu.”
why.en: “And gold ornament. But all that is not but the enjoyment of worldly life.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače nečistoću. Prema ar-Rāġibu, رِجْس je prljava stvar, gadna po prirodi, razumu ili šerijatu (ili po svemu troje), a نَجَس je nečistoća koja se opaža čulima ili pronicljivošću – i ovu drugu Allah pripisuje mnogobošcima.
shared.en: Both words mean uncleanness. According to ar-Rāġib, رِجْس is a filthy thing, repugnant by nature, by reason or by the Sharia (or by all three), while نَجَس is filth perceived either by the senses or by insight — and it is the second that Allah ascribes to the polytheists.

tellApart.bs: Gadost – stvar od koje se treba kloniti: vino, kocka, strvina, svinjetina, kipovi, pa i nevjerovanje → رِجْس; nečist – samo jednom u Kur'anu, o mnogobošcima; ar-Rāġib je shvaća kao nečistoću koja se opaža pronicljivošću → نَجَس.
tellApart.en: Defilement — a thing to be shunned: wine, gambling, carrion, pork, idols, and unbelief itself → رِجْس; unclean — only once in the Quran, of the polytheists; ar-Rāġib takes it as an uncleanness perceived by insight → نَجَس.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رجس, نجس
notes: ar-Rāġib (رجس): rijs is the filthy thing; it is so in four ways: by nature, by reason, by the Sharia, or by all of these, like carrion; wine and gambling are rijs by the Sharia — and it has been said (qīla) by reason too, as 2:219 hints; disbelievers are made rijs because shirk is, to reason, the ugliest of things (9:125); on 10:100 it has been said rijs is stench, and it has been said punishment, like 9:28; pork (6:145) is rijs by the Sharia. (نجس, the text misprints النحاسة): najāsa is filth, of two kinds — perceived by the senses and perceived by insight; Allah described the polytheists with the second (9:28).

نَجَس occurs once in the Quran (9:28); رِجْس 10× in 9 ayat (counted from the corpus). The jurists' question whether polytheists are bodily impure is not taken up; we give only ar-Rāġib's classification.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 of 3 flagged, fixed: 9:28 shown as ar-Rāġib's reading (perceived by insight) with 'scholars differ on how far it reaches'; bs 'nečist' instead of 'pogan'; 6:145 en 'defilement' so رِجْس and نَجَس keep distinct words.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, prljava, gadna stvar – gadna po prirodi, po razumu, po šerijatu ili po svemu troje (kao strvina). Vino i kocka su gadost po šerijatu, a svinjetina također; nevjernike Kur'an naziva gadošću jer je širk razumu najružnija stvar.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a filthy, repugnant thing — repugnant by nature, by reason, by the Sharia, or by all three (like carrion). Wine and gambling are defilement by the Sharia, and so is pork; the Quran calls the disbelievers defilement because shirk is, to reason, the ugliest of things.

why.bs: „Vino, kocka, kumiri i strelice za gatanje su gadost, šejtanovo djelo – zato se toga klonite.” – ar-Rāġib: gadost po šerijatu.
why.en: “Intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it” — ar-Rāġib: defilement by the Sharia.

why.bs: „…ili svinjsko meso – jer je to gadost” – ar-Rāġib: po šerijatu.
why.en: “…or the flesh of swine — for indeed, it is a defilement (rijs)” — ar-Rāġib: by the Sharia.

why.bs: „A onima u čijim je srcima bolest, ona još više poveća gadost njihovu” – ar-Rāġib: nevjerovanje kao gadost razumu.
why.en: “But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it has [only] increased them in evil [in addition] to their evil” — ar-Rāġib: unbelief as defilement to reason.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nečistoća je dvojaka: ona koja se opaža čulima i ona koja se opaža pronicljivošću; ovom drugom Allah opisuje mnogobošce. U Kur'anu samo jednom (9:28).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, uncleanness is of two kinds: one perceived by the senses and one perceived by insight; it is with the second that Allah describes the polytheists. In the Quran only once (9:28).

why.bs: „O vjernici, mnogobošci su nečisti, pa neka se ne približuju Mesdžidu-l-haramu” – ar-Rāġib to shvaća kao nečistoću koja se opaža pronicljivošću; učenjaci se razilaze koliko ona seže.
why.en: “O you who have believed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram” — ar-Rāġib takes it as an uncleanness perceived by insight; scholars differ on how far it reaches.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače skriveni naum protiv nekoga. Prema ar-Rāġibu, كَيْد je vrsta smicalice, a مَكْر odvraćanje drugoga od onoga što namjerava, putem smicalice; i jedno i drugo može biti pokuđeno ili pohvalno, iako se كَيْد češće kaže za pokuđeno.
shared.en: Both words mean a hidden design against someone. According to ar-Rāġib, كَيْد is a kind of stratagem, and مَكْر is turning another away from what he intends, by a stratagem; either can be blameworthy or praiseworthy, though كَيْد is used more often of the blameworthy.

tellApart.bs: Lukavstvo, smicalica – ženâ, sihirbaza, nevjernika; kod Allaha, kako Njemu priliči, ostavljanje vremena koje vodi kazni (7:183) → كَيْد; spletka kojom se drugi odvraća od svog cilja; kod Allaha, kako Njemu priliči, što mufessiri objašnjavaju kao uzvraćanje na njihovu spletku (27:50) → مَكْر.
tellApart.en: Stratagem, ploy — of women, of a magician, of disbelievers; of Allah, as befits Him, the respite that leads to punishment (7:183) → كَيْد; scheming that turns another from his aim; of Allah, as befits Him, which mufassirun explain as requital of their scheme (27:50) → مَكْر.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كيد, مكر
notes: ar-Rāġib (كيد): kayd is a kind of iḥtiyāl (stratagem); it may be blameworthy or praiseworthy, though used more of the blameworthy — likewise istidrāǧ and makr; 12:76 (kidnā li-Yūsuf); on 7:183 some said kayd is punishment, but the correct view is that it is the respite (imlāʾ, imhāl) leading to punishment; 12:52 'Allah does not guide the kayd of the treacherous' — specifying the treacherous shows He may guide the kayd of one who intends no treachery, like Joseph's with his brother; 20:69 kayd of a magician. (مكر): makr is turning another from what he intends by a stratagem; two kinds: praiseworthy, seeking a fine deed (3:54 'Allah is the best of planners'), and blameworthy (35:43); 27:50 has both; some said that of Allah's makr is giving the servant respite and worldly ease.

Content policy: Allah's kayd and makr are given only with a gloss — ar-Rāġib's (kayd: respite leading to punishment) or the mufassirun's (makr: requital of their plotting), never as human deceit. 86:15–16 and 7:99 are not cited.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, vrsta smicalice; može biti pokuđeno i pohvalno, ali se češće kaže za pokuđeno. Kada se pripisuje Allahu (7:183), on kaže da je ispravno tumačenje – Allahovo ostavljanje vremena koje vodi kazni, a neki su rekli da je to sama kazna.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a kind of stratagem; it can be blameworthy or praiseworthy, but is said more often of the blameworthy. When ascribed to Allah (7:183), he says the correct reading is Allah's granting of respite that leads to punishment; some said it is the punishment itself.

why.bs: „Ovo je jedno od vaših lukavstava, a vaša lukavstva su zaista velika” – pokuđena smicalica.
why.en: “Indeed, it is of the women's plan. Indeed, your plan is great” — a blameworthy ploy.

why.bs: „Ono što su oni napravili samo je lukavstvo sihirbaza” – smicalica obmane.
why.en: “What they have made is but the trick of a magician” — a ploy of illusion.

why.bs: „I Ja ću im vremena ostaviti, a plan Moj je zaista čvrst” – kako Njemu priliči; ar-Rāġib: ostavljanje vremena koje vodi kazni.
why.en: “And I will give them time. Indeed, my plan is firm” — as befits Him; ar-Rāġib: the respite that leads to punishment.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, odvraćanje drugoga od onoga što namjerava, putem smicalice; pohvalno je kad se njime traži dobro djelo, pokuđeno kad se traži ružno. On navodi 27:50 za obje vrste: njihova spletka (pokuđena vrsta) i Allahovo, kako Njemu priliči (pohvalna vrsta); mufessiri često objašnjavaju ovo drugo kao uzvraćanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, turning another away from what he intends, by a stratagem; praiseworthy when it seeks a fine deed, blameworthy when it seeks an ugly one. He cites 27:50 for both kinds: their scheme (the blameworthy kind) and Allah's, as befits Him (the praiseworthy kind); mufassirun often explain the latter as requital.

why.bs: „A ružna spletka pogađa samo one koji je smišljaju” – pokuđena spletka se vraća svom vlasniku.
why.en: “But the evil plot does not encompass except its own people” — the blameworthy scheme returns on its maker.

why.bs: „I oni su smišljali spletku, a i Mi smo smislili spletku, a oni nisu ni slutili” – ar-Rāġib: obje vrste u jednom ajetu; Allahova, kako Njemu priliči, je pohvalna vrsta; mufessiri je objašnjavaju kao uzvraćanje.
why.en: “And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, while they perceived not” — ar-Rāġib: both kinds in one ayah; Allah's, as befits Him, is the praiseworthy kind; mufassirun explain it as requital.

why.bs: Nuhov narod: „i spletkarili su spletkom velikom” – spletkarenje.
why.en: Noah's people: “and they conspired an immense conspiracy” — scheming.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o tijesnom. Prema ar-Rāġibu, ضِيق je suprotnost prostranosti i izražava tugu, siromaštvo ili škrtost, a حَرَج dolazi od gustog, zbijenog skupa stvari, pa znači i tjeskobu i grijeh.
shared.en: Both words speak of tightness. According to ar-Rāġib, ضِيق is the opposite of spaciousness and expresses grief, poverty or stinginess, while حَرَج comes from a thick, close-packed cluster of things, and so means both constriction and sin.

tellApart.bs: Biti stiješnjen – grudi, duša, Zemlja; nemoć i tuga pred nečim → ضَاقَ; teškoća koja se nameće, a i grijeh („nema ḥaraja na…”) → حَرَج.
tellApart.en: To be straitened — the breast, the soul, the earth; helplessness and grief before a thing → ضَاقَ; a hardship laid on someone, and also sin (“there is no ḥaraj upon…”) → حَرَج.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ضيق, حرج
notes: ar-Rāġib (ضيق): ḍīq is the opposite of saʿa; ḍayq/ḍīqa is used for poverty, stinginess, grief and the like; 11:77 'ḍāqa bihim ḏarʿan' = he was unable to deal with them; 11:12, 26:13, 6:125, 9:25, 9:118, 16:127 — 'all of that expresses grief'. (حرج): the root of ḥaraǧ is a close gathering of a thing, from which the narrowness between is imagined, so narrowness is called ḥaraǧ and sin is called ḥaraǧ; 4:65, 22:78; 6:125 'constricted by his unbelief', and it has been said 'constricted towards Islam'; on 7:2 he lists three readings (prohibition, prayer, ruling).

That the verb ضَاقَ in its seven uses (9:25, 9:118 ×2, 11:77, 15:97, 26:13, 29:33) is said of the breast, the soul, the earth and of Lot 'with them', never of a rule or of sin, is our observation. 7:2 and 6:125 are not cited (readings differ).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, suprotnost prostranosti; o grudima, duši i Zemlji izražava tugu, a „ضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا” znači da je bio nemoćan pred njima. U kur'anskoj upotrebi glagol se kaže samo za grudi, dušu, Zemlju i za Luta pred gostima – nikad za propis ili grijeh.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the opposite of spaciousness; said of the breast, the soul and the earth it expresses grief, and “ضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا” means he was at a loss with them. In Quranic usage the verb is said only of the breast, the soul, the earth and of Lot before his guests — never of a rule or of sin.

why.bs: „…kad im je Zemlja, onako prostrana, postala tijesna, i kad su im duše njihove postale stiješnjene” – tijesnoća i tuga.
why.en: “…until, when the earth closed in on them in spite of its vastness and their souls confined them” — the constriction of soul and earth, of grief.

why.bs: Lut se „zbog njih zabrinu i nemoćan osjeti” – ar-Rāġib: bio je nemoćan pred njima.
why.en: Lot “was anguished for them and felt for them great discomfort” — ar-Rāġib: he was at a loss with them.

why.bs: Musa: „i grudi će mi se stegnuti, a jezik mi se neće razvezati” – tjeskoba pred velikim zadatkom.
why.en: Moses: “And that my breast will tighten and my tongue will not be fluent” — distress before a great task.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korijen je gust, zbijen skup stvari, pa se tjeskoba među njima zove حَرَج, a tako i grijeh. Zato Kur'an kaže da u vjeri nema teškoće (22:78) i da „nema smetnje” bolesnom i slijepom (24:61).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is a thick, close-packed cluster of things, so the tightness among them is called حَرَج, and so is sin. Hence the Quran says there is no hardship in the religion (22:78) and “no constraint” upon the sick and the blind (24:61).

why.bs: „…i u vjeri vam nije nametnuo nikakvu teškoću” – teškoća koja se nameće.
why.en: “…and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty” — a hardship laid upon people.

why.bs: „Nema smetnje slijepom…” – skidanje teškoće; mnogi mufesiri to shvaćaju i kao krivicu.
why.en: “There is not upon the blind [any] constraint…” — a lifting of hardship; many mufassirun also take it as blame.

why.bs: „…i da potom u dušama svojim ne osjete nikakve tegobe zbog onoga što si presudio” – tjeskoba u duši.
why.en: “…and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged” — tightness within the soul.

title.en: Making clear and setting out in detail

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače učiniti nešto razumljivim. Prema ar-Rāġibu, بَيَان je otkrivanje stvari, a فَصْل razdvajanje jedne stvari od druge tako da među njima ostane razmak – a تَفْصِيل Knjige povezuje s time da je ona „objašnjenje svega”.
shared.en: Both verbs mean making a thing understood. According to ar-Rāġib, بَيَان is uncovering a thing, and فَصْل is separating one thing from another so that a gap stays between them — and he ties the Book's تَفْصِيل to its being “an explanation of all things”.

tellApart.bs: Pojasniti, otkriti ono što je skriveno ili nejasno – Allah, poslanik, i učeni ljudi → بَيَّنَ; potanko izložiti, razdvojiti dio od dijela – u Kur'anu uvijek Allahovi ajeti, Knjiga, zabranjeno → فَصَّلَ.
tellApart.en: To make clear, to uncover what was hidden or unclear — Allah, a messenger, and people of learning → بَيَّنَ; to set out in detail, separating part from part — in the Quran always Allah's verses, the Book, what is forbidden → فَصَّلَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بان, فصل
notes: ar-Rāġib (بان): bayān is uncovering (kašf) a thing, more general than speech; bayyantuhu / abantuhu = I gave it a bayān that discloses it (16:44); what explains the summary and the obscure is called bayān (75:19); clear signs bayyināt. (فصل): faṣl is separating one of two things from the other until there is a gap between them; used of acts and words; 17:12 'everything We set out in detail', 11:1 'perfected, then set out in detail', pointing to 16:89 'an explanation of all things'.

Our observation of the corpus: the active فَصَّلَ (17 uses) has Allah as subject every time, and its passive forms are said of the Book's verses (11:1, 41:3, 41:44); بَيَّنَ is also said of messengers (16:44, 14:4, 43:63) and of people (2:160, 3:187).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dati stvari objašnjenje koje je otkriva; بَيَان je otkrivanje, šire od govora. U Kur'anu pojašnjava Allah (ajete), poslanik (Objavu ljudima), ali i ljudi od Knjige, kojima je naređeno da je pojasne a ne skrivaju.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, giving a thing an explanation that uncovers it; بَيَان is disclosure, wider than speech. In the Quran Allah makes clear (the verses), a messenger makes clear (the revelation to people), and so must the People of the Book, who were told to make it clear and not conceal it.

why.bs: „Eto tako vam Allah jasno iznosi ajete Svoje da biste razumjeli.”
why.en: “Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you might understand.”

why.bs: „…da bi ljudima objasnio ono što im se objavljuje” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za بَيَّنَ.
why.en: “…that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for بَيَّنَ.

why.bs: „Objasnite je ljudima i ne skrivajte je!” – pojasniti je suprotno od skriti.
why.en: “You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it” — to make clear is the opposite of to conceal.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, فَصْل je razdvajanje dviju stvari tako da među njima ostane razmak; تَفْصِيل Knjige povezuje s time da je ona „objašnjenje svega”. U kur'anskoj upotrebi onaj ko potanko izlaže uvijek je Allah, a izloženo su ajeti, Knjiga, zabranjeno, „sve”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, فَصْل is separating two things so that a gap stays between them; the Book's تَفْصِيل he ties to its being “an explanation of all things”. In Quranic usage the one who sets out in detail is always Allah, and what is set out is the verses, the Book, what is forbidden, “everything”.

why.bs: „Knjiga čiji su ajeti učvršćeni, a zatim potanko izloženi, od Mudroga i Sveznajućeg” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “A Book whose verses are perfected and then presented in detail from [one who is] Wise and Acquainted” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „…a On vam je potanko izložio ono što vam je zabranio” – zabranjeno, potanko izloženo.
why.en: “…while He has set out in detail to you what He has forbidden you” — what is forbidden, set out in detail.

why.bs: „…i sve smo potanko izložili” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And everything We have set out in detail” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi imenuju kaznu koja je zadesila ranije narode. Prema ar-Rāġibu, رَجْفَة je snažno potresanje, صَيْحَة podizanje glasa, a صَاعِقَة silan zvuk s neba od kojeg dolazi vatra, kazna ili smrt. Isti narod, Semud, opisan je svakom od tri riječi. Mufesiri često objašnjavaju da je to jedna kazna opisana s različitih strana: strašni glas odozgo i potres tla.
shared.en: All three words name the punishment that seized earlier peoples. According to ar-Rāġib, رَجْفَة is violent shaking, صَيْحَة is raising the voice, and صَاعِقَة is a mighty sound from the sky that brings fire, punishment or death. One people, Thamud, is described with each of the three. Mufassirun often explain that this is one punishment described from different sides: the dreadful sound from above and the quaking of the ground.

tellApart.bs: Potres – tlo se snažno trese (Semud, Medjen) → رَجْفَة; krik – glas koji obuzme strahom; i puhanje u rog → صَيْحَة; munja – silan prasak s neba, i grom koji pogađa → صَاعِقَة.
tellApart.en: Quake — the ground shakes violently (Thamud, Midian) → رَجْفَة; shriek — a sound that seizes with terror; also the blast of the Horn → صَيْحَة; thunderbolt — a mighty crash from the sky, the bolt that strikes → صَاعِقَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رجف, صاح, صعق
notes: ar-Rāġib (رجف): rajf is violent agitation, of the earth and the sea; 79:6, 73:14, 'fa-aḫaḏathumu r-rajfa'; irǧāf is causing rajfa by act or word (33:60). (صاح): ṣayḥa is raising the voice (36:29; 50:42 = the blowing of the Horn); its root is the splitting of sound; because a shout terrifies, it expresses terror in 15:73. (صعق): ṣāʿiqa and ṣāqiʿa are close — a great crash; ṣaqʿ for earthly bodies, ṣaʿq for heavenly ones; some linguists say ṣāʿiqa is of three kinds (death 39:68, punishment 41:13, fire 13:13); he answers that these are effects of it: the ṣāʿiqa is the violent sound from the sky, from which come fire alone, or punishment, or death.

Thamud: الرَّجْفَة 7:78, الصَّيْحَة 11:67, صَاعِقَة 41:17 and 51:44; Midian: الرَّجْفَة 7:91 and 29:37, الصَّيْحَة 11:94 — our listing. That mufassirun reconcile these as one punishment described from different sides is given as 'mufassirun often explain', not as ar-Rāġib's.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, snažno potresanje, kaže se za zemlju i more. U Kur'anu (4 puta) kazna koja je zadesila Semud i Medjen, i potres koji je obuzeo sedamdesetoricu odabranih od Musaovog naroda.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, violent shaking, said of the earth and the sea. In the Quran (4 times) the punishment that seized Thamud and Midian, and the quake that seized the seventy chosen from Moses' people.

why.bs: Semud: „I zadesi ih potres…” – što 11:67 naziva krikom; mnogi mufessiri to shvaćaju kao jednu kaznu viđenu s dvije strane.
why.en: Thamud: “So the earthquake seized them…” — which 11:67 calls the shriek; many mufassirun take it as one punishment seen from two sides.

why.bs: Medjen, Šuajbov narod: „I zadesi ih potres…” – što 11:94 naziva krikom; mnogi mufessiri to shvaćaju kao jednu kaznu viđenu s dvije strane.
why.en: Midian, the people of Shuʿayb: “So the earthquake seized them…” — which 11:94 calls the shriek; many mufassirun take it as one punishment seen from two sides.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, podizanje glasa; korijen je pucanje zvuka, a pošto krik plaši, kaže se i za sam strah (15:73). U Kur'anu kazna Semudu, Medjenu i Lutovom narodu, ali i puhanje u rog kod proživljenja (50:42).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, raising the voice; the root is the cracking of sound, and since a shout terrifies, it is said of terror itself (15:73). In the Quran the punishment of Thamud, Midian and Lot's people, and also the blast of the Horn at the resurrection (50:42).

why.bs: Semud: „A one koji su činili nepravdu zadesi strašan glas, i oni osvanuše mrtvi u kućama svojim, ničice.”
why.en: Thamud: “And the shriek seized those who had wronged, and they became within their homes [corpses] fallen prone.”

why.bs: Lutov narod: „I njih u osvit zore zadesi strašan glas” – ar-Rāġib: ovdje krik u značenju straha.
why.en: Lot's people: “So the shriek seized them at sunrise” — ar-Rāġib: here the shriek in the sense of terror.

why.bs: „Na Dan kada će zaista čuti glas” – ar-Rāġib: puhanje u rog.
why.en: “The Day they will hear the blast in truth” — ar-Rāġib: the blowing of the Horn.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, silan zvuk s neba; od njega dolazi vatra, kazna ili smrt – to su njegovi učinci, a sam je jedna stvar. Neki jezikoslovci su, prenosi on, razlikovali tri značenja: smrt, kaznu i vatru. U Kur'anu kazna Semudu i Adu, ali i munje u oluji (13:13).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a mighty sound from the sky; from it come fire, punishment or death — these are its effects, while it is itself one thing. Some linguists, he reports, distinguished three senses: death, punishment and fire. In the Quran the punishment of Thamud and ʿĀd, and also the bolts in a storm (13:13).

why.bs: Semud: „…pa ih je pogodila munja ponižavajuće kazne” – treća riječ za istu propast.
why.en: Thamud: “…so the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them” — a third word for the same ruin.

why.bs: „Ja vas opominjem munjom kakva je pogodila Ad i Semud” – ar-Rāġib (prenoseći neke jezikoslovce): munja kao kazna.
why.en: “I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt [that struck] ʿĀd and Thamud” — ar-Rāġib (reporting some linguists): the thunderbolt as punishment.

why.bs: „…i šalje munje i pogađa njima koga hoće” – šalje ih Allah i usmjerava.
why.en: “…and He sends thunderbolts and strikes therewith whom He wills” — sent and aimed by Allah.

shared.bs: Oba glagola su položaji poniznosti i dijelovi namaza. Prema ar-Rāġibu, سُجُود je u osnovi spuštanje i poniznost, i kaže se za ljude, životinje i neživo, dok je رُكُوع pregibanje – položaj u namazu, ili poniznost u ibadetu i izvan njega.
shared.en: Both verbs are postures of humility and parts of the prayer. According to ar-Rāġib, سُجُود is at root lowering and humbling oneself, and is said of people, animals and lifeless things, while رُكُوع is bending — the posture in prayer, or humility in worship and outside it.

tellApart.bs: Sedždu činiti – čelom na zemlju; i pokornost svega stvorenog Allahu, htjelo ili ne htjelo → سَجَدَ; ruku' činiti, pregnuti se – položaj u namazu; u Kur'anu glagol samo o ljudima → رَكَعَ.
tellApart.en: To prostrate — the forehead to the ground; also the submission of all creation to Allah, willingly or not → سَجَدَ; to bow — the posture in prayer; in the Quran the verb is used only of people → رَكَعَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سجد, ركع
notes: ar-Rāġib (سجد): the root of sujūd is lowering oneself and humility; it was made an expression of humility to Allah and worship; it is general to people, animals and lifeless things; two kinds: by choice — only of man, rewarded (53:62) — and of subjection (tasḫīr) — of man, animals and plants (13:15, 16:48), the silent testimony that they are created; 16:49 holds both kinds; in the Sharia it is specified for the known pillar of the prayer, and the Quran and thanks prostrations; on 2:34 he reports two views (Adam as qibla, or humility and service to him). (ركع): rukūʿ is bending; used sometimes for the specific posture in the prayer, sometimes for humility and lowering oneself, in worship or otherwise (22:77, 2:43, 2:125, 9:112).

That the verb رَكَعَ (5 uses in 4 ayat: 2:43, 3:43, 22:77, 77:48) is used only of people, while سَجَدَ is also said of shadows, creatures and the angels (13:15, 16:49, 22:18), is our observation. 2:34 and 55:6 are not cited (readings differ); 38:24 (Dāwūd, rākiʿan) is not cited.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, osnova je spuštanje i poniznost. Sedžda je dvojaka: svojevoljna – samo kod čovjeka, i za nju je nagrada – i sedžda pokornosti, kojom sve stvoreno, i ljudi, životinje i biljke, svjedoči da je stvoreno. U šerijatu je to poznati rukn namaza.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the root is lowering oneself and humility. Prostration is of two kinds: by choice — only of man, and it is rewarded — and the prostration of subjection, by which all creation, people, animals and plants, testifies that it is created. In the Sharia it is the known pillar of the prayer.

why.bs: „Zato Allahu sedždu činite i Njemu se klanjajte!” – ar-Rāġib: svojevoljna sedžda, za koju je nagrada.
why.en: “So prostrate to Allah and worship [Him]” — ar-Rāġib: prostration by choice, which is rewarded.

why.bs: „Allahu sedždu čini (pokorava se) sve što je na nebesima i na Zemlji, htjelo ili ne htjelo, a i sjene njihove” – ar-Rāġib: sedžda pokornosti.
why.en: “And to Allah prostrates whoever is within the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and their shadows” — ar-Rāġib: the prostration of subjection.

why.bs: „Allahu sedždu čini sve što je na nebesima i na Zemlji od živih bića, i meleki, i oni se ne ohole” – ar-Rāġib: obje vrste sedžde u jednom ajetu.
why.en: “And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and on the earth of creatures, and the angels, and they are not arrogant” — ar-Rāġib: both kinds in one ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, pregibanje: nekad poseban položaj u namazu, nekad poniznost i pokornost, u ibadetu ili izvan njega. U Kur'anu se glagol kaže samo za ljude, i uglavnom uz namaz i sedždu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, bending: sometimes the special posture in the prayer, sometimes humility and submission, in worship or outside it. In the Quran the verb is said only of people, and mostly together with the prayer and prostration.

why.bs: „…i ruku' činite s onima koji ruku' čine” – mnogi mufessiri: ruku' u namazu s onima koji klanjaju.
why.en: “…and bow with those who bow” — many mufassirun: bowing in prayer with the worshippers.

why.bs: „O vjernici, ruku' i sedždu činite i Gospodaru svome se klanjajte” – oba položaja jedan za drugim.
why.en: “O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord” — the two postures one after the other.

why.bs: „A kad im se kaže: ‘Učinite ruku’!’ – oni ruku’ ne čine” – odbijaju naredbu da ruku' učine.
why.en: “And when it is said to them, ‘Bow,’ they do not bow” — they refuse the command to bow.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače baciti. Prema ar-Rāġibu, رَمْي se kaže za predmete poput strijele i kamena, a قَذْف je bacanje u daljinu; oba se prenesena značenja kažu i za vrijeđanje.
shared.en: Both verbs mean to throw. According to ar-Rāġib, رَمْي is said of objects such as an arrow or a stone, while قَذْف is throwing far; both are also used figuratively for insult.

tellApart.bs: Gađati, bacati nešto na nekoga – kamen, strijelu; i potvoriti nekoga (24:4) → رَمَى; hitnuti, baciti daleko ili snažno – u rijeku, strah u srca, istinu na laž → قَذَفَ.
tellApart.en: To throw something at someone — a stone, an arrow; also to accuse someone falsely (24:4) → رَمَى; to hurl, to throw far or with force — into the river, terror into hearts, truth upon falsehood → قَذَفَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رمى, قذف
notes: ar-Rāġib (رمى): ramy is said of objects such as an arrow and a stone (8:17); in speech it is a metonymy for abuse, like qaḏf (24:6, 24:4). (قذف): qaḏf is throwing far — hence a far dwelling is qaḏaf; 20:39 = throw him into it; 33:26, 34:48, 21:18, 37:8; qaḏf is borrowed for abuse and reproach as ramy is.

That the Quran uses رَمَى, never قَذَفَ, for the accusation of chaste women (24:4, 24:6, 24:23; 4:112) — the later legal term qaḏf notwithstanding — is our observation. 8:17: the throw of a handful of earth at Badr; tafsir differs little on it, and it is not a reproach.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, kaže se za predmete poput strijele i kamena; u govoru je prenesen izraz za vrijeđanje. U kur'anskoj upotrebi upravo se ovim glagolom, a ne s قَذَفَ, kaže potvaranje čestitih žena (24:4).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, said of objects such as an arrow or a stone; in speech it is a figurative term for insult. In Quranic usage it is this verb, not قَذَفَ, that names the false accusation of chaste women (24:4).

why.bs: „I nisi ti bacio kad si bacio, nego je Allah bacio” (kako Njemu priliči) – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za bacanje predmeta; mufesiri: šaka prašine na Bedru.
why.en: “And you threw not when you threw, but it was Allah who threw” (as befits Him) — ar-Rāġib cites it for throwing an object; mufassirun: the handful of dust at Badr.

why.bs: „Koje su ih gađale kamenčićima od pečene gline” – gađanje predmetom.
why.en: “Striking them with stones of hard clay” — throwing an object at a target.

why.bs: „One koji potvore čestite žene…” – ar-Rāġib: رَمْي u govoru, kao vrijeđanje.
why.en: “And those who accuse chaste women…” — ar-Rāġib: رَمْي in speech, as abuse.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, bacanje u daljinu; otuda i daleko mjesto se zove قَذَف. U Kur'anu Musaova majka ga baca u rijeku, Allah ubacuje strah u srca neprijatelja i „baca istinu na laž”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, throwing far; hence a distant place is called قَذَف. In the Quran Moses' mother casts him into the river, Allah casts terror into the hearts of the enemy, and “hurls the truth upon falsehood”.

why.bs: „Stavi ga u kovčeg i baci ga u rijeku” – ar-Rāġib: baci ga u nju.
why.en: “Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river” — ar-Rāġib: throw him into it.

why.bs: „…i u srca njihova ubaci strah” – bacanje preneseno na ono što obuzme iznutra.
why.en: “…and cast terror into their hearts” — casting said of what seizes from within.

why.bs: „Naprotiv, Mi istinu na laž obrušavamo pa je ona uništava” – snažan udar.
why.en: “Rather, We dash the truth upon falsehood, and it destroys it” — a forceful hurl.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače nešto teško što se nosi. Prema ar-Rāġibu, وِزْر je težina, nazvana po planinskom skloništu (وَزَر), i njime se izražava grijeh, kao što se izražava i težinom (ثِقْل).
shared.en: Both words mean a heavy thing that is carried. According to ar-Rāġib, وِزْر is weight, named after a mountain refuge (وَزَر), and sin is expressed by it, as it is also expressed by heaviness (ثِقْل).

tellApart.bs: Breme – u Kur'anu najčešće grijeh koji čovjek nosi; niko neće nositi tuđe breme → وِزْر; teret – u Kur'anu najčešće tjelesni tovar, a jednom i grijesi (29:13) → ثَقَل / أَثْقَال.
tellApart.en: Burden — in the Quran mostly the sin a person carries; no one bears another's burden → وِزْر; load — in the Quran mostly a physical load, and once sins (29:13) → ثَقَل / أَثْقَال.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries وزر, ثقل
notes: ar-Rāġib (وزر): wazar is the refuge one takes in a mountain (75:11); wizr is heaviness, by comparison with the mountain's wazar, and sin is expressed by it as it is by ṯiql (16:25, like 29:13); bearing another's wizr is as in the hadith of whoever starts a bad practice — the like of their burden; 6:164 'no bearer bears another's burden' in the sense that it is not lifted off the other; awzār of war are its weapons; 20:87 awzār of the people's ornament. (ثقل): ṯiql and ḫiffa are opposites; at root of bodies, then of meanings (a debt or a wizr weighs one down); 16:7 your heavy loads; 29:13 their sins that weigh them down, like 16:25; on 99:2 it has been said her treasures, and it has been said the bodies of men at the resurrection.

Corpus: the lemma ثَقَل includes its broken plural أَثْقَال and the dual الثَّقَلَان (55:31, men and jinn) — summed by the corpus. That وِزْر means sin in most of its places (6:31, 6:164, 16:25, 17:15, 20:100, 35:18, 39:7, 53:38) and something else in 20:87 (loads of ornaments) and 47:4 (war's burdens) is our observation. 94:2 (said to the Prophet; readings differ) is not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 of 3 flagged, fixed: bs breme for وِزْر, teret for ثَقَل; en burden / load kept apart (29:13, 99:2 'loads').

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, težina – nazvana po planinskom skloništu – kojom se izražava grijeh. U kur'anskoj upotrebi najčešće grijeh koji čovjek nosi na Sudnjem danu; nositi tuđe breme znači, kaže on, nositi isto toliko, a da se drugome ne skida.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, weight — named after a mountain refuge — by which sin is expressed. In Quranic usage mostly the sin a person carries on the Day of Resurrection; bearing another's burden means, he says, bearing as much again, without its being lifted off the other.

why.bs: „…i nijedan grješnik neće nositi tuđe breme” – grijeh se ne prenosi s jednog na drugog.
why.en: “…and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another” — sin does not pass from one to another.

why.bs: „…da bi na Sudnjem danu nosili potpuno svoja bremena, i dio bremena onih koje su zaveli” – ar-Rāġib: kao 29:13.
why.en: “That they may bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection and some of the burdens of those whom they misguide” — ar-Rāġib: like 29:13.

why.bs: „…nego smo bili natovareni bremenima nakita naroda” – breme u doslovnom smislu.
why.en: “…but we were made to carry burdens from the ornaments of the people” — burdens in the literal sense.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, težina je u osnovi svojstvo tijela, a onda se kaže i za značenja – za dug i grijeh koji pritišću. U Kur'anu أَثْقَال su najčešće tovari koje nose životinje ili Zemlja, a jednom grijesi (29:13).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, heaviness is at root a property of bodies, and is then said of meanings — of a debt or a sin that weighs one down. In the Quran أَثْقَال are mostly loads carried by animals or by the earth, and once sins (29:13).

why.bs: „I nose vaše terete do krajeva…” – ar-Rāġib: vaši teški tovari.
why.en: “And they carry your loads to a land…” — ar-Rāġib: your heavy loads.

why.bs: „A nosiće, sigurno, terete svoje i terete uz terete svoje” – ar-Rāġib: grijesi koji ih pritišću.
why.en: “But they will surely carry their [own] loads and [other] loads along with their loads” — ar-Rāġib: the sins that weigh them down.

why.bs: „I kad zemlja izbaci terete svoje” – ar-Rāġib prenosi dva tumačenja: njena blaga, ili tijela umrlih pri proživljenju.
why.en: “And the earth discharges its loads” — ar-Rāġib reports two readings: its treasures, or the bodies of the dead at the resurrection.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o tome da čovjek drži sebe u vlasti. Razlikuju se po tome šta se drži i kada: duša na onome što traže razum i vjera, narav koja ne da srdžbi da se uzburka, ili srdžba koja se već podigla pa se zadržava.
shared.en: All three words speak of a person holding himself in check. They differ in what is held and when: the soul kept to what reason and the Law require, a nature that does not let anger stir, or anger already risen that is held in.

tellApart.bs: Držati dušu na onome što traže razum i vjera, opća riječ → صَبْر; narav koja obuzdava dušu da se srdžba ne uzburka → حَلِيم; zadržati u sebi srdžbu ili tjeskobu koja se već podigla, kao što se zadržava dah → كَاظِم.
tellApart.en: Keeping the soul to what reason and the Law require, the general word → صَبْر; a nature that restrains the soul so that anger does not stir → حَلِيم; holding in an anger or distress already risen, as breath is held → كَاظِم.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries صبر, حلم, كظم
notes: ar-Rāġib (صبر): ṣabr is holding back in narrowness; restraining the soul to what reason and the Law require, or from what they require it to be kept from; a general word whose names differ by situation (in calamity ṣabr, against jazaʿ; in battle courage; in an irksome affair 'breadth of breast'; in holding speech kitmān), and Allah called all of it ṣabr (2:177). (حلم): ḥilm is controlling the soul and nature against the stirring of anger; 11:75 Ibrāhīm ḥalīm; 37:101 ġulām ḥalīm = one in whom the strength of ḥilm was found; aḥlām in 52:32 'it was said' = minds, which he says is not its real meaning. (كظم): kaẓm is the outlet of breath, kuẓūm the holding of breath; kaẓm al-ġayẓ is holding anger in (3:134); 68:48 makẓūm.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 15 places read): حَلِيم is said of Allah in 11 places (always beside another Name: غَفُور, غَنِيّ, عَلِيم, شَكُور), of Ibrāhīm (9:114, 11:75), of the boy given to him (37:101), and of Šuʿayb by his mocking people (11:87). The gloss 'He does not hasten punishment' for Allah's ḥilm is the mufassirun's, not ar-Rāġib's entry. كَاظِم is 2× (3:134, 40:18); كَظِيم (12:84, 16:58, 43:17) is a different lemma and not counted.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 6 flags, fixed: distinct words per member (držati dušu / obuzdavati / zadržati u sebi; keeping / mastering / holding in); 'a trait, not a moment's effort' marked as our observation; 11:75 bs and en aligned; 40:18 'grief held in' given to many mufassirun; 3:134 Allah's love 'as befits Him'.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries صبر, حلم, كظم (2026-11-06): 25 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): The trait-vs-moment contrast is our gloss; the closest support is his 'quwwat al-ḥilm' for 37:101. Mild; alternatively drop the dash clause

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, držati dušu na onome što traže razum i vjera, ili je držati podalje od onoga od čega oni traže da se čuva. To je opća riječ: u nesreći je to strpljenje, u borbi hrabrost, u govoru čuvanje tajne – a Allah je sve to nazvao strpljenjem.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, keeping the soul to what reason and the Law require, or away from what they require it to be kept from. It is a general word: in calamity it is patience, in battle courage, in speech keeping a secret — and Allah called all of it patience.

why.bs: „I tražite pomoć u strpljenju i molitvi.”
why.en: “And seek help through patience and prayer.”

why.bs: Talutovi vojnici pred Džalutom: „Gospodaru naš, izlij na nas strpljenje i učvrsti korake naše” – strpljenje u borbi, koje ar-Rāġib naziva i hrabrošću.
why.en: Saul's soldiers facing Goliath: “Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet” — patience in battle, which ar-Rāġib also calls courage.

why.bs: Jakub, kad su mu donijeli košulju s lažnom krvlju: „Lijepo strpljenje!”
why.en: Jacob, when the shirt with false blood was brought to him: “Patience is most fitting.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḥilm je ovladavanje duše i naravi nad uzburkavanjem srdžbe; za obećanog dječaka kaže da je u njemu bila snaga blagosti. To upućuje na osobinu, a ne na trenutni napor (naše zapažanje). Blagim Kur'an naziva Ibrahima i dječaka koji mu je obećan, a najčešće Allaha, kako Njemu priliči: mufessiri to objašnjavaju time da On ne požuruje s kaznom.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḥilm is the soul and nature mastering the stirring of anger; of the promised boy he says the strength of ḥilm was found in him. This suggests a trait rather than a moment's effort (our observation). The Quran calls Abraham and the boy promised to him forbearing, and most often Allah, as befits Him: the mufassirun explain it as His not hastening punishment.

why.bs: „Ibrahim je, zaista, bio blag, sažaljiv i pokajnik” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, tender-hearted and [frequently] returning [to Allah]” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I Mi smo ga obradovali blagim dječakom” – ar-Rāġib: dječak u kome je bila snaga blagosti.
why.en: “So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy” — ar-Rāġib: one in whom the strength of forbearance was found.

why.bs: „Lijepa riječ i oprost bolji su od milostinje koju prati uvreda; a Allah je Bogat i Blag” – blagost kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “Kind speech and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And Allah is Free of need and Forbearing” — forbearance as befits Him.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, kaẓm je izvorno mjesto kuda izlazi dah, a kuẓūm zadržavanje daha; zato kaẓm al-ġayẓ znači zadržati srdžbu u sebi, ne pustiti je van. Srdžba je već tu – suzdržava se njeno izbijanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, kaẓm is at root the outlet of breath, and kuẓūm the holding of breath; so kaẓm al-ġayẓ is to hold anger in, not letting it out. The anger is already there — what is held back is its breaking out.

why.bs: „I koji srdžbu suzdržavaju i ljudima opraštaju – a Allah voli one koji dobro čine” (Njegova ljubav kako Njemu priliči) – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And who restrain anger and who pardon the people — and Allah loves the doers of good” (His love as befits Him) — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Na Dan koji se približava „srca će doći do grla, a oni će se gušiti” – mnogi mufessiri to shvataju kao zadržanu tugu, poput zadržanog daha.
why.en: On the Approaching Day “the hearts are at the throats, choking” — many mufassirun understand it as grief held in, like held breath.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o neuspjehu. Razlikuju se po tome da li se gubi ono što se već imalo ili se promašuje ono čemu se težilo.
shared.en: Both words speak of failure. They differ in whether one loses what one already had or misses what one was seeking.

tellApart.bs: Izgubiti od onoga što se imalo – kapital, a u Kur'anu samoga sebe i nagradu → خَسِرَ; ostati bez onoga čemu se težilo i nadalo → خَابَ.
tellApart.en: To lose from what one had — capital, and in the Quran one's own self and reward → خَسِرَ; to miss what one sought and hoped for → خَابَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries خسر, خاب
notes: ar-Rāġib (خسر): ḫusr / ḫusrān is the diminishing of capital, said of a man (ḫasira fulān) and of his deed (his trade lost); used of outward acquisitions such as wealth and standing in this world, which is most common, and of inner ones such as health, soundness, reason, faith and reward — which Allah made 'the manifest loss' (39:15); every ḫusrān Allah mentions in the Quran is in this latter sense, not worldly trade. (خاب): ḫayba is missing what was sought (fawt aṭ-ṭalab), with 14:15, 20:61, 91:10.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 16 / 4 places read): the object of خَسِرَ is 'themselves' (أَنْفُسَهُم) in 8 places (6:12, 6:20, 7:9, 7:53, 11:21, 23:103, 39:15, 42:45); خَابَ is said of the tyrant (14:15), the one who invents a lie (20:61), the one who carries wrongdoing (20:111) and the one who corrupts his soul (91:10). 22:11 (ḫasira d-dunyā wa-l-āḫira) is not cited: it names this world too, against ar-Rāġib's general remark.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, gubitak je umanjenje glavnice – kao u trgovini. Kaže se za imetak i ugled na ovom svijetu, ali i za zdravlje, razum, vjerovanje i nagradu; on kaže da je svaki gubitak koji Allah spominje u Kur'anu ove druge vrste. U Kur'anu se često gube „sami sebe”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, loss is the diminishing of capital — as in trade. It is said of wealth and standing in this world, but also of health, reason, faith and reward; he says every loss Allah mentions in the Quran is of this second kind. In the Quran people often lose “themselves”.

why.bs: „Gubitnici su oni koji na Sudnjem danu izgube sebe i porodice svoje; to je, zaista, očiti gubitak” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “The losers are the ones who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A oni čije vage budu lake – oni su sami sebe izgubili.”
why.en: “And those whose scales are light — they are the ones who will lose themselves.”

why.bs: „Izgubili su oni koji poriču susret s Allahom.”
why.en: “Those will have lost who deny the meeting with Allah.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḫayba je promašiti ono čemu se težilo. Naglasak je na nadi koja se ne ostvari, a ne na glavnici koja se smanjuje (naše zapažanje). U Kur'anu (4×) se kaže za silnika, lažca, nepravednika i onoga ko svoju dušu grijesima zaprlja.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḫayba is missing what one sought. The stress falls on the hope that does not come, not on a stock that shrinks (our observation). In the Quran (4×) it is said of the tyrant, the liar, the wrongdoer and the one who corrupts his soul.

why.bs: „I zatražiše pobjedu, a razočaran ostade svaki silnik, inadžija” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And they sought victory, and disappointed was every obstinate tyrant” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A razočaran će ostati onaj ko je (dušu) grijesima zaprlja” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And he has failed who corrupts it [his soul]” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Musa vračarima: „Ne izmišljajte laži o Allahu … razočaran ostaje onaj ko izmišlja.”
why.en: Moses to the magicians: “Do not invent a lie against Allah … he has failed who invents.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače mjesto gdje leže mrtvi. U Kur'anu se razlikuju po prizoru u kojem stoje.
shared.en: Both words mean the place where the dead lie. In the Quran they differ in the scene in which they stand.

tellApart.bs: Mjesto gdje mrtvi borave – i na ovom svijetu i pri proživljenju → قَبْر; grobišta iz kojih ljudi izlaze na Sudnji dan – sva tri puta → أَجْدَاث.
tellApart.en: The place where the dead stay — in this world and at the raising → قَبْر; the burial places people come out of on the Day of Resurrection — all three times → أَجْدَاث.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قبر, جدث
notes: ar-Rāġib (قبر): qabr is the resting place of the dead; qabartuhu = I put him in the grave, aqbartuhu = I gave him a place to be buried (80:21, 'it was said': taught how to bury); 102:2 'you visited the graveyards' = death; 82:4 points to the raising, 'and it was said' to the uncovering of secrets; 35:22 'those in the graves' = those who are as the dead. (جدث): only that ajdāṯ is the plural of jadaṯ (also jadaf), with 70:43 and 36:51.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 6 / 3 places read): قَبْر is said of a grave in this world (9:84, 60:13) and of the raising (22:7, 82:4, 100:9), and figuratively in 35:22; أَجْدَاث is in all three places what people come out of at the Resurrection (36:51, 54:7, 70:43). The contrast is our own observation; ar-Rāġib's جدث entry gives no meaning beyond the plural. 9:84 (addressed to the Prophet) is not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: his 'points to the raising' is on 100:9 (bi'ṯira mā fī l-qubūr), not 82:4; 'in haste' only for 36:51 and 70:43, not 54:7.
