nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, mjesto gdje mrtvi borave. U Kur'anu se spominje i grob na ovom svijetu i proživljenje iz grobova; ar-Rāġib kaže da 100:9 ukazuje na proživljenje, a navodi i mišljenje da se misli na otkrivanje tajni.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the resting place of the dead. The Quran speaks both of a grave in this world and of the raising from the graves; ar-Rāġib says 100:9 points to the raising, and also reports the view that it means the uncovering of secrets.

why.bs: „I da će Allah, sigurno, oživiti one koji su u grobovima.”
why.en: “And that Allah will resurrect those in the graves.”

why.bs: „I kad se grobovi ispreturaju” – proživljenje iz grobova.
why.en: “And when the graves are scattered [open]” — the raising from the graves.

why.bs: „A zar on ne zna – kad bude izbačeno ono što je u grobovima…” – ar-Rāġib: ukazuje na proživljenje.
why.en: “But does he not know that when the contents of the graves are scattered…” — ar-Rāġib: it points to the raising.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib kaže samo da je to množina od jadaṯ. U Kur'anu sva tri puta stoji u istom prizoru: na Sudnji dan ljudi izlaze iz grobišta (žurno, u 36:51 i 70:43) – to je naše zapažanje o kur'anskoj upotrebi.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib says only that it is the plural of jadaṯ. In the Quran all three times it stands in the same scene: on the Day of Resurrection people come out of the burial places (hastening, in 36:51 and 70:43) — this is our observation of Quranic usage.

why.bs: „I puhnut će se u rog, i oni će odjednom iz grobišta svojih Gospodaru svome pohitati” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And the Horn will be blown; and at once from the burial places to their Lord they will hasten” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Na Dan kada će iz grobišta žurno izlaziti” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “The Day they will emerge from the burial places rapidly” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Pogleda oborenih izlazit će iz grobišta kao skakavci raštrkani.”
why.en: “Their eyes humbled, they will emerge from the burial places as if they were locusts spreading.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače da nešto više nije manjkavo. Prema ar-Rāġibu, mjerilo je različito: kod prve da stvari ništa izvana ne treba, kod druge da je postignuto ono radi čega stvar postoji.
shared.en: Both words mean that a thing is no longer lacking. According to ar-Rāġib, the measure differs: for the first that the thing needs nothing outside itself, for the second that what it exists for has been attained.

tellApart.bs: Dovesti do granice gdje stvari ništa izvana ne treba – broj, rok, obred, blagodat → أَتَمَّ; dovesti do toga da je postignuta svrha stvari → أَكْمَلَ (2×; u 5:3 oba glagola stoje jedan uz drugi).
tellApart.en: To bring to the point where the thing needs nothing outside itself — a number, a term, a rite, a favour → أَتَمَّ; to bring it to where its purpose is attained → أَكْمَلَ (2×; in 5:3 the two verbs stand side by side).

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries تمام, كمل
notes: ar-Rāġib (تمام): a thing's tamām is its reaching a limit where it needs nothing outside itself, and the lacking (nāqiṣ) is what needs something outside itself; said of the counted and the measured (a complete number, a complete night); with 6:115, 61:8, 7:142. (كمل): kamāl of a thing is the attaining of what is the purpose of it; 2:233 'two full years' — the utmost on which the child's welfare depends; 16:25 'their burdens in full' — the full measure of punishment; 2:196 'ten complete' — two views reported with 'qīla'.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 16 / 2 places read): أَتَمَّ is said of Allah's light (9:32; the participle مُتِمّ in 61:8 is another lemma) and favour (5:3, 12:6, 48:2), of rites (2:196), the fast (2:187), a covenant's term (9:4), nights and years (7:142, 28:27), and Abraham's fulfilling the words he was tested with (2:124, not cited: readings differ); أَكْمَلَ is only 2:185 (the number of days) and 5:3 (the religion). In 5:3 the religion is 'perfected' and the favour 'completed'; we do not put a reason for the choice in ar-Rāġib's mouth.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, stvar je potpuna (tāmm) kad dođe do granice na kojoj joj ništa izvana ne treba, a manjkava je ona kojoj nešto izvana treba; kaže se za ono što se broji i mjeri. U Kur'anu se upotpunjuju broj noći, obredi hadža, post i Allahova blagodat.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a thing is complete (tāmm) when it reaches the limit at which it needs nothing outside itself, and lacking when it needs something outside; it is said of what is counted and measured. In the Quran a number of nights, the rites of Hajj, the fast and Allah's favour are completed.

why.bs: „I obećali smo Musau trideset noći, i upotpunili ih sa još deset, pa se vrijeme Gospodara njegova navršilo – četrdeset noći” – broj kojem više ništa ne treba; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And We made an appointment with Moses for thirty nights and completed them with ten; so the term of his Lord was completed as forty nights” — a number needing nothing more; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I upotpunite hadž i umru radi Allaha.”
why.en: “And complete the Hajj and ʿumrah for Allah.”

why.bs: „… i blagodat Svoju prema vama upotpunio …” – u istom ajetu vjera je „usavršena” (أَكْمَلْتُ).
why.en: “… and completed My favour upon you …” — in the same ayah the religion is “perfected” (أَكْمَلْتُ).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, savršenstvo (kamāl) stvari je da se postigne ono što je njena svrha. Tako „dvije pune godine” dojenja (2:233) znače, kaže on, krajnje do čega ide djetetova dobrobit. Glagol je u Kur'anu samo dva puta.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the perfection (kamāl) of a thing is the attaining of what is its purpose. So the “two full years” of nursing (2:233) mean, he says, the utmost on which the child's welfare depends. The verb occurs only twice in the Quran.

why.bs: „Danas sam vam vjeru vašu usavršio …” – a blagodat „upotpunio” (أَتْمَمْتُ) u istom ajetu.
why.en: “This day I have perfected for you your religion …” — and the favour “completed” (أَتْمَمْتُ) in the same ayah.

why.bs: „… da biste broj (dana) usavršili i da biste Allaha veličali što vas je uputio.”
why.en: “… and [wants] for you to perfect (fill out) the period and to glorify Allah for that to which He has guided you.”

shared.bs: Sve četiri riječi znače ono što ukazuje na istinu. Prema ar-Rāġibu, razlikuju se po načinu ukazivanja: vidljivo koje upućuje na nevidljivo, najčvršći dokaz, jasno ukazivanje razumom ili osjetilima, i dokaz koji pokazuje pravi put i potvrđuje jednu od dvije suprotne tvrdnje.
shared.en: All four words mean what points to the truth. According to ar-Rāġib, they differ in how they point: the seen that leads to the unseen, the firmest proof, a clear indication by reason or the senses, and a proof that shows the straight way and settles which of two contraries is sound.

tellApart.bs: Vidljiv znak koji je nerazdvojno vezan za nešto što se ne vidi (i ajet Kur'ana) → آيَة; najčvršći dokaz, koji uvijek vodi istini → بُرْهَان; jasno ukazivanje, razumsko ili osjetilno (i svjedoci) → بَيِّنَة; argument koji pokazuje ispravan put u sporu – zove se tako i kad je oboren → حُجَّة.
tellApart.en: A visible sign inseparably joined to something unseen (and a verse of the Quran) → آيَة; the firmest proof, one that always leads to truth → بُرْهَان; a clear indication, by reason or by the senses (also witnesses) → بَيِّنَة; an argument showing the right way in a dispute — so called even when refuted → حُجَّة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries أي, بره, بان, حج
notes: ar-Rāġib (أي): āya is the evident sign; in truth anything apparent that is inseparable from something not apparent, so that whoever perceives the one knows the other — in sensibles and intelligibles (a made thing tells of a maker); every passage of the Quran indicating a ruling, or separated by a verbal break, is an āya; 23:50: 'āya', not 'two āyas', because each became a sign through the other; 29:49. (بره): burhān is the making-plain of a proof (bayān li-l-ḥujja); 'some' derive it from bariha, to be white; it is the firmest of proofs (awkad al-adilla), the one that always entails truth, in his scale of five kinds of indication; with 2:111, 21:24, 4:174. (بان): bayyina is the clear indication, rational or sensible; two witnesses are called bayyina (the hadith 'the bayyina is on the claimant'); with 'a-fa-man kāna ʿalā bayyina min rabbihi' and 8:42. (حج): ḥujja is the indication that makes plain the maḥajja, the straight goal, and entails the soundness of one of two contradictories; 6:149; in 2:150 what the wrongdoers argue with is excepted from ḥujja though it is none, or it is so called as in 42:16 'their argument is refuted'.

Counts: آيَة (382) includes every use, the Quranic verse as well as the sign; بَيِّنَة counts the singular and its plural بَيِّنَات as the corpus files them. 12:24 (burhān rabbihi) is not cited: tafsir differs widely on what Joseph saw.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 6 flags, fixed: ḥujja is 'argument', burhān 'proof' (no shared word); 'Produce your proof' is said to those who claim without evidence (Jews and Christians in 2:111, idolaters in 21:24, 27:64); 29:49 'the Quran' as many mufassirun explain; 30:21 bs 'supruge'; 28:32 no longer draws on the staff of 28:31; 42:16 bs keeps the passive.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries أي, بره, بان, حج (2026-11-06): 35 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): His definition of ḥujja is not about dispute; disputing is muḥājja, discussed later in the entry; members/2/nuance (reworded): The she-camel example is not in his entry; it reads as his continuation. 7:73 itself calls her bayyina, so mark it as Quranic usage; members/3/nuance (reworded): Minor: 'in debate' is not part of his definition; he does say what they argue with (mā yaḥtajjūna bihi) is called ḥujja

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, jasan znak: nešto vidljivo što je nerazdvojno vezano za nešto nevidljivo, pa ko spozna prvo, zna i drugo – kao što stvoreno govori o Stvoritelju. Ajetom se zove i svaki odlomak Kur'ana koji ukazuje na propis ili je odvojen stankom.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a clear sign: something seen that is inseparably joined to something unseen, so that whoever grasps the first knows the second — as a made thing tells of its Maker. Every passage of the Quran that indicates a ruling or is set off by a break is also called a verse (āya).

why.bs: „I sina Merjemina i majku njegovu učinili smo znakom” – ar-Rāġib: rečeno je „znakom”, a ne „dvama znakovima”, jer je svako od njih znak po onom drugom.
why.en: “And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign” — ar-Rāġib: “a sign”, not “two signs”, because each became a sign through the other.

why.bs: „Naprotiv, on (Kur'an, kako to objašnjavaju mnogi mufessiri) je jasni ajeti u grudima onih kojima je dato znanje” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Rather, it [the Quran, as many mufassirun explain] is distinct verses within the breasts of those who have been given knowledge” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I jedan od Njegovih znakova je to što vam je od vas samih stvorio supruge da se uz njih smirite.”
why.en: “And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquillity in them.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, burhān je razjašnjenje dokaza i najčvršći od svih dokaza – onaj koji uvijek vodi istini. U Kur'anu se četiri puta onima koji tvrde bez dokaza kaže: „Dajte svoj dokaz!”
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, burhān is the making-plain of a proof and the firmest of all proofs — the one that always leads to truth. Four times in the Quran those who make a claim without evidence are told: “Produce your proof!”

why.bs: „Reci: ‘Dajte vaš dokaz ako istinu govorite!’” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Say, ‘Produce your proof, if you should be truthful’” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „O ljudi, već vam je stigao dokaz od Gospodara vašeg” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “O mankind, there has come to you a conclusive proof from your Lord” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Musau, kad je izvukao ruku bijelu: „To su dva dokaza od Gospodara tvoga faraonu i glavešinama njegovim.”
why.en: To Moses, as he drew out his hand white: “These two are proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his establishment.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, jasno ukazivanje, bilo razumsko bilo osjetilno; zato se i dva svjedoka zovu bayyina. U Kur'anu je kamila poslana Semudu takvo svjedočanstvo (7:73) koje se vidi očima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a clear indication, whether by reason or by the senses; so two witnesses are also called bayyina. In the Quran the she-camel sent to Thamūd is such evidence (7:73), seen with the eyes.

why.bs: Salih: „Došlo vam je očigledno svjedočanstvo od Gospodara vašeg: ova Allahova kamila vama je znak” – svjedočanstvo osjetilima.
why.en: Ṣāliḥ: “There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah [sent] to you as a sign” — evidence to the senses.

why.bs: „… da bi nastradao onaj koji treba da nastrada nakon očiglednog svjedočanstva, i da bi ostao živ onaj koji treba da ostane nakon očiglednog svjedočanstva” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… that those who perished [through disbelief] would perish upon clear evidence and those who lived would live upon clear evidence” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, argument koji upućuje na ispravan put i zahtijeva da je od dvije suprotne tvrdnje jedna tačna – a ḥujjom se može zvati i ono čime se ljudi argumentiraju. Kur'an argumentom naziva i oboreni argument nevjernika (42:16).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the argument that points the right way and requires that of two contrary claims one is sound — and what people argue with may also be called ḥujja. The Quran also calls the disbelievers' refuted plea an argument (42:16).

why.bs: „Reci: ‘Allahu pripada konačni argument’” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Say, ‘With Allah is the far-reaching argument’” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A onima koji se o Allahu raspravljaju poslije odaziva Njemu – njihov argument je kod Gospodara njihova ništavan” – ar-Rāġib: i oboreni se zove argumentom.
why.en: “And those who argue concerning Allah after He has been responded to — their argument is invalid with their Lord” — ar-Rāġib: even a refuted one is called an argument.

why.bs: „To je Naš argument koji smo dali Ibrahimu protiv naroda njegova.”
why.en: “And that was Our [conclusive] argument which We gave Abraham against his people.”

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače ono što se jede od biljaka i drveća. Razlikuju se po tome da li se plod gleda kao prinos i opskrba, ili kao voće koje se iznosi, u Kur'anu najčešće u Dženetu.
shared.en: Both words mean what is eaten from plants and trees. They differ in whether it is seen as yield and provision, or as fruit set out to eat, in the Quran mostly in Paradise.

tellApart.bs: Ono što daje drvo, kao prinos i opskrba, a u prenesenom smislu svaka korist koja iz nečega proizlazi → ثَمَرَة; voće – jedinski oblik dolazi jedanaest puta, a u devet njih je u opisu Dženeta → فَاكِهَة.
tellApart.en: What a tree yields, as produce and provision, and figuratively any benefit that comes from a thing → ثَمَرَة; fruit — the singular occurs eleven times, nine of them describing Paradise → فَاكِهَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries ثمر, فكه
notes: ar-Rāġib (ثمر): ṯamar is a name for all that is eaten of the yields of trees; one is ṯamara, plurals ṯimār and ṯamarāt ('fa-aḫraǧa bihi mina ṯ-ṯamarāti rizqan lakum', 16:67, 6:99); of ṯamar 'it was said' it is ṯimār, and 'it was said' its plural, and it is used figuratively for acquired wealth — so Ibn ʿAbbās read 18:34 'wa-kāna lahu ṯamar'; any benefit coming from a thing is its ṯamara (the fruit of knowledge is good deeds). (فكه): fākiha 'it was said' is all fruits, and 'it was said' fruits except grapes and pomegranates — whoever said so looked at their being named apart and joined to it (he cites no verse here; cf. 55:68); fukāha is the pleasant talk of companions; 56:65 tafakkahūn read two ways.

The member sums the corpus lemmas ثَمَرَة (17, mostly the plural ثَمَرَات) and ثَمَر (5). Quranic usage (our observation, all 11 places read): فَاكِهَة describes Paradise in 9 places (36:57, 38:51, 43:73, 44:55, 52:22, 55:52, 55:68, 56:20, 56:32) and the earth's produce in 55:11 and 80:31; the plural فَوَاكِه is another lemma and not counted.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 5 flags, fixed: 'nine of eleven' is of the singular فَاكِهَة only (the plural fawākih not counted); ثَمَرَة is 'produce', not 'fruit'; Ibn ʿAbbās 'understood' 18:34 (not a reading); 80:31 no longer borrows 80:32.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ime za sve što se jede od onoga što drveće daje. Prenosi se i na imetak (tako je Ibn Abbas razumio 18:34) i na svaku korist koja iz nečega proizlazi – „plod znanja je dobro djelo”. U Kur'anu plodovi su najčešće opskrba (رِزْق) koju Allah izvodi kišom.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a name for all that is eaten of what trees yield. It is carried over to wealth (so Ibn ʿAbbās understood 18:34) and to any benefit that comes from a thing — “the fruit of knowledge is good deeds”. In the Quran produce is mostly provision (رِزْق) that Allah brings forth with rain.

why.bs: „… i spušta s neba kišu pa njome izvodi plodove kao hranu za vas” – ar-Rāġib navodi ove riječi.
why.en: “… and sent down from the sky rain and brought forth thereby from the produce as provision for you” — ar-Rāġib quotes these words.

why.bs: „Pogledajte plod njegov kad zametne plod, i kako sazrijeva!” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Look at its produce when it yields and [at] its ripening” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I imao je on plodova (ثَمَر)” – ar-Rāġib prenosi da je Ibn Abbas to razumio kao imetak.
why.en: “And he had produce (ثَمَر)” — ar-Rāġib reports that Ibn ʿAbbās understood it as wealth.

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib prenosi dva mišljenja: da su to svi plodovi, ili svi osim grožđa i šipka, drugo jer se ta dva spominju posebno uz voće – u Kur'anu u 55:68. Jedinski oblik „voće” u Kur'anu dolazi jedanaest puta, a u devet njih je u opisu Dženeta.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib reports two views: that it is all fruits, or all except grapes and pomegranates, the second because these two are named apart beside it — in the Quran in 55:68. The singular “fruit” occurs eleven times in the Quran, nine of them in the description of Paradise.

why.bs: „U njima će biti voća, i palmi, i šipaka” – na ovome počiva mišljenje da voće ne obuhvata šipak.
why.en: “In both of them are fruit and palm trees and pomegranates” — the view that fruit excludes the pomegranate rests on this.

why.bs: „U njemu ćete imati mnogo voća, od kojeg ćete jesti” – voće u Dženetu.
why.en: “For you therein is much fruit from which you will eat” — fruit in Paradise.

why.bs: „I voće i travu” – mjesto gdje je voće ovoga svijeta, a ne Dženeta.
why.en: “And fruit and herbage” — a place where fruit is of this world, not of Paradise.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o djelu koje više ništa ne vrijedi. Razlikuju se po obliku i po tome šta se poništava: prva kaže da su djela sama propala, druga da se nešto čini ništavnim.
shared.en: Both words speak of a deed that is no longer worth anything. They differ in form and in what is voided: the first says the deeds themselves have come to nothing, the second that something is made void.

tellApart.bs: Djela su propala – postala bezvrijedna zbog onoga što ih kvari (nevjerovanje, rđava namjera, pretegnuta loša djela); u Kur'anu uvijek o djelima → حَبِطَ; poništiti nešto, učiniti ga ništavnim – milostinju, djela, sihr, neistinu → أَبْطَلَ.
tellApart.en: Deeds have become worthless — through what spoils them (disbelief, a wrong intention, outweighing bad deeds); in the Quran always of deeds → حَبِطَ; to invalidate a thing, make it void — charity, deeds, magic, falsehood → أَبْطَلَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حبط, بطل
notes: ar-Rāġib (حبط): ḥabṭ of deeds is of kinds: (1) worldly deeds that avail nothing at the Resurrection (25:23 'scattered dust'); (2) deeds of the Hereafter not done for Allah's face (the report of the man who recited the Quran to be called a reciter); (3) good deeds against which there are bad deeds that outweigh them — the light scales; the root is ḥabaṭ, an animal eating so much that its belly swells (the hadith: some spring pasture kills by ḥabaṭ). (بطل): bāṭil is the opposite of ḥaqq, what has no firmness when examined (ḏālika bi-anna llāha huwa l-ḥaqq …); ibṭāl is said of corrupting and removing a thing, true or false (8:8); mubṭilūn are those who say what has no reality, or who void the truth.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 12 / 4 places read): the subject of حَبِطَ is always deeds (أَعْمَال, عَمَل, مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ, مَا صَنَعُوا); it is intransitive — the transitive أَحْبَطَ (Allah voided their deeds) is another verb. أَبْطَلَ has as object charities (2:264), deeds (47:33), magic (10:81) and falsehood (8:8). 39:65 and 6:88 (conditionals about prophets) are not cited.

nuance.bs: Izvorno, prema ar-Rāġibu, kad se životinja toliko najede da joj se trbuh nadme – a, kako kaže hadis koji navodi, to može ubiti. On navodi tri vrste: djela ovoga svijeta koja na Sudnjem danu ne koriste, djela ahireta koja nisu činjena radi Allaha, i dobra djela koja loša djela pretegnu. U Kur'anu su subjekt uvijek djela.
nuance.en: At root, according to ar-Rāġib, when an animal eats so much that its belly swells — and, as the hadith he cites says, it can kill. He gives three kinds: worldly deeds that avail nothing at the Resurrection, deeds of the Hereafter not done for Allah, and good deeds outweighed by bad ones. In the Quran the subject is always deeds.

why.bs: „To su oni koji ne vjeruju u ajete Gospodara svoga i u susret s Njim, pa su njihova djela propala i Mi im na Sudnjem danu nikakvu težinu nećemo dati.”
why.en: “Those are the ones who disbelieve in the verses of their Lord and in [their] meeting Him, so their deeds have become worthless; and We will not assign to them on the Day of Resurrection any weight.”

why.bs: „A onome ko ne bude vjerovao, propala su djela njegova, i on će na onom svijetu biti među izgubljenima.”
why.en: “And whoever denies the faith — his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.”

why.bs: „A onima koji od vas otpadnu od vjere svoje i umru kao nevjernici – njihova djela propala su i na ovom i na onom svijetu.”
why.en: “And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever — for those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter.”

nuance.bs: Od bāṭil, što je prema ar-Rāġibu suprotnost istini (ḥaqq): ono što nema postojanosti kad se ispita. Ibṭāl je, kaže on, kvarenje i uklanjanje nečega, bilo istinitog ili neistinitog: u Kur'anu se poništava milostinja, ali i sihr i neistina.
nuance.en: From bāṭil, which according to ar-Rāġib is the opposite of truth (ḥaqq): what has no firmness when examined. Ibṭāl, he says, is spoiling and removing a thing, whether true or false: in the Quran charity is invalidated, but so are magic and falsehood.

why.bs: „O vjernici, ne poništavajte svoje milostinje prigovaranjem i uvredom.”
why.en: “O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders [of it] or injury.”

why.bs: Musa vračarima: „Ono što ste vi priredili je sihr, a Allah će ga, sigurno, poništiti.”
why.en: Moses to the magicians: “What you have brought is [only] magic. Indeed, Allah will invalidate it.”

why.bs: „Da bi istinu utvrdio, a neistinu poništio, makar to grešnicima bilo mrsko” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “That He should establish the truth and invalidate falsehood, even if the criminals disliked it” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

title.bs: Čuvati se, strepiti s brigom, drhtati

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi su vrste straha. Prema ar-Rāġibu, prva je čuvanje od onoga čega se boji, druga briga pomiješana sa strahom, treća strah koji se osjeti u sebi.
shared.en: All three words are kinds of fear. According to ar-Rāġib, the first is guarding against what is feared, the second care mixed with fear, the third fear felt within.

tellApart.bs: Čuvati se onoga čega se boji, biti na oprezu → حَذِرَ; brižan strah – strah pomiješan s pažnjom prema onome do čega je stalo → مُشْفِق; osjetiti strah u sebi, da srce zadrhti → وَجِلَ.
tellApart.en: To guard against what is feared, to be on one's guard → حَذِرَ; anxious care — fear mixed with concern for what one holds dear → مُشْفِق; to feel fear within, the heart trembling → وَجِلَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حذر, شفق, وجل
notes: ar-Rāġib (حذر): ḥaḏar is guarding against something feared (iḥtirāz ʿan muḫīf); 39:9, 'Allah warns you of Himself', 'take your precaution' (ḫuḏū ḥiḏrakum) = what holds caution, weapons and the like; 63:4, 64:14. (شفق): išfāq is care mixed with fear, because the mušfiq loves the one he is anxious for and fears what may befall him; with min the sense of fear is more apparent, with fī the sense of care; 21:49, 52:26, 42:18, 42:22. (وجل): waǧal is feeling fear inwardly (istišʿār al-ḫawf); 8:2, 15:52–53, 23:60.

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): وَجِلَ (3×) is twice the hearts of believers when Allah is mentioned (8:2, 22:35) and once the angels' word to Ibrāhīm (15:53; his fear of the strangers, 15:52, is a natural one). مُشْفِق is joined to ḫašya in 21:28 and 23:57 — see the خَوْف/خَشْيَة group. 5:41 and 5:49 (حَذِرَ said to the Prophet) are not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: the root's places named in full (8:2, 22:35, 23:60, 15:52, 15:53 — the verb is 3 of them); 15:53 no longer borrows the fear from 15:52.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḥaḏar je čuvanje od onoga čega se boji. Naglasak je na postupku: čovjek se pazi, sklanja i oprema – „uzmite svoj oprez”, kaže on, znači oružje i slično.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḥaḏar is guarding against what is feared. The weight is on the action: one takes care, keeps away, prepares — “take your precaution”, he says, means weapons and the like.

why.bs: „Zar je isti onaj koji u noćnim satima … čuva se ahireta i nada se milosti Gospodara svoga?” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night … wary of the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]?” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „O vjernici, i među ženama vašim i djecom vašom ima vam neprijatelja, pa ih se čuvajte! A ako oprostite … Allah zaista prašta” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon … then indeed, Allah is Forgiving” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Licemjeri se čuvaju da im ne bude objavljena sura koja će im kazati šta je u njihovim srcima.”
why.en: “The hypocrites are wary lest a surah be revealed about them, informing them of what is in their hearts.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, išfāq je briga pomiješana sa strahom: ko brižno strepi, voli onoga za koga strepi i boji se onoga što bi ga moglo zadesiti. S min (od) jače se čuje strah, a s fī (u) briga.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, išfāq is care mixed with fear: one who is anxious loves the one he is anxious for and fears what may befall him. With min (of) the fear is heard more, with fī (among) the care.

why.bs: „… koji se Gospodara svoga boje i kad ih niko ne vidi, i koji od Časa strepe” – s min: jače se čuje strah; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Who fear their Lord unseen, while they are of the Hour apprehensive” — with min: the fear is heard more; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Stanovnici Dženeta: „Mi smo prije, među svojima, brižno strepili” – s fī: briga za porodicu; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: The people of Paradise: “Indeed, we were previously among our people anxious” — with fī: care for one's family; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… a vjernici od njega (Časa) strepe i znaju da je istina” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “… but those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, waǧal je osjetiti strah u sebi. U Kur'anu srca vjernika drhte kad se spomene Allah (8:2, 22:35; i 23:60), a Ibrahim svojim gostima kaže da ih se boji (15:52), pa mu oni odgovore: „Ne drhti!” (15:53).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, waǧal is feeling fear within. In the Quran the hearts of believers tremble when Allah is mentioned (8:2, 22:35; also 23:60), and Abraham tells his guests that he fears them (15:52) and they answer: “Do not tremble” (15:53).

why.bs: „Pravi vjernici su samo oni čija srca zadrhte kad se spomene Allah” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „… čija srca zadrhte kad se Allah spomene, i koji trpe ono što ih zadesi.”
why.en: “Who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and [to] the patient over what has afflicted them.”

why.bs: Meleki, Ibrahimovi gosti, rekoše mu: „Ne drhti! Mi ti donosimo radosnu vijest o dječaku koji će biti učen”; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: The angels, Abraham's guests, said to him: “Do not tremble. Indeed, we give you good tidings of a learned boy”; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače riječ upućenu drugome za njegovo dobro. Razlikuju se po tonu i po onome što se u riječi ističe: odvraćanje uz upozorenje, ili iskrena briga za dobro onoga kome se govori.
shared.en: Both words mean speech addressed to another for his good. They differ in tone and in what the word stresses: restraint with a warning, or sincere care for the good of the one addressed.

tellApart.bs: Opomena koja odvraća i upozorava (najčešće je izriče Allah ili poslanik) → وَعَظَ; iskreno nastojanje oko dobra drugoga; glagol u Kur'anu uvijek dolazi sa „za” nekoga (نَصَحَ لِـ) → نَصَحَ.
tellApart.en: An admonition that restrains and warns (in the Quran mostly from Allah or a prophet) → وَعَظَ; sincere striving for another's good; the verb in the Quran always takes “for” someone (نَصَحَ لِـ) → نَصَحَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries وعظ, نصح
notes: ar-Rāġib (وعظ): waʿẓ is restraint (zajr) joined with causing fear; he quotes al-Ḫalīl: reminding of good in a way the heart softens to; ʿiẓa and mawʿiẓa are the noun; he cites 16:90 (yaʿiẓukum laʿallakum taḏakkarūn), 34:46, 4:63. (نصح): nuṣḥ is seeking out a deed or word in which lies the other's good (taḥarrī fiʿl aw qawl fīhi ṣalāḥ ṣāḥibihi); cites 7:79 and 11:34; from naṣaḥtu lahu l-wudd, I made my love pure for him, or from naṣaḥtu l-jild, I sewed the hide; tawba naṣūḥ (66:8) from one of the two: sincerity or firmness.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 15 / 5 places read): وَعَظَ takes its hearer as direct object (يَعِظُكُمْ); its subject is Allah in 2:231, 2:232, 4:58, 11:46, 16:90, 24:17 and the passive tūʿaẓūn of 58:3, 65:2, a prophet or Luqmān in 4:63, 26:136, 31:13, 34:46, and people in 7:164. نَصَحَ comes all 5 times with li- (لَكُمْ, لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ): four times a prophet to his people (7:62 Nūḥ, 7:79 Ṣāliḥ, 7:93 Šuʿayb, 11:34 Nūḥ), once the believers who cannot go out to fight, 'when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger' (9:91).
Not cited: 4:34 (tafsir and context need more than a line) and 11:46 (said to a prophet in correction).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: 'always with li-' is of the verb نَصَحَ only (7:68, 66:8 have none); 9:91 names only who the ayah names.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, opomena je odvraćanje povezano s upozorenjem; on navodi i al-Ḫalīlovo objašnjenje: podsjećanje na dobro na način od kojeg srce omekša. U Kur'anu ga najčešće izriče Allah, a onda poslanici i Lukman svome sinu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, admonition is restraint joined with a warning; he also quotes al-Ḫalīl: reminding of good in a way that softens the heart. In the Quran it is mostly Allah who admonishes, then the prophets, and Luqmān to his son.

why.bs: „On vas opominje (يَعِظُكُمْ) da biste pouku primili” – nakon naredbe pravde i zabrane razvrata; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded” — after the command of justice and the forbidding of immorality; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Allah vas opominje da tako nešto nikada više ne ponovite, ako ste vjernici” – opomena koja odvraća.
why.en: “Allah admonishes you against returning to the likes of this [conduct], ever, if you should be believers” — an admonition that restrains.

why.bs: Lukman je opominjao sina: „O sinko moj, ne smatraj nikoga Allahu ravnim!”
why.en: Luqmān, admonishing his son: “O my son, do not associate [anything] with Allah.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, to je tražiti djelo ili riječ u kojoj je dobro onoga kome se savjet daje; korijen je ili u „iskrenoj, čistoj ljubavi”, ili u „šivenju” – iskrenost ili čvrstina. U Kur'anu je to najčešće riječ poslanika svome narodu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, it is seeking out the deed or word that holds the good of the one advised; the root is either “pure, sincere love” or “sewing” — sincerity or firmness. In the Quran it is mostly a prophet's word to his people.

why.bs: Salih: „Prenio sam vam poslanicu Gospodara svoga i iskreno sam vas savjetovao, ali vi ne volite iskrene savjetnike” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Ṣāliḥ: “I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you sincerely, but you do not like sincere advisors” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Nuh: „Prenosim vam poslanice Gospodara svoga i iskreno vas savjetujem.”
why.en: Noah: “I convey to you the messages of my Lord and advise you sincerely.”

why.bs: Nema grijeha na slabima, bolesnima i onima koji nemaju čime da troše „ako su iskreni prema Allahu i Poslaniku Njegovu” – ista riječ, iskrenost prema Allahu.
why.en: There is no blame on the weak, the ill and those without means to spend “if they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger” — the same word, sincerity toward Allah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o onome po čemu je čovjek živ. Prema ar-Rāġibu, nafs se ponekad kaže za ruh, a ruh se naziva i imenom nafsa; ipak, Kur'an ih upotrebljava vrlo različito.
shared.en: Both words speak of that by which a person is alive. According to ar-Rāġib, nafs is sometimes said for rūḥ, and rūḥ is also used as a name for the nafs; yet the Quran uses them very differently.

tellApart.bs: Duša, sâmo biće čovjeka – ona umire, žudi, odgovara za djela → نَفْس; duh koji Allah udahnjuje, šalje s objavom, ili meleki koji se tako nazivaju → رُوح.
tellApart.en: The soul, the person's own self — it dies, desires and answers for its deeds → نَفْس; the spirit that Allah breathes in, sends with revelation, or the angels so named → رُوح.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries نفس, روح
notes: ar-Rāġib (نفس): nafs is the rūḥ in 6:93 (aḫrijū anfusakum); he also cites 2:235 and 5:116, and gives the nafs of Allah (3:28) as His essence: in meaning there is nothing other than Him, exalted above any duality (not cited on the page). (روح): rūḥ and rawḥ are at root one; rūḥ was made a name for the nafs, the nafs being part of the rūḥ, like naming a species by its genus; and a name for the part by which life, movement, gaining benefit and warding off harm come about — that, he says, is the rūḥ of 17:85 and of 15:29 'I breathed into him of My rūḥ', whose ascription to Allah is one of possession, singled out for honour like 'My House'; the noblest angels are called arwāḥ (78:38, 70:4); Jibrīl is al-rūḥ al-amīn (26:193) and rūḥ al-qudus; ʿĪsā is called rūḥ (4:171) for his raising of the dead (by Allah's leave, as 3:49 says); the Quran is called rūḥ (42:52) as a cause of the life to come.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 21 rūḥ places read): rūḥ is never a person's own self in the Quran — it is breathed in by Allah (15:29, 32:9, 38:72, 21:91, 66:12), sent down with revelation or as an angel (16:2, 16:102, 26:193, 40:15, 70:4, 78:38, 97:4, 19:17), the support of prophets and believers (2:87, 2:253, 5:110, 58:22), ʿĪsā (4:171), revelation (42:52) and 17:85. It is never said to die or desire; nafs is (3:185, 79:40). nafs counts 295 places, including the reflexive 'oneself'.
17:85 is shown only with the ayah's own words ('of the affair of my Lord'): mufassirun differ on what rūḥ there refers to. 4:171 and 42:52 are left out of the ayat for the same reason.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 3 flags, fixed: Allah's nafs (3:28) added — his 'His very Being', as befits Him; 'rūḥ never the self' softened to 'not spoken of as the self that answers for deeds'; 17:85 leaves its reality with Allah and says the mufassirun differ.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries نفس, روح (2026-11-06): 19 attributed points confirmed; changed — notes/0 (reworded): 'as befits Him' and 'by Allah's leave' are our wording, not his; the fixes keep the theology but stop attributing it to him. He also reports (qāla baʿḍ an-nās) a view that nafs in 3:28 is ascribed by possession — not used, fine; members/1/nuance (reworded): Minor: the honour he names is to the rūḥ (tašrīfan lahu), and 'as befits Him' is ours. Note the last sentence ('never the person's own self') is our Quranic observation; ar-Rāġib himself says rūḥ was made a name for the nafs, so it must not be read as his

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nafs se kaže i za ruh, kao u 6:93: „Izvadite duše svoje!” U Kur'anu je nafs najčešće sâmo biće čovjeka: duša koja okusi smrt, koja žudi i koju treba suzdržati, i koja odgovara za ono što je stekla. Kad se kaže za Allaha („Allah vas upozorava na Sebe”, 3:28), ar-Rāġib kaže da znači Njegovo Biće, kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, nafs is also said for the rūḥ, as in 6:93: “Discharge your souls!” In the Quran the nafs is mostly the person's own self: the soul that tastes death, that desires and must be held back, and that answers for what it has earned. When it is said of Allah (“Allah warns you of Himself”, 3:28), ar-Rāġib says it means His very Being, as befits Him.

why.bs: Meleki govore nepravednicima na samrti: „Izvadite duše svoje!” – ar-Rāġib: ovdje je nafs isto što i ruh.
why.en: The angels say to the wrongdoers at death: “Discharge your souls!” — ar-Rāġib: here nafs is the rūḥ.

why.bs: „Svaka duša će smrt okusiti” – nafs umire.
why.en: “Every soul will taste death” — the nafs dies.

why.bs: „A onaj ko se bude bojao stajanja pred Gospodarom svojim i dušu od strasti uzdržavao…” – duša koju treba suzdržati.
why.en: “But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination…” — the soul that must be held back.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ruh je ono čime nastaje život, kretanje, pribavljanje koristi i odbijanje štete; kad ga Allah naziva „Mojim duhom”, to je pripisivanje vlasništva, kojim se ruh izdvaja i počastvuje. Ruhom se nazivaju i najodličniji meleki: Džibril je „Povjerljivi Duh”. U Kur'anu se ruh uvijek pripisuje Allahu („od Mog duha”, „od stvari Gospodara mog”) i ne govori se o njemu kao o biću koje odgovara za djela.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the rūḥ is that by which life, movement, gaining benefit and warding off harm come about; when Allah calls it “My spirit”, it is ascription of possession, singling it out for honour. The noblest angels are also called rūḥ: Jibrīl is “the Trustworthy Spirit”. In the Quran the rūḥ is always ascribed to Allah (“of My spirit”, “of the affair of my Lord”) and is not spoken of as the self that answers for deeds.

why.bs: „Pa kad ga uobličim i u nj udahnem od Svoga duha…” – ar-Rāġib: pripisivanje Allahu je počast, kao „Moja Kuća”.
why.en: “And when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit…” — ar-Rāġib: the ascription to Allah is one of honour, like “My House”.

why.bs: „Donosi ga Povjerljivi Duh” – Džibril, kako ga ar-Rāġib objašnjava.
why.en: “The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down” — Jibrīl, as ar-Rāġib explains.

why.bs: „Pitaju te o duhu. Reci: ‘Duh je od stvari Gospodara mog’” – ovdje Kur'an njegovu suštinu prepušta Allahu; mufessiri se razilaze oko toga šta se tačno misli.
why.en: “And they ask you about the spirit. Say, ‘The spirit is of the affair of my Lord’” — here the Quran leaves its reality with Allah; mufassirun differ on what exactly is meant.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače razum, i obje dolaze u izrazu „oni koji imaju…” (أُولُو). Prema ar-Rāġibovim definicijama, razlikuju se po onome što se u razumu ističe: njegova čistota, ili to što odvraća od ružnog.
shared.en: Both words mean the intellect, and both come in the phrase “those who have…” (أُولُو). Going by ar-Rāġib's definitions, they differ in what they stress about the mind: its purity, or its holding back from what is vile.

tellApart.bs: Razum očišćen od primjesa, srž čovjekova uma, kojem se upućuju pouke i opomene → أَلْبَاب; pamet koja odvraća od ružnog, uz znakove u prirodi i povijesti → نُهَى.
tellApart.en: The intellect cleansed of admixture, the kernel of a person's mind, to which lessons and reminders are addressed → أَلْبَاب; the intelligence that restrains from what is vile, beside signs in nature and history → نُهَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries لب, نهى
notes: ar-Rāġib (لب): lubb is the intellect pure of admixture, so called because it is the pure of what is in a person, like the kernel (lubāb) of a thing; 'it has been said' (qīla) it is the intellect that has grown pure, so every lubb is an intellect but not every intellect a lubb; therefore, he says, Allah tied the judgements only purified minds grasp to ulū l-albāb, citing 2:269. (نهى): nuhya is the intellect that restrains from vile things (al-ʿaql al-nāhī ʿan al-qabāʾiḥ), plural nuhā, citing the phrase 'inna fī ḏālika la-āyātin li-ulī n-nuhā' (identical in 20:54 and 20:128) (the OpenITI text misprints the singular as نهبة).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 16 / 2 places read): أَلْبَاب is always in ulū / ulī l-albāb; six times with taḏakkur, taking heed (2:269, 3:7, 13:19, 14:52, 38:29, 39:9), four times with a call to taqwā (2:179, 2:197, 5:100, 65:10). نُهَى is in 20:54 and 20:128, both 'signs for those of intelligence' after the earth's pasture and the ruins of destroyed generations.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): all claims OK.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries لب, نهى (2026-11-06): 14 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): He defines each in its own entry; the comparison is ours, drawn from the two definitions; notes/0 (reworded): He quotes only the shared closing phrase, so the verse cannot be pinned to 20:54; members/1/ayat/0/why (reworded): He quotes only 'inna fī ḏālika la-āyātin li-ulī n-nuhā', which closes both 20:54 and 20:128

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, lubb je razum očišćen od primjesa, srž čovjeka; neki kažu: razum koji se pročistio, pa je svaki lubb razum, a nije svaki razum lubb. Zato, kaže on, Allah ono što shvataju samo čisti umovi veže za „one koji imaju razuma”. U Kur'anu im se najčešće kaže da prime pouku ili da se boje Allaha.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, lubb is the intellect pure of admixture, the kernel of a person; some say: the intellect that has grown pure, so every lubb is an intellect but not every intellect a lubb. That is why, he says, Allah ties what only purified minds grasp to “those of understanding”. In the Quran they are mostly told to take heed or to fear Allah.

why.bs: „Kome je mudrost data, dato mu je veliko dobro, a samo razumom obdareni pouku primaju” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Whoever has been given wisdom has certainly been given much good. And none will remember except those of understanding” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „U stvaranju nebesa i Zemlje i u smjeni noći i dana su znakovi za razumom obdarene.”
why.en: “Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.”

why.bs: „Zar je onaj koji zna da je istina ono što ti se objavljuje od Gospodara tvoga kao onaj koji je slijep? Samo razumom obdareni pouku primaju.”
why.en: “Then is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? They will only be reminded who are people of understanding.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od korijena „zabraniti, odvratiti”: pamet koja odvraća od ružnih djela. U Kur'anu dolazi dvaput, oba puta „znakovi za one koji imaju pameti”, uz ono što se vidi očima: ispašu na zemlji i ruševine uništenih naroda.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from the root of forbidding and holding back: the intelligence that restrains from vile deeds. It comes twice in the Quran, both times as “signs for those of intelligence”, beside what the eyes can see: pasture on the earth and the ruins of destroyed peoples.

why.bs: „Jedite i napasajte stoku svoju! To su, zaista, znakovi za one koji imaju pameti” – ar-Rāġib navodi njegove završne riječi.
why.en: “Eat [therefrom] and pasture your livestock. Indeed, in that are signs for those of intelligence” — ar-Rāġib cites its closing words.

why.bs: „Zar ih nije poučilo koliko smo prije njih naroda uništili, a oni hodaju po njihovim nastambama? To su, zaista, znakovi za one koji imaju pameti.”
why.en: “Then has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them as they walk among their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence.”

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi govore o putu koji je Allah propisao ljudima. Prema ar-Rāġibovim objašnjenjima, razlikuju se po tome odakle se taj put gleda: od onoga ko ga se pokorno drži, od onoga što je Allah propisao preko poslanika, ili kao jasna staza propisa.
shared.en: All three words speak of the way Allah has prescribed for people. Following ar-Rāġib, they differ in where that way is seen from: from the one who keeps to it in obedience, from what Allah laid down through a prophet, or as the clear track of its laws.

tellApart.bs: Vjera kao pokornost i predanost, i ono za što se plaća (Dan sudnji) → دِين; vjerski put koji se pripisuje poslaniku (Ibrahimov) ili zajednici, nikad „Allahov” → مِلَّة; zakon, jasna staza propisa koja se razlikuje od zajednice do zajednice → شِرْعَة.
tellApart.en: Religion as obedience and submission, and that for which one is repaid (the Day of Judgement) → دِين; the creed ascribed to a prophet (Abraham's) or to a community, never “Allah's” → مِلَّة; the law, the clear track of rulings that differs from one community to another → شِرْعَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries دين, ملل, شرع
notes: ar-Rāġib (دين): dīn is said for obedience and for requital, and borrowed for the revealed law; dīn is like milla but said with regard to obedience and submission to the law; he cites 3:19 and 4:125 ('aḥsanu dīnan' = obedience), and 56:86 ġayra madīnīn = not requited. (ملل): milla is like dīn, a name for what Allah prescribed for His servants by the tongues of the prophets; the difference is that milla is ascribed only to the prophet on whom it rests (3:95 'fa-ttabiʿū millata Ibrāhīm', 12:38 'millata ābāʾī'), hardly ever to Allah or to single members of a prophet's community — one does not say millat Allāh or millatī as one says dīn Allāh; it is said with regard to what Allah prescribed, dīn with regard to the one who upholds it; its origin is amlaltu l-kitāb, I dictated the writing (2:282). (شرع): šarʿ is the clear beaten track, borrowed for the divine way; 5:48 šir'atan wa-minhājan points to two things, the second being the part of religion in which laws differ and abrogation enters; he reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that šir'a is what the Quran brought and minhāj what the Sunna brought; 42:13 šaraʿa lakum mina d-dīn points to the principles all the millas share and that are not abrogated.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 15 مِلَّة places read): eight are Abraham's (2:130, 2:135, 3:95, 4:125, 6:161, 12:38, 16:123, 22:78); seven are the creed of a people or community (2:120, 7:88, 7:89, 12:37, 14:13, 18:20, 38:7) — a counter-example to 'only a prophet's', so the page says 'a prophet or a community'; never 'Allah's milla', while dīn Allāh occurs (3:83, 24:2, 110:2). The count of دِين (92) includes the dīn of requital (1:4 and 'yawm ad-dīn'); دَيْن 'debt' is a separate lemma. شِرْعَة is only in 5:48; شَرِيعَة (45:18) is a separate lemma.
2:256 (lā ikrāha fī d-dīn) is not cited: ar-Rāġib himself reports two interpretations (both as qīla).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 4 flags, fixed: his limit restored (milla is hardly ever ascribed to Allah or to an individual); the community's milla (14:13) marked as Quranic usage; bs 'vjerski put' (not 'millet'), 'Allahov put', 3:19 bs 'Vjera je kod Allaha islam'.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries دين, ملل, شرع (2026-11-06): 30 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): His explicit angle for milla is 'with regard to what Allah prescribed'; being ascribed only to the prophet is a usage rule, not the angle. He contrasts only dīn and milla; šarʿa joins the comparison through our framing; notes/0 (reworded): The verse he quotes is 3:95 (fa-ttabiʿū millata Ibrāhīm), not 2:135. He also adds that milla is used only of the whole body of laws, never of a single rule ('one does not say: prayer is millat Allāh') — not in our note, harmless; notes/2 (reworded): These are two interpretations he reports with qīla (obedience cannot be forced; specific to jizya-paying People of the Book), not qirāʾāt. Second: 'وقيل إن ذلك مختص بأهل الكتاب الباذلين للجزية'; members/2/nuance (reworded): He says 'šir'atan wa-minhājan' (the pair) points to two things: (1) the way each person is set on for public welfare, (2) the chosen religion where laws differ and abrogation enters. He does not equate šir'a alone with (2)

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dīn se kaže za pokornost i za obračun (nagradu i kaznu), a preneseno i za šerijat; sličan je riječi milla, ali se kaže s obzirom na pokornost i predanost propisima. Zato je dīn i Allahov („Allahova vjera”) i čovjekov.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, dīn is said for obedience and for requital, and by extension for the revealed law; it is like milla, but said with regard to obedience and submission to the law. So dīn is both Allah's (“the religion of Allah”) and a person's.

why.bs: „Vjera je kod Allaha islam” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ko je bolje vjere od onoga koji se iskreno preda Allahu…” – ar-Rāġib: vjera ovdje znači pokornost.
why.en: “And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah…” — ar-Rāġib: religion here means obedience.

why.bs: „Vladaru Dana sudnjeg (يَوْمِ الدِّينِ)” – dīn u značenju obračuna.
why.en: “Sovereign of the Day of Recompense (يَوْمِ الدِّينِ)” — dīn in the sense of requital.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, milla je kao dīn: ono što je Allah propisao preko poslanika; pripisuje se poslaniku na kojem počiva, a gotovo se nikad ne nalazi pripisana Allahu ili pojedincu – ne kaže se „Allahova milla”. U Kur'anu je to najčešće „Ibrahimov vjerski put”; upotrebljava se i za vjerski put neke zajednice (14:13) – nikada za Allahov.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, milla is like dīn: what Allah prescribed through the prophets; it is ascribed to the prophet on whom it rests, and is hardly ever found ascribed to Allah or to an individual — one does not say “Allah's milla”. In the Quran it is mostly “the creed of Abraham”; it is also used of a community's creed (14:13) — never of Allah's.

why.bs: Jusuf: „I slijedim vjerski put svojih predaka, Ibrahima, Ishaka i Jakuba” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Joseph: “And I have followed the creed of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Reci: ‘Allah govori istinu, zato slijedite vjerski put Ibrahima, pravovjernika.’”
why.en: “Say, ‘Allah has told the truth. So follow the creed of Abraham, inclining toward truth.’”

why.bs: Nevjernici poslanicima: „Ili ćete se vratiti u naš vjerski put…” – milla zajednice, ne poslanika.
why.en: The disbelievers to their messengers: “…or you must return to our creed” — the creed of a community, not of a prophet.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, šarʿ je jasna, utrta staza, prenesena na Allahov put. U 5:48, kaže on, izraz upućuje, između ostalog, na onaj dio vjere u kojem se zakoni razlikuju i u koji ulazi derogacija, dok su temelji koje svi poslanici dijele isti (42:13). Prenosi i od Ibn Abbasa: šir'a je ono što je donio Kur'an, a minhādž ono što je donio sunnet.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, šarʿ is the clear, beaten track, transferred to the divine way. In 5:48, he says, the phrase points, among other things, to the part of religion in which laws differ and abrogation enters, while the principles all prophets share stay the same (42:13). He also reports from Ibn ʿAbbās: šir'a is what the Quran brought, and minhāj what the Sunna brought.

why.bs: „Svima vama smo zakon i pravac propisali” – jedini spomen ove riječi; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “To each of you We prescribed a law and a method” — the only place of this word; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače privlačnost duše prema nečemu. Prema ar-Rāġibu, hawā je naginjanje duše prema požudi, a šahwa je sâmo stremljenje duše prema onome što želi.
shared.en: Both words mean the soul's pull toward something. According to ar-Rāġib, hawā is the soul's leaning toward shahwa, and shahwa is the soul's very yearning for what it wants.

tellApart.bs: Naginjanje duše koje se slijedi umjesto upute, u Kur'anu uvijek pokuđeno → هَوًى; stremljenje duše prema onome što želi, i ono što se želi – istinsko (glad) ili lažno → شَهْوَة.
tellApart.en: The soul's leaning that is followed instead of guidance, in the Quran always blamed → هَوًى; the soul's yearning for what it wants, and the thing wanted — genuine (hunger) or false → شَهْوَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries هوى, شها, نهى
notes: ar-Rāġib (هوى): hawā is the soul's leaning toward shahwa, also said of the soul so inclined; 'it has been said' (qīla) it is so named because it makes its holder fall (yahwī) into every calamity in this world and into the hāwiya in the next; Allah made following hawā a grave matter (45:23, 38:26); the plural ahwāʾ in 'ahwāʾahum' notes that each has a hawā other than the other's, and each one's hawā has no end, so following their ahwāʾ is the utmost of straying. (شها): shahwa is at root the soul's yearning (nuzūʿ) for what it wants; in this world of two kinds, genuine (the body suffers without it, like food in hunger) and false; the thing desired is also called shahwa; 3:14 may bear both kinds; 19:59 'they followed the shahawāt' is of the false kind; of Paradise he cites 41:31 'mā tashtahī anfusukum'. (نهى): in 79:40 'restrained the soul from hawā' he says the meaning is not telling oneself 'don't' but suppressing the soul from its shahwa.

The corpus files the singular هَوَى under the lemma هَوَاء (11 places: 10 × hawā, plus 14:43 hawāʾ 'void'); the member sums هَوَاء and أَهْوَاء and counts that one place too. شَهْوَة sums the corpus's شَهْوَة (2) and شَهَوَة (the plural, 3).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 28 hawā / ahwāʾ places read): hawā is always blamed — followed by those who stray (e.g. 7:176, 18:28, 28:50, 45:23), forbidden to follow (4:135, 38:26), restrained (79:40), or denied of the Prophet's speech (53:3). The noun shahwa is blamed in 4:27, 19:59, 7:81, 27:55 and set out as worldly enjoyment in 3:14; the verb ištahā is said approvingly of Paradise (41:31). 7:81 and 27:55 (Lot's people) are not cited.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: bs meaning 'požuda, žudnja' (not 'užitak'); spelling.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, hawā je naginjanje duše prema požudi; neki kažu da je tako nazvan jer onoga ko ga slijedi obara u svaku nesreću. Množinu „njihove strasti” Kur'an upotrebljava, kaže on, da ukaže da svako ima svoju strast, i da joj nema kraja. U Kur'anu je strast uvijek pokuđena.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, hawā is the soul's leaning toward shahwa; some say it is so named because it makes its follower fall into every calamity. The Quran uses the plural “their desires”, he says, to show that each has his own desire, and that it has no end. In the Quran desire is always blamed.

why.bs: „Zar ne vidiš onoga koji je strast svoju za boga svoga uzeo?” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Have you seen he who has taken as his god his [own] desire?” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A onaj ko se bude bojao stajanja pred Gospodarom svojim i dušu od strasti uzdržavao” – ar-Rāġib: suzdržati dušu od njene požude.
why.en: “But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] desire” — ar-Rāġib: to hold the soul back from its shahwa.

why.bs: „Da se istina povodi za njihovim strastima, nebesa i Zemlja i oni na njima bi propali” – množina, mnoge strasti.
why.en: “But if the Truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been ruined” — the plural, many desires.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, šahwa je stremljenje duše prema onome što želi; na ovom svijetu je dvojaka: istinska, bez koje tijelo trpi, kao želja za hranom u gladi, i lažna, bez koje može. I ono što se želi naziva se šahwa. Glagol od istog korijena Kur'an kaže i za ono što duše žele u Dženetu (41:31).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, shahwa is the soul's yearning for what it wants; in this world it is of two kinds: genuine, without which the body suffers, like the wish for food in hunger, and false, which it can do without. The thing wanted is also called shahwa. The Quran uses the verb of this root for what souls desire in Paradise too (41:31).

why.bs: „Ljudima je uljepšana ljubav prema požudama: ženama, sinovima, gomilama zlata i srebra…” – ar-Rāġib: može obuhvatiti obje vrste.
why.en: “Beautified for people is the love of that which they desire [i.e. passions] — of women and sons, heaped-up sums of gold and silver…” — ar-Rāġib: it may cover both kinds.

why.bs: „Zatim su poslije njih došla pokoljenja koja su molitvu zapostavila i za požudama se povela” – ar-Rāġib: lažne požude.
why.en: “But there came after them successors who neglected prayer and pursued passions” — ar-Rāġib: the false kind.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače strah koji obuzme čovjeka. Prema ar-Rāġibovim definicijama, razlikuju se po slici koju nose: strah koji ispuni i presiječe, grč i uzmicanje pred strašnim, i strah ubačen u nutrinu.
shared.en: All three words mean a fear that seizes a person. Going by ar-Rāġib's definitions, they differ in the image they carry: fear that fills and cuts off, a shrinking back from the frightening, and fear cast into the inner self.

tellApart.bs: Strah koji ispuni srce i presiječe, u Kur'anu najčešće ubačen u srca neprijatelja → رُعْب; grč i uzmicanje pred strašnim, u Kur'anu prepast Sudnjeg dana → فَزَع; strah ubačen u nutrinu, koji prođe (Ibrahim) → رَوْع.
tellApart.en: Fear that fills the heart and cuts off, in the Quran mostly cast into the hearts of enemies → رُعْب; a shrinking and recoiling before the frightening, in the Quran the alarm of the Last Day → فَزَع; fear cast into the inner self, which passes (Abraham) → رَوْع.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رعب, فزع, روع
notes: ar-Rāġib (رعب): ruʿb is being cut off (inqiṭāʿ) from the fullness of fear; from the image of filling, raʿabtu l-ḥawḍ, I filled the basin, and a sayl rāʿib that fills the valley; from the image of cutting, raʿabtu s-sanām, I cut the hump; he cites 33:26/59:2 (qaḏafa fī qulūbihimu r-ruʿb), 3:151 and 18:18 (la-muliʾta minhum ruʿban). (فزع): fazaʿ is a contraction and recoil that befalls a person from a frightening thing, of the genus of jazaʿ; one does not say faziʿtu mina llāh as one says ḫiftu minhu; the 'greatest fazaʿ' of 21:103 is the fazaʿ of entering the Fire; he cites 27:87, 27:89, 34:23. (روع): ar-rūʿ is the mind (al-ḫalad), as in the hadith 'the Holy Spirit breathed into my rūʿ'; ar-rawʿ is what strikes it, used for the fazaʿ cast into it; he cites 11:74. The OpenITI text is unvocalised: rūʿ / rawʿ are read from the sense.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 5 / 2 / 1 places read): رُعْب is cast by Allah into the hearts of those fighting the believers in 3:151, 8:12, 33:26, 59:2, and in 18:18 fills whoever would look on the sleepers of the cave; the noun فَزَع is only in 21:103 and 27:89, both of the Last Day; رَوْع is only in 11:74.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: 21:103 'the greatest alarm' as the alarm of entering the Fire is his reading, with the mufassirun's others named.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رعب, فزع, روع (2026-11-06): 22 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): Each definition is his; the comparison is ours

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ruʿb je stanje kad se čovjek presiječe od straha kojim se ispunio; zato se od istog korijena kaže „napuniti bazen” i „odsjeći”. U Kur'anu ga Allah četiri puta ubacuje u srca onih koji se bore protiv vjernika, a peti put njime bi se ispunio onaj ko bi ugledao stanovnike pećine.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ruʿb is being cut off by a fear one is filled with; so the same root says “to fill a basin” and “to cut off”. In the Quran Allah casts it four times into the hearts of those fighting the believers, and the fifth time it would fill whoever looked on the people of the cave.

why.bs: „Ulit ćemo užas u srca onih koji ne vjeruju zato što Allahu druge ravnim smatraju” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve for what they have associated with Allah” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Da si ih vidio, od njih bi pobjegao i užasom bi se ispunio” – ar-Rāġib: slika ispunjenosti.
why.en: “If you had looked at them, you would have turned from them in flight and been filled by them with terror” — ar-Rāġib: the image of being filled.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, fazaʿ je grč i uzmicanje koje obuzme čovjeka pred nečim strašnim, srodno uznemirenosti (džazaʿ); zato se ne kaže „uplašio sam se (faziʿtu) Allaha” kao što se kaže „bojim se (ḫiftu) Allaha”. Imenica fazaʿ u Kur'anu dolazi samo za Sudnji dan.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, fazaʿ is the shrinking and recoil that seizes a person before something frightening, akin to agitation (jazaʿ); so one does not say “I took alarm (faziʿtu) at Allah” as one says “I fear (ḫiftu) Allah”. The noun fazaʿ in the Quran is said only of the Last Day.

why.bs: „Neće ih ožalostiti najveća prepast” – ar-Rāġib to tumači kao prepast od ulaska u vatru; drugi mufessiri navode i druga tumačenja.
why.en: “They will not be grieved by the greatest alarm” — ar-Rāġib takes it to be the alarm of entering the Fire; other mufassirun give other readings.

why.bs: „Ko dođe s dobrim djelom dobit će bolje od njega, i oni će toga Dana od prepasti sigurni biti.”
why.en: “Whoever comes [at Judgement] with a good deed will have better than it, and they, from the alarm of that Day, will be safe.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, riječ je vezana za rūʿ, nutrinu, um: rawʿ je ono što ga pogodi, strah ubačen u njega. U Kur'anu dolazi samo jednom: za Ibrahima, kad mu je strepnja prošla.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the word is tied to rūʿ, the inner mind: rawʿ is what strikes it, the fear cast into it. It comes only once in the Quran: of Abraham, when his fright had passed.

why.bs: „I kad je Ibrahima strepnja prošla i radosna vijest mu stigla…” – strepnja koju je osjetio kad gosti nisu htjeli jesti (11:70); ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And when the fright had left Abraham and the good tidings had reached him…” — the fright he felt when his guests would not eat (11:70); ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače bol zbog onoga što je prošlo. Prema ar-Rāġibu, nadam je žaljenje zbog promijenjenog mišljenja o prošloj stvari, a ḥasra je tuga za propuštenim uz kajanje.
shared.en: Both words mean pain over what is past. According to ar-Rāġib, nadam is grief at a changed opinion about a past matter, and ḥasra is sorrow over what was missed together with regret.

tellApart.bs: Tuga za propuštenim i žaljenje zbog toga, često na Sudnjem danu → حَسْرَة; kajanje kad se uvidi da je odluka bila pogrešna, u Kur'anu uvijek „osvanuti pokajan” → نَادِم.
tellApart.en: Sorrow over what was missed and regret for it, often on the Last Day → حَسْرَة; regret on seeing that a decision was wrong, in the Quran always “to become (aṣbaḥa) regretful” → نَادِم.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حسر, ندم
notes: ar-Rāġib (حسر): ḥasr is uncovering; al-ḥasra is grief over what one has missed and regret (nadam) over it, as though the ignorance that drove him to his deed were lifted off him, or his strength were stripped by excess of grief, or weariness overtook him so that he could not make up for what he neglected; he cites 3:156, 69:50, 39:56, 2:167, 36:30. (ندم): nadam and nadāma are grief (taḥassur) from a change of opinion in a past matter; its root is grief keeping one company (munādama); he cites 5:31 and 23:40.
The corpus splits حَسْرَة (7), حَسْرَت (6:31 yā ḥasratanā) and حَسْرَتَى (39:56 yā ḥasratā); the member sums them (9).

Quranic usage (our observation, all places read): ḥasra is the disbelievers' grief in the Hereafter (2:167, 6:31, 19:39, 39:56, 69:50), and also in this world (3:156, 8:36); 36:30 is a cry of grief over people who mocked their messengers. نَادِم comes all five times with aṣbaḥa, 'to become, to wake up as' (5:31, 5:52, 23:40, 26:157, 49:6). 35:8 (said to the Prophet) is not cited.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 4 flags, fixed: tellApart without 'exhaustion' and 'too late' (one of his three images, and not his); ḥasra 'grižnja savjesti / remorse' apart from nadim's 'kajanje / regret'; 19:39 and 26:157 say only what the ayah says.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries حسر, ندم (2026-11-06): 15 attributed points confirmed; changed — shared (reworded): Inability to make up is only the third of three alternative images he gives (ignorance lifted / strength stripped by grief / weariness from making up); we turned it into a defining condition

meaning.en: anguish, sorrow over what is lost

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, ḥasra je tuga za onim što je čovjeku promaklo, uz grižnju savjesti zbog toga, kao da se s njega skinulo neznanje koje ga je na djelo navelo, ili mu je snaga klonula od tuge, ili je nemoćan da popravi propušteno. Riječ je od korijena „otkriti, ogoliti”.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, ḥasra is grief over what one has missed, with remorse for it, as though the ignorance that drove him to the deed were stripped off him, or his strength had failed from grief, or he were powerless to make up what he neglected. The word is from the root of uncovering, laying bare.

why.bs: „Da ne bi neko rekao: ‘Teško meni (doslovno: o jade moj) zbog onoga što sam prema Allahu propustio!’” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Lest a soul should say, ‘Oh [how great is] my anguish over what I neglected in regard to Allah’” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Tako će im Allah pokazati djela njihova kao jad za njih” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Thus will Allah show them their deeds as anguish upon them” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I upozori ih na Dan jada, kad stvar bude presuđena” – Dan kad se stvar odluči.
why.en: “And warn them of the Day of Anguish, when the matter will be decided” — the Day on which the matter is settled.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nadam je žaljenje zbog promijenjenog mišljenja o nečemu što je prošlo: čovjek uvidi da je pogrešno odlučio. U Kur'anu dolazi pet puta, i svaki put s glagolom „osvanuti, postati” (أَصْبَحَ) – kajanje koje dođe nakon djela.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, nadam is grief at a changed opinion about something past: one sees that one decided wrongly. It comes five times in the Quran, each time with the verb “to wake up as, to become” (أَصْبَحَ) — regret that comes after the deed.

why.bs: Ademov sin, kad je vidio gavrana: „…i postade jedan od onih koji se kaju” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Adam's son, on seeing the raven: “…and he became of the regretful” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ako vam nepouzdan čovjek donese kakvu vijest, provjerite je, da ne biste… pa se kajali zbog onoga što ste učinili” – kajanje zbog prenagljene odluke.
why.en: “If there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful” — regret for a hasty decision.

why.bs: Semud: „Pa su je zaklali, i pokajali se (doslovno: osvanuli su pokajani)” – kajanje koje dođe nakon djela.
why.en: Thamūd: “But they hamstrung her and so became regretful” — regret that came after the deed.

title.bs: Napojiti i dati vode za piće
title.en: Giving to drink and providing drink

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače dati nekome da pije. Prema ar-Rāġibu, IV vrsta je jača: ne samo dati piće, nego učiniti da onaj drugi ima izvor iz kojeg pije kako hoće.
shared.en: Both verbs mean to give someone to drink. According to ar-Rāġib, Form IV is the stronger: not only to give a drink, but to make for the other a source he drinks from as he wishes.

tellApart.bs: Dati nekome piće, napojiti (čašu, stado, njivu) → سَقَى; učiniti nekome vodu ili mlijeko dostupnim kao izvor – kiša, slatka voda, mlijeko stoke → أَسْقَى.
tellApart.en: To give someone a drink, to water (a cup, a flock, a field) → سَقَى; to make water or milk available to someone as a supply — rain, sweet water, the milk of cattle → أَسْقَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries سقى
notes: ar-Rāġib (سقى): saqy and suqyā are giving someone what he drinks; isqāʾ is making it for him so that he takes it as he wishes, so isqāʾ is more far-reaching (ablaġ) than saqy — 'asqaytuhu nahran', I gave him a river; for saqy he cites 76:21, 47:15, 26:79; for isqāʾ 77:27 and 15:22 ('We made it a supply of drink for you'), and nusqīkum mimmā fī buṭūnihā (the wording of 23:21; 16:66 has buṭūnihī and the same two readings), read with fatḥa and ḍamma.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 12 / 8 places read): أَسْقَى is said of rain and abundant water (15:22, 25:49, 72:16, 77:27), of milk from cattle (16:66, 23:21), and of the drink of Paradise in the passive (76:17, 83:25). سَقَى is said of single acts of giving drink or watering: the cupbearer (12:41), Moses watering the women's flock (28:23-25), Abraham's 'He gives me drink' (26:79), the cow that does not water the tilth (2:71), land watered with one water (13:4), the pure drink of Paradise (76:21), and the drink of Hell (14:16, 47:15, 88:5, not cited). Paradise has both verbs, so no rule is drawn from it.
16:66: Ḥafṣ reads nusqīkum (Form IV); Nāfiʿ and others read nasqīkum (Form I) — ar-Rāġib mentions both readings, quoting the identical phrase of 23:21 (buṭūnihā); the why says so.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 4 flags, fixed: 'rivers' was his example sentence, not Quranic usage; 'single acts' dropped (26:79 is continual); the drink of Paradise left to سَقَى (76:21) — the corpus files the passive yusqawna (76:17, 83:25) under Form IV, where the two forms coincide; 15:22 bs past tense.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

meaning.en: to give to drink, to water

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dati nekome ono što pije. U Kur'anu je to čin davanja pića: peharnik poji svoga gospodara, Musa napaja stado dviju žena, njiva se zalijeva, Ibrahim kaže da ga Allah poji, a Gospodar daje stanovnicima Dženeta čisto piće.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to give someone what he drinks. In the Quran it is the act of giving a drink: a cupbearer gives his master drink, Moses waters the two women's flock, a field is watered, Abraham says that Allah gives him drink, and the Lord gives the people of Paradise a pure drink.

why.bs: Ibrahim: „…i Koji me hrani i poji” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Abraham: “And it is He who feeds me and gives me drink” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I on im napoji stado, pa se skloni u hlad” – Musa, pojedinačno djelo.
why.en: “So he watered [their flocks] for them; then he went back to the shade” — Moses, a single act.

why.bs: „I Gospodar njihov će ih napojiti čistim pićem” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za sakā.
why.en: “And their Lord will give them a purifying drink” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for saqā.

meaning.bs: dati vode za piće, opskrbiti pićem

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, isqāʾ je jači od saqy: učiniti nekome izvor iz kojeg pije kako hoće, kao kad se kaže „dao sam mu rijeku”. U Kur'anu je to kiša i obilna voda, te mlijeko iz stoke.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, isqāʾ is stronger than saqy: to make for someone a source he drinks from as he wishes, as one says “I gave him a river”. In the Quran it is rain and abundant water, and milk from cattle.

why.bs: „I s neba smo spustili vodu i njome vas opskrbili, a vi je ne čuvate” – ar-Rāġib: učinili smo je izvorom vašeg pića.
why.en: “And We sent down water from the sky and provided you with it to drink, and you are not its retainers” — ar-Rāġib: We made it a supply of drink for you.

why.bs: „I na njoj čvrsto usađena brda visoka postavili i slatkom vas vodom opskrbili” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And We placed therein lofty, firmly set mountains and provided you with sweet water to drink” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Mi vas opskrbljujemo pićem od onoga što je u utrobama njihovim” – mlijeko stoke; ar-Rāġib, navodeći iste riječi iz 23:21, bilježi i čitanje nasqīkum (I vrsta).
why.en: “We provide you with drink from what is in their bellies” — the milk of cattle; ar-Rāġib, quoting the same words from 23:21, notes the reading nasqīkum (Form I).

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o obrađenoj zemlji i onome što na njoj raste. Ar-Rāġib ih razdvaja po tome čije je djelo: čovjekovo je da zemlju pripremi i baci sjeme, a dati da nikne je Allahovo djelo.
shared.en: Both words speak of cultivated land and what grows on it. Ar-Rāġib sets them apart by whose act each is: man's part is to prepare the soil and cast the seed, while making it grow is Allah's act.

tellApart.bs: Bacanje sjemena i pripremljena, obrađena zemlja, pa i plod rada → حَرْث; ono što nikne i raste, usjev → زَرْع.
tellApart.en: Casting seed and the prepared, tilled land, and so the yield of one's labour → حَرْث; what sprouts and grows, the crop → زَرْع.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries حرث, زرع
notes: ar-Rāġib (حرث): ḥarṯ is casting seed into the earth and preparing it for zarʿ; the tilled land is also called ḥarṯ (68:22); from it is imagined the flourishing that results (42:20, the ḥarṯ of the Hereafter and of this world); 2:223 is by way of simile; 2:205 'covers both tilths'. (زرع): zarʿ is causing to grow (inbāt), and in reality that belongs to divine, not human, matters; in 56:63–64 Allah attributes ḥarṯ to them, denies them zarʿ and attributes it to Himself; when said of a man it is because he does the causes; zarʿ is at root a verbal noun used for what is sown (32:27, 44:26).

56:63–64 (أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تَحْرُثُونَ ۝ أَأَنتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُ) has the verbs, not the nouns, so it is described in the nuance texts and not cited as a member ayah. 2:223 is not cited (a simile ar-Rāġib explains; it needs more context than a card gives).
The corpus files the plural زُرُوع (26:148, 44:26) under زَرْع.
