nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, bacanje sjemena u zemlju i njeno pripremanje za usjev; zatim i sama obrađena zemlja, pa i ono što rad donese. U 56:63–64 Allah ljudima pripisuje oranje (تَحْرُثُونَ), a nicanje sebi.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, casting seed into the earth and preparing it for the crop; then the tilled land itself, and also what labour yields. In 56:63–64 Allah ascribes the tilling (تَحْرُثُونَ) to people and the growing to Himself.

why.bs: „Poranite rano na svoje njive (حَرْث) ako želite brati plodove” – obrađena zemlja; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Go early to your tilth (حَرْث) if you would cut the fruit” — the tilled land; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Onome ko želi njivu (حَرْث) budućeg svijeta, Mi ćemo njegovu njivu povećati” – prema ar-Rāġibu, ono što rad donese.
why.en: “Whoever desires the tilth (حَرْث) of the Hereafter – We increase for him in his tilth” — according to ar-Rāġib, what labour yields.

why.bs: Davud i Sulejman sude o njivi (حَرْث) u koju su noću zalutale tuđe ovce.
why.en: David and Solomon judge concerning the tilth (حَرْث) into which other people's sheep had strayed by night.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, zarʿ je dati da nikne, a to je u svojoj suštini Allahovo, a ne ljudsko djelo; čovjeku se pripisuje samo zato što čini uzroke. Izvorno glagolska imenica, kaže se i za ono što je posijano: usjev.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, zarʿ is making to grow, and that in its reality is Allah's act, not man's; it is said of a man only because he does the causes. At root a verbal noun, it is said of what is sown: the crop.

why.bs: „Mi tjeramo vodu na neplodnu zemlju i njome izvodimo usjev (زَرْع)” – nicanje je Allahovo djelo; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “We drive the water to the dry land and bring forth thereby crops (زَرْع)” — the growing is Allah's act; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Faraonovi ljudi ostavili su „i usjeve (زُرُوع) i lijepe dvorce” – množina, koju ar-Rāġib također navodi.
why.en: Pharaoh's people left behind “crops (زُرُوع) and noble sites” — the plural, which ar-Rāġib also cites.

why.bs: Ibrahim: „Nastanio sam dio porodice svoje u dolini bez usjeva (زَرْع)” – zemlja na kojoj ništa ne raste.
why.en: Abraham: “I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley (غَيْرِ ذِي زَرْعٍ)” — land where nothing grows.

shared.bs: Obje riječi znače plovilo na vodi. Razlikuju se po porijeklu riječi koje ar-Rāġib navodi (samo za safīnu) i po tome koliko se u Kur'anu javljaju.
shared.en: Both words mean a craft on the water. They differ in the origin ar-Rāġib gives for the word (only for safīna) and in how often the Quran uses them.

tellApart.bs: Lađa, i za jednu i za više njih, opća riječ za plovidbu i za Nuhovu lađu → فُلْك; brod, imenovan po struganju površine, u Kur'anu u kazivanju o Musau i Hidru i o Nuhovim ljudima → سَفِينَة.
tellApart.en: A ship, said of one or many, the general word for sailing and for Noah's ark → فُلْك; a vessel, named after scraping a surface, in the Quran in the story of Moses and al-Khidr and of Noah's people → سَفِينَة.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فلك, سفن
notes: ar-Rāġib (فلك): fulk is the ship (as-safīna), used for one and for many, with a different underlying pattern for each (singular like qufl, plural like ḥumr); he cites 10:22, 2:164, 35:12, 43:12; falak, the course of the stars (21:33), is named so for its likeness to it — a different word in the corpus. (سفن): safn is scraping (naḥt) the surface of a thing (wood, skin; the wind scraping dust off the ground); the safīna is named after safn (18:79), and then by extension any easy mount is likened to it.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 23 / 3 places read): سَفِينَة is only in 18:71, 18:79 (twice) and 29:15 (Noah's ark: 'the people of the ship'); فُلْك is the word for ships people sail (2:164, 10:22, 17:66), for Noah's ark (11:37, 23:27) and for the ship Jonah fled to (37:140).
Decision: bs lađa for فُلْك, brod for سَفِينَة (Korkut uses lađa for both); en ship for فُلْك, vessel for سَفِينَة (Sahih International uses ship for both), so each member keeps its own word.
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: he gives an origin only for safīna.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, lađa – riječ ista za jednu i za više njih. U Kur'anu je to opća riječ za plovidbu (2:164, 17:66) i za Nuhovu lađu (11:37). Riječ فَلَك – putanja zvijezda – po njemu je tako nazvana po sličnosti s njom.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the ship — one word for one and for many. In the Quran it is the general word for sailing (2:164, 17:66) and for Noah's ark (11:37). The word فَلَك, the course of the stars, is in his view named after its likeness to it.

why.bs: „…i u lađama (فُلْك) koje plove morem s onim što ljudima koristi” – mnoge lađe; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “…and the ships (فُلْك) which sail through the sea with that which benefits people” — many ships; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Nuhu je rečeno: „Gradi lađu (فُلْك) pod Našim nadzorom i prema Našem nadahnuću” – jedna lađa.
why.en: Noah is told: “Construct the ship (فُلْك) under Our observation and Our inspiration” — one ship.

why.bs: „Kad ste na lađama (فُلْك) i one plove s njima uz povoljan vjetar…” – plovidba ljudi.
why.en: “When you are in ships (فُلْك) and they sail with them by a good wind…” — people's sailing.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, nazvan po riječi safn – struganje, tesanje površine nečega; zatim se brodu prispodobljuje svako lahko jahalo. U Kur'anu samo u kazivanju o Musau i čovjeku od znanja (18:71, 18:79) i o Nuhovim ljudima (29:15).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, named after safn — scraping, planing the surface of a thing; then any easy mount is likened to it. In the Quran only in the story of Moses and the man of knowledge (18:71, 18:79) and of Noah's people (29:15).

why.bs: „Što se tiče broda (سَفِينَة), on je pripadao siromasima koji su radili na moru” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “As for the vessel (سَفِينَة), it belonged to poor people working at sea” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I pođoše njih dvojica, pa kad se ukrcaše u brod (سَفِينَة), on ga probuši.”
why.en: “So they set out, until when they had embarked on the vessel (سَفِينَة), he tore it open.”

why.bs: „Pa smo spasili njega (Nuha) i one koji su bili u brodu (سَفِينَة) i učinili ga poukom svjetovima.”
why.en: “But We saved him (Noah) and the companions of the vessel (سَفِينَة), and We made it a sign for the worlds.”

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi su posude za piće, i sve tri u Kur'anu dolaze u opisu Dženeta. Ar-Rāġibove zasebne definicije razlikuju se po obliku posude i po tome je li u njoj piće.
shared.en: All three words are vessels for drink, and all three come in the Quran in the description of Paradise. Ar-Rāġib's separate definitions differ by the vessel's shape and by whether drink is in it.

tellApart.bs: Posuda s pićem u njoj, a i samo piće → كَأْس; čaša bez drške → أَكْوَاب; ibrik, za koji ar-Rāġib kaže samo da je poznat → أَبَارِيق.
tellApart.en: The vessel with drink in it, and also the drink itself → كَأْس; a cup with no handle → أَكْوَاب; a pitcher, of which ar-Rāġib says only that it is well known → أَبَارِيق.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries كأس, كوب, برق
notes: ar-Rāġib (كأس): the ka's is the vessel with the drink in it, and each of the two alone is also called ka's ('I drank a ka's'; 'a good ka's' meaning the drink); he cites 76:17 and 'ka's min maʿīn'. (كوب): the kūb is a cup (qadaḥ) without a handle, plural akwāb; he cites 56:18. (برق): al-ibrīq maʿrūf — he gives no description beyond 'well known' under the root of lightning; we do not give him an etymology for it.

Quranic usage (our observation, all 6 / 4 / 1 places read): كَأْس (37:45, 52:23, 56:18, 76:5, 76:17, 78:34), أَكْوَاب (43:71, 56:18, 76:15, 88:14) and أَبَارِيق (56:18) are all said of Paradise; 56:18 names all three together. The cards say only what the ayat say.
Bosnian follows Korkut's 56:18 (čaše, ibrici, pehari); English: cup, goblets, pitchers (Sahih International has 'vessels' for akwāb in 56:18 — goblets keeps it apart from the general word).
Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: spelling (Dženet throughout the batch).
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, posuda zajedno s pićem u njoj; a i jedno i drugo posebno zove se كَأْس, pa se kaže „popio sam pehar”, misleći na piće.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the vessel together with the drink in it; and each of the two alone is also called كَأْس, so one says “I drank a cup”, meaning the drink.

why.bs: „I tamo će im se davati da piju iz pehara (كَأْس) pomiješanog s đumbirom” – posuda s pićem; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And they will be given to drink a cup (كَأْس) whose mixture is of ginger” — the vessel with its drink; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Oni će jedni drugima pehar (كَأْس) dodavati, od kojeg nema ni besmislica ni grijeha.”
why.en: “They will exchange with one another a cup (كَأْس) wherein [results] no ill speech or sin.”

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, كُوب je čaša bez drške; أَكْوَاب je njena množina. U Kur'anu sva četiri puta u opisu Dženeta.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a كُوب is a cup without a handle; أَكْوَاب is its plural. In the Quran all four times in the description of Paradise.

why.bs: „…sa čašama (أَكْوَاب), ibricima i peharom od pića iz izvora” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet za čašu bez drške.
why.en: “With goblets (أَكْوَاب), pitchers and a cup [of drink] from a flowing spring” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah for the handleless cup.

why.bs: „Među njima će se kružiti sa srebrenim posudama i čašama (أَكْوَاب) prozirnim kao staklo.”
why.en: “And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver and goblets (أَكْوَاب) having been [created] clear [as glass].”

nuance.bs: Ar-Rāġib je spominje pod korijenom munje (برق) i kaže samo da je ibrik poznat. U Kur'anu jednom, uz čaše i pehar.
nuance.en: Ar-Rāġib mentions it under the root of lightning (برق) and says only that the pitcher is well known. In the Quran once, beside the goblets and the cup.

why.bs: „…sa čašama, ibricima (أَبَارِيق) i peharom od pića iz izvora” – jedino mjesto u Kur'anu.
why.en: “With goblets, pitchers (أَبَارِيق) and a cup [of drink] from a flowing spring” — the only place in the Quran.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o planinama. جَبَل je samo ime planine; رَوَاسِي ih imenuje po jednom svojstvu – po tome što su čvrsto usađene.
shared.en: Both words speak of mountains. جَبَل is the plain name of the mountain; رَوَاسِي names them by one quality — that they are firmly set.

tellApart.bs: Planina kao takva, i u slikama čvrstine i veličine → جَبَل; ono što je čvrsto usađeno, planine kao oslonac Zemlje → رَوَاسِي.
tellApart.en: The mountain as such, also in images of firmness and greatness → جَبَل; what is firmly set, the mountains as the earth's anchors → رَوَاسِي.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries جبل, رسا
notes: ar-Rāġib (جبل): jabal, plural ajbāl and jibāl (78:7, 79:32, 24:43, 35:27, 20:105, 26:149); its meanings are taken over: firmness ('so-and-so is a mountain that does not budge'), one's innate nature (jabalahu Allāh ʿalā…), and greatness — jibill for a great crowd (36:62). (رسا): rasā is to stand firm, arsāhu to make it firm; 34:13 'qudūr rāsiyāt'; 77:27 'rawāsiya šāmiḵāt' = firm mountains; 79:32 points to 78:7 (the mountains as pegs).

Quranic usage (our observation, all 37 / 10 places read): رَوَاسِي is said nine times of what Allah has placed in the earth (جَعَلَ / أَلْقَى), three times with 'lest it shift with you' (16:15, 21:31, 31:10); the tenth place (34:13) is the firm-standing cauldrons of Solomon. The scenes of the Last Day (18:47, 20:105, 52:10, 77:10, 78:20, 81:3, 101:5) all use الْجِبَال, never رَوَاسِي.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: 34:13 is رَاسِيَات (same root, another word), so رَوَاسِي is nine times, always of the earth.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

nuance.bs: Opća riječ za planinu. Ar-Rāġib kaže da je iz nje izvedena slika čvrstine („planina koja se ne pomjera”), urođene naravi i veličine. U Kur'anu se ovom riječju opisuje i kako se planine na Sudnjem danu pomjeraju i raspadaju.
nuance.en: The general word for mountain. Ar-Rāġib says images of firmness (“a mountain that does not budge”), of innate nature and of greatness are drawn from it. In the Quran this word also describes how the mountains move and crumble on the Last Day.

why.bs: „I planine (جِبَال) je učvrstio (أَرْسَاهَا)” – ime planine s glagolom istog korijena kao رَوَاسِي; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And the mountains (جِبَال) He set firmly (أَرْسَاهَا)” — the name of the mountain with a verb of the root of رَوَاسِي; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Da ovaj Kur'an kakvoj planini (جَبَل) spustimo, ti bi vidio kako je strahopoštovanjem prema Allahu ponizno i raspuklo” – slika čvrstoga koje se predaje.
why.en: “If We had sent down this Quran upon a mountain (جَبَل), you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of Allah” — an image of the firm thing yielding.

why.bs: „I planine (جِبَال) će se kretati.” – Sudnji dan.
why.en: “And the mountains (جِبَال) will pass on, departing” — the Last Day.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od rasā – stajati čvrsto; رَوَاسِي su čvrsto usađene planine. U Kur'anu se riječ javlja devet puta, uvijek uz Zemlju u koju ih je Allah postavio, a tri puta uz „da se s vama ne ljulja”; isti korijen daje i „nepomične kotlove” (رَاسِيَات, 34:13).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from rasā, to stand firm; رَوَاسِي are firmly set mountains. In the Quran the word comes nine times, always with the earth in which Allah has placed them, three of them with “lest it shift with you”; the same root also gives “firm cauldrons” (رَاسِيَات, 34:13).

why.bs: „I po Zemlji je nepomična brda (رَوَاسِي) pobacao da se s vama ne ljulja.”
why.en: “And He has cast into the earth firmly set mountains (رَوَاسِي), lest it shift with you.”

why.bs: „I na njoj smo nepomična, visoka brda (رَوَاسِي) postavili” – ar-Rāġib: čvrste planine.
why.en: “And We placed therein lofty, firmly set mountains (رَوَاسِي)” — ar-Rāġib: firm mountains.

why.bs: Džini su Sulejmanu pravili „i kotlove nepomične (رَاسِيَات)” – isto svojstvo čvrstine, izvan planina; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: The jinn made for Solomon “stationary kettles (رَاسِيَات)” — the same quality of firmness, outside mountains; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače uzeti nešto u ruku ili ne pustiti ga, i oba se kažu za uskraćivanje. Razlikuju se po pokretu: jedan je skupljanje šake, drugi je držanje i čuvanje onoga što se drži.
shared.en: Both verbs mean to take a thing in hand or not let it go, and both are said of withholding. They differ in the movement: one is closing the hand, the other is holding and keeping what is held.

tellApart.bs: Uhvatiti cijelom šakom, skupiti, uskratiti – i za Allaha: uskraćuje i daje, kako Njemu priliči → قَبَضَ; prihvatiti se nečega i čuvati ga, držati da ne padne, zadržati → أَمْسَكَ.
tellApart.en: To grasp with the whole hand, to draw in, to withhold — and of Allah: He withholds and grants, as befits Him → قَبَضَ; to hold on to a thing and keep it, hold it up so it does not fall, keep back → أَمْسَكَ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries قبض, مسك, بسط
notes: ar-Rāġib (قبض): qabḍ is taking a thing with the whole palm; closing the hand on a thing after taking it, or closing it before taking it, which is holding back (imsāk) from it — hence holding the hand back from giving is called qabḍ: 9:67 'yaqbiḍūna aydiyahum' = they refrain from spending; on 2:245 'yaqbiḍu wa yabsuṭu' he gives several readings: He takes away at one time and gives at another, or from some and to others, or gathers and scatters, or causes death and gives life; 25:46 is the shade withdrawn by the sun. (مسك): imsāk is holding on to a thing and keeping it (al-taʿalluq bihi wa ḥifẓuhu): 2:229, and 22:65 'yumsiku as-samāʾa' = preserves it; amsaktu ʿanhu = I withheld; imsāk is used as a metonymy for stinginess.
Quranic usage: 67:19 has both verbs — the birds spread and fold (يَقْبِضْنَ) their wings, and none holds them up (يُمْسِكُهُنَّ) but the Most Merciful.
Not cited: 33:37 (said to the Prophet).

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 1 flag, fixed: 2:245 given as one of the several readings he lists, as befits Him; 'holding back' left to أَمْسَكَ.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

meaning.en: to clench, to draw in, to withhold

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, uhvatiti cijelom šakom; skupiti ruku na nečemu kad se uzme, ili prije nego se uzme – a to je ustezanje od toga, pa „stisnuti ruke” znači ne davati. Kad je Allah subjekt (2:245), on navodi više tumačenja, među njima da On jednom oduzima, a drugi put daje, kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to grasp with the whole palm; to close the hand on a thing after taking it, or before taking it — which is refraining from it, so “to clench the hands” means not to give. With Allah as subject (2:245) he gives several readings, among them that He takes away at one time and gives at another, as befits Him.

why.bs: „Allah uskraćuje (يَقْبِضُ) i obilno daje” – ar-Rāġib navodi više tumačenja: oduzima pa daje, jednima oduzima a drugima daje, ili usmrćuje i oživljava; kako Njemu priliči.
why.en: “It is Allah who withholds (يَقْبِضُ) and grants abundance” — ar-Rāġib gives several readings: He takes away and gives, takes from some and gives to others, or causes death and gives life; as befits Him.

why.bs: Licemjeri „stežu (يَقْبِضُونَ) ruke svoje” – prema ar-Rāġibu, ustežu se od trošenja.
why.en: The hypocrites “close (يَقْبِضُونَ) their hands” — according to ar-Rāġib, they refrain from spending.

why.bs: Ptice nad njima „šire i skupljaju (يَقْبِضْنَ) krila” – skupljanje; a drži ih samo Milostivi (أَمْسَكَ).
why.en: The birds above them, “with wings outspread and folded in (يَقْبِضْنَ)” — drawing in; and none holds them up but the Most Merciful (أَمْسَكَ).

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, prihvatiti se nečega i čuvati ga; zato Allah „drži” nebo da ne padne, tj. čuva ga, kako Njemu priliči. Kaže se i za zadržavanje supruge u braku, a „zadržati” kod njega je i slika škrtosti.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to hold on to a thing and keep it; so Allah “holds” the sky lest it fall, that is, preserves it, as befits Him. It is said of keeping a wife in marriage, and “holding back” is for him also an image of stinginess.

why.bs: „Allah drži (يُمْسِكُ) nebesa i Zemlju da se ne bi pomjerili” – drži i čuva, kako Njemu priliči (ar-Rāġib tako tumači 22:65).
why.en: “Indeed, Allah holds (يُمْسِكُ) the heavens and the earth, lest they cease” — holds and preserves, as befits Him (so ar-Rāġib explains 22:65).

why.bs: „A kad se približi istek roka njihova, onda ih na lijep način zadržite (أَمْسِكُوهُنَّ) ili se na lijep način od njih rastavite” – zadržati u braku.
why.en: “And when they have [nearly] fulfilled their term, either retain them (أَمْسِكُوهُنَّ) according to acceptable terms or part with them according to acceptable terms” — keeping in marriage.

why.bs: „Da vi raspolažete riznicama milosti Gospodara moga, vi biste ih zadržali (أَمْسَكْتُمْ) iz straha da ne potrošite” – zadržavanje kao škrtost.
why.en: “If you possessed the depositories of the mercy of my Lord, then you would hold back (أَمْسَكْتُمْ) out of fear of spending” — holding back as stinginess.

title.en: To spread out and to draw out

shared.bs: Oba glagola znače da se nešto širi dalje od sebe, i oba se kažu za ruku i za Zemlju. Ar-Rāġib i sam objašnjava pružanje ruke (بَسْط) kao njeno „mad”, pa se značenja dodiruju; po njegovim definicijama (širenje naspram vučenja) razlikuju se po pravcu: jedan je širenje u širinu, drugi izvlačenje u dužinu.
shared.en: Both verbs mean that a thing reaches out beyond itself, and both are said of the hand and of the earth. Ar-Rāġib himself explains reaching out the hand (بَسْط) as its “madd”, so the meanings touch; by his definitions (spreading vs. pulling) they differ in direction: one is spreading in breadth, the other drawing out in length.

tellApart.bs: Raširiti i proširiti – prostirku, oblak, ruku, opskrbu → بَسَطَ; vući, izvlačiti u dužinu – sjenu, Zemlju, rok, kaznu → مَدَّ.
tellApart.en: To spread and widen — a carpet, the clouds, the hand, provision → بَسَطَ; to pull, to draw out in length — the shade, the earth, a span of time, punishment → مَدَّ.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries بسط, مد
notes: ar-Rāġib (بسط): basṭ of a thing is spreading it out and widening it — sometimes both are meant, sometimes one; bisāṭ is anything spread (71:19); 42:27 law basaṭa = had He widened (provision); basṭ al-yad is madduhā, extending the hand: for asking (13:14), taking (6:93), attacking (60:2) and giving (5:64). (مد): the root of madd is pulling (al-jarr); hence mudda, a stretch of time; 25:45 'madda ẓ-ẓill'; imdād comes mostly in what is liked and madd in what is disliked (19:79, 2:15, 7:202); 31:27 yamudduhu is from 'one river feeds another', not from that.
Not cited: 15:88 and 20:131 (said to the Prophet), 2:15 (Allah's act needs more tafsir than a card gives).

meaning.en: to spread out, to reach out, to widen

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, raširiti nešto i proširiti ga. Pružiti ruku znači ispružiti je – da se traži, uzme, napadne ili da. Kad Allah „proširuje opskrbu”, znači da je čini obilnom, kako Njemu priliči.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to spread a thing out and widen it. To reach out the hand is to extend it — to ask, take, attack or give. When Allah “widens provision” it means He makes it ample, as befits Him.

why.bs: „Kad bi Allah proširio (بَسَطَ) opskrbu robovima Svojim, oni bi se na Zemlji osilili” – prema ar-Rāġibu, učinio je obilnom.
why.en: “And if Allah had extended provision for His servants, they would have committed tyranny throughout the earth” — according to ar-Rāġib, made it ample.

why.bs: Ademov sin bratu: „Ako ti pružiš (بَسَطْتَ) ruku svoju prema meni da me ubiješ, ja svoju neću pružiti prema tebi” – pružiti ruku za napad.
why.en: Adam's son to his brother: “If you should reach out (بَسَطْتَ) your hand against me to kill me, I shall not reach out my hand against you” — the hand reached out to attack.

why.bs: „Allah šalje vjetrove koji pokreću oblake, pa ih rasprostire (يَبْسُطُ) po nebu kako hoće” – širenje u širinu.
why.en: “It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir the clouds and spread them (يَبْسُطُ) in the sky however He wills” — spreading in breadth.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, izvorno vući, izvlačiti; odatle i مُدَّة – vrijeme koje se proteže. Kad znači opskrbljivati nekoga, on primjećuje da Form IV (أَمَدَّ) najčešće dolazi o onome što je drago, a مَدَّ o onome što je mrsko – kao produžena kazna.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, at root to pull, to draw out; hence مُدَّة, time that stretches on. When it means supplying someone, he notes that Form IV (أَمَدَّ) comes mostly of what is liked, and مَدَّ of what is disliked — such as punishment drawn out.

why.bs: „Zar ne vidiš kako Gospodar tvoj sjenu proteže (مَدَّ)” – izvlačenje u dužinu; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Have you not considered your Lord – how He extends (مَدَّ) the shadow” — drawing out in length; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „On je Taj Koji je Zemlju protegao (مَدَّ) i po njoj nepomična brda i rijeke stvorio.”
why.en: “And it is He who extended (مَدَّ) the earth and placed therein firmly set mountains and rivers.”

why.bs: „Mi ćemo mu kaznu produžiti (نَمُدُّ)” – prema ar-Rāġibu, مَدَّ o onome što je mrsko.
why.en: “And We will extend (نَمُدُّ) for him from the punishment extensively” — according to ar-Rāġib, مَدَّ of what is disliked.

shared.bs: Obje riječi se kažu za bračnog druga. زَوْج je svaki od dvoje koji čine par – i muž i žena, i više od braka; بَعْل je muž, jer se na njega gledalo kao na onoga ko stoji nad ženom, a otuda i sve što stoji nad drugim.
shared.en: Both words are said of a marriage partner. زَوْج is each of the two who make a pair — husband or wife, and more than marriage; بَعْل is the husband, since he was seen as standing over the woman, and from that anything that stands over another.

tellApart.bs: Jedan od dvoje u paru – supružnik, muž ili žena, a i par, vrsta → زَوْج; muž, muški od dvoje supružnika → بَعْل.
tellApart.en: One of a pair — a spouse, husband or wife, and also a pair, a kind → زَوْج; the husband, the male of the two spouses → بَعْل.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries زوج, بعل
notes: ar-Rāġib (زوج): zawj is each of the pair, male and female, among animals that pair, and each of any two that go together, like or opposite; 2:35 'anta wa zawjuka'; zawja (with tāʾ) is 'a poor usage' (luġa radīʾa); 51:49 shows that everything in the world is a zawj, having an opposite, a like, or composition, so that Allah alone is the One (al-fard); 20:53 azwāj = kinds; 6:143 = sorts. (بعل): baʿl is the male of the two spouses (11:72), plural buʿūla (2:228); since the man was seen as standing over the woman, her manager (4:34), anything standing over another was called baʿl, and so the Arabs called the god they worshipped Baʿl (37:125).

Count: the corpus files بُعُولَة (2:228, 24:31) under بَعْل, and the 7 include 37:125, the idol Baʿl — so the card counts every place of the word, not only 'husband'. The corpus has no زَوْجَة: the Quran says زَوْج for a wife too, as ar-Rāġib's remark implies.
Not cited: 33:37 (said to the Prophet); the later observation that the Quran says زَوْج where there is harmony and بَعْل where there is not is not ar-Rāġib's and is left out.

Blind review (2026-11-06, fresh Sonnet reviewer, claims checked against the cited ayat and the Mufradāt): 2 flags, fixed: بَعْل extended, as he says, to anything that stands over another (37:125 the idol Baʿl); the verifier's wording kept ('since the husband was seen as standing over the woman'), not 'named for'.
al-ʿAskarī's al-Furūq is not used: its wording on this pair could not be verified here.

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries زوج, بعل (2026-11-06): 21 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/1/nuance (reworded): Direction of the derivation is reversed in our text: the husband sense is primary; 'standing over' explains the extension to others

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, svaki od dvoje koji čine par, muški ili ženski, i svako od dvoje što idu zajedno – slični ili suprotni. Riječ je ista za muža i za ženu (oblik زَوْجَة on smatra slabim jezikom), a znači i vrstu.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, each of the two who make a pair, male or female, and each of any two that go together — alike or opposite. The word is the same for husband and wife (the form زَوْجَة he calls poor usage), and it also means a kind.

why.bs: „O Ademe, živite ti i supruga (زَوْج) tvoja u Dženetu” – ista riječ za ženu; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “O Adam, dwell, you and your wife (زَوْج), in Paradise” — the same word for a wife; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „I od svega po par (زَوْجَيْنِ) stvaramo” – prema ar-Rāġibu, sve ima suprotnost, sličnost ili sastav, a samo je Allah Jedan.
why.en: “And of all things We created two mates (زَوْجَيْنِ)” — according to ar-Rāġib, everything has an opposite, a like or a composition, and Allah alone is the One.

why.bs: „…i Mi njome izvodimo razne vrste (أَزْوَاج) bilja” – prema ar-Rāġibu, vrste.
why.en: “…and We have brought forth thereby categories (أَزْوَاج) of various plants” — according to ar-Rāġib, kinds.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, muški od dvoje supružnika; budući da je muž viđen kao onaj koji je nad ženom, kao onaj koji se o njoj stara i odgovoran je za nju (4:34). Zato se بَعْل zvalo i ono što je iznad drugog, pa i idol Baal (37:125), koji se također broji u ovoj riječi.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, the male of the two spouses; since the husband was seen as standing over the woman, as the one who looks after her and is in charge of her (4:34). So whatever stood over another was called بَعْل, and so the idol Baʿl (37:125), which is also counted under this word.

why.bs: Ibrahimova žena: „Zar ću ja roditi kad sam starica, a i ovaj moj muž (بَعْل) je starac?” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Abraham's wife: “Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband (بَعْل), is an old man?” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „A muževi (بُعُولَة) njihovi imaju pravo da ih u toku tog vremena vrate” – množina; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And their husbands (بُعُولَة) have more right to take them back in this [period]” — the plural; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: Ilijas svom narodu: „Zar da se Baalu (بَعْل) klanjate, a da najljepšeg Stvoritelja ostavljate?” – prema ar-Rāġibu, ime za ono što se smatralo nadređenim.
why.en: Elias to his people: “Do you call upon Baʿl (بَعْل) and leave the best of creators?” — according to ar-Rāġib, a name for what was held to stand above.

shared.bs: Sve tri riječi znače izlazak iz onoga što Allah traži. Ar-Rāġib svaku izvodi iz druge slike: izlazak iz okvira, raskidanje zastora, odupiranje štapom.
shared.en: All three words mean going out of what Allah requires. Ar-Rāġib derives each from another image: leaving a bound, tearing a veil, resisting with a staff.

tellApart.bs: Izaći iz okvira šerijata, kao datula iz kore – i manjim i većim grijesima, a obično kad ih je mnogo → فَاسِق; raskinuti zastor vjere, otvoreni grijeh → فَاجِر; ne poslušati, izaći iz poslušnosti → عَصَى.
tellApart.en: To go out of the bounds of the Sharia, as a ripe date out of its skin — by small or great sins, though customarily of many → فَاسِق; to tear the veil of religion, open sin → فَاجِر; to disobey, to leave obedience → عَصَى.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries فسق, فجر, عصا
notes: ar-Rāġib (فسق): fasaqa = went out of the bounds (ḥijr) of the Sharia, from fasaqa ar-ruṭab, the ripe date coming out of its skin; it is more general than kufr; it happens with few or many sins but is customarily said of many; fāsiq is mostly said of one who accepted the Sharia's ruling and then broke all or some of it, and when an original unbeliever is called fāsiq it is because he broke what reason and the fiṭra required of him; 32:18 sets it against faith; 'the fāsiq is more general than the kāfir, and the ẓālim more general than the fāsiq'; he cites 24:4; Ibn al-Aʿrābī: fāsiq as a description of a person was not heard in Arab speech before. (فجر): fajr is splitting widely; fujūr is tearing the veil of religion (šaqq sitr ad-diyāna); fājir, plural fujjār and fajara (82:14, 83:7, 80:42); the liar is called fājir because lying is part of fujūr. (عصا): ʿaṣā ʿiṣyānan = went out of obedience, at root 'to resist with one's staff'; he cites 4:14, 10:91.

The corpus files فَجَرَة (80:42) under فُجّار; the member sums فُجّار (4) and the singular فَاجِر (71:27), one word. Quranic usage (our observation, all 5 places read): the fujjār are set against the abrār (82:13–14; 83:7 with 83:18) and against the muttaqūn (38:28).
عَصَى of Adam (20:121) is not cited (a prophet; the Quran itself adds his repentance and choosing, 20:122); 71:27 is not cited.

meaning.bs: fasik, onaj koji izlazi iz granica vjere

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, onaj ko izađe iz okvira šerijata, kao datula iz svoje kore; šire od nevjerstva. Može biti i s malo grijeha, ali se obično kaže kad ih je mnogo, i najčešće za onoga ko je prihvatio vjerske propise pa ih krši.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, one who goes out of the bounds of the Sharia, as a ripe date out of its skin; wider than unbelief. It can be by few sins, but is customarily said when they are many, and mostly of one who accepted the religious rulings and then breaks them.

why.bs: „Zar je onaj koji je vjernik isti kao onaj koji je fasik (فَاسِق)? Nisu jednaki!” – ar-Rāġib: suprotstavljen vjeri.
why.en: “Then is one who was a believer like one who was a transgressor (فَاسِق)? They are not equal” — ar-Rāġib: set against faith.

why.bs: Oni koji potvore čestite žene, a ne dovedu četiri svjedoka, „oni su fasici (فَاسِقُون)” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: Those who accuse chaste women and do not produce four witnesses — “those are the transgressors (فَاسِقُون)”; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Ako vam fasik (فَاسِق) donese kakvu vijest, dobro je provjerite.”
why.en: “If there comes to you a transgressor (فَاسِق) with information, investigate.”

meaning.bs: razvratnik, onaj koji razdire zastor vjere

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, od fajr – široko rascijepiti; fudžur je raskidanje zastora vjere. Lažov se zove فَاجِر jer je laž dio toga. U Kur'anu su فُجَّار suprotstavljeni dobrima (أَبْرَار) i bogobojaznima.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, from fajr, to split widely; fujūr is tearing the veil of religion. The liar is called فَاجِر because lying is part of it. In the Quran the فُجَّار are set against the righteous (أَبْرَار) and the God-fearing.

why.bs: „A razvratnici (فُجَّار) će, sigurno, u ognju biti” – iza 82:13, gdje su dobri (أَبْرَار) u blagodatima; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And indeed, the wicked (فُجَّار) will be in Hellfire” — after 82:13, where the righteous (أَبْرَار) are in pleasure; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Zar ćemo bogobojazne izjednačiti s razvratnicima (فُجَّار)?”
why.en: “Or should We treat those who fear Allah like the wicked (فُجَّار)?”

why.bs: „To su nevjernici, razvratnici (فَجَرَة)” – nevjerstvo i razvrat zajedno; ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “Those are the disbelievers, the wicked ones (فَجَرَة)” — unbelief and wickedness together; ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, izaći iz poslušnosti; izvorno – oduprijeti se svojim štapom (عَصًا).
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, to go out of obedience; at root, to resist with one's staff (عَصًا).

why.bs: „A onoga ko se bude Allahu i Poslaniku Njegovu protivio (يَعْصِ) i preko granica Njegovih prelazio…” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “And whoever disobeys (يَعْصِ) Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits…” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: O melekima nad vatrom: „koji se Allahu ne protive (لَا يَعْصُونَ) u onome što im naredi” – poslušnost suprotno neposlušnosti.
why.en: Of the angels over the Fire: “who do not disobey (لَا يَعْصُونَ) Allah in what He commands them” — obedience as the opposite.

why.bs: Faraonu u času utapanja: „Zar sada, a prije si se protivio (عَصَيْتَ)?” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: To Pharaoh as he drowned: “Now? And you had disobeyed (عَصَيْتَ) [Him] before” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

shared.bs: Obje riječi govore o onome od čega čovjek ima koristi u životu. Razlikuju se po tome šta naglašavaju: jedna ono što se daje, druga korištenje koje traje neko vrijeme.
shared.en: Both words speak of what a person benefits from in life. They differ in what they stress: one what is given, the other a use that lasts a while.

tellApart.bs: Ono što se daje i dodjeljuje – na ovom i na onom svijetu, udio, hrana, pa i znanje → رِزْق; korist koja traje neko vrijeme, prolazno uživanje, pa i stvari koje se koriste → مَتَاع.
tellApart.en: What is given and allotted — in this world and the next, a share, food, and knowledge too → رِزْق; benefit that lasts for a time, passing enjoyment, and also the goods one uses → مَتَاع.

sources: ar-Rāġib al-Iṣfahānī, Mufradāt alfāẓ al-Qurʾān — entries رزق, متع
notes: ar-Rāġib (رزق): rizq is said of a continuing gift, of this world or the next; of a share (naṣīb); and of what reaches the stomach and nourishes; 63:10 'spend from what We have provided you' covers wealth, standing and knowledge; 18:19 'bi-rizqin minhu' = food; on 51:22 'it was said' (qīla) the rain is meant; 3:169 and 19:62 are the rizq of the Hereafter; ar-razzāq is said only of Allah. (متع): mutūʿ is extending and rising; matāʿ is benefit extended over time (intifāʿ mumtadd al-waqt); 2:36/7:24 'mustaqarrun wa matāʿun ilā ḥīn' tells that each person has an enjoyment in this world for a known span; 'matāʿ of this world is little' (4:77) — of no account beside the Hereafter (13:26); what is used in a house is matāʿ; 12:65 matāʿahum = their food, or it was said their containers; the gift to a divorced woman is matāʿ (2:241).
Not cited: 56:82 (ar-Rāġib reads rizq there as 'share'; tafsir differs).

ar-Rāġib verified against OpenITI 0502RaghibIsbahani.Mufradat.JK001150-ara1, entries رزق, متع (2026-11-06): 22 attributed points confirmed; changed — members/0/nuance (reworded): Mild: restore the verse he ties it to

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, dar koji neprestano pristiže – ovosvjetski ili onosvjetski; zatim udio, i ono što se pojede i od čega se hrani. U „trošite od onoga čime smo vas opskrbili” obuhvata, kaže on, imetak, ugled i znanje.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a gift that keeps coming — of this world or of the next; then a share, and what is eaten and nourishes. In “spend from what We have provided you” it covers, he says, wealth, standing and knowledge.

why.bs: Stanovnici pećine: „neka pogleda koja je hrana najčistija, pa neka vam od nje donese opskrbe (رِزْق)” – prema ar-Rāġibu, hrana.
why.en: The people of the cave: “let him look to which is the best of food and bring you provision (رِزْق) from it” — according to ar-Rāġib, food.

why.bs: „U njemu će oni ujutro i navečer opskrbu (رِزْق) svoju imati” – prema ar-Rāġibu, onosvjetski dar.
why.en: “And they will have their provision (رِزْق) therein, morning and afternoon” — according to ar-Rāġib, the gift of the Hereafter.

why.bs: „A na nebu je opskrba (رِزْق) vaša” – kod ar-Rāġiba: „kaže se” da je to kiša.
why.en: “And in the heaven is your provision (رِزْق)” — in ar-Rāġib: “it was said” that the rain is meant.

nuance.bs: Prema ar-Rāġibu, korist koja se proteže kroz vrijeme. Zato je ovaj svijet مَتَاع – uživanje za određeni rok, malo prema budućem svijetu; a مَتَاع su i stvari koje se koriste, kao prtljag i hrana.
nuance.en: According to ar-Rāġib, a benefit that stretches over time. So this world is مَتَاع — enjoyment for a set span, little beside the Hereafter; and مَتَاع is also the goods one uses, such as baggage and food.

why.bs: „Na Zemlji ćete boraviti i do roka određenog uživati (مَتَاع)” – prema ar-Rāġibu, svako ima uživanje u ovom svijetu za poznati rok.
why.en: “And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and enjoyment (مَتَاع) for a time” — according to ar-Rāġib, each person has an enjoyment in this world for a known span.

why.bs: „A život na ovom svijetu prema onom drugom samo je kratko uživanje (مَتَاع)” – ar-Rāġib navodi ovaj ajet.
why.en: “But what is the worldly life compared to the Hereafter except [brief] enjoyment (مَتَاع)” — ar-Rāġib cites this ayah.

why.bs: „Kad otvoriše svoje stvari (مَتَاع), nađoše da im je roba vraćena” – prema ar-Rāġibu, njihova hrana, a kaže se i njihove vreće.
why.en: “And when they opened their baggage (مَتَاع), they found their merchandise returned to them” — according to ar-Rāġib, their food, or, it was said, their containers.
